## Purpose and Scope

SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), optimized for low-latency and high-throughput inference [python/pyproject.toml:11-16](). It provides a complete runtime environment featuring automatic prefix caching via `RadixAttention`, multi-tier memory management, speculative decoding, and multi-dimensional parallelism across tensor, pipeline, expert, and data dimensions [python/pyproject.toml:14-14]().

This page serves as a high-level parent overview of the SGLang architecture, components, and design principles. Detailed explorations of repository layout, entry points, and low-level dataflow are delegated to child pages.

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:11-16]()

---

## Architectural Overview and Process Model

SGLang utilizes a multi-process architecture to isolate resource profiles, bypass Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), and maximize concurrency. CPU-bound tasks such as tokenization, request parsing, and scheduling run in separate processes from GPU-bound model execution [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:64-110]().

Title: SGLang Process Architecture Mapping to Code Entities

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Orchestrator Process"
        Engine["Engine\n(python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Tokenization Process"
        TokenizerMgr["TokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Scheduler and Execution Group"
        SchedulerProc["Scheduler\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py)"]
        ModelRunner["ModelRunner\n(python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Detokenization Process"
        DetokenizerMgr["DetokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Distributed Control Plane"
        DpController["DataParallelController\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py)"]
    end

    Engine -->|"spawns"| TokenizerMgr
    Engine -->|"spawns"| SchedulerProc
    SchedulerProc -->|"invokes"| ModelRunner
    TokenizerMgr -->|"ZMQ IPC"| SchedulerProc
    SchedulerProc -->|"ZMQ IPC"| DetokenizerMgr
    DetokenizerMgr -->|"ZMQ IPC"| TokenizerMgr
    DpController -.->|"control signals"| SchedulerProc
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:64-110](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:109-110]()

## Request Lifecycle and Dataflow

Incoming requests flow from client APIs through the asynchronous engine stack, getting tokenized, matched against prefix caches, scheduled into batches, executed on hardware accelerators, and finally detokenized back into text streams [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:73-100]().

Title: Request Lifecycle and Dataflow Mapping to Code Entities

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as "Client"
    participant Engine as "Engine\n(python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py)"
    participant TokenizerMgr as "TokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"
    participant Scheduler as "Scheduler\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py)"
    participant ModelRunner as "ModelRunner\n(python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py)"
    participant DetokenizerMgr as "DetokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py)"

    Client->>Engine: generate(GenerateReqInput)
    Engine->>TokenizerMgr: submit request
    Note over TokenizerMgr: Tokenize text & multimodal inputs
    TokenizerMgr->>Scheduler: tokenized batch (ZMQ IPC)
    Note over Scheduler: Match prefix cache & form batch
    loop Inference Iteration
        Scheduler->>ModelRunner: ForwardBatch execution
        ModelRunner-->>Scheduler: logits & KV cache states
        Scheduler->>DetokenizerMgr: token IDs output
        DetokenizerMgr->>TokenizerMgr: decoded text chunks
        TokenizerMgr->>Engine: partial response
        Engine->>Client: streamed stream / final JSON
    end
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:73-100](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:109-110]()

---

## Core Runtime Components

- **Engine**: Orchestrates subprocesses and exposes Python generation APIs (`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:64-64]().
- **TokenizerManager**: Handles asynchronous text and multimodal tokenization (`python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:110-110]().
- **Scheduler**: Manages GPU memory allocation, prefix caching, batch formation, and execution scheduling (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:109-109]().
- **ModelRunner**: Executes forward passes, CUDA graphs, and tensor operations (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`).
- **DetokenizerManager**: Translates output token sequences back into strings (`python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:71-71]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:64-110](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:1-1]()

---

## Memory Management and Caching

SGLang manages KV cache efficiently via pooled allocators (`ReqToTokenPool`, `TokenToKVPool`) and tree-structured prefix sharing (`RadixCache`) to minimize redundant computations across requests [python/pyproject.toml:14-16]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:14-16]()

This page provides a technical orientation to the SGLang monorepo layout, detailing major packages, internal implementation roles, and primary user-facing entry points. SGLang is a fast serving framework for large language models (LLMs) and vision language models (VLMs), leveraging a multi-process architecture for scalability and low latency [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:1-211](), [python/pyproject.toml:14-21]().

---

## Monorepo Layout

The SGLang repository is organized into several key directories, each fulfilling a specific function in building, deploying, or executing the framework components:

| Directory | Description |
|---|---|
| `python/` | Core Python package implementing the SGLang Runtime (SRT), CLI tools, API entrypoints, multimodal generation (diffusion), and runtime utilities [python/pyproject.toml:14-21](). |
| `sgl-kernel/` | High-performance custom kernel implementations targeting CUDA, ROCm, and CPU hardware, encompassing attention, MoE, quantization, and fused operators [python/pyproject.toml:88-88](). |
| `sgl-model-gateway/` | A high-throughput model routing gateway supporting multi-node orchestration, worker load balancing, and dynamic workflow management. |
| `sgl-router/` | Rust-based lightweight router implementing KV-event-driven cache-aware routing with Kubernetes EndpointSlice discovery and static worker pools [docker/npu.Dockerfile:128-139](). |
| `rust/` | Rust extension crates including `sglang-grpc`, which provides high-performance gRPC server capabilities and protobuf bindings [python/pyproject.toml:227-230](), [docker/Dockerfile:189-194](). |
| `tools/` | Utility tools, featuring `sglang-simulator` for offline trace replay, synthetic workload generation, and latency prediction. |
| `docs/` | Documentation source files covering user guides, feature references, and architectural specifications [docs/docs.json:1-10](). |
| `examples/` | Code examples demonstrating the SGLang domain-specific language (DSL), API client usage, and multimodal runtime integration. |
| `scripts/` | Development, continuous integration (CI), benchmarking, release automation, and utility scripts [python/pyproject.toml:216-217](). |
| `.agents/` | Internal skill and agent scripts supporting debugging and development automation workflows. |

### Diagram: Repository to Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph RepoRoot["Monorepo Root"]
        python_dir["python/"]
        sgl_kernel_dir["sgl-kernel/"]
        rust_dir["rust/"]
        sgl_router_dir["sgl-router/"]
    end

    subgraph PythonSubgraph["python/sglang/"]
        srt_runtime["srt/entrypoints/engine.py"]
        cli_entry["cli/main.py"]
        multimodal_gen["multimodal_gen/"]
    end

    subgraph KernelSubgraph["sgl-kernel/"]
        wheel_package["python/sgl_kernel/"]
    end

    subgraph RustSubgraph["rust/sglang-grpc"]
        grpc_server["sglang-grpc"]
    end

    cli_entry -->|launches| srt_runtime
    srt_runtime -->|invokes| wheel_package
    srt_runtime -->|interfaces| grpc_server
    srt_runtime -->|integrates| multimodal_gen
```
Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:14-21](), [python/pyproject.toml:88-88](), [python/pyproject.toml:216-217](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:1-211]()

## Major Packages and Modules

### 1. `sglang` (Python Core)

SGLang's primary Python package implements the SGLang Runtime (SRT), command-line interfaces, API entrypoints, and runtime subsystems:

- **Runtime (`srt/`)**: Implements the multi-process serving engine. Key components include:
  - `TokenizerManager`: Runs as an isolated subprocess handling tokenization of input text and prompt encoding [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-116]().
  - `Scheduler`: Core batch scheduler managing request queues, memory allocation, batch formation, and dispatching execution batches to model runners [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-114]().
  - `DetokenizerManager`: Runs separately to convert output token streams back into text efficiently [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:77-77]().

- **Command-Line Interface (`cli/`)**: Defines entrypoints such as `sglang = sglang.cli.main:main` and `killall_sglang = sglang.cli.killall:main` to start servers, manage runtime state, and clean up GPU resources [python/pyproject.toml:221-224]().

- **Multimodal Generation (`multimodal_gen/`)**: Provides the diffusion runtime supporting image, video, and vision-language generation using Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures [python/pyproject.toml:225-231]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:14-21](), [python/pyproject.toml:221-231](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-116]()

### 2. `sgl-kernel` (Kernel Package)

- Provides optimized custom operators and kernels for attention mechanisms, quantization (FP8, FP4, INT8), fused Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) operations, and elementwise transformations [python/pyproject.toml:88-88]().
- Distributed as the `sglang-kernel` wheel, wrapping low-level C++/CUDA implementations [python/pyproject.toml:88-88]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:88-88]()

### 3. Rust Extension Crates (`rust/`)

- Houses Rust extension crates including `sglang-grpc`, providing performant gRPC server endpoints, protobuf serialization, and streaming transport layers integrated into the Python backend [python/pyproject.toml:227-230](), [docker/Dockerfile:189-194]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:227-230](), [docker/Dockerfile:189-194]()

### 4. `sgl-model-gateway/` and `sgl-router/`

- **`sgl-model-gateway/`**: Provides control-plane worker registry, job queues, circuit breakers, and routing policies for multi-node deployments.
- **`sgl-router/`**: A lightweight Rust crate delivering KV-event-driven cache-aware routing, Kubernetes EndpointSlice discovery, and static worker load balancing [docker/npu.Dockerfile:128-139]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:14-21](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:128-139]()

---

## Primary User Entry Points

Interactions with SGLang occur through three primary user entry points:

### 1. Command Line Interface (CLI)

- Exposed via the `sglang` console script mapped to `sglang.cli.main:main` [python/pyproject.toml:221-222]().
- Translates command-line arguments into structured `ServerArgs` configuration objects that govern the initialization of the runtime engine [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:146-151]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:221-222](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:146-151]()

### 2. HTTP Server (OpenAI-Compatible API)

- Implemented via FastAPI, serving endpoints such as `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, and `/v1/embeddings`.
- Coordinates inter-process communication (IPC) via ZeroMQ sockets between the main HTTP server process, `TokenizerManager`, `Scheduler`, and `DetokenizerManager` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-116]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:14-21](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-116]()

### 3. Python Engine API

- Programmatic interface provided by the `Engine` class (`sglang.srt.entrypoints.engine.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:62-65]().
- Allows embedding the inference engine directly into Python applications to invoke `generate()` or `async_generate()` without HTTP server overhead [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:17-18]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:17-65]()

---

## Internal Request Lifecycle and Data Flow

### Diagram: Request Processing Flow Across Subprocesses

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "UserClient"
    participant HTTP as "FastAPIServer"
    participant TokenizerManager as "TokenizerManager"
    participant Scheduler as "Scheduler"
    participant DetokenizerManager as "DetokenizerManager"

    User->>HTTP: "POST /v1/chat/completions"
    HTTP->>TokenizerManager: "GenerateReqInput via ZMQ IPC"
    TokenizerManager->>TokenizerManager: "Tokenize input text"
    TokenizerManager->>Scheduler: "Send tokenized request"
    loop "Batch Scheduling Loop"
        Scheduler->>Scheduler: "Form ScheduleBatch & ForwardBatch"
    end
    Scheduler->>TokenizerManager: "Send generated tokens"
    TokenizerManager->>DetokenizerManager: "Pass token stream"
    DetokenizerManager->>HTTP: "Return decoded text response"
    HTTP->>User: "Stream JSON completion"
```
This sequence illustrates how requests traverse the multi-process architecture, utilizing ZeroMQ IPC channels and asynchronous managers to achieve high-throughput request processing.
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:68-116](), [python/pyproject.toml:14-21]()

---

## Build and Dependency Management

- **Python Packaging:** Configured through `pyproject.toml` utilizing `setuptools` and `setuptools-rust` [python/pyproject.toml:1-9]().
- **Dependencies:** Core packages include `torch`, `transformers`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, and `pyzmq`, alongside optional extras for diffusion (`diffusion`), tracing (`tracing`), and hardware-specific builds [python/pyproject.toml:24-159]().
- **Containerization:** Multi-stage Dockerfiles establish the CUDA development environment, install system packages, compile Rust extensions, and install framework wheels [docker/Dockerfile:1-179]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:1-159](), [docker/Dockerfile:1-179]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page establishes the conceptual request lifecycle across the SGLang Runtime (SRT) architecture. It defines the core multi-process execution boundaries, key classes responsible for each phase, and how data structures transform, enabling efficient serving of LLMs and multimodal models without entangling implementation-specific details.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]()`

---

## 1. Request Lifecycle Overview

SRT partitions the workload into separate asynchronous processes for concurrency and scalability. Requests transition through four distinct stages, each handled by dedicated managers or components communicating over ZeroMQ:

1. **TokenizerManager**: Accepts incoming text and multimodal data, normalizes and tokenizes requests, and constructs tokenized IPC payloads `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`.
2. **Scheduler**: Receives tokenized requests, manages admission, applies batching policies, allocates KV cache slots, and produces batch objects `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`.
3. **ModelRunner**: Converts batches into GPU tensors and executes neural network forward passes on hardware accelerators `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`.
4. **DetokenizerManager**: Consumes token ID output, performs incremental token decoding, handles streaming response formatting, and sends output back to clients `[python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:139-140]()`.

### Diagram: End-to-End Request Transformation (Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space)

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural_Language_Space"
        User["UserPromptOrHTTPRequest"]
    end

    subgraph "TokenizerManager_Process"
        TM["TokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"]
        RI["GenerateReqInput\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py)"]
        TI["TokenizedGenerateReqInput\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Scheduler_Process"
        S["Scheduler\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py)"]
        SB["ScheduleBatch\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py)"]
        RQ["Req\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "ModelRunner_Process"
        MR["ModelRunner\n(python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py)"]
        FB["ForwardBatch\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "DetokenizerManager_Process"
        DM["DetokenizerManager\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py)"]
        BTO["BatchTokenIDOutput\n(python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py)"]
    end

    User -->|"HTTP/gRPC Request"| TM
    TM -->|"GenerateReqInput (normalized)"| RI
    RI -->|"Tokenize to TokenizedGenerateReqInput"| TI
    TI -->|"Send via ZMQ IPC"| S
    S -->|"Batch formation ScheduleBatch"| SB
    SB -->|"Track requests Req instances"| RQ
    SB -->|"Send via ZMQ IPC"| MR
    MR -->|"Convert to ForwardBatch GPU tensors"| FB
    FB -->|"Forward pass execution"| MR
    MR -->|"BatchTokenIDOutput token ID batch"| DM
    DM -->|"Incremental detokenization & streaming output"| TM
    TM -->|"Respond to User"
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:108-112]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`

---

## 2. Core Runtime Components and Their Roles

### 2.1 TokenizerManager

- **Role**: Acts as the IPC boundary receiving raw user requests via HTTP/gRPC and translates them into normalized structured types (`GenerateReqInput`) and then tokenizes into `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` objects for scheduling `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`.
- **Multimodal Handling**: Invokes multimodal processors when relevant to embed images, video, or audio features before tokenization `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:137-137]()`.
- **Lifecycle Tracking**: Manages the request's tokenization state, streaming offsets, and collects metrics related to tokenization `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:158-163]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:111-123]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:137-163]()`

### 2.2 Scheduler

- **Role**: Central coordinator for batch scheduling and memory resource management. It receives tokenized requests, performs batching, and schedules them onto GPU workers `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`.
- **Batch Structures**: Groups multiple requests into `ScheduleBatch` containers holding CPU-bound scheduling data and `Req` objects representing individual requests within a batch `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`.
- **Scheduling Policies**: Implements cache-aware batch formation using strategies like Last-Position-Minimized (LPM), First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), and Highest Response Ratio Next (HRRN) `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-22]()`.
- **Memory Management**: Allocates KV cache slots through mechanisms like `ReqToTokenPool` and `UnifiedRadixCache` to ensure physically contiguous token memory assignments and efficient prefix sharing `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:133-133]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py:99-99]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1-10]()`

### 2.3 ModelRunner

- **Role**: Executes neural network forward passes using GPU-accelerated backends. It converts CPU `ScheduleBatch` objects into GPU tensor batches called `ForwardBatch` `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`.
- **ForwardBatch Details**: Holds GPU-resident tensors including input tokens, attention masks, and auxiliary structures like block tables that describe sequence segmentation and dependencies `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`.
- **Execution Modes**: Supports different forward pass modes such as PREFILL, DECODE, EXTEND, MIXED, and specialized verification passes for speculative decoding `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:136-136]()`.
- **Backend Support**: Interfaces with different hardware backends and supports optimizations like CUDA graphs for fast replay `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-22]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:136-136]()`

### 2.4 DetokenizerManager

- **Role**: Watches for output token ID batches produced by the `ModelRunner` and progressively decodes token IDs back to text strings `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`.
- **Streaming Support**: Implements prefix-safe incremental decoding to allow partial outputs streamed back to users with low latency `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`.
- **Output Management**: Handles stop criteria detection and finalizes responses, handling edge cases like beam search outputs or sampling fallback `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:128-130]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:128-130]()`

---

## 3. Data Structure Transitions Through the Pipeline

The lifecycle for a request traverses several core data representations distributed across processes:

| Object Name              | Owning Process/Component    | Description                                                                                  |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `GenerateReqInput`       | TokenizerManager             | Normalized user input from HTTP/gRPC payloads representing raw generation requests `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:111-123]()` |
| `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` | TokenizerManager → Scheduler | Tokenized version including token ID arrays, routing flags, model and sampling parameters `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:104-104]()` |
| `Req`                    | Scheduler                    | Internal per-request structure tracking tokens, KV cache allocations, session state `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()` |
| `ScheduleBatch`          | Scheduler                    | CPU-side aggregate representing a batch of `Req` objects scheduled together `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()` |
| `ForwardBatch`           | ModelRunner                  | GPU tensor container derived from `ScheduleBatch`, used for efficient model forward execution `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:45-48]()` |

These transitions are intentionally separated by IPC boundaries to ensure modularity and scalability.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:104-123]()`

---

## 4. IPC Boundaries and Communication

Communication between core processes uses ZeroMQ sockets and msgspec for structured serialization. The design isolates CPU-bound stages (TokenizerManager, Scheduler) from GPU-intensive stages (ModelRunner) and streaming stages (DetokenizerManager).

### Diagram: Inter-Process Communication & Dataflow Architecture (Code Entity Space)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant TM as "TokenizerManager\n(tokenizer_manager.py)"
    participant S as "Scheduler\n(scheduler.py)"
    participant MR as "ModelRunner\n(model_runner.py)"
    participant DM as "DetokenizerManager\n(detokenizer_manager.py)"

    TM->>S: "TokenizedGenerateReqInput (ZMQ IPC)"
    S->>S: "Batch Formation ScheduleBatch instances"
    S->>MR: "ForwardBatch Payload (ZMQ IPC)"
    MR->>MR: "Model Forward Pass Torch/CUDA"
    MR->>DM: "BatchTokenIDOutput (ZMQ IPC)"
    DM->>TM: "Streaming Text Output"
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:97-120]()`

### IPC Boundaries Summary

| Components Communicating      | Protocol               | Data Structures Exchanged                |
|------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| TokenizerManager → Scheduler  | ZeroMQ (msgspec/Pickle) | `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:104-124]()` |
| Scheduler → ModelRunner       | ZeroMQ (msgspec)        | `ScheduleBatch` → `ForwardBatch` payload `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-59]()` |
| ModelRunner → DetokenizerManager | ZeroMQ (msgspec)     | `BatchTokenIDOutput` `[python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:101-102]()` |
| DetokenizerManager → TokenizerManager | Internal / IPC   | Streaming text output `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()` |

The IPC design ensures efficient and decoupled scaling of tokenization, scheduling, model execution, and response streaming, respecting hardware boundaries and process isolation.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:104-124]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-59]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`

---

# Summary

This document outlines the conceptual flow and component roles for handling user requests from raw inputs to generated text outputs within the SGLang serving framework. Requests progress sequentially through:

- Tokenization by `TokenizerManager` (ingest and tokenize),
- Scheduling by `Scheduler` (batch formation, KV cache allocation),
- Execution by `ModelRunner` (GPU-accelerated forward passes),
- Detokenization by `DetokenizerManager` (incremental decoding and streaming outputs).

These core runtimes communicate via well-defined IPC boundaries using ZeroMQ and serialized structured data, enabling modular scaling and maintaining separation of concerns.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:1-20]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-15]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-13]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:43-48]()`

# End of Page

## Package Architecture Overview

The `sglang` Python distribution includes runtime package data and exposes the `sglang` CLI [python/pyproject.toml:221-223](), [python/pyproject.toml:225-231](). Its runtime engine entrypoint is implemented in `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py`, which coordinates the tokenizer manager, scheduler processes, detokenizer, data-parallel controller, and platform interfaces [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:72-78](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:113-132](). The standard dependency set defined in `python/pyproject.toml` includes PyTorch and a collection of runtime and kernel-related packages [python/pyproject.toml:24-108]().

## Docker Deployment

The primary `docker/Dockerfile` starts from an NVIDIA CUDA development image, establishes a virtual environment using `uv`, installs system packages, and defines parallel builder stages [docker/Dockerfile:5-18](), [docker/Dockerfile:44-64](), [docker/Dockerfile:66-136](), [docker/Dockerfile:162-179](). The `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` variant targets CUDA 13.4 and exposes build arguments for selecting source builds or prebuilt wheels [docker/Dockerfile.cu134:5-27]().

### Multi-Stage Docker Build Pipeline

The Dockerfile implements a BuildKit stage layout where a base stage feeds dependency builders, whose artifacts are combined in the framework stage [docker/Dockerfile:162-179](). Image variants and deployment best practices are documented in the child section.

Title: "Docker Build Stage Relationships"
```mermaid
graph TB
    Base["base"]
    TorchDeps["torch_deps"]
    FlashCache["flashinfer_cache"]
    HPC["hpc_ops_builder"]
    DevTools["devtools_builder"]
    Router["router_builder"]
    Framework["framework"]
```

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the procedures for installing SGLang and its core kernel library, covering multiple hardware architectures and deployment targets. It details the multi-platform build system, dependency management via `pyproject.toml` and its platform-specific variants (`python/pyproject_cpu.toml`, `python/pyproject_xpu.toml`, `python/pyproject_npu.toml`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`), as well as platform-specific installation instructions. SGLang serves as a fast serving framework for large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), encompassing Python-level orchestration and native kernel integration.

For containerized deployment, consult **2.3 Docker Deployment**. For hardware-specific runtime configuration, see **2.2 Hardware Platform Configuration**.

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:11-15](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:6-10]()

---

## Installation Architecture Overview

SGLang supports a modular installation strategy that accommodates a wide range of hardware backends including NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm/HIP, Intel Xeon/XPU, Ascend NPU, Moore Threads MUSA, and Apple Silicon MPS. The Python package and its dependencies are distributed via PyPI, using separate platform-specific configuration files that declare tailored dependency sets and wheels.

Native components such as kernels and Rust extensions are compiled using `setuptools-rust` and specialized CMake builds. The relational flow from platform-specific config files to final distribution artifacts is illustrated below.

### Installation Artifact Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Configuration_Space
        P_OTH["python/pyproject_other.toml"] -- "AMD/MUSA/MPS platforms" --> BUILD["Build Process"]
        P_XPU["python/pyproject_xpu.toml"] -- "Intel XPU platform" --> BUILD
        P_CPU["python/pyproject_cpu.toml"] -- "Intel Xeon CPU platform" --> BUILD
        P_NPU["python/pyproject_npu.toml"] -- "Ascend NPU platform" --> BUILD
        P_SGLANG["python/pyproject.toml"] -- "NVIDIA CUDA platform" --> BUILD
    end

    subgraph Build_Entity_Space
        SCM["setuptools_scm"] -- "Versioning & Git tags" --> VER_GEN["Generate python/sglang/_version.py"]
        VER_FILE["python/sglang/_version.py"] -- "Version file" --> VER_GEN
        TAGS["scripts/release/get_version_tag.py"] -- "Git metadata" --> SCM
    end

    subgraph Output_Artifacts
        W_SGL["sglang Wheel (Python)"]
        W_KER_CUDA["sgl-kernel Wheel (CUDA)"]
        W_KER_ROCM["sgl-kernel Wheel (ROCm)"]
        W_KER_CPU["sglang-cpu Package"]
        W_KER_XPU["sglang-kernel-xpu Wheel"]
    end

    BUILD --> SCM
    SCM --> VER_FILE
    VER_FILE --> W_SGL

    P_SGLANG -- "Depends on sgl-kernel (CUDA)" --> W_KER_CUDA
    P_OTH -- "Depends on sgl-kernel (ROCm/MUSA/MPS)" --> W_KER_ROCM
    P_XPU -- "Depends on sglang-kernel-xpu" --> W_KER_XPU
    P_CPU -- "Depends on CPU-specific dependencies" --> W_KER_CPU
```

Sources:
[python/pyproject_other.toml:1-15](), [python/pyproject_cpu.toml:1-15](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:1-15](), [python/pyproject_npu.toml:1-15](), [python/pyproject.toml:1-15]()

## Method 1: PyPI Installation

Install SGLang from PyPI using `pip`, leveraging variant extras tailored to your target hardware platform and usage scenario. This method installs pre-built binary wheels including Python bindings, native kernels, and platform-specific dependencies.

### Standard Runtime Dependencies

The base runtime dependencies include core utilities and libraries such as `aiohttp`, `requests`, `tqdm`, `numpy`, `IPython`, and `setproctitle` to support asynchronous HTTP services, JSON processing, and system introspection [python/pyproject_other.toml:16-17]().

### Serving Stack and Extras

For full model serving functionality, additional dependencies include:
- HTTP/Web serving: `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `uvloop`, `pyzmq` [python/pyproject.toml:40-103]()
- Transformers & tokenization: `transformers==5.19.0`, `timm==1.0.25`, `sentencepiece==0.2.1`, `tiktoken` [python/pyproject.toml:82-101]()
- Output formatting and constrained generation tools: `xgrammar==0.2.7`, `llguidance>=1.7.6,<2.0.0`, `outlines==0.1.11` [python/pyproject.toml:50-105]()
- API clients: `openai==2.8.0`, `anthropic>=0.20.0` [python/pyproject.toml:24-61]()

Install with:

```bash
pip install sglang
```

This command automatically resolves and installs platform-specific dependencies as declared by your environment and selected extras.

Sources:
[python/pyproject.toml:24-108](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:16-68]()

---

## Method 2: Source Builds and Kernel Compilation

Building SGLang from source grants flexibility for advanced customization, native kernel extension, or bespoke platform support.

### Build System and Multi-Architecture Support

- The build is managed using `setuptools` and `setuptools-rust` to compile Python extensions and Rust components such as the gRPC server [python/pyproject.toml:1-9](), [docker/Dockerfile:193-199]().
- Rust toolchain (version ≥ 1.85) is required, installed via helper scripts if missing [docker/Dockerfile:193-199]().
- GPU kernel compilation utilizes CMake with architecture-specific flags for supported compute capabilities [docker/Dockerfile:80-81]().
- Pre-built kernel wheels like `sglang-kernel` are also available to simplify installation on compatible platforms and CUDA versions [docker/Dockerfile:200-209]().

Sources:
[python/pyproject.toml:1-9](), [docker/Dockerfile:80-81](), [docker/Dockerfile:193-209]()

---

## Platform-Specific Installation

SGLang uses separate project configuration files to manage dependencies and wheels for specific hardware platforms, enabling optimized builds per backend. These variants are:

### 1. NVIDIA CUDA

- The default `python/pyproject.toml` is used for NVIDIA CUDA GPUs [python/pyproject.toml:1-15]().
- It includes dependencies like `flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.7.4`, `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.2.post1`, `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.8`, and `sglang-kernel==0.4.11` [python/pyproject.toml:41-88]().
- The `sglang-kernel` package provides optimized CUDA kernels.

### 2. AMD ROCm (HIP)

- Managed by `python/pyproject_other.toml` with optional feature sets like `srt_hip` or `srt_hip_rocm724` [python/pyproject_other.toml:133-151]().
- Includes ROCm-compatible dependencies such as `petit_kernel==0.0.2`, `wave-lang==3.8.2`, along with ROCm-specific PyTorch wheels and kernel wheels [python/pyproject_other.toml:133-151]().

### 3. Intel XPU

- Uses `python/pyproject_xpu.toml`, which pins to `torch==2.14.0+xpu` and related audio/libtorch packages [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:1-73]().
- Installs specialized `sglang-kernel-xpu` wheel from prebuilt GitHub releases targeted at Intel Xe architecture [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:66-66]() via a direct index mapping [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:83-100]().

### 4. Intel CPU (Xeon)

- `python/pyproject_cpu.toml` configures this variant under project name `sglang-cpu`.
- Uses `intel-openmp` on x86_64 for optimized parallelism and supports CPU-only execution paths.

### 5. Ascend NPU

- Uses the `python/pyproject_npu.toml` configuration [python/pyproject_npu.toml:1-122]().
- Includes runtime dependencies and optional dependency sets for Huawei Ascend NPU platforms [python/pyproject_npu.toml:18-76]().

### 6. Moore Threads MUSA and Apple Silicon MPS

- `srt_musa` variant includes `torch_musa`, `torchada`, `deep_ep`, `flashinfer-python` variants optimized for Moore Threads GPUs, bundled with relevant kernel and runtime packages [python/pyproject_other.toml:196-217]().
- `srt_mps` variant provides Apple Metal optimized runtime wheels and dependencies like `mlx` and `mlx-lm` for Apple Silicon platforms [python/pyproject_other.toml:227-230]().

Sources:
[python/pyproject.toml:41-88](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:133-151](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:196-217](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:227-230](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:66-100](), [python/pyproject_npu.toml:18-76]()

## Installation Implementation Details

The installation workflow tightly couples packaging metadata, CLI entry points, and runtime orchestration components. The following diagram maps critical project files and runtime code entities involved in installation and execution entry points, bridging Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space.

### Relationship Diagram: Project Metadata to Runtime Entry Points

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Project_Metadata
        PYP["python/pyproject.toml"] --- SCRIPTS["[project.scripts] section"]
        VER["python/pyproject.toml (setuptools_scm)"] --- ENGINE_CLASS["sglang.srt.entrypoints.engine.Engine (class)"]
    end

    subgraph Entry_Points
        CLI_MAIN["sglang.cli.main:main"] --- SGL_CMD["sglang CLI command"]
        KILL_CMD["sglang.cli.killall:main"] --- KILL_SCRIPT["killall_sglang CLI command"]
    end

    subgraph Runtime_Execution
        SCHED_RUN["sglang.srt.managers.scheduler.run_scheduler_process()"] --- ENGINE_CLASS
        TOK_MANAGER["sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager.TokenizerManager (class)"] --- ENGINE_CLASS
        ENGINE_CLASS -- "Initializes" --> TOK_MANAGER
        ENGINE_CLASS -- "Spawns" --> SCHED_RUN
    end

    PYP --- CLI_MAIN
    PYP --- KILL_CMD
    CLI_MAIN --> ENGINE_CLASS
    SCHED_RUN -.-> TOK_MANAGER
```

This diagram links the package metadata scripts registered in `python/pyproject.toml` under `[project.scripts]` (`sglang` CLI main and killall commands) to the Python runtime entrypoints that bootstrap the scheduler and tokenizer manager processes essential for inference serving [python/pyproject.toml:221-223](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:28-118]().

### Versioning and CLI scripts

- Versioning is managed via `setuptools_scm` which uses git tags to generate version info dynamically during build [python/pyproject.toml:5]().
- The package registers user commands:
  - `sglang` runs the main CLI interface (`sglang.cli.main:main`)
  - `killall_sglang` terminates running SGLang processes (`sglang.cli.killall:main`) [python/pyproject.toml:221-223]().

[python/pyproject.toml:5](), [python/pyproject.toml:221-223](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:28-118]()

This page provides a technical explanation of how SGLang detects hardware platforms at runtime, supports CUDA, ROCm, NPU, XPU, CPU, and MLX/MPS backends, manages platform-specific dependencies, and exposes out-of-tree (OOT) platform extension mechanisms.

---

## 1. Platform Detection and Resolution Lifecycle

SGLang determines the active hardware backend at runtime through cached introspection queries against PyTorch and environment variables. The platform selection logic is coordinated by module-level lazy singletons and discovery hooks in `python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py` and `python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py` [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:1-12](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-11]().

The base class `DeviceMixin` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py`) defines shared device identity queries (`is_cuda()`, `is_hip()`, `is_npu()`, `is_xpu()`, `is_cpu()`, `is_musa()`, `is_mps()`, `is_sail()`) [python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:115-141](). Subclassing `SRTPlatform` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py`) binds these device traits to runtime subsystem factories such as attention backends, graph runners, and memory pools [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:78-86](). Platform capabilities are explicitly declared using `PlatformCapabilities` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py`), which dictates features like Triton execution, graph capture, and PyNccl support before subsystems are constructed [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-76]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    Title["Platform Resolution Lifecycle Dataflow"]
    Start["Access current_platform"] --> CheckEnv{"SGLANG_PLATFORM env set?"}
    CheckEnv -- "Yes" --> FrontLoad["Front-loading filter: load specified entry point in sglang.srt.platforms"]
    CheckEnv -- "No" --> AutoDiscover["Auto-discover: query all plugins & check torch capabilities"]
    
    AutoDiscover --> CheckCPU["CpuSRTPlatform if SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1"]
    CheckCPU --> CheckSail["SailSRTPlatform if SAIL available"]
    CheckSail --> CheckCUDA["CudaSRTPlatform if torch.cuda available"]
    CheckCUDA --> CheckNPU["NPUSRTPlatform if torch.npu available"]
    CheckNPU --> CheckROCm["RocmSRTPlatform if ROCm available"]
    CheckROCm --> CheckXPU["XpuSRTPlatform if torch.xpu available"]
    CheckXPU --> CheckMLX["MlxSRTPlatform if MLX available"]
    CheckMLX --> CheckFallback["Fallback to base SRTPlatform"]

    FrontLoad --> Instantiate["Instantiate SRTPlatform subclass"]
    CheckFallback --> Instantiate
    Instantiate --> Active["current_platform ready"]
```
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:75-107](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-86](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:115-141]()

## 2. Supported Platforms and Build Configurations

SGLang structures its platform-specific Python dependencies and build targets across distinct dependency files and configuration matrices, supporting specialized device arches like AMD ROCm (`gfx942`, `gfx950`, `gfx1250`) [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-27](), Ascend NPU (`a3`, `950`) [scripts/ci/npu/npu_ci_install_dependency.sh:55-59](), and Intel XPU [docker/xpu.Dockerfile:1-60]().

| Platform | Device Type | Detection Function | Build Config File | Kernel Package |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| NVIDIA CUDA | GPU | `is_cuda()` | `python/pyproject.toml` | `sglang-kernel` |
| AMD ROCm (HIP) | GPU | `is_hip()` | `python/pyproject_other.toml` | `sglang-kernel` (ROCm) |
| Intel XPU | GPU | `is_xpu()` | `python/pyproject_xpu.toml` | `sgl-kernel-xpu` |
| Intel CPU | CPU | `is_cpu()` | `python/pyproject_cpu.toml` | `sglang-kernel-cpu` |
| Ascend NPU | NPU | `is_npu()` | `python/pyproject_npu.toml` | `sgl-kernel-npu` |
| Moore Threads GPU | GPU | `is_musa()` | `python/pyproject_other.toml` | `srt_musa` extra |
| Apple Silicon MLX | GPU | `is_mlx()` | `python/pyproject_other.toml` | `srt_mlx` extra |
| Apple Silicon MPS | GPU | `is_mps()` | `python/pyproject_other.toml` | `srt_mps` extra |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:21-29](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:1-73](), [python/pyproject_npu.toml:1-69]()

## 3. Out-of-Tree (OOT) Plugin System

External hardware vendors can integrate custom platform runtimes without modifying the core SGLang codebase by implementing setuptools entry points under the `sglang.srt.platforms` group [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx:11-38]().

### Plugin Contract and Lifecycle
An OOT platform must subclass `SRTPlatform` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py`) and expose an activation callback matching [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx:56-61]():
```python
def activate() -> str | None:
    """Return the platform class qualname when this hardware is available."""
```

The runtime loader (`_resolve_platform` in `python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py`) discovers these plugins dynamically [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:112-138]() and validates their compute capabilities before assigning them to `current_platform`.

Sources: [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx:11-116](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:112-138](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:78-86]()

---

## 4. Platform-Specific Backend Subsystems

Each platform implementation overrides specific hooks in `SRTPlatform` to inject custom graph runners, memory pools, and compilation backends:

- **Ascend NPU**: Implements `NPUCudaGraphBackend` (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py`) using `torch.npu.NPUGraph` and `replay_with_input_update` to rebind input shapes dynamically [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py:1-46](). Specialized memory pools like `NPUMHATokenToKVPool` manage complex KV caching structures [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:92-125](). NPU dependencies are managed by `scripts/ci/npu/npu_ci_install_dependency.sh` [scripts/ci/npu/npu_ci_install_dependency.sh:1-96]() and Dockerfiles like `docker/npu.Dockerfile` [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-150]().
- **Intel XPU**: Integrates through `XpuSRTPlatform` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/xpu.py`), leveraging `sgl-kernel-xpu` and optimized oneAPI kernels for Triton and grouped GEMM operations. XPU dependencies are managed by `docker/xpu.Dockerfile` [docker/xpu.Dockerfile:1-120]().
- **Apple Silicon MLX**: Uses `MlxModelRunner` (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py`) for model execution and `MlxModelRunnerStub` (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py`) for lightweight scheduler-side bookkeeping without loading PyTorch weights [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:97-103](). It manages attention KV and auxiliary state internally via `_DummyKVCache`, bypassing standard `KVCache` allocation [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:43-81]().
- **Intel CPU and NUMA Topology**: Utilizes `CpuSRTPlatform` (`python/sglang/srt/platforms/cpu.py`) with `intel-openmp` threading, AMX extensions, and automated NUMA node binding via `configure_subprocess` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py`) to align worker processes with physical socket topologies [python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py:32-85]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py:1-46](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:92-125](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/xpu.py](), [python/sglang/srt/platforms/cpu.py](), [scripts/ci/npu/npu_ci_install_dependency.sh:1-96](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-150](), [docker/xpu.Dockerfile:1-120](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py:1-192](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:43-103](), [python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py:32-85]()

## Purpose and scope

This page details the Docker build architecture, image variants, multi-stage build pipelines, platform dependency configurations, and deployment best practices for SGLang containers. It covers the primary Dockerfiles provided in the codebase (NVIDIA CUDA, CUDA 13.4, AMD ROCm, and Huawei Ascend NPU) along with their corresponding build-time arguments, parallel builder stages, and runtime environment requirements. [docker/Dockerfile:1-210]()[docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-120]()[docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-159]()

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:1-210](), [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-120](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-159]()

---

## Overview

SGLang provides containerized deployment options across multiple hardware accelerators. The container build system utilizes Docker BuildKit for parallel stage execution, isolated Python virtual environments (typically located at `/opt/sglang` or `/workspace`), and platform-specific dependency injection. 

| Build family | Primary Dockerfile | Key Target Platforms & Configurations |
|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA CUDA | `docker/Dockerfile` | CUDA 13.0.3 default, Ubuntu 24.04 CUDA development base, parallel builder stages [docker/Dockerfile:5-12]()[docker/Dockerfile:162-178]() |
| NVIDIA CUDA 13.4 | `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` | CUDA 13.4.1, custom PyTorch cu134 wheels, optional source/wheel toggles [docker/Dockerfile.cu134:5-27]() |
| AMD ROCm | `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` | Architecture-specific flavors (`gfx942`, `gfx950`, `gfx1250`), optional MoRI/NIXL/uTLX components [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-48]() |
| Huawei Ascend NPU | `docker/npu.Dockerfile` | CANN toolkit base, `torch-npu`, Ascend Triton, MemFabric integration [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-35]()[docker/npu.Dockerfile:111-126]() |

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:5-12](), [docker/Dockerfile.cu134:5-27](), [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-48](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-35]()

---

## Image Variants and Multi-Stage Build Architecture

### NVIDIA build stages and parallel compilation

The NVIDIA Dockerfile (`docker/Dockerfile`) uses a multi-stage approach where dependency builders execute in parallel via BuildKit before feeding into the final `framework` image assembly. The `base` stage configures CUDA runtime paths and system packages, while `torch_deps` sets up the Rust toolchain and installs `sglang-kernel` without triggering full dependency resolution cascades [docker/Dockerfile:11-64]()[docker/Dockerfile:181-208]().

**Diagram: NVIDIA BuildKit stages and artifact flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    base["base"]
    torch_deps["torch_deps"]
    flashinfer_cache["flashinfer_cache"]
    hpc_ops_builder["hpc_ops_builder"]
    halops_wheel["halops_wheel"]
    devtools_builder["devtools_builder"]
    router_builder["router_builder"]
    framework["framework"]

    base --> torch_deps
    torch_deps --> flashinfer_cache
    torch_deps --> hpc_ops_builder
    torch_deps --> halops_wheel
    base --> devtools_builder
    base --> router_builder
    torch_deps --> framework
    flashinfer_cache --> framework
    hpc_ops_builder --> framework
    halops_wheel --> framework
    devtools_builder --> framework
    router_builder --> framework
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:162-178]()

Optional components can be enabled via build arguments such as `ENABLE_MORI`, `ENABLE_NIXL`, and `BUILD_UTLX` [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:29-48]().

## Core Docker Build Arguments and Configuration

The build process accepts a variety of build arguments (`ARG`) and sets corresponding environment variables (`ENV`) to customize the compilation and dependency resolution steps.

| Argument Name | Default / Role | File Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `CUDA_VERSION` | `13.0.3` (main), `13.4.1` (CUDA 13.4) | `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` [docker/Dockerfile:5]()[docker/Dockerfile.cu134:26-27]() |
| `PYTHON_VERSION` | `3.12` default for isolated virtual environment | `docker/Dockerfile` [docker/Dockerfile:7]() |
| `SGL_KERNEL_VERSION` | `0.4.11` version pin for `sglang-kernel` | `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` [docker/Dockerfile:16]()[docker/Dockerfile.cu134:15]() |
| `GPU_ARCH` | Selects AMD GPU architecture (e.g., `gfx950`) | `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:65-66]() |
| `CANN_VERSION` | `9.1.0` toolkit version for Huawei NPU images | `docker/npu.Dockerfile` [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1]() |
| `DEVICE_TYPE` | Device model identifier (e.g., `950`, `a3`) | `docker/npu.Dockerfile` [docker/npu.Dockerfile:2]() |

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:5-16](), [docker/Dockerfile.cu134:15-27](), [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:65-66](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:1-2]()

## Platform Dependency Management

SGLang manages vendor-specific dependency stacks through specialized project manifests and extras defined in `python/pyproject.toml` and auxiliary TOML files [python/pyproject.toml:11-24]()[python/pyproject_other.toml:124-158]()[python/pyproject_xpu.toml:5-18]()[python/pyproject_npu.toml:5-18]().

| Platform | Manifest / Extra Reference | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA CUDA | `python/pyproject.toml` | Standard runtime dependencies, PyTorch, and FlashInfer integrations [python/pyproject.toml:11-24]()[python/pyproject.toml:80-99]() |
| AMD ROCm | `python/pyproject_other.toml` (`srt_hip`, `srt_hip_rocm724`) | Custom ROCm torch stacks, `petit_kernel`, and `wave-lang` [python/pyproject_other.toml:124-151]() |
| Intel XPU | `python/pyproject_xpu.toml` | Explicit `pytorch-xpu` indexes and `sglang-kernel-xpu` [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:18-23]()[python/pyproject_xpu.toml:83-96]() |
| Huawei NPU | `python/pyproject_npu.toml` | CANN bindings, `torch-npu`, and MemFabric packages [python/pyproject_npu.toml:5-18]() |

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:11-99](), [python/pyproject_other.toml:124-151](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:18-96](), [python/pyproject_npu.toml:5-18]()

## Container Deployment Best Practices

When deploying SGLang containers in production, adhere to the following operational guidelines informed by the codebase structure:

1. **Environment Isolation**: The Docker images establish a dedicated Python environment (e.g., `/opt/sglang`) via `uv` to avoid conflicts with host or system Python packages [docker/Dockerfile:44-64]().
2. **GPU Runtime Integration**: Ensure the container runtime (such as NVIDIA Container Toolkit or AMD ROCm container runtime) is correctly configured so that device nodes and shared libraries (`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `CUDA_HOME`, or `ASCEND_HOME_PATH`) are properly exposed [docker/Dockerfile:29-37]()[docker/npu.Dockerfile:140-142]().
3. **Server Argument Configuration**: At runtime, configure the entrypoint using `ServerArgs` parameters parsed by the engine entrypoint [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:146-151]() to manage tensor parallelism, KV cache memory fractions, and port bindings.

**Diagram: Container runtime initialization flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph ContainerRuntime["Container Execution"]
        docker_container["Docker Container Start"]
        env_vars["Environment & Device Paths Setup"]
        engine_entry["python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py"]
    end

    subgraph RuntimeEntities["SGLang SRT Components"]
        server_args["ServerArgs"]
        scheduler["Scheduler & ModelRunner"]
    end

    docker_container --> env_vars
    env_vars --> engine_entry
    engine_entry --> server_args
    server_args --> scheduler
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:29-37](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:114-151](), [docker/npu.Dockerfile:140-142]()

This page documents SGLang's architecture and implementation details for multi-node setup, distributed initialization, and network configuration, including orchestration strategies such as Kubernetes-native fleet management (`llm-d`, `sgl-router`, and `RayEngine`) [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115](). It covers how SGLang initializes process groups via `bootstrap.py` and `parallel_state.py`, configures communication backends, manages multi-node parallelism degrees (`tp`, `pp`, `ep`, `dp`), and coordinates disaggregated inference workflows [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:9-24]().

---

## Multi-Node Deployment Overview

SGLang supports serving large language and vision-language models on multiple physical hosts to scale memory capacity and throughput. This enables:

- **Large Model Serving:** Models exceeding single-node GPU memory limits are distributed across multiple hosts through tensor parallelism (TP), pipeline parallelism (PP), expert parallelism (EP), and data parallelism (DP) [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115]().
- **Disaggregated Execution:** Prefill and decode stages can be separated on dedicated node pools coordinated by transfer engines, load inquirers, and data parallel controllers to optimize resource utilization [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/disagg.py:1-10]().
- **Distributed Initialization:** Uses PyTorch Distributed-based rendezvous and process group creation managed by `init_parallel_runtime` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115]() and `init_distributed_environment` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:9-24]().
- **Distributed Communication:** Supports high-performance collective operations with NCCL/RCCL/HCCL backends and custom all-reduce optimizations like FlashInfer fusion and symmetric memory allocators [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:178-202]().
- **Ray-Based Orchestration:** Employs Ray actors, placement groups, and bundle index resolutions in `RayEngine` for managing multi-node clusters with workload placement [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-156]().

**Key concepts and components:**

| Component | Role | Code Location |
| :------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------- |
| `init_parallel_runtime` | Entry point for distributed hardware and process group setup | `python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115` |
| `init_distributed_environment` | Initializes the PyTorch distributed backend and world group | `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:9-24` |
| `GroupCoordinator` | Abstraction for managing collective communication subgroups | `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:171-176` |
| `RayEngine` | Manages Ray scheduler actors across placement groups | `python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-80` |
| `SchedulerLoadInquirer` | Aggregates load metrics across DP ranks for balancing and reporting | `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py:33-95` |
| `DataParallelController` | Dispatches requests across multiple data parallel workers | `python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py:157-192` |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:9-25](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115](), [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-80](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py:33-95](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py:157-192](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/disagg.py:1-10]()

## Distributed Initialization Architecture

### Coordination Parameters and Bootstrap

Distributed initialization in SGLang occurs during server startup via the `init_parallel_runtime` function [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:93-115](). This function performs the following core tasks:

- Resolves the communication backend (NCCL, GLOO, HCCL) through `_resolve_backend` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:117]().
- Applies monkey-patch for P2P access checks disabling when necessary [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:118-119]().
- Invokes CPU thread binding routines if running on CPU-based nodes to optimize resource affinity [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:75-87]().
- Sets the current device using `torch.get_device_module(device).set_device()` to activate the target GPU or accelerator [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:127]().
- Initializes shared transfer engines, such as Mooncake, to enable inter-node tensor transfer [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:138]().
- Constructs the multi-node parallel groups (world, TP, PP, EP, DP) with `_init_parallel_groups` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:146]().

SGLang uses runtime rank computation utilities, such as `spawn_world_rank` and `derive_spawn_ranks` defined in `runtime_context.py` [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:95-137](), to map local subgroup ranks (`tp_rank`, `pp_rank`) and offsets (`ep_join_rank_offset`) into global `WORLD` ranks for proper distributed coordination.

## Ray-Based Multi-Node Orchestration

When deployed with Ray, SGLang manages multi-node topology with Ray Placement Groups and Scheduler Actors (`SchedulerActor`) for coordinated scheduling and job distribution [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-34]().

### Ray Placement Group Bundle Resolution and Validation

- `_find_engine_bundle(placement_group, nnodes)` inspects Ray placement group bundles to determine which bundle contains the main Engine node, ensuring the rank-0 scheduler resides with the Engine node for optimal local communication [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:50-80]().
- `_compute_world_size()` calculates the complete distributed world size by multiplying `tp_size`, `pp_size`, `dp_size` dimensions, and factoring attention-DP enabling when applicable [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:108-120]().
- `_resolve_bundle_indices(pg, world_size)` derives the sequence of bundle indices for scheduler instantiation, using the `SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` environment variable or otherwise assigning bundles sequentially [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:122-156]().
- `_validate_custom_placement_group(pg, world_size)` enforces placement group sanity by asserting one GPU device per bundle and guaranteeing placement group capacity meets or exceeds the world size requirements [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:158-184]().

This integration enables Kubernetes-native deployment patterns and flexible orchestration of heterogeneous node resources with minimal manual configuration [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-184]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:14-184]()

## Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and Load Management

SGLang supports the architectural pattern of disaggregated inference, splitting the prefill phase (token context building) and decode phase (token extension) onto distinct node groups for optimized resource utilization [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/disagg.py:1-10](). The `ServerArgs` dataclass includes fields like `disaggregation_mode`, `disaggregation_transfer_backend`, and `disaggregation_decode_allocation_policy` to configure this behavior [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/disagg.py:1-10](). The `handle_pd_disaggregation` function in `pd_disaggregation_hook.py` validates and normalizes these arguments, including handling `mooncake_tcp` backend aliases and compatibility checks with other features like HiSparse [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/pd_disaggregation_hook.py:23-168]().

### SchedulerLoadInquirer and Load Snapshots

The `SchedulerLoadInquirer` class aggregates performance and workload metrics essential for load balancing and status reporting [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py:33-95]():

- `get_num_waiting_uncached_tokens()` estimates the amount of input tokens asynchronously queued and waiting for prefill model computation, considering cache miss statistics and disaggregation modes [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py:78-93]().
- `get_loads()` compiles a comprehensive snapshot of running workloads per data parallel rank (`LoadSnapshot`), including queue lengths, token count statistics, memory metrics via `MemoryMetrics`, and speculative decoding metrics via `SpeculativeMetrics` [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py:95-163]().

### Load Snapshot Transport: SHM vs. ZMQ

Load snapshots are published periodically by each scheduler and consumed by `DataParallelController` or `TokenizerManager` (exposed via `/v1/loads` in `v1_loads.py`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/v1_loads.py:96-150]():
- **SHM Mode (Single-Node):** Schedulers write snapshots to a memory-mapped `/dev/shm` file via `ShmLoadSnapshotWriter`, which `ShmLoadSnapshotReader` reads [python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py:10-16]().
- **ZMQ Mode (Multi-Node):** When `attn_dp_enabled` and `nnodes > 1`, schedulers push snapshots over ZeroMQ. `ZmqShmLoadSnapshotReader` on node 0 drains the ZMQ stream and populates the local SHM file for controllers [python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py:17-33]().

## Network Communication Stack

### 1. Collective Operations and Custom All-Reduce Ops

SGLang defines and registers custom collective communication operators over distributed process groups, enabling optimized distributed tensor communication [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:178-202]():

- `inplace_all_reduce(tensor, group_name)`: Executes an all-reduce in-place on the provided tensor using the named group’s collective communication context [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:183-191]().
- `outplace_all_reduce(tensor, group_name, method)`: Performs an out-of-place all-reduce on a tensor with selectable algorithmic variants [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:193-197]().
- `flashinfer_allreduce(tensor, group_name)`: Specialized all-reduce leveraging FlashInfer libraries for improved performance on compatible hardware.

### 2. Data-Parallel Attention Padding Modes (`DpPaddingMode`)

The data-parallel attention mechanism controls token padding modes for efficient communication and memory usage [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:141-191]():

- `MAX_LEN`: Pads all token batches to the maximum token count across all data parallel replicas, enabling symmetric memory layouts and using an `all_gather_into_tensor` collective [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:141-142]().
- `SUM_LEN`: Pads batches to the sum of tokens across replicas and performs a reduction with `all_reduce` operations [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:144-145]().

SGLang dynamically selects padding modes based on runtime environment, workload shape, and hardware backend constraints [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:156-192]().

## Environment Variables for Distributed Deployment

SGLang leverages several environment variables to configure distributed behavior, network settings, and resource allocation. These variables are managed through the `envs` singleton [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:52](), which provides a structured way to access and parse environment settings.

| Environment Variable | Description | Default Value | Code Reference |
| :------------------- | :---------- | :------------ | :------------- |
| `SGLANG_HOST_IP` | Host IP address for the server. | `0.0.0.0` | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:32-35]() |
| `SGLANG_PORT` | Port for the server. | auto-detected | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:36-39]() |
| `SGLANG_EPLB_HEATMAP_COLLECTION_INTERVAL` | Interval of passes to collect the metric of selected count of physical experts on each layer and GPU rank. `0` means disabled. | `0` | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:57-60]() |
| `SGLANG_EPLB_P2P_BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE` | Number of expert IDs per batch when submitting P2P ops during EPLB rebalance (CUDA and ROCm). Smaller values prevent NCCL/RCCL GPU-side accumulation hangs but increase overhead. | `32` | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:61-65]() |
| `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_FORCE_MAX_LEN` | Forces `MAX_LEN` padding mode for DeepEP V2 to ensure symmetric token counts across ranks. | `false` | [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:174]() |
| `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` | Controls staging of aiter custom all-gather/reduce-scatter inputs through IPC pool during CUDA graph capture. | `0` | [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:92]() |
| `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A` | Workaround for ROCm 7.0.0A issues. | `false` | [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:148]() |
| `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` | Cache directory for model weights and other data. | `~/.cache/sglang` | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:82-85]() |
| `SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` | Comma-separated list of Ray bundle indices for scheduler instantiation. | Not set | [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:130]() |

The `EnvField` class and its subclasses (`EnvStr`, `EnvBool`, `EnvInt`, `EnvFloat`, `EnvTuple`, `EnvJSON`) provide the parsing logic for these environment variables [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-208](). The `_DeprecatedEnvFallback` mixin handles legacy `SGL_` prefixes, issuing deprecation warnings when encountered [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:163-189]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-208](), [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:32-85](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:148-174](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:92](), [python/sglang/srt/ray/engine.py:130]()

This page describes SGLang's multi-process server architecture, covering key processes, inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms, and core configuration systems. It provides a high-level view to orient developers on how components interact and collaborate to serve inference requests efficiently.

## Purpose and Scope

SGLang employs a **multi-process architecture** separating tokenization, scheduling, model execution, and detokenization into dedicated processes. This design supports:

- **Avoiding Python GIL contention:** Each major task runs in its own process, allowing independent CPU and GPU utilization [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-58]().
- **Asynchronous pipelining:** Tokenization, scheduling, and detokenization proceed concurrently, enabling high throughput [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-58]().
- **Fault isolation:** Subprocess watchdogs monitor critical processes to increase resilience [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:197-200]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:137-143]().

The core architecture centers around four primary process types:
1. **HTTP Server + Engine (Main Process):** Handles API requests and manages child process lifecycles [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:15-18]().
2. **TokenizerManager (Subprocess):** Responsible for tokenizing requests and multimodal input encoding [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-14]().
3. **Scheduler (Subprocess):** Manages batching, KV cache memory, and forwards execution to the model runner [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/output_streamer.py:88-106]().
4. **DetokenizerManager (Subprocess):** Handles incremental detokenization of model outputs and returns text [python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:14-14]().

For detailed architectural explanation of processes and IPC, server configuration, and tokenizer internals, see these child pages:
- [Multi-Process Architecture and IPC](#3.1) — Document the process model, ZMQ IPC channels, and inter-process communication patterns.
- [Server Configuration (ServerArgs)](#3.2) — Document ServerArgs parameters, the arg_groups resolution pipeline, runtime context, and their effects.
- [TokenizerManager and DetokenizerManager](#3.3) — Explain tokenization/detokenization processes, multi-tokenizer support, and template handling.

## Multi-Process Design Overview

SGLang uses a multiprocess design with asynchronous ZeroMQ (ZMQ) communication channels connecting its core components. Payloads transferred between processes (such as `BaseReq`, `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`, and `BatchStrOutput`) are defined in `io_struct.py` using `msgspec` for high-performance serialization [python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py:14-48]().

### System Components and IPC
Title: "System Components and IPC"

## `TokenizerManager` and `DetokenizerManager`

Tokenization and detokenization are handled by dedicated subprocesses to eliminate GIL bottlenecks and maintain high throughput.

- **TokenizerManager** (`tokenizer_manager.py`) handles text tokenization, multimodal feature extraction, and request state bookkeeping (`rid_to_state`) [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:14-58]().
- **DetokenizerManager** (`detokenizer_manager.py`) manages incremental token decoding, stop-string trimming, and tool call parsing [python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:75-136]().
- **Multi-Tokenizer Routing** (`multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`) supports multi-process HTTP workers and socket mapping for distributed frontends [python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py:17-40]().
