## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a detailed technical overview of the model execution pipeline in SGLang, focusing on how scheduled request batches are transformed into GPU-resident data structures, the handling of different forward pass modes (`prefill`, `decode`, `extend`, `mixed`), the selection and operation of runner backends (`ModelRunner`, `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`, `EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner`), and subsequent output processing including logits handling and sampling.

Key architectural components documented here include the `ModelRunner` class orchestrating forward passes [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-180](), the `ForwardMode` enumeration describing forward pass types [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:57](), various runner backend implementations optimizing CUDA graph usage, and the memory pool management underlying CUDA graph execution. This page also details the data flow from high-level scheduling batches through IPC serialization to low-level forward batches executed on device.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-180](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-185](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]()

---

## System Overview & Data Flow

Model execution transforms input batches from request-level scheduling into device-specific tensors optimized for efficient GPU processing.

Title: "End-to-End Request Execution Data Flow"
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace
        UserReq["User Prompt + Sampling Parameters"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace
        subgraph SchedulerProcess
            SB["ScheduleBatch<br/>python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py"]
        end
        
        subgraph IPCChannel
            MWB["ModelWorkerBatch (Serialized)<br/>python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py"]
        end
        
        subgraph WorkerProcess
            FB["ForwardBatch (Device tensors)<br/>python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py"]
            MR["ModelRunner<br/>python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py"]
            Model["Model Forward<br/>Model.forward()"]
            LP["LogitsProcessor<br/>python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py"]
            Sampler["Sampler<br/>python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py"]
        end
    end
    
    UserReq --> SB
    SB -->|"serialize_and_send"| MWB
    MWB -->|"ForwardBatch.init_new"| FB
    FB --> MR
    MR --> Model
    Model -->|"logits"| LP
    LP --> Sampler
    Sampler -->|"sampled tokens"| UserReq
```

#### Explanation:

-   `ScheduleBatch`: High-level batch combining multiple requests, containing token IDs, metadata, and scheduling info at CPU host.
-   `ModelWorkerBatch`: Serialized form of `ScheduleBatch` to transmit across process boundaries.
-   `ForwardBatch`: GPU-resident batch created from `ModelWorkerBatch`, including device-pinned tensors and cache state [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-80]().
-   `ModelRunner`: Core logic that executes forward passes on the `ForwardBatch` using selected runner backends [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-15]().
-   `Model.forward`: Actual model network forward call producing logits.
-   `LogitsProcessor`: Applies logprob transformations and penalties [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:66-68]().
-   `Sampler`: Samples tokens from processed logits to produce final output tokens [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:1-100]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-26](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-15](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:66-68]()

---

## Batch Data Structure Transformations and Forward Modes

### Data Representations

| Data Structure | Location | Responsibility |
|:---------------|:---------|:---------------|
| `ScheduleBatch` | CPU (host) | High-level scheduling info, request metadata |
| `ModelWorkerBatch` | CPU / serialization | IPC-friendly serialized batch for transmission |
| `ForwardBatch` | GPU device | Low-level tensor inputs and cache state |

The conversion from `ModelWorkerBatch` to `ForwardBatch` pins host memory, transfers to GPU asynchronously when possible, and prepares indices and masks required for forward execution [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-80]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-80]()

---

### ForwardMode Enumeration

The `ForwardMode` enum directs the model's forward behavior for different token generation phases [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_mode.py]():

| Mode | Meaning | Usage Context |
|:-----|:--------|:--------------|
| `EXTEND` | Extend prompt tokens, typically prefill mode | Feeding new prompt tokens into KV cache |
| `DECODE` | Autoregressive decoding, generating one token at a time | Standard next-token generation |
| `MIXED` | Combined extend + decode within chunked prefill (hybrid mode) | Chunked prompt forwarding overlapping with decode phase |
| `IDLE` | Placeholder mode, no tokens processed, marks worker idle | Internal synchronization during parallelism |
| `DRAFT_DECODE` | Speculative decoding: draft model generates tokens | Draft model generating initial tokens for verification |
| `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` | Speculative decoding: draft model extends tokens | Draft model extending a sequence of tokens [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:121]() |
| `TARGET_VERIFY` | Speculative decoding: target model verifies draft tokens | Target model verifying tokens proposed by a draft model [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:57](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:121]()

---

## Runner Backends and CUDA Graph Architecture

SGLang supports multiple runner backends encapsulating different CUDA graph strategies to optimize kernel launches and forward pass performance.

### Runner Types

| Runner Backend | Description | Typical Forward Phase Use |
|:---------------|:------------|:--------------------------|
| **DecodeCudaGraphRunner** | Base class for CUDA graph runners, handling decode, target verify, and DLLM extend modes. | Decode, Target Verify, DLLM Extend [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]() |
| **EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner** | Captures and replays CUDA graphs for EAGLE draft model's decode phase. | DRAFT_DECODE [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:101-115]() |
| **EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner** | Captures and replays CUDA graphs for EAGLE draft model's extend phase. | DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-101]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:101-115](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-101]()

---

### Execution Phases and Backend Mapping

Title: "Execution Phase to Runner Backend Mapping"
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph ExecutionPhase
        Prefill["Prefill (Prompt Extension)"]
        Decode["Decode (Token Generation)"]
        DraftDecode["Draft Decode (Speculative)"]
        DraftExtend["Draft Extend (Speculative)"]
        TargetVerify["Target Verify (Speculative)"]
    end

    subgraph RunnerBackend
        DecodeGraph["DecodeCudaGraphRunner<br/>python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py"]
        EagleDraftGraph["EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner<br/>python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py"]
        EagleDraftExtendGraph["EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner<br/>python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py"]
    end

    Prefill --> DecodeGraph
    Decode --> DecodeGraph
    DraftDecode --> EagleDraftGraph
    DraftExtend --> EagleDraftExtendGraph
    TargetVerify --> DecodeGraph
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:101-115](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-101]()

## Forward Pass Execution Pipeline and Memory Pool Management

### ModelRunner: Forward pass orchestration

`ModelRunner` is the central orchestrator of forward passes. It receives a `ForwardBatch`, inspects the `ForwardMode`, and dispatches to the correct model forward variant [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-180]().

Key steps:

1.  **Batch conversion:** From CPU input (`ScheduleBatch` → `ModelWorkerBatch` → `ForwardBatch`) [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:17-26]().
2.  **Runner selection:** Based on config and hardware platform, picks suitable runner backend [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/utils.py]().
3.  **Forward pass:** Runs the forward method on the model, guarded or accelerated by CUDA graph runners [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14]().
4.  **Output capture:** Captures logits and ancillary outputs for post-processing and sampling.

### Process-wide CUDA Graph Pool

CUDA graph backends rely on a preallocated shared GPU memory pool called the `CudaGraphBufferRegistry` to handle large contiguous workspace allocations once per process to reduce overhead during capture [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:69-74]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-180](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:69-74]()

---

## Output Processing and Logits Handling

After model forward calls produce raw logits, these undergo a series of processing steps before token sampling:

-   **Logprob computation and penalties:** The `LogitsProcessor` applies temperature scaling, frequency and presence penalties, repetition penalties, and other logit modifications [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:66-68]().
-   **Sampling:** Processed logits are fed into sampling algorithms implemented in the sampler module [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:102]().
-   **Output tokens:** Sampled tokens are sent upstream to the scheduler or HTTP frontend for client response.

Title: "Logits Processing and Sampling Flow"
```mermaid
graph LR
    ModelRunner["ModelRunner<br/>python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py"]
    ModelForward["Model.forward()"]
    LogitsProcessor["LogitsProcessor<br/>python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py"]
    Sampler["Sampler<br/>python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py"]
    OutputTokens["Generated Tokens"]

    ModelRunner --> ModelForward
    ModelForward --> LogitsProcessor
    LogitsProcessor --> Sampler
    Sampler --> OutputTokens
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:14-180](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:66-68](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:102]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes SGLang’s CUDA graph paths for prefill and decode: capture and replay, full, breakable, and `torch.compile` piecewise prefill backends, shape and batch padding, and the static buffers used to feed captured graphs. The available code excerpts cover prefill backend selection and setup, shared graph buffers, graph backend behavior, attention handling, and selected decode-buffer definitions. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-35]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py:38-43]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py:14-20]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-35](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py:38-43](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py:14-20]()

## CUDA Graphs Overview

A CUDA graph captures GPU work into a reusable execution graph. In SGLang’s full backend, a `FullCudaGraphBackend` instance stores graphs and outputs keyed by shape; capture uses warmup forwards before capturing the graph. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:104-123]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:137-169]()

Graph replay requires stable input storage and compatible shapes. The `CudaGraphBufferRegistry` mirrors `ForwardBatch` attributes into graph-resident buffers, while the static buffer dataclasses provide phase-specific storage. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:14-23]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py:14-20]()

### Prefill Backend Choices

`PrefillCudaGraphRunner` documents four prefill settings: `breakable`, `full`, `tc_piecewise`, and `disabled`. `disabled` is handled at the model-runner level, so no prefill graph runner is constructed. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-35]()

| Backend | Capture and replay approach | Batch and metadata considerations |
|---|---|---|
| `breakable` | `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` captures segments without `torch.compile`. | Captures the transformer body with one request slot. Multi-request prefill is supported by running attention metadata and the LM-head/logits tail outside the captured body. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:16-22]() |
| `full` | `FullCudaGraphBackend` captures one graph per `num_tokens` bucket for the captured transformer body. | Uses a configured number of request slots; replay pads tokens to a bucket and pads unused request slots with zero-length sentinels. Batches larger than the captured slot count fall back to eager execution. Attention metadata is refreshed out of graph against the slot-padded batch. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:23-30]() |
| `tc_piecewise` | `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend` uses `torch.compile`; per-shape compiled/captured pieces reside in the compiler’s internal cache. | Supports multi-request prefill. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:31-34]() |
| `disabled` | The model-runner layer handles the setting. | The prefill graph runner is not constructed. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:35]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-35]()

## CUDA Graph Runner and Replay Data Flow

The prefill path is selected through `resolve_prefill_backend` and the backend classes imported by `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`. During replay, the graph needs stable storage for batch inputs; the buffer registry provides a `ForwardBatch`-to-slot mirror, while backend-private buffers remain owned by the attention backend. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:77-111]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:14-23]()

### Diagram: Prefill Workload to Graph Backend Entities (Code Space Bridge)

```mermaid
graph LR
    PrefillWorkload[""ForwardBatch(ForwardMode.EXTEND)""] --> PrefillRunner[""PrefillCudaGraphRunner""]
    PrefillRunner --> ResolveBackend[""resolve_prefill_backend""]
    ResolveBackend --> BreakableBackend[""BreakableCudaGraphBackend""]
    ResolveBackend --> FullBackend[""FullCudaGraphBackend""]
    ResolveBackend --> PiecewiseBackend[""TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend""]
    PrefillRunner --> ForwardBatchObj[""ForwardBatch""]
    ForwardBatchObj --> BufferRegistry[""CudaGraphBufferRegistry""]
    BufferRegistry --> GraphSlots[""GraphSlot""]
    GraphSlots --> BreakableBackend
    GraphSlots --> FullBackend
    GraphSlots --> PiecewiseBackend
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:77-111](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:14-23](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:155-170]()

### Static Inputs, Slots, and Padding

`CudaGraphBufferRegistry` is the graph-buffer mirror for `ForwardBatch`. Each `GraphSlot` mirrors a batch attribute, and its name must match that attribute so `fill_from` can read it from the batch and replay can expose the slot view back on a batch. Slot shape and slicing are defined with respect to batch-size and token axes. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:14-23]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:155-170]()

The registry defines padding policies for regions beyond the raw batch or token counts. `KEEP_PAD` leaves the tail unchanged when the caller guarantees it will not be read; `FILL_SENTINEL` resets it to a slot-specific sentinel; `ZERO` clears it; `FOREACH_COPY` copies only raw elements; and `FILL_ONCE` initializes the buffer at allocation rather than every replay. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:106-133]()

For eligible CUDA copies, the registry may use `torch._foreach_copy_` or the `try_small_copy` helper; otherwise it groups copies by source and destination dtype and applies foreach copies or individual `copy_` operations. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:45-81]()

| Policy | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `KEEP_PAD` | Leave the padded region as-is; the caller must ensure it will not be read. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:106-113]() |
| `FILL_SENTINEL` | Reset the padded region to the slot’s `pad_value`. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:109-114]() |
| `ZERO` | Reset the padded region to zero; the documented examples include `out_cache_loc` and `req_pool_indices`. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:113-117]() |
| `FOREACH_COPY` | Copy raw elements while leaving the padded region unchanged. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:118-121]() |
| `FILL_ONCE` | Initialize the whole buffer once at allocation and do not reset it per iteration. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:122-125]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:14-23](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:45-81](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:106-170]()

### Diagram: Replay Buffer Population Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    ForwardBatchInput[""ForwardBatch""] --> RegistryFill[""CudaGraphBufferRegistry.fill_from""]
    RegistryFill --> FillContextObj[""FillContext""]
    FillContextObj --> SlotObj[""GraphSlot""]
    SlotObj --> PaddingPolicyCheck{""PaddingPolicy""}
    PaddingPolicyCheck --> KeepPad[""KEEP_PAD""]
    PaddingPolicyCheck --> FillSentinel[""FILL_SENTINEL""]
    PaddingPolicyCheck --> ZeroPad[""ZERO""]
    PaddingPolicyCheck --> ForeachCopy[""FOREACH_COPY""]
    PaddingPolicyCheck --> FillOnce[""FILL_ONCE""]
    KeepPad --> ReplayAction[""Captured_graph_replay""]
    FillSentinel --> ReplayAction
    ZeroPad --> ReplayAction
    ForeachCopy --> ReplayAction
    FillOnce --> ReplayAction
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:106-170](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py:135-152]()

## Full, Breakable, and Piecewise Prefill Graphs

### Full CUDA Graphs

`FullCudaGraphBackend` stores captured graphs and their outputs in dictionaries keyed by shape. It also tracks a graph memory pool, the graph runner, and a capture stream. Its capture session obtains the global graph memory pool and assigns its pool ID before capture. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:104-135]()

For each shape, `capture_one` runs the forward function twice as warmup before graph capture. The warmups synchronize the device and barrier the tensor-parallel group; the implementation also supports a post-warmup hook and optional output-buffer reuse. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:137-169]()

For prefill, the documented `full` behavior uses token buckets and a configured request-slot capacity. It pads tokens to the nearest bucket and unused request slots with zero-length sentinels; if the live batch exceeds the captured slot count, it uses eager execution. Attention metadata is refreshed out of graph against the padded batch. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:23-30]()

### Breakable CUDA Graphs

`BreakableCudaGraphBackend` captures graph segments separated by eager break markers; it does not use `torch.compile`. The backend documentation describes attention and Mamba boundaries as break points, with attention metadata recomputed at replay outside captured segments. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/breakable_cuda_graph_backend.py:14-17]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/breakable_cuda_graph_backend.py:65-68]()

A capture session sets up the graph pool and enables breakable capture. For each shape, `capture_one` performs two warmup forwards, creates a `BreakableCUDAGraph`, and captures the forward under `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`. Capture inputs are retained because CUDA graphs retain tensor addresses, not Python tensor lifetimes. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/breakable_cuda_graph_backend.py:70-111]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/breakable_cuda_graph_backend.py:113-159]()

For prefill, the breakable backend captures the transformer body with one request slot. Its multi-request support keeps attention metadata and the LM-head/logits tail outside the captured body. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:16-22]()

The `eager_on_graph` decorator is used to mark functions that should execute eagerly even when inside a CUDA graph capture. This is crucial for breakable CUDA graphs, allowing parts of the computation (like attention or KV cache updates) to run dynamically. For example, `RadixAttention._eager_attention` is decorated with `eager_on_graph` [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:37](), and `_breakable_qsa_indexer` in Qwen4-Exp also uses it. The `BreakableCUDAGraph` class manages the segments of the graph using `cuda-python` bindings to interact with the CUDA runtime for stream capture status [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend_utils/breakable_cuda_graph/breakable_cuda_graph.py:89-93](). It also hooks `torch.cuda.Stream.wait_stream` to track side-stream forks and joins during capture [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend_utils/breakable_cuda_graph/breakable_cuda_graph.py:118-144]().

### `torch.compile` Piecewise Graphs

The `tc_piecewise` backend wraps the model with `torch.compile`. Its per-shape compiled/captured pieces reside in the compiler’s internal cache, and the prefill runner documentation states that it supports multi-request prefill. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:31-34]()

### Diagram: Capture and Replay by Backend

```mermaid
graph TD
    BackendSelection[""resolve_prefill_backend""] --> FullGraphBackend[""FullCudaGraphBackend""]
    BackendSelection --> BreakableGraphBackend[""BreakableCudaGraphBackend""]
    BackendSelection --> PiecewiseGraphBackend[""TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend""]
    FullGraphBackend --> FullCaptureAction[""capture_one(per num_tokens bucket)""]
    FullCaptureAction --> FullReplayAction[""replay with padded token/request axes""]
    BreakableGraphBackend --> SegmentedCaptureAction[""capture transformer body segments""]
    SegmentedCaptureAction --> EagerAttentionAction[""eager attention metadata & LM-head/logits tail""]
    EagerAttentionAction --> BreakableReplayAction[""replay segments with live batch metadata""]
    PiecewiseGraphBackend --> CompileAction[""torch.compile model wrapper""]
    CompileAction --> PiecewiseCache[""internal compiler cache""]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:16-34](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/breakable_cuda_graph_backend.py:65-68](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:104-123](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:37](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend_utils/breakable_cuda_graph/breakable_cuda_graph.py:89-93](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend_utils/breakable_cuda_graph/breakable_cuda_graph.py:118-144]()

## Attention Behavior Around Prefill Graphs

`RadixAttention.forward` identifies when execution is inside a breakable graph or full prefill graph. When the prefill attention wrapper is enabled and the batch is an extend operation inside prefill graph scope, attention uses `_eager_attention` for breakable and full prefill graphs. Otherwise it uses real-row handling when applicable or delegates to the active attention backend. [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176]()

This division allows graph-captured transformer work to coexist with attention execution that handles live prefill metadata. The prefill runner documentation specifically describes out-of-graph attention metadata refresh for full graphs, and out-of-graph attention metadata and logits-tail execution for breakable graphs. [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:16-30]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:16-30]()

## Batch Size and Token Bucket Selection

Prefill graph capture uses a set of token sizes, and full prefill uses one graph per `num_tokens` bucket. During replay, full prefill rounds the token count up to a bucket and pads request slots to the configured capture capacity; batches larger than that capacity fall back to eager execution. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:23-30]()

The prefill runner defines a maximum token-padding factor of 2 to avoid excessive extra model work when a sparse bucket list forces replay at a larger captured size. It also defines geometric chunked-prefix variants `(1, 2, 4, 8, 16)` because prefix attention adds a loop body per chunk. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py:38-43]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:23-30](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py:38-43]()

## Decode Buffers and Performance Optimizations

`DecodeInputBuffers` is the static-buffer dataclass backing decode-phase capture and replay. It includes stable storage for token inputs, request indices, sequence lengths, cache locations, positions, masks, logits, and other optional decode inputs. The shown `create` method allocates these tensors at configured maximum batch and token dimensions and initializes several of them with zero or sentinel values. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py:14-20]()

The shared copy path in `runner_utils/buffers.py` attempts `try_small_copy` for CUDA tensors and otherwise groups copies by dtype pair before using `torch._foreach_copy_` or individual copies. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py]()

For prefill attention, graph padding must be bounded: the runner’s documented padding-factor limit exists because replay executes every padded token in the bucket. A larger bucket can therefore trade fewer graph shapes and lower launch overhead for more model work per replay. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/buffers.py:14-20]()

## Distributed Admission and Compatibility

The scheduler’s DP-attention component imports CUDA graph backend and configuration checks, the prefill graph runner, and `ForwardMode`. Its `MLPSyncBatchInfo` carries per-rank eligibility flags for decode, draft, and prefill CUDA graphs, alongside token counts and forward-mode information. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:33-41]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:155-184]()

The same file’s `_spec_input_cuda_graph_compatible` helper treats absent, idle, and prebuilt batches as permissive; otherwise it checks speculative input compatibility through `spec_info.cuda_graph_compatible`. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:93-110]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:33-41](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:93-110](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py:155-184]()

This page documents SGLang's memory management system and KV (Key-Value) cache architecture. It covers the hierarchical caching subsystem, memory pools, prefix sharing mechanisms, and their integration with the scheduler and model execution pipeline.

## 5.1. Memory Pools and Token-to-KV Mapping

SGLang separates the abstraction of requests and tokens from physical KV storage through a layered pool design, enhancing efficient memory management and reuse. `ReqToTokenPool` allocates tokens per request, mapping each request’s token ranges into a global token index space [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-19](). Meanwhile, `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` variants (such as `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` and `PageInterleavePoolAllocator`) allocate physical KV cache slots to tokens, coordinating indices with the physical KV cache memory [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py:52-61]().

Specialized allocators and memory pools support diverse model and attention architectures, including `MHATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, and page-interleaved sharded pools [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py:73-88](). These ensure that token sequences and multi-tier layouts map correctly onto physical or host-backed buffers.

For details, see [Memory Pools and Token-to-KV Mapping](#5.1).

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NL[""UserPromptInput""]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        TokenizerMgr[""TokenizerManager""]
        ReqPool[""ReqToTokenPool (python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py)""]

```

## 5.2. RadixCache and Prefix Sharing

SGLang leverages radix tree data structures (`UnifiedRadixCache`) to enable prefix sharing of KV cache between requests [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/storage_attachment.py:41-45](). Nodes represent prefix substrings of tokens and hold references to VRAM or host KV cache segments. `UnifiedTreeCore` owns the tree structure and LRU eviction components [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py:1-12]().

Reference counting, locking, and unified LRU eviction policies ensure that cached nodes currently in use by active requests or execution phases cannot be prematurely evicted. SGLang also supports flexible radix tree tree-core backends and unified cache components for managing complex prompt prefix trees via `RustUnifiedTreeCore` bindings [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:1-8]().

For comprehensive data structures, runtime locking behaviors, eviction policies, and cross-language radix tree implementations, see [RadixCache and Prefix Sharing](#5.2).

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Query and Prompt Space"
        Prompt[""UserPromptMatch""]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Cache[""UnifiedRadixCache (python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py)""]
        TreeCore[""UnifiedTreeCore (python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py)""]
        RustCore[""RustUnifiedTreeCore (rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs)""]
    end

    Prompt --> Cache
    Cache --> TreeCore
    TreeCore --> RustCore
```
*Diagram: Bridging Prefix Matching Prompts to Radix Tree Code Entities.*

## 5.3. HiCache Multi-Tier Storage

HiCache is SGLang's hierarchical multi-tier cache system spanning device, host, and storage tiers. The device tier manages active VRAM KV caches, while the host tier holds evicted or prefetched KV cache blocks in CPU RAM pools or sidecar buffers [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/storage_attachment.py:1-10]().

The cache controller (`HybridCacheController`) coordinates runtime events, backend attachments/detachments via `StorageAttachment`, and asynchronous prefetch operations [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/storage_attachment.py:41-56](). Specialized components and sparse memory pool allocators handle sparse attention and sidecar pool layouts without sacrificing cache consistency.

For a detailed breakdown of architecture, memory pools, events, and backend management, see [HiCache Multi-Tier Storage](#5.3).

**Sources:**
[python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/storage_attachment.py:1-56]()

---

## 5.4. Storage Backends and Transfer Optimization

SGLang supports various storage backends (Mooncake, HF3FS, LMCache, NIXL) for distributed, disaggregated, and heterogeneous caching needs [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/kv_shard_hook.py:32-35](). These backends provide high-throughput synchronization between prefill and decode workers or persistent object storage loading.

Transfer queues and non-blocking asynchronous pipelines manage contiguous memory block transfers across tiers, minimizing stalls and VRAM contention during model execution.

See [Storage Backends and Transfer Optimization](#5.4) for the full design and backend descriptions.

**Sources:**
[python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/kv_shard_hook.py:32-35]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents SGLang's memory pool architecture that supports efficient mapping from logical requests to tokens, and from tokens to physical key-value (KV) cache memory. It explains fundamental components such as:

- `ReqToTokenPool`: manages the mapping from concurrent requests to their tokens.
- `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` and its derivatives: allocators managing tokens' physical KV slot allocations.
- `KVCache`: holds the actual physical KV cache tensors.
- Specialized memory pools like `MambaPool` for state-space models and `SWAKVPool` for sliding window attention.
- Diverse allocator strategies including paged allocations, hybrid pools, hierarchical sparse allocations, and unified memory pools.
- KV index translation and mapping between different pool regions.
- The SWA memory pool implementation specifics.

These components collectively provide the basis for optimized, large-scale memory management, eviction, sharing, and quantization in SGLang's serving framework.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-21](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py:68-82]()

---

## Memory Pool Architecture Overview

SGLang's memory management is layered in two main levels and specialized extensions:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Level1["ReqToTokenPool (Req -> Token)"]
        Req["Request (Req)"]
        ReqToToken["ReqToTokenPool: req_to_token tensor\nshape (size+1, max_context_len)"]
        TokenIndices["Token Indices (logical token positions)"]
    end

    subgraph Level2["TokenToKVPoolAllocator + KVCache (Token -> KV Cache)"]
        TokenToKV["BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator\n(manages token indices mapping KV slots)"]
        KVCache["KVCache\n(physical key-value cache memory buffers)"]
        PhysicalMemory["Physical Device Memory (k_buffer, v_buffer)"]
    end

    subgraph SpecializedPools["Specialized Pools"]
        MambaPool["MambaPool (state-space model cache)"]
        HybridPool["HybridReqToTokenPool\n(combines attention + Mamba)"]
        SWA["SWAKVPool (Sliding Window Attention Pool)"]
        HiSparse["HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator\n(hierarchical GPU/Host memory paging)"]
        DeepSeekV4["DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool\n(compressed MLA + SWA model)"]
        UnifiedKVPool["UnifiedKVPool (shared buffer for multiple sub-pools)"]
    end

    Req -->|"alloc(reqs)"| ReqToToken
    ReqToToken -->|"stores token indices"| TokenIndices
    TokenIndices -->|"token index lookup"| TokenToKV
    TokenToKV -->|"manages allocation"| KVCache
    KVCache -->|"backed by"| PhysicalMemory

    HybridPool -.-> ReqToToken
    HybridPool --> MambaPool
    SWA --> TokenToKV
    HiSparse --> TokenToKV
    DeepSeekV4 --> TokenToKV
    UnifiedKVPool --> KVCache
```

**Explanation:**

- **ReqToTokenPool** maps each concurrent request slot to its token indices, serving as the logical layer.
- **TokenToKVPoolAllocator** manages the mapping of tokens to physical slots in the KV cache.
- **KVCache** exposes the actual device memory buffers holding keys and values.
- Specialized pools extend this architecture to support hybrid attention + state-space models (`HybridReqToTokenPool`), sliding-window attention (`SWAKVPool`), hierarchical sparse caching (`HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator`), compressed DeepSeek-V4 layouts, and the `UnifiedKVPool` for shared buffer management.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-21](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py:68-82](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_memory_pool.py:21-173](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:61-62](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/base.py:41-57]()

---

## ReqToTokenPool: Request to Token Index Mapping

The `ReqToTokenPool` is a core runtime structure mapping concurrent requests to their *logical* token indices.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | `int` | Max number of concurrent requests |
| `max_context_len`| `int` | Max tokens per request |
| `req_to_token` | `torch.Tensor` | Tensor of shape `[size + 1, max_context_len]`, mapping request slots to tokens |
| `free_slots` | `List[int]` | Stack of free request slots (1-based) |

**Key points:**

- The 0th row of `req_to_token` is a dummy slot filled with zeros, reserved for kernels that may access out-of-bounds indices without causing illegal writes.
- Allocation of request slots is done through `alloc(reqs)`, which assigns tokens to a free slot.
- Supports token mapping updates for prefill and decode operations.
- For disaggregated deployments (e.g., separate prefill/decode workers), `DecodeReqToTokenPool` extends the slot capacity with `pre_alloc_size` for buffered tokens arriving late [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:100-101]().
- Writes to the token mapping use a straightforward `write` method assigning token indices to slots.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:18-21](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:100-101]()

---

## TokenToKVPoolAllocator and KVCache: Physical Memory Management

### Overview

This level manages mapping from *logical tokens* to *physical KV cache slots*, operating over the actual KV buffers.

### Allocator Variants and Responsibilities

- **`TokenToKVPoolAllocator`**: Base class managing mapping and allocation of tokens to KV slots [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/token.py]().
- **`PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator`**: Uses page-aligned token groups for improved memory locality and reduced fragmentation [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/paged.py]().
- **`SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`**: Specialized for sliding window attention, managing dual pools for full and sliding-window KV caches [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:37-107]().
- **`HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator`**: Implements hierarchical sparse caching with token residency across GPU and host memory, using a paging model [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py]().
- **`DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator`**: A specialized HiSparse allocator for DeepSeekV4 models [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py]() (see also [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/dsv4/dsv4_allocator.py]()).
- **`UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator`**: Exposes unified state slots through the `MambaSlotAllocator` interface, translating virtual IDs to physical slots [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:29-58]().

### KVCache: Physical Tensor Buffers

`KVCache` provides the actual contiguous memory tensors `k_cache` and `v_cache` on the device, storing keys and values of tokens [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-21]().

### Physical Writing of KV Cache

The internal helper `_set_kv_buffer_impl` in `memory_pool.py` performs efficient batched copies of key and value tensors into their physical KV locations using platform-optimized kernels:

- **On CUDA/HIP**: Uses `store_cache` Triton kernels for rapid transfers [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:180-183]().
- **On XPU**: Uses an XPU-specific kernel variant `store_cache_xpu` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:185-187]().
- **Fallback**: Uses naive tensor copy.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:164-191](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:37-107](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:67-70](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:29-147](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/token.py](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/paged.py]()

---

## MambaPool: State-Space Model Cache

`MambaPool` supports state-space models (SSMs) which require caching *convolutional states* and *temporal states* rather than classic KV caches.

### State Layout

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph MambaPoolNormal["MambaPool.State"]
        ConvState["conv_state: List[Tensor] shape=[layers, size+1, dim, kernel_size]"]
        TemporalState["temporal_state: Tensor shape=[layers, size+1, HV, K, V]"]
    end

    subgraph MambaPoolSpeculative["MambaPool.SpeculativeState (Extended)"]
        ConvStateSpec["conv_state"]
        TemporalStateSpec["temporal_state"]
        IntermSSM["intermediate_ssm: Tensor shape=[layers, size+1, draft_tokens, HV, K, V]"]
    end

    MambaPoolNormal --> ConvState
    MambaPoolNormal --> TemporalState

    MambaPoolSpeculative --> ConvStateSpec
    MambaPoolSpeculative --> TemporalStateSpec
    MambaPoolSpeculative --> IntermSSM
```

- `conv_state` stores convolutional intermediate states.
- `temporal_state` stores SSM-related temporal states per token.
- For speculative decoding, an intermediate SSM tensor extends capacity to draft tokens.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-21]()

---

## HybridReqToTokenPool: Combining Attention and SSM Pools

Hybrid models requiring both classical attention KV caching and state-space model (SSM) caches use `HybridReqToTokenPool`.

- Combines a `ReqToTokenPool` managing tokens for attention.
- Contains a `MambaPool` managing state-space model states.
- Allocations coordinate across both pools to produce token indices accommodating both types of memory.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:17-21]()

---

## SWA (Sliding Window Attention) Memory Pool

`SWAKVPool` facilitates hybrid caching for Sliding Window Attention (SWA) architectures by holding **two KV sub-pools:**

- **Full attention pool**: For full attention layers.
- **SWA pool**: For sliding window attention layers.

It manages:
- Two separate token-to-KV pools and allocators (full and SWA) [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:69-107]().
- Mapping from full attention token indices to their corresponding SWA indices (`full_to_swa_index_mapping`) [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:110-119]().
- Memory saver mode enabling transparent reclaiming and lazy compaction.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_memory_pool.py:21-173](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:37-107]()

---

## HiSparse: Hierarchical Sparse Memory Pool and Manager

The HiSparse scheme implements hierarchical caching that partitions token memory between:

- **GPU device memory** for resident tokens.
- **Host memory (PagedHostPool)** as a fallback paging space.

### Dataflow: Token Movement Under HiSparse

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Scheduler as "Scheduler"
    participant HiSparseCoord as "HiSparseCoordinator [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py]"
    participant HostPool as "PagedHostPool"
    participant DevicePool as "HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hisparse_memory_pool.py]"

    Scheduler->>HiSparseCoord: "prefill_backup(reqs)"
    HiSparseCoord->>HostPool: "store tokens into host memory"

    Note over HiSparseCoord, DevicePool: During decode phase:
    HiSparseCoord->>HiSparseCoord: "select top-k resident tokens"
    HiSparseCoord->>DevicePool: "page in top-k tokens to device memory"
```

- On prefill, token blocks are stored in the host memory pool.
- In decode, the coordinator selects a top-k subset for residency and pages tokens into device memory.
- The device pool employs a translation table to map token logical locations into physical GPU slots while preserving padding.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:159-199](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hisparse_memory_pool.py]()

---

## UnifiedKVPool: Shared Buffer for Multiple Sub-Pools

The `UnifiedKVPool` provides a single physical `uint8` byte buffer that is shared by multiple sub-pools.

### Key Concepts

- **Sub-Pools**: The `UnifiedKVPool` can contain multiple sub-pools, each defined by a `SubPoolSpec`.
- **`MultiEndedAllocator`**: Each sub-pool uses a `MultiEndedAllocator` to manage its virtual-to-physical page mappings within the shared buffer [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:29-58]().
- **Virtual Slot IDs**: Allocators work with virtual slot IDs, translating them to physical slots via `translate()` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:55-58]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:29-147]()

---

## KV Index Translation and Mapping

Memory pools often maintain auxiliary mappings to translate between token indices and physical KV cache slots:

- **SWA pools:** Maintain a `full_to_swa_index_mapping` tensor mapping each full attention slot index to its corresponding sliding window pool slot [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:110-119]().
- **HiSparse pools:** Translate logical token locations into physical slices using efficient kernels or indices.
- **Unified pools:** Map virtual token IDs to physical page indices.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:110-119](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py:55-58]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document details SGLang's `RadixCache` and unified radix tree systems, implemented to provide compact radix prefix trees that enable efficient prefix sharing of Key-Value (KV) caches across concurrent requests. By sharing cached states for common input token prefixes, SGLang reduces redundant prefill computations and dynamic memory allocations for large language and vision-language model workloads.

We examine core data structures (`RadixKey`, `UnifiedTreeNode`), prefix matching (`match_prefix`), insertion workflows (`InsertParams`, `InsertResult`), lock reference management, eviction policies, specialized cache variants (`UnifiedRadixCache`, `StreamingSession`), the Rust-backed radix tree implementation (`sglang-radix-tree`), and their integration with the scheduler for memory-aware request handling.

For related memory management internals, see [Memory Pools and Token-to-KV Mapping (5.1)](5.1), and for hierarchical storage extensions, see [HiCache Multi-Tier Storage (5.3)](5.3).

Sources:  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:209-221`  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:47-137`  

---

## RadixCache Tree Structure and Unified Components

SGLang organizes cached KV tokens into a radix tree data structure, where each node represents a contiguous segment of tokens from input prefixes, mapped to device and/or host memory pools. This tree structure enables key operations such as shared prefix matching, inserting suffixes, and eviction in a coordinated manner.

The `UnifiedRadixCache` class acts as the unified cache front-end, managing multiple cache components and delegating tree operations to a backend tree core (`UnifiedTreeCore`, implemented in Python or Rust) [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:209-221](). It supports several main component types registered in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:176-180]():

- `FULL` (`TREE_TOKEN`) — full attention key-value caches managed by `FullComponent` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:177]()
- `SWA` (`TREE_WINDOW`) — sliding window attention caching managed by `SWAComponent` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:178]()
- `MAMBA` (`TREE_STATE`) — auxiliary state management for hybrid architectures managed by `MambaComponent` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:179]()

### Key Data Structures

- **RadixKey**: Wraps a sequence of tokens (`token_ids`) with metadata, supporting page-aligned slicing and prefix lookup [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py:59-182]().

- **UnifiedTreeNode**: Represents a node in the radix tree with children nodes keyed by tokens, references to parent nodes, and an array of per-component state data (`ComponentData`). Includes timestamps for LRU eviction, hash values for cache events, priority, and linkage pointers for per-component LRU lists [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py:118-168]().

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space"
        URC["UnifiedRadixCache"]
        UTC["UnifiedTreeCore"]
        UTN["UnifiedTreeNode"]
        RK["RadixKey"]
        LRU["UnifiedLRUList"]
    end

    URC -->|manages components and delegates tree ops| UTC
    UTC -->|manages nodes and LRU| UTN
    UTN -->|stores keys and metadata| RK
    UTN -->|tracked in| LRU
```

*Figure: Mapping of RadixCache natural language concepts to code entities*

Sources:  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:176-221`  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py:59-182`  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py:118-168`

## Prefix Matching and Splitting Algorithm

A core operation of the radix cache is prefix matching, which identifies the longest cached token prefix shared between the request’s tokens and existing radix tree nodes. This enables reuse of cached KV states and avoids duplicated prefill effort.

The `match_prefix` method on `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` searches the tree for the longest matching sequence using `MatchPrefixParams` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:71-83](). It returns a `MatchResult` containing the device prefix length, best match node ID, and host hit metrics [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:134-166]().

During a match, the radix tree is traversed recursively while comparing token sequences in nodes. When a partial mismatch occurs inside a node, a node split operation restructures the tree to maintain proper prefix segmentation.

### Prefix Matching Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant SP as "SchedulePolicy"
    participant URC as "UnifiedRadixCache"
    participant UTC as "UnifiedTreeCore"
    participant UTN as "UnifiedTreeNode"

    SP->>URC: "match_prefix_for_req(req)"
    URC->>UTC: "match_prefix(MatchPrefixParams)"
    UTC->>UTN: "Traverse radix nodes matching tokens"
    Note over UTN: "On partial mismatch -> split node"
    UTN-->>UTC: "Return MatchResult (prefix_len, matched nodes)"
    UTC-->>URC: "Return matched prefix details"
```

*Figure: Data flow for prefix matching across scheduler and radix tree modules*

Splitting nodes during prefix matching triggers tree restructuring coordinated via `InsertParams` and `InsertResult` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:85-174]().

Sources:  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:71-174`  
- `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:134-166`  

---

## Insertion, Lock Reference Management, and Streaming Sessions

After prefix matching, unmatched suffix tokens are inserted as new nodes in the radix tree with their associated KV cache tensors. Insertions use `InsertParams` encapsulating keys and device-side values [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:85-137]().

To prevent eviction of nodes currently in use, reference counts are handled by increment and decrement operations (`inc_lock_ref` / `dec_lock_ref`) which return receipts (`IncLockRefResult`, `DecLockRefParams`) detailing anchors and component lock UUIDs [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:73-127]().

### Streaming Sessions and Session Cache Slots

The system supports streaming session caching via `StreamingSession` to maintain KV cache consistency across incremental chat turns [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:59-66](). Per-session slots (`SessionSlot`) hold virtual sentinel nodes (`_VirtualNode`), representing session-owned KV state with specialized no-op locking semantics [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-52]().

When matching prefixes, these streaming session slots provide cache hits directly without recursing into the tree, enabling low-latency state reuse [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-164]().

Sources:  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:85-137`  
- `python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-121`  
- `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:73-127`  

---

## Eviction Policies and Memory Management

Memory pressure triggers eviction mechanisms in radix caches targeting unlocked leaf nodes holding KV slots. Eviction operations receive parameters encapsulated in `EvictParams` indicating how many tokens to evict by component, and return corresponding `EvictResult` statistics [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:167-184]().

The underlying tree core supports strategies such as `joint_lru` (joint Full/SWA eviction) through `uses_joint_lru` and per-component LRU tracking [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core_interface.py:122-125](). Coordinated evictions keep the cache size within limits while maintaining correct reuse semantics for shared prefixes and sliding windows.

Sources:  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py:167-184`  
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core_interface.py:122-125`  

---

## The Rust/C++ Radix Tree Implementation (`sglang-radix-tree`)

To minimize Python interpreter overhead in critical paths, SGLang offers a Rust-based radix tree core implemented in the `sglang-radix-tree` crate. This Rust core mirrors the Python `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` contract and manages node arena allocation, LRU list updates, node splits, eviction queues, and concurrency control efficiently [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-46]().

The Rust crate exposes PyO3 bindings (`RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding`) allowing it to plug into the Python runtime seamlessly as a high-performance backend [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-143]().

Sources:  
- `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-143`  

---

## Scheduler Integration and Code Architecture Mapping

The SGLang scheduler uses radix cache prefix matching to optimize request dispatch and batch formation, reusing cached KV states.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Scheduler and Cache Code Architecture"
        SP["SchedulePolicy"]
        URC["UnifiedRadixCache"]
        UTC["UnifiedTreeCore"]
        AL["BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator"]
        SS["StreamingSession"]
    end

    SP -->|calls match_prefix| URC
    URC -->|delegates tree operations| UTC
    URC -->|allocates KV memory| AL
    URC -->|manages session state| SS
```

*Figure: Code entity mapping showing interactions between scheduler, radix cache, memory pools, and streaming session*

# Summary

SGLang's radix caching system is a foundational component enabling efficient memory reuse and prefix sharing across concurrent model requests. This system combines Python-controlled layered components with performant radix tree cores (including a Rust implementation) and supports streaming session state management to reduce prefill overhead and memory usage. The unified radix tree cache supports multiple component types (`FULL`, `SWA`, `MAMBA`), advanced prefix matching, node splitting algorithms, and seamless integration with the scheduler to provide high-throughput serving of large language and vision-language models.

Sources:
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:209-221`

## Purpose and Scope

HiCache extends KV-cache management beyond device memory by coordinating device pools, host pools, and optional storage backends. This page describes the tier model, pool assembly, transfer controller, storage interface, event synchronization, and the boundaries of what can be concluded about runtime backend changes from the available implementation excerpts [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:41-57](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:26-55](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:41-57](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:26-55](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53]()

---

## Three-Tier Storage Architecture

HiCache separates KV-cache handling into device-resident pools, host-resident pools, and an optional storage interface. Device pools describe the active KV buffers; host pools provide corresponding host-side storage and transfer operations; storage backends implement the `HiCacheStorage` contract [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:41-57](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53]().

**Diagram: HiCache Tiers and Code Entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Device["MHATokenToKVPool"]
    Host["HostKVCache"]
    Controller["HiCacheController"]
    HybridController["HybridCacheController"]
    Storage["HiCacheStorage"]
    Radix["UnifiedRadixCache"]

    Radix -->|"manages"| Controller
    Controller -->|"drives"| Device
    Controller -->|"drives"| Host
    HybridController -->|"extends"| Controller
    HybridController -->|"coordinates"| Storage
    Host <-->|"transfers"| Device
    Host <-->|"syncs"| Storage
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:26-55](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-49](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:26-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:41-57]()

- **Device tier:** `kv_cache_builder.py` imports device-pool classes such as `MHATokenToKVPool` and constructs the tree cache through `create_tree_cache` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:42-57]().
- **Host tier:** `build_kv_host_pool` selects a host-pool implementation based on device-pool metadata, including MHA and MLA buffer formats [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187]().
- **Storage tier:** `HiCacheStorageConfig` carries storage identity and layout information, while `PoolTransfer` describes transfers among host, device, and storage representations [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:174-184]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:42-57](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:174-184]()

### Bridging Cache Concepts to Implementation Entities

`UnifiedRadixCache` is the tree-cache type imported by `kv_cache_builder.py`; the builder returns the selected cache as part of `KVCacheBuildResult`. The controller layer has a base `HiCacheController` and a derived `HybridCacheController`, which uses the base controller’s operation and event types [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:14-24](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:55-57](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-24]().

## HiCacheController: Orchestrating Tier Operations

The base `HiCacheController` module defines transfer-operation structures, layer-level completion events, and storage-related configuration and helpers. `HybridCacheController` derives from it and specializes storage operations with pool-transfer metadata, prefetch state, and hybrid host-pool behavior [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:26-55](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-149](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-24](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:185-204]().

| Component | Role in Implementation |
|---|---|
| `CacheOperation` | Carries host and device indices, node IDs, priority, and optional per-pool transfers; `merge_ops` combines operation indices and pool transfers [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:128-149](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:150-197]() |
| `LayerLoadingEvent` | Maintains per-layer device events; `complete` records a layer’s event and `wait` makes the current stream wait for it [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-97]() |
| `LayerDoneCounter` | Maintains three event sets and producer/consumer indices for layer-transfer synchronization [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:99-124]() |
| `HybridCacheController` | Subclasses the base controller and defines hybrid storage and prefetch operation structures [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-24](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:185-204]() |

**Diagram: Controller Entities and Transfer Records**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Hybrid["HybridCacheController"]
    Base["HiCacheController"]
    CacheOp["CacheOperation"]
    LayerEvents["LayerLoadingEvent"]
    DoneCounter["LayerDoneCounter"]
    StorageOp["StorageOperation"]
    PrefetchOp["PrefetchOperation"]
    PoolTransfer["PoolTransfer"]

    Hybrid -->|"inherits"| Base
    Base -->|"issues"| CacheOp
    Base -->|"uses"| LayerEvents
    Base -->|"uses"| DoneCounter
    Hybrid -->|"defines"| StorageOp
    StorageOp -->|"subclasses"| PrefetchOp
    StorageOp -->|"contains"| PoolTransfer
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-124](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:128-197](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-24](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:185-204]()

### Layer Synchronization

`LayerLoadingEvent` allocates one device event per layer and a start event. A producer calls `complete(layer_index)` to record the corresponding event; a consumer calls `wait(layer_index)` to wait on it from the current device stream. `LayerDoneCounter` rotates among three event sets and can wait on a consumer’s layer event at a threshold [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-124]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-124]()

---

## L2 Host Memory and HiSparse Memory Pools

### HostKVCache and Subclasses

`build_kv_host_pool` obtains buffer metadata from the device pool, distinguishes MLA from non-MLA buffers, resolves host geometry, and chooses the host-pool class [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](). For non-MLA pools it uses `_mha_host_inputs`; for MLA it selects `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`.

`MHATokenToKVPoolHost` derives from `HostKVCache` and accepts device-capacity, layer-range, draft-buffer, and optional staging-buffer parameters. `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` also derives from `HostKVCache`, and mixes in `HiSparseHostPoolMixin` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:140-163](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:42-44](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:96-127]().

`LogicalHostPool` is a logical page-slot anchor for V4 HiCache: it holds no KV tensor, enforces page-aligned allocation and free operations, and does not own backing buffers to destroy [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:93-137](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:154-184]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:140-163](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:42-44](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:96-127](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:93-137](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:154-184]()

### Host-Pool Layouts and Transfer Staging

`prepare_hicache_staging` prepares write-back staging before final KV sizing when the configured layout and cache settings require it. It handles `page_first` and `page_unified` layouts, derives a staging page capacity, and uses the host-pool layout geometry when building the buffers [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:77-157]().

For MHA host pools, `prepare_mha_write_back_staging` returns no staging buffer unless the platform is CUDA or HIP, the layer count is nonzero, and the required write-back kernel geometry is supported. Otherwise it creates or validates staging tensors for K and V data [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:101-137]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:77-157](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:101-137]()

### HiSparse Memory-Pool Support

`HiSparseHostPoolMixin` is mixed into `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` and imported by `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` to support sparse hierarchical attention pools [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:42-44](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:96-101](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:49-56]().

`LogicalHostPool` acts as a logical anchor rather than a tensor-backed pool. Its allocation and free-list operations are page-aligned, and its `backup_from_device_all_layer` methods serve as anchors for compressed V4 side pools [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:93-123](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:154-197]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:42-44](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py:96-101](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py:49-56](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:93-123](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py:154-197]()

---

## L3 Storage Backend System

The storage abstraction includes `HiCacheStorageConfig`, `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo`, pool identifiers, hit policies, and `PoolTransfer` descriptors [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:98-103](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:106-184]().

### Storage Configuration and Transfer Descriptors

`HiCacheStorageConfig` carries parallel-rank, model, layout, and storage configuration information. It also includes unified key suffixes and chunk spans for topology-independent storage shard identity. Its validation requires DCP storage to use MLA, compatible TP/DCP ranks, and a DCP-aligned logical page size [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-76]().

`PoolName` identifies pool types, including KV, Mamba, SWA, indexer, DeepSeek V4 components, and draft pools. `PoolHitPolicy` defines `ALL_PAGES`, `TRAILING_PAGES`, and `BLOCK_GROUPS`; `PoolTransfer` records a pool name plus host/device indices and storage keys [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:106-172](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:174-184]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:27-76](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:106-172](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:174-184]()

### MooncakeStore Backend

The Mooncake module defines `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`, which requests host memory from `MooncakeHostMemAllocator` and wraps the allocated address in a PyTorch tensor. It also defines `MooncakeStoreConfig`, with fields for metadata, transport, server addresses, optional SSD offload, tenant identity, and local transfer-buffer size [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:41-80](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:106-127]().

`MooncakeStoreConfig.from_file` loads JSON configuration from the configured path, requires a master or client server address, and resolves values using configuration and environment settings [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:148-188]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:41-80](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:106-127](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:148-188]()

---

## KV Cache Event System

Device events are used for layer-level transfer synchronization. `LayerLoadingEvent` owns one event per layer and exposes `complete`, `wait`, and `finish_event`; `LayerDoneCounter` rotates producer event sets and tracks a consumer index [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-124]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-124]()

---

## Runtime Attach/Detach of Backends and Pools

Storage configurations and operation data structures manage backend interaction. While initialization of backends like Mooncake occurs via configuration loaders (`MooncakeStoreConfig.from_file`), runtime dynamic attachment and detachment of storage backends or pools relies on controller-managed transfers and lifecycle hooks [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:148-188]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:148-188]()

---

## Summary

HiCache combines device KV pools, host-pool implementations, transfer operations, and a storage abstraction. `build_kv_host_pool` selects host pools from device buffer metadata; `HiCacheController` defines operation and layer-event structures; and `HybridCacheController` extends that layer with pool-aware storage operations [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-149](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-49](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:23-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:41-80]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py:146-187](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:81-149](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:16-49](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py:23-53](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py:41-80]()

This page documents the storage backends (Mooncake, HF3FS, LMCache, NIXL, UMBP), internal transfer queues, asynchronous operations, the buffer-mode pipeline, and object storage loading mechanisms used in SGLang's hierarchical KV cache system. These components optimize large-scale storage and retrieval of KV cache data across device memory, host memory, and persistent storage.

---

## 1. Storage Backend Architecture and Initialization

SGLang extends its KV cache hierarchy beyond GPU and CPU memory tiers by integrating external L3 storage backends for offloading cold KV cache data. This system enables efficient eviction, persistence, multi-node sharing, and reuse.

The abstraction `HiCacheStorage` (defined in [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py]()) specifies the interface for external storage backend key-value storage operations tailored for multi-pool cache transfers.

The hierarchy is orchestrated primarily through two controller components:

- **`UnifiedRadixCache`**: Organizes cache nodes and manages hierarchical radix cache indexing, controlling cache misses and eviction writing [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py]() (see also registry factory logic in [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/registry.py:103-153]()).
- **`HybridCacheController`**: Manages asynchronous transfers between host memory and storage backends with internal operation queues.

The initialization sequence for storage backend setup involves `UnifiedRadixCache` parsing backend configuration, creating controllers, and attaching the appropriate backend instance via a factory pattern:

```mermaid
graph TD
    UnifiedRadixCache["UnifiedRadixCache"] --> ParseConfig["_parse_storage_backend_extra_config"]
    ParseConfig --> CreateController["HybridCacheController"]
    CreateController --> AttachBackend["attach_storage_backend"]
    AttachBackend --> BackendFactory["StorageBackendFactory.create_backend"]
    
    BackendFactory -->|"mooncake"| MooncakeStore["MooncakeStore"]
    BackendFactory -->|"hf3fs"| HF3FS["HiCacheHF3FS"]
    BackendFactory -->|"lmcache"| LMCache["LMCacheUnifiedRadixCache"]
    BackendFactory -->|"nixl"| NIXL["HiCacheNIXL"]
    
    MooncakeStore --> RegisterMemPool["register_mem_host_pool_v2"]
    HF3FS --> RegisterMemPool
    LMCache --> RegisterMemPool
    NIXL --> RegisterMemPool
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/registry.py:103-153](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py]()

---

## 2. Supported Storage Backends Overview

SGLang supports multiple distinct storage backends varying in protocol, deployment mode, and feature set. These backends implement the standard interface for consistent multi-pool KV cache transfer operations.

| **Backend** | **Transport / Deployment** | **Use Case** | **Key Features** |
| :---------- | :------------------------- | :----------- | :--------------- |
| `mooncake` | RDMA/ROCE-based network | Distributed multi-node KV cache sharing | Zero-copy RDMA transfers, multi-node synchronization, tenant and metrics support. Implements `MooncakeStore` and `MooncakeDirectLinker` with zero-copy host tensor allocator [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py:120-185](). |
| `hf3fs` | User-space filesystem (UsrBio) | Local high-performance storage | Asynchronous batch IO, `io_uring`-based async, metadata-driven cache consistency. |
| `lmcache` | LMCache protocol | Cross-framework cache sharing | Radix-tree based unified cache, supports sidecar pools and nested radix key usage via `LMCacheUnifiedRadixCache` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/registry.py:103-129](). |
| `nixl` | Custom NIXL protocol | Interconnect storage | Low-latency hierarchical caching with fine-grained page transfer and compression-aware pooling. |
| `umbp` | UMBP protocol | Scalable multi-block storage | Range-based batching, `UMBPDirectLinker` layer-wise loading without prefetch dependency [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/umbp/umbp_direct_linker.py:134-183](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/registry.py:103-129](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py:120-185](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/umbp/umbp_direct_linker.py:134-183]()

---

## 3. Transfer Queues and Asynchronous Operations

The **`HybridCacheController`** manages transfer operations asynchronously via several internal queues designed to overlap work efficiently:

- **`write_queue`**: For Device (GPU) → Host (CPU) transfers on eviction; accumulated dirty KV pages staged and flushed.
- **`load_queue`**: For Host → Device transfers to bring back evicted cache on a hit.
- **`prefetch_queue`**: For Storage → Host async prefetching, warming host memory caches before device demand.
- **`backup_queue`**: For Host → Storage asynchronous backup, persisting evicted cache pages externally.

These queues enable decoupling of device eviction/loading from slow storage access, mounted with multi-threaded and event-driven synchronization primitives in CUDA/ROCm streams and CPU threads [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_cache_linker.py:143-154]().

### Transfer Queue Dataflow Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "L1: GPU Memory"
        DeviceKV["MHATokenToKVPool"]
    end
    
    subgraph "L2: CPU Memory"
        HostKV["HostKVCache"]
    end
    
    subgraph "L3: External Storage"
        Storage["HiCacheStorage"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transfer Queues and Operations"
        WriteQ["write_queue"]
        LoadQ["load_queue"]
        PrefetchQ["prefetch_queue"]
        BackupQ["backup_queue"]
    end
    
    DeviceKV -->|"Evict_dirty_pages"| WriteQ
    WriteQ -->|"Async_D2H_copy"| HostKV
    HostKV -->|"Restore_on_demand"| LoadQ
    LoadQ -->|"Async_H2D_copy"| DeviceKV
    Storage -->|"Prefetch_requests"| PrefetchQ
    PrefetchQ -->|"Async_read"| HostKV
    HostKV -->|"Backup_dirty_pages"| BackupQ
    BackupQ -->|"Async_write"| Storage
```

## 4. Buffer-Mode Pipeline for Host Memory

With the **buffer-only mode** enabled (`--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:14-18]()), SGLang turns host memory into a transient streaming buffer managed by `BufferModePipeline` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:3-24]() instead of a persistent caching pool. 

- **Backup Path**: An admission-gated FIFO intent queue (`_UnifiedBackupIntent` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:99-114]()) handles device→host staging launches (`_UnifiedBufferBackupEntry` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:116-131]()), storing to persistent storage at the D2H ack and freeing staging buffers upon the storage ack.
- **Load Back Path**: Completed storage fetches are parked as op-owned host bounces (`_StagedPrefetch` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:133-149]()), consumed at prefill admission via device allocation, layer-gated H2D copies (`_OngoingBufferLoadBack` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/buffer_mode/pipeline.py:151-171]()), and plain tree insertion.

### BufferModePipeline Dataflow Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "BufferModePipeline Backup"
        BackupIntent["_UnifiedBackupIntent"]
        D2HLaunch["HostStagingTransferLaunch"]
        StorageWrite["AsyncStorageWrite"]
        AckFree["StorageACKAndFree"]
        
        BackupIntent --> D2HLaunch --> StorageWrite --> AckFree
    end
    
    subgraph "BufferModePipeline Load"

    end
```

## 5. MooncakeStore and Direct Linker Implementations

The `MooncakeStore` backend provides high-speed distributed multi-node cache sharing leveraging RDMA/RoCE technology. It facilitates near zero-copy lifecycle by pooling memory pages that are directly allocated and managed with native Mooncake allocators.

Zero-copy linker views across physical device pools are resolved via `resolve_hybrid_device_pool_group` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/linker_pool_assembler.py:23-40](), allowing direct data pointers to be passed to batch transfer engines like `MooncakeDirectLinker` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py:120-185]() and `UMBPDirectLinker` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/umbp/umbp_direct_linker.py:134-183]().
