## Supported MoE and advanced architectures

MoE model implementations use shared routing and execution components, including `TopK`, `FusedMoE`, and expert-parallel implementation selection. A model may also provide architecture-specific gates, weight mappings, shared-expert behavior, and hardware-specific execution paths. Qwen2 MoE, for example, defines shared-expert helpers and imports `TopK`, `FusedMoE`, and expert-parallel utilities. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:65-74](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:125-167]()

| Family | Representative implementation | Notable implementation details |
|---|---|---|
| **DeepSeek V2/V3/V4** | `models/deepseek_v2.py` | The module imports MLA attention support, DSA indexer components, MoE routing, and expert-parallel utilities. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:55-63](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:67-77](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:106-126]() |
| **Qwen2 MoE / Qwen3 MoE** | `models/qwen2_moe.py`, `models/qwen3_moe.py` | Qwen3 MoE reuses `Qwen2MoeMLP` and `Qwen2MoeModel` while providing Qwen3-specific configuration and attention handling. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py:63-68]() |
| **Qwen3.5 MoE** | `models/qwen3_5.py` | The module describes inference-only Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.5 MoE implementations compatible with HuggingFace weights; it imports `FusedMoE` and model-specific configuration classes. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:15-15](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:41-45](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:89-90]() |
| **GLM-4 MoE** | `models/glm4_moe.py` | The module describes inference-only GLM-4.5, 4.6, and 4.7 implementations compatible with HuggingFace weights and imports MoE routing and fused execution components. [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py:15-15](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py:60-72]() |
| **GLM-4 MoE Lite** | `models/glm4_moe_lite.py` | The module describes an inference-only GLM-4.7-Flash model and defines `Glm4MoeLiteSparseMoeBlock`. [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py:15-15](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py:173-195]() |

| **Bailing** | `models/bailing_moe.py`, `models/bailing_moe_linear.py`, `models/bailing_moe_v3.py` | Dedicated Bailing MoE and linear-attention model modules are present. | **MiniMax** | `models/minimax_m2.py`, `models/minimax_m3.py` | MiniMax M3 is an inference-only HuggingFace-compatible model adapted from DeepSeek and Mixtral implementations; it imports MoE and quantization components. ## Supported multimodal and vision-language architectures

Vision-language model implementations connect multimodal processing to a language-model backbone. The Kimi K3 module imports `KimiK3MultiModalProjector` and `KimiK3VisionTower` and uses multimodal input and feature utilities. Qwen3.5 imports `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`, and GLM-5 Next imports GLM OCR vision components. [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:102-110](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:125-138](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:124-125](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py:103-110]()

|---|---|---|
| **Qwen VL** | `models/qwen3_vl.py` | Qwen3.5 imports `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` as a model implementation dependency. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:124-125]() |
| **Kimi K3 VL** | `models/kimi_k3_vl.py`, `models/kimi_k3.py` | The K3 model imports its vision tower and multimodal projector, alongside multimodal input and feature utilities. [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:102-110](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:125-138]() |
| **MiniMax M3 VL** | `models/minimax_m3_vl.py` | A dedicated multimodal model module is present. [python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3_vl.py:1-40]() |
| **GLM vision models** | `models/glm4v.py`, `models/glm5_next.py` | GLM-5 Next imports GLM OCR vision blocks, model, patch embedding, and patch merger components. [python/sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py:103-110]() |
| **Gemma multimodal** | `models/gemma4_mm.py` | A dedicated Gemma 4 multimodal model module is present. [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py:1-40]() |
| **Nemotron vision-language** | `models/nano_nemotron_vl.py` | A dedicated Nano Nemotron VL module is present. [python/sglang/srt/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py:1-40]() |
| **MiMo V2** | `models/mimo_v2.py` | MiMo V2 supports multimodal inputs (text, image, audio) and integrates `MiMoVisionTransformer` and `AudioEncoderMixin`. [python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py:105-106](), [python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py:108-109]() |

## MoE layer architecture and expert routing

MoE layers use a router to select experts for each token and execute the selected expert computations. The model modules share components such as `TopK`, `FusedMoE`, and expert-parallel implementation selection, while retaining model-specific routing and checkpoint handling. Qwen2 MoE also has helpers to identify shared experts and determine whether shared-expert fusion is valid for the active configuration and backend. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:65-74](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:125-167]()

### MoE sparse block and routing flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    hidden_states["hidden_states"]
    router["Model-specific router"]
    TopK["TopK selection"]
    FusedMoE["FusedMoE expert execution"]
    shared_experts["Optional shared experts"]
    combine["Combine routed and shared outputs"]
    layer_output["Decoder layer output"]

    hidden_states --> router
    router --> TopK
    TopK --> FusedMoE
    hidden_states --> shared_experts
    FusedMoE --> combine
    shared_experts --> combine
    combine --> layer_output
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:65-74](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py:125-167](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py:60-72](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py:54-69]()

## Summary

SGLang associates HuggingFace architecture metadata with Python model implementations through its model registry. Model modules define architecture-specific structures and weight handling while composing shared runtime components such as attention layers, parallel linear layers, `ForwardBatch`, and MoE execution utilities. [python/sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py:98-103](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:97-116](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:89-116]()

The model package includes dense, hybrid, MoE, and vision-language families, including LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Bailing, MiniMax, Nemotron, MiMo, and GPT-OSS. The exact implementation selected depends on the configuration architecture name and its registry mapping. [python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py:1-68](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-7](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py:15-15](), [python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py:15-16](), [python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py:1-40]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py:98-103](), [python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py:1-68](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:97-116](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:89-116](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-7](), [python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py:15-15](), [python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py:15-16](), [python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py:1-40]()

## Purpose and scope

This parent page provides a high-level map of SGLang’s Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture and DeepSeek-specific model implementations. It connects the model's MoE layers, DeepSeek-specific attention and cache components, expert routing mechanisms, and optimization strategies, while detailed low-level implementations are delegated to the child pages. The DeepSeek-V4 model module integrates `FusedMoE`, MoE utilities, DeepSeek attention backends, and DeepSeek-specific transport helpers [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:68-77](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:109-115](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:180-183]().

For deep technical details, see:
- [MoE Layer Architecture](#8.1)

## MoE Layer Architecture

In the DeepSeek-V4 model architecture, `FusedMoE` serves as the primary model-level MoE component [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:110](). It interacts with `get_moe_a2a_backend` and shared expert utilities to manage expert computations across distributed ranks [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:109-115](). Additionally, `OverlappedMoeTransport` is utilized to overlap communication and compute during expert execution [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:185-186]().

The codebase separates expert computation, kernel selection, and model-level integration. For details on `FusedMoE` implementations, MoE runner backends, expert computation kernels, and FlashInfer/TrtLLM MoE integration, see [MoE Layer Architecture](#8.1).

### MoE Model and Dispatch Mapping

```mermaid

    Model --> Transport["OverlappedMoeTransport python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/moe_transport.py"]
    FusedMoE --> A2A["get_moe_a2a_backend python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/__init__.py"]
    FusedMoE --> Shared["get_num_fused_shared_experts python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py"]
```

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:109-115`, `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:185-186`

## DeepSeek Architecture and MLA

DeepSeek models incorporate advanced attention mechanisms such as Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and sparse indexing strategies. The DeepSeek-V4 model relies on `DSV4Metadata`, `Compressor`, and `DeepseekV4AttnBackend` to coordinate attention execution [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:68-77](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:60-89](). KV cache management is backed by `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`, which handles specialized memory layouts for compressed and paged states [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:50-55](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:68]().

For comprehensive documentation on DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4 architectures, MLA, indexers (DSA/DSV4), and NSA attention, see [DeepSeek Architecture and MLA](#8.2).

```mermaid
    Model --> Comp["Compressor python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/compressor.py"]
    Backend --> Pool["DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py"]
```

## Expert Routing and Token Dispatch

Token dispatch and expert routing coordinate how tokens are assigned to sparse experts across distributed processes. The DeepSeek-V4 implementation integrates expert distribution recorders via `get_global_expert_distribution_recorder` and relies on all-to-all backends for token exchange [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:57-58](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:109](). 

For details on TopK routing algorithms, token dispatch mechanisms, hierarchical expert selection, and Expert Parallelism Load Balancer (EPLB), see [Expert Routing and Token Dispatch](#8.3).

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:57-58`, `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:109-115`

---

## MoE Quantization and Optimization

MoE models demand specialized quantization schemes and kernel optimizations to maintain high throughput. DeepSeek-V4 integrates FP8 configuration classes (`Fp8Config`, `Fp8LinearMethod`), MXFP8 quantization utilities, and DeepGEMM scaling components (`DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0`) [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:90-98](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:116-125](). These components couple low-precision weight loading with specialized high-performance GEMM wrappers.

For details on MoE-specific quantization, DeepGEMM and CUTLASS kernels, mega-MoE structures, and two-batch overlap techniques, see [MoE Quantization and Optimization](#8.4).

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:90-98`, `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:116-125`, `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:180-183`

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer and expert-computation architecture implemented in the SGLang source codebase. It focuses on `FusedMoE`, the runner and dispatcher abstractions, expert GEMM computation, and the FlashInfer/TRT-LLM, CuteDSL, and DeepGEMM paths. Routing and token dispatch are treated here as interfaces to this layer; their algorithms are documented separately [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-39](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-37]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-39](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-37]()

---

## 1. MoE Layer Overview and High-Level Data Flow

An MoE layer connects top-k routing output to token dispatch, expert computation, and output combination. In the implementation, `FusedMoE` imports the `TopKOutput` types and dispatcher interfaces, and `create_moe_dispatcher` selects a dispatcher using the configured all-to-all backend and hardware context [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:35-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186]().

The expert-computation path is represented by `MoeRunnerConfig` and runner backends. The Triton utility exposes `inplace_fused_experts`, which forwards its arguments to `fused_experts_impl`; the arguments include expert weights, top-k IDs and weights, activation, quantization metadata, and routing-scaling options [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210]().

The diagram below distinguishes layer-level concepts from concrete code entities. It does not imply that every model uses the same dispatcher, runner, activation, or quantization configuration [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:35-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210]().

**Diagram: MoE layer data flow and code entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["hidden_states"] --> Routing["TopKOutput"]
    Routing --> Dispatch["BaseDispatcher"]
    Input --> Dispatch
    Dispatch --> Layer["FusedMoE.forward_impl"]
    Layer --> Runner["MoeRunner"]
    Runner --> Expert["w13_weight and w2_weight"]
    Expert --> Combine["CombineInput"]
    Combine --> Output["MoE output"]
    Layer -.-> Config["MoeRunnerConfig"]
    Layer -.-> Quant["FusedMoEMethodBase"]
    Dispatch -.-> Standard["StandardDispatcher"]
    Dispatch -.-> Flash["FlashinferDispatcher"]
    Dispatch -.-> DeepEP["DeepEPv2Dispatcher"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210]()

## 2. `FusedMoE` and `DeepEPMoE` Layer Implementation

`FusedMoE` is the central layer implementation in `fused_moe_triton/layer.py`; its imports establish the interfaces it composes, including `MoeRunnerConfig`, `BaseDispatcher`, `TopKOutput`, and quantization methods derived from `FusedMoEMethodBase`. The codebase also defines `create_moe_dispatcher`, which chooses a dispatcher based on the configured all-to-all backend and platform [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-69](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186]().

`DeepEPMoE` subclasses `FusedMoE` and initializes its base with expert count, top-k, hidden and intermediate sizes, layer ID, shared-expert count, dtype, quantization configuration, activation, and routed scaling factor [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-99](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:101-152]().

The EP implementation’s documented class description says it is based on DeepEP and that Mooncake EP shares the same class interface. The method `_a2a_forward_with_output_impl` temporarily sets the extend-in-batch flag, invokes `forward_impl` with a `StandardTopKOutput`, copies the result into the supplied output, and restores the previous flag in a `finally` block [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-68](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:180-198]().

**Diagram: Layer construction and composition**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Init["FusedMoE construction"] --> Config["MoeRunnerConfig"]
    Init --> Method["FusedMoEMethodBase"]
    Init --> Dispatcher["create_moe_dispatcher"]
    Dispatcher --> Standard["StandardDispatcher"]
    Dispatcher --> Flash["FlashinferDispatcher"]
    Dispatcher --> DeepEPv2["DeepEPv2Dispatcher"]
    Init --> Forward["FusedMoE.forward_impl"]
    Forward --> Runner["MoeRunner"]
    EP["DeepEPMoE"] --> Init
    EP --> A2A["DeepEPMoE._a2a_forward_with_output_impl"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-69](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-99](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:180-198]()

## 3. Expert Weight Organization and Quantization Layouts

The Triton fused-expert interface accepts `w1` and `w2` tensors alongside top-k IDs and weights. It also accepts optional bias, activation, quantization flags and scale tensors, block shape, routed scaling, and gate/up layout options. This interface supports multiple execution configurations [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-195]().

The `FusedMoE` layer imports quantization implementations including `Fp8MoEMethod`, `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod`, `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, and `CompressedTensorsMxInt4MoE`. `fp8.py` also imports runner-specific quant-info types, including `DeepGemmMoeQuantInfo`, `FlashInferTrtllmFp8MoeQuantInfo`, and `TritonMoeQuantInfo` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:59-69](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:31-42]().

The API makes quantization and layout choices explicit: the fused-expert call includes separate weight-scale and zero-point parameters for its two projections, activation scales, block shape, and a `gate_up_interleaved` option. Backend-specific weight preparation can therefore differ [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:176-195]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-195](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:59-69](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:31-42]()

---

## 4. MoE Runner Backends

`MoeRunnerBackend` is an enum in `moe/utils.py`. The definition includes `AUTO`, `DEEP_GEMM`, `TRITON`, `TRITON_KERNELS`, `ASCEND`, FlashInfer/TRT-LLM variants, `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`, `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL`, `FLASHINFER_MXFP4`, `CUTLASS`, `MARLIN`, `HUMMING`, `AITER`, `HPC_OPS`, and `INTEL_XPU`, among others [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216]().

The enum’s predicates provide a stable way for other code to test backend families. For example, `is_flashinfer_trtllm()` recognizes both `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` and `EXPERIMENTAL_SGL_TRTLLM`; `is_marlin()` similarly groups `MARLIN` and `EXPERIMENTAL_SGL_MARLIN` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:133-172]().

| Backend family or value | What the source code establishes |
|---|---|
| `TRITON` | A runner backend enum value; the fused-expert Triton utility defines `inplace_fused_experts` and `fused_experts_impl` entry points [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-200](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](). |
| `DEEP_GEMM` | A runner backend enum value; `deep_gemm.py` imports `MoeRunnerCore`, `RunnerInput`, and `RunnerOutput` and contains DeepGEMM-specific helpers and quantization/layout logic [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-200](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-34](). |
| `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` | A runner backend enum value; `flashinfer_trtllm.py` adapts FlashInfer routing and defines wrappers and deferred-finalize support [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-205](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-37](). |
| `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_ROUTED` | A separate runner backend value used for routed FlashInfer/TRT-LLM execution [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-205](). |
| `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`, `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL`, `FLASHINFER_MXFP4` | Distinct backend values represented in the enum, supporting Blackwell architectures (`SM100`/`SM103`) via CuteDSL and swap-ab layouts [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py:48-63](). |
| `AITER`, `ASCEND`, `INTEL_XPU` | Platform/backend values represented in the enum [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:112-216](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-34](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-37](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py:48-63]()

## 5. FlashInfer, TRT-LLM, and DeepGEMM MoE Backends

### FlashInfer/TRT-LLM integration

`moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py` imports the `trtllm_fp8_*` wrapper functions from `flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`, including block-scale and per-tensor-scale variants, as well as routed variants. The file also defines routing adaptation and deferred-finalize support [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-30]().

The deferred-finalize mechanism uses a context variable controlled by `flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_finalize_context`. `finalize_flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_output` passes the stored GEMM2 output, expert weights, permuted-index mapping, optional shared output, and top-k value to `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`; it also determines whether to enable PDL through `trtllm_moe_enable_pdl` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:47-100]().

`_make_deferred_finalize_output` adapts the first three values of the FlashInfer result into `FlashInferTrtllmDeferredFinalizeOutput` and checks the expected dtypes of the expert weights, GEMM2 output, and index mapping [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:87-132]().

### FlashInfer CuteDSL and Blackwell Support

`moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py` provides integration utilities for Blackwell SM100/SM103 architectures (`use_cutedsl_moe_swap_ab`), scale reduction functions (`cutedsl_quant_scale_to_scalar` reducing per-expert scale vectors to global scalar minimums matching TRT-LLM conventions), and standard scale resolution [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py:48-96](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py:99-174]().

### DeepGEMM integration

`deep_gemm.py` imports `MoeRunnerCore`, `RunnerInput`, and `RunnerOutput`, along with registration hooks for pre- and post-permute operations. It also imports DeepGEMM support and utilities for activation, expert-count padding, and per-token-group quantization [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:11-39]().

The file contains memory-budget and peak-memory estimation helpers for a masked standard layout. The estimate accounts for padded token rows, activation and scale storage, intermediate gate/up output, and down-projection output; the configured budget fraction is validated to be in `(0, 1]` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:116-170]().

**Diagram: Runner-specific MoE execution and finalization**

```mermaid
graph TB
    TopK["TopKOutput"] --> Adapt["FlashInfer routing adaptation"]
    Adapt --> FlashCall["trtllm_fp8_*_moe wrapper"]
    FlashCall --> Deferred["FlashInferTrtllmDeferredFinalizeOutput"]
    Deferred --> Finalize["finalize_flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_output"]
    Shared["shared_output"] --> Finalize
    Finalize --> FusedOutput["moe_finalize_fuse_shared"]
    Input["RunnerInput"] --> DG["DeepGemmRunnerCore path"]
    DG --> Pre["register_pre_permute"]
    Pre --> GEMM["DeepGEMM grouped expert computation"]
    GEMM --> Post["register_post_permute"]
    Post --> Result["RunnerOutput"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:25-37](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:47-132](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py:48-174](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:11-39](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:116-170]()

## 6. Token Dispatchers and Expert Parallelism

The layer’s dispatcher factory obtains the MoE all-to-all backend and selects among dispatcher implementations. The branches include `AscendTPDispatcher` for the no-all-to-all NPU case, and the imported `StandardDispatcher`, `FlashinferDispatcher`, and `DeepEPv2Dispatcher` implementations. Some backend configurations bypass the dispatcher abstraction [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:35-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186]().

The dispatcher backend enum is separate from the runner backend enum. `MoeA2ABackend` includes values such as `DEEPEP`, `MOONCAKE`, `NIXL`, `MORI`, `FLASHINFER`, `MEGAMOE`, `DEEPEP_V2`, and `PPLX`; `MoeRunnerBackend` represents expert-computation choices such as `TRITON`, `DEEP_GEMM`, and `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216]().

`DeepEPMoE` is the EP-facing layer subclass. Its class documentation identifies DeepEP as its basis and says Mooncake EP shares its interface [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-68]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:35-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-68]()

This diagram maps layer-level concepts to names that can be searched directly in the repository. The mappings are based on the imports, definitions, and interfaces in the source code [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216]().

**Diagram: MoE concepts mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    ConceptLayer["MoE layer"] --> EntityLayer["FusedMoE"]
    ConceptEPLayer["Expert-parallel layer"] --> EntityEPLayer["DeepEPMoE"]
    ConceptRouting["Router output"] --> EntityRouting["TopKOutput and StandardTopKOutput"]
    ConceptDispatch["Token dispatch"] --> EntityDispatch["BaseDispatcher and create_moe_dispatcher"]
    ConceptCompute["Expert computation"] --> EntityCompute["inplace_fused_experts and fused_experts_impl"]
    ConceptRunner["Runner configuration"] --> EntityRunner["MoeRunnerBackend and MoeRunnerConfig"]
    ConceptFlash["FlashInfer TRT-LLM path"] --> EntityFlash["flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_finalize_context"]
    ConceptDG["DeepGEMM runner"] --> EntityDG["MoeRunnerCore and DeepGemmMoeQuantInfo"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:25-50](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py:62-68](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py:47-100](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-34](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216]()

The runner and communication backend names belong to different configuration dimensions: `MoeRunnerBackend` names the expert-computation implementation, while `MoeA2ABackend` names the all-to-all or dispatch implementation. This distinction is useful when tracing configuration and execution through `FusedMoE` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186]().

**Diagram: Runner backend and communication backend as separate choices**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Layer["FusedMoE"] --> RunnerChoice["MoeRunnerBackend"]
    Layer --> DispatchChoice["MoeA2ABackend"]
    RunnerChoice --> Triton["TRITON"]
    RunnerChoice --> DeepGemm["DEEP_GEMM"]
    RunnerChoice --> Trtllm["FLASHINFER_TRTLLM"]
    RunnerChoice --> Cutlass["FLASHINFER_CUTLASS"]
    RunnerChoice --> CuteDSL["FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL"]
    DispatchChoice --> DeepEP["DEEPEP"]
    DispatchChoice --> Mooncake["MOONCAKE"]
    DispatchChoice --> Nixl["NIXL"]
    DispatchChoice --> FlashInfer["FLASHINFER"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:36-49](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:194-216](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:171-186]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page explains the DeepSeek-V2/V3 attention path and the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 architecture exposed by SGLang’s implementation. It focuses on MLA, DSA/V4 indexers, compressed and sliding-window KV storage, backend selection, and the relationship between these concepts and code entities. The available source excerpts do not expose every implementation body, so details are limited to behavior supported by the cited code and documentation. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:123-140](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-161](), [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:98-104]()

## DeepSeek Model Architecture

DeepSeek-V2/V3 attention in the supplied implementation is represented by `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA`. The MLA forward mixin is shared code that handles forward-mode decisions, indexer reuse, and attention preparation. The V3 attention comments document separate non-RoPE and RoPE query/key dimensions, plus a value dimension; they also describe MHA forward modes used for cases such as chunked KV processing. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:63-68](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-161](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:123-165]()

The supplied V4.1 deployment documentation describes a sparse-attention MoE model with 40 decoder layers, 384 routed experts selected at top-6, and one shared expert. It describes one 512-wide KV latent per position, reused as key and value across 64 query heads, with no separate value projection. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:98-104]()

| Model or concept | Implementation or architectural detail |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA | `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` is the MLA module referenced by the shared forward mixin. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:63-68]() |
| DeepSeek-V3 attention dimensions | The implementation comments list `qk_nope_head_dim = 128`, `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, `qk_head_dim = 192`, and `v_head_dim = 128`. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:123-128]() |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 attention | One 512-wide latent per position supplies key and value information for 64 query heads, according to the deployment architecture description. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:100-104]() |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse retrieval | The documentation distinguishes KV source layers from index source layers and states that retrieving layers select a top-512 candidate set. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:102-104]() |

## Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)

### Forward path and dataflow

`DeepseekMLAForwardMixin` provides MLA-specific forward behavior around a `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` module. It identifies DCP decode-related modes, initializes MLA execution state, decides whether an indexer should run, and gates a BMM-to-attention fusion path. The fusion predicate checks conditions including DCP size, prefill graph scope, DSA use, DeepGEMM use, LoRA activity, and learnable sink parameters. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-184]()

The code shown here does not include the complete projection and attention body. The diagram therefore shows the supported execution relationship—attention module, forward mixin, backend, and KV pool—without asserting unshown projection internals. The implementation imports `get_attn_backend` and `get_token_to_kv_pool`; the forward-mixin logic uses `ForwardBatch` to make mode-dependent decisions. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:28-32](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-161]()

**Diagram: MLA forward coordination**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    BATCH["ForwardBatch"] --> MODE["is_dcp_mla_decode_phase"]
    BATCH --> INDEXER_DECISION["should_run_indexer"]
    MODULE["DeepseekV2AttentionMLA"] --> MIXIN["DeepseekMLAForwardMixin"]
    MODE --> MIXIN
    INDEXER_DECISION --> MIXIN
    MIXIN --> BACKEND["get_attn_backend"]
    MIXIN --> CACHE["get_token_to_kv_pool"]
    BACKEND --> OUTPUT["MLAResultTensor"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:28-32](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:63-68](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-184]()

### Indexer reuse and distributed modes

`is_dcp_mla_decode_phase` returns false when DCP size is one; otherwise it recognizes decode, target-verify, and DSA extend modes. `is_dcp_q_replicate_phase` identifies decode and target-verify when query projection replication is enabled. These checks let the forward path distinguish attention phases that need distributed handling. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-135]()

`should_run_indexer` prevents shared `skip_topk` layers from running an indexer whose weights are absent, and permits the NextN fallback when that layer has its own weights. The method’s comments also explain why missing carried top-k indices alone must not trigger recomputation: that could invoke an uninitialized indexer whenever cross-layer propagation is unavailable (e.g. the TBO op path drops topk_indices), reintroducing the >index_topk garbling. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:142-161]()

The MHA-side `forward_dsa_indexer_for_mha` runs an indexer using hidden states, `q_lora`, positions, the forward batch, and layer ID. When speculative metadata requests a DSA seed, it requires returned top-k indices and writes them using `write_mtp_seed`. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:95-120]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-161](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:95-120]()

### MHA and MLA execution modes

The DeepSeek-V3 MHA comments describe three paths: normal attention for an empty KV prefix, one-shot attention for a short prefix, and chunked-KV attention when the prefix exceeds the configured chunk capacity. In the chunked case, successive prefix chunks produce outputs and log-sum-exp values that are accumulated. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:142-165]()

`resolve_attn_backend` unwraps `TboAttnBackend`, selects the full-attention child of hybrid backends, and selects a prefill/decode child when a backend exposes `_select_backend`. This resolves the actual backend serving the current forward mode. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:45-66]()

| Path | Condition described in implementation comments | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `forward_normal` | First chunked-prefill batch with no KV prefix. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:142-149]() | Performs attention over the current extended tokens. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:142-149]() |
| `forward_normal_one_shot` | Prefix fits within the configured chunk capacity. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:150-156]() | Uses combined prefix and extended KV indices. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:150-156]() |
| `forward_normal_chunked_kv` | Prefix exceeds maximum KV chunk capacity. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:157-165]() | Processes multiple KV chunks and accumulates partial attention results. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:157-165]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:45-66](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:123-165]()

## DSA, DSV4 Indexers, and Sparse Retrieval

### DSA indexer path

The shared MHA forward helper invokes an indexer with `hidden_states`, `q_lora`, `positions`, `forward_batch`, and `layer_id`. Its purpose is to populate indexer state and, when requested by speculative metadata, publish top-k indices as an MTP seed. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:95-120]()

`DSATopKBackend` is imported by the V4 attention backend, while the DSV4 indexer module exposes kernels and helpers including `plan_topk_v2`, `topk_transform_paged`, and `topk_transform_paged_v2`. The shown code establishes these integration points; it does not expose all scoring or selection implementation details. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:53-70](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:19-42]()

### DSV4 indexer and candidate selection

The V4 attention backend imports `C4IndexerBackendMixin`, DSV4 indexer metadata types, and V4.1 indexer factories `make_candidate_indexer` and `make_full_topk_indexer`. It also imports `prefill_k_slots` and `SparseTableBackend`, connecting candidate scoring and sparse-table handling to backend execution. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:69-95]()

The general DSV4 indexer module includes FP8 and FP4 quantization-related paths and paged MQA-logit helpers. For example, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` consumes a query, paged FP8 KV cache, weights, sequence lengths, and a page table; it computes per-token scores and masks positions beyond each sequence length. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:73-103](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:106-145]()

V4.1’s documented retrieval design separates KV source layers and index source layers. The documentation states that extra index layers can rescore keys from a source layer, and that retrieving layers select top-512 candidates. These are model-specific architecture facts; the backend and indexer modules are the corresponding implementation areas. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:102-104](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:69-95]()

## DeepSeek-V4 Compressed KV and Sliding-Window Attention

### V4 KV organization

The V4.1 architecture description distinguishes compressed latents from a 128-position sliding window. It states that compressed latents are produced at source layers and shared forward, while the sliding-window state is computed per layer and remains bounded by the window size. It also describes compression ratios that change across layer ranges. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:100-104]()

The memory-pool helpers support compression ratios 2, 4, and 128 for compression-state rings. `collect_sources_by_ratio` validates configured ratios and groups source layers by ratio; ratios 1 and 2 use `kv_source_layers`, while ratios 4 and 128 use layers directly. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-115]()

`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` is imported by the V4 attention backend and is the pool type used there. The memory-pool module also defines `resolve_compress_state_ring_size`, which derives draft-token count from speculative configuration before calculating ring capacity. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:109-115](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-91]()

**Diagram: V4 attention and compressed-state flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    TOKENS["TokenPositions"] --> SWA["SlidingWindowAttentionState128"]
    TOKENS --> SOURCE["KVSourceLayer"]
    SOURCE --> COMPRESS["CompressedKVState"]
    COMPRESS --> CONSUMER["AttentionConsumerLayer"]
    INDEX_SOURCE["IndexSourceLayer"] --> TOPK["TopKCandidateIndices"]
    TOPK --> CONSUMER
    SWA --> CONSUMER
    POOL["DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool"] --> SWA
    POOL --> COMPRESS
```

Sources: [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:100-104](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-115](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:109-115]()

### Compression state and cache layout

The memory-pool code defines ring sizing for speculative and non-speculative use. For ratio 2, speculative sizing grows to a power of two based on draft-token count; for ratios 4 and 128, it selects different ring sizes, and online C128 compression can reduce the ring size to one subject to an MTP guard. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-79]()

The V4 attention backend imports compression metadata preparation, paged compressor data creation, KV layout handling, and dequantization helpers. The HIP backend shares the main V4 backend types and adds ROCm-specific sparse-prefill and attention operations. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:23-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:59-75](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:23-75]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-79](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:23-75](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:23-75]()

## Attention Backend Selection and Platform Constraints

`apply_deepseek_v4_defaults` resolves the default V4 attention backend. Its selection logic chooses `flashmla_mega` only for DeepSeek-V4.1 on CUDA with supported SM100 hardware, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and an allowed KV layout; otherwise it chooses `flashmla`. It also validates explicit `flashmla_mega` and `trtllm` choices. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:29-42](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:45-93]()

For the `trtllm` backend, the shown validation requires CUDA and SM100/SM103 support, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, no HiSparse, no context parallelism, no PD disaggregation, and positive chunked-prefill size. The hook also sets a default `max_running_requests` of 256 when none is configured. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:83-128]()

The V4 attention backend defines defaults including `SWA_WINDOW = 128` and `DEFAULT_INDEX_TOPK = 512`. The HIP backend defines the same constants and has a separate backend module with ROCm-specific attention, sparse-prefill, and indexer helpers. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:156-163](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:130-136]()

| Backend/configuration behavior | Constraint or default |
|---|---|
| Automatic backend | `flashmla_mega` is selected only under the stated V4.1/CUDA/SM100/FP8/layout conditions; otherwise automatic selection returns `flashmla`. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:29-42]() |
| `flashmla_mega` | Requires DeepSeek-V4.1 on CUDA with SM100/SM103 support. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:74-81]() |
| `trtllm` | Requires FP8 E4M3 KV, chunked prefill, and excludes HiSparse, context parallelism, and PD disaggregation in the shown validation. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:83-118]() |
| Prefill context parallelism | V4 accepts `interleave` or `zigzag`; zigzag is restricted to NPU in the shown validation. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:143-158]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:29-42](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:74-128](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:143-158](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:156-163](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py:130-136]()

## Quantization and Indexer Arithmetic

The V4 indexer imports FP4 and FP8 quantization helpers and selects FP8 dtype according to platform support. Its paged FP8 MQA-logit helper checks tensor layouts, gathers pages through a page table, computes scores, masks invalid positions using sequence lengths, and pads or truncates to the requested maximum sequence length. [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:19-42](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:73-145]()

The V4 memory-pool utility `get_dsv4_indexer_bytes_per_token` returns a different payload-and-scale byte estimate depending on whether the FP4 indexer is used. This supports memory accounting for compressed indexer tokens; it is separate from the model’s expert-weight quantization. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:53-58]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:19-42](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:73-145](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:53-58]()

## Speculative Decoding Integration

The V4 defaults hook restricts the shown speculative-algorithm choices to `EAGLE` and `DSPARK`; for EAGLE it requires `speculative_eagle_topk == 1`. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:130-140]()

The V4.1 deployment documentation identifies DSpark as a bundled three-stage draft and gives the deployment flag `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` with a configurable block size. The V4 memory pool includes draft-aware ring sizing and DSpark-specific SWA ring helpers, connecting speculative execution to cache-state allocation. [docs/src/snippets/configs/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.jsx:91-100](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-79](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:125-153]()

`DeepseekModelNextN` is an inference-only model class that constructs a `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` with `is_nextn=True`, and defines token embedding and normalization components used by that model path. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:3649]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:130-140](), [docs/src/snippets/configs/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.jsx:91-100](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-79](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:125-153](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:3649]()

## Correctness Coverage

The DSV4 attention test module covers SWA-only cases through the `dsv4` backend, CUDA-graph-style decode cases, and compression-ratio cases including C2, C4, and C128. Its test comments state that the compression cases compare the attention integration against an independent PyTorch SWA plus extra-K reference, while compressor-math correctness is deferred in that test suite. [test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py:1-12](), [test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py:47-85](), [test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py:86-150]()

The tests include eager extend/decode and CUDA-graph decode runner cases, and define target-verify cases for SWA and compressed paths. [test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py:47-85](), [test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py:152-181]()

## Summary

- The DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA forward mixin makes execution decisions from `ForwardBatch`, including DCP phase checks, indexer reuse, and fusion eligibility. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-184]()
- The V3 MHA implementation documents normal, one-shot, and chunked-KV attention paths, and resolves nested or phase-specific attention backends. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:45-66](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:142-165]()
- DSA indexing invokes an indexer and can provide top-k seeds for speculative execution; V4 backend modules connect indexer factories, top-k helpers, sparse tables, compression metadata, and attention execution. [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:95-120](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:59-95]()
- V4.1 combines compressed KV state, bounded sliding-window state, and sparse candidate retrieval; the memory-pool utilities account for compression ratios and speculative ring sizing. [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:100-104](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-115]()
- V4 backend selection and validation depend on hardware, KV dtype, context-parallel settings, and prefill configuration. [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:29-42](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:74-128]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py:116-184](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:45-66](), [python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py:95-120](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:59-95](), [docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx:100-104](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:60-115](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:29-42](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py:74-128]()

## Purpose and scope

This page details expert routing, token dispatch, hierarchical expert selection, and Expert Load Balancing (EPLB) in SGLang's Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) execution paths. It covers router score calculations, top-k selection, fused kernel integrations (`moe_fused_gate` and `mega_gate`), `HashTopK` and lookup-based routers, expert location metadata (`ExpertLocationMetadata`), physical weight updates (`ExpertLocationUpdater`), and expert distribution recording (`ExpertDistributionRecorder`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:52-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:1-182](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:37-144](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:63-95](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py:120-151]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:52-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:1-182](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:37-144](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:63-95](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py:120-151]()

---

## TopK Routing

TopK routing transforms router logits into expert indices and scaling weights for each token. SGLang supports multiple routing execution paths depending on the hardware platform, quantization scheme, and model architecture: Triton-based fused kernels (`moe_fused_gate` and `mega_gate`), DeepGEMM Mega-MoE gates, and PyTorch fallback paths. [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:52-87](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:33-80](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:99-144]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:52-87](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:33-80](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:99-144]()

### Routing inputs, scores, and weights

The router accepts hidden states and router logits, applies scoring functions (`softmax`, `sigmoid`, or `sqrtsoftplus`), and computes expert selection. For instance, `run_mega_gate` in `mega_gate.py` evaluates specialized Mega-MoE routing conditions for DeepSeek architectures using hardware-accelerated bf16 gate functions (`bf16_mega_gate`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:33-97](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/mega_gate.py:9-10]()

When using Triton-backed routing in `topk.py`, routing invokes custom Triton kernels (`_router_triton_kernel`), producing dispatch indices, combine indices, gather/scatter mappings, and gate scaling factors [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:56-87](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:100-147]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:33-97](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/mega_gate.py:9-10](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:56-87](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:100-147]()

### Scoring, ranking, and numerical safeguards

SGLang handles potential numerical instability in sigmoid and softmax scoring by introducing an epsilon term, `_RENORMALIZE_SUM_EPSILON` (`1e-20`), before renormalization. This prevents `0/0` NaN poisonings when router logits severely underflow [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:110-119]().

Specialized hardware paths—such as the AMD ROCm Triton softmax top-k (`_use_rocm_triton_softmax_topk`)—optimize decode-sized rows for specific models by bypassing full general reductions [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:129-151]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:110-151]()

---

## Hierarchical Expert Selection and Hash Routing

Hierarchical selection groups experts and limits top-k candidate pools. The fused gate kernel accepts compile-time parameters (`N_GROUP`, `TOPK_GROUP`, `EXPERTS_PER_GROUP`) to execute grouped routing [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:41-44]().

### HashTopK implementation

`HashTopK` (`hash_topk.py`) uses a token-to-expert ID mapping table (`tid2eid`) rather than dynamic logits argmax for routing [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:37-70]().

It supports `softmax`, `sigmoid`, and `sqrt(softplus)` scoring options, manages optional waterfill load balancing via `_apply_waterfill`, and handles shared-expert slots by appending them to the routed expert selections [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:134-182]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:41-44](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:37-182]()

---

## Expert Load Balancing (EPLB) and Expert Location

SGLang manages expert placement across Expert Parallel (EP) ranks using `ExpertLocationMetadata` and updates physical expert weights dynamically via `ExpertLocationUpdater` [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:63-74](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py:45-57]().

### ExpertLocationMetadata

`ExpertLocationMetadata` tracks physical-to-logical and logical-to-physical expert mappings across model layers:
- `physical_to_logical_map`: Maps physical expert indices to logical experts per layer `(layers, num_physical_experts)` [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:75]()
- `logical_to_all_physical_map`: Maps logical experts to all replica physical locations `(layers, num_logical_experts, X)` [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:77]()
- `logical_to_rank_dispatch_physical_map`: Rank-dispatch layout tensor [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:82]()

Initialized via `ExpertLocationMetadata.init_trivial()` or `ExpertLocationMetadata.init_by_mapping()`, it provides the foundation for expert migration and dispatch remapping [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:120-155]().

### ExpertDistributionRecorder

`ExpertDistributionRecorder` collects expert token frequencies and balancedness metrics across forward passes to guide EPLB solvers [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py:135-151]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:63-155](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py:135-151]()

## Routing and Dispatch Data Flow

The following diagrams bridge natural-space routing concepts to exact code entities and function calls in the SGLang codebase.

### Diagram 1: TopK Routing and Mega-Gate Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["HiddenStates and Router Logits"] --> CheckMega["should_use_mega_gate()"]
    CheckMega -->|Yes| RunMega["run_mega_gate() using bf16_mega_gate"]
    CheckMega -->|No| CheckHash{"is_hash / HashTopK"}
    CheckHash -->|Yes| HashForward["HashTopK._forward_torch()"]
    CheckHash -->|No| RoutingTr["topk.py routing or _router_triton_kernel"]
    RunMega --> Output["StandardTopKOutput / Weights & IDs"]
    HashForward --> Output
    RoutingTr --> Output
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py:56-87](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:82-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py:145-182](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:23-68]()

### Diagram 2: EPLB Metadata and Weight Update Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Recorder["ExpertDistributionRecorder"] --> Collect["Record Expert Frequencies"]
    Collect --> Solver["EPLB Solver"]
    Solver --> NewMeta["ExpertLocationMetadata.init_by_mapping()"]
    NewMeta --> Updater["ExpertLocationUpdater.update()"]
    Updater --> RawUpdate["_update_expert_weights_raw()"]
    RawUpdate --> DistributedSync["torch.distributed P2P / NCCL Swap"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py:151-175](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py:135-151]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers Mixture of Experts (MoE) specific quantization and execution paths, including MXFP4 weight and activation preparation, FlashInfer CUTLASS and TRT-LLM runner interfaces, DeepGEMM MegaMoE, MegaGate, token dispatchers, JIT compilation utilities, and optimization techniques. It also explains how the codebase manages aligned layouts, temporary SM budgets, and kernel execution hooks.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:63-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-184]()

## Quantization Methods Overview

MoE quantization paths are distinguished by their weight and activation formats, scale conventions, and runner contracts. In the codebase, MXFP4 and FP8 quantization are supported through multiple kernel-oriented paths.

| Path or Payload | Weight Format and Layout | Activation or Scale Information | Code-Level Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer CUTLASS Generic MoE | BF16/FP16 weights, FP8 weights, or packed NVFP4 weights | Input and weight scale tensors via `quant_scales` | `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` is passed toward the fused CUTLASS MoE function. |
| CUTLASS MXFP4 MoE | MXFP4 packed weights and E8M0 block scales | SM120 payload can select MXFP8 activations; SM90 can use a Humming W4A8 triplet | `FlashInferCutlassMxfp4MoeQuantInfo` records weight layouts and path selection fields. |
| FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP4 MoE | Packed FP4 weights with inverse block scales | Prepares and routes inputs for TRT-LLM fused-MoE paths | `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod` selects the FlashInfer MXFP4 runner backend. |
| DeepGEMM MegaMoE | Selected by `mma_type` (`fp8xfp4`, `mxf4xmxf4`, `nvfp4xnvfp4`) | Uses a shared symmetric buffer keyed by shape, expert, top-k, and MMA configuration | `mega_moe.py` chooses MMA type and manages the DeepGEMM symmetric buffer. [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:56-60](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:119-158]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:50-69](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:112-154](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:120-169](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:56-60](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:119-158]()

## MoE Quantization Architecture

The quantization-method and runner boundary carries packed weights, scale tensors, activation conventions, and optional fused-activation parameters. For the CUTLASS route, `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` and `FlashInferCutlassMxfp4MoeQuantInfo` describe these inputs before routing through `MoeRunner`.

## MXFP4 MoE Quantization and Layout Preparation

The MXFP4 TRT-LLM method creates packed `w13_weight` and `w2_weight` parameters using an FP4 block size of 32. Its input preparation pads the MoE intermediate dimension to a multiple of 128 after tensor-parallel weight loading, inserting zero tails into weight tensors and neutral scale tails into inverse-scale tensors.

`Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod.configure_bypassed_topk` permits the FlashInfer routing contract only when the configuration uses grouped top-k, sigmoid scoring, correction bias, and no custom routing functions or shared top-k slots. On success, it records `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3` and `MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_MXFP4`.

**Diagram: MXFP4 weights from layout preparation to the runner payload**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Checkpoint["CheckpointWeights"]
    Load["WeightLoading"]
    Pad["_pad_intermediate_size"]
    Layout["InterleavedOrPackedLayout"]
    Payload["FlashInferCutlassMxfp4MoeQuantInfo"]
    Kernel["cutlass_fused_moe"]
    Checkpoint --> Load --> Pad --> Layout --> Payload --> Kernel
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:55-102](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:120-193](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:112-165]()

## DeepGEMM and CUTLASS Kernels

The CUTLASS runner module owns calls to FlashInfer's `cutlass_fused_moe` for unquantized, ModelOpt FP8, ModelOpt NVFP4, and CUTLASS MXFP4 paths. Its quantization payloads carry weight tensors, scales, optional output dtypes, and optional SwiGLU values.

### DeepGEMM MegaMoE Buffer, Shape Constraints, and SM Budgeting

`mega_moe.py` selects the MegaMoE MMA type: NVFP4 uses `nvfp4xnvfp4`, W4A4 uses `mxf4xmxf4`, and dense FP8 uses `fp8xfp4`. `check_mega_moe_shapes` applies alignment requirements and raises a `ValueError` when dimensions are incompatible [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:56-60](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:100-117]().

`_get_mega_moe_symm_buffer` imports `deep_gemm`, applies an SM budget, and uses a cache key containing process-group identity, token capacity, expert count, top-k, hidden sizes, MMA type, and effective SM count. On cache miss, it calls `deep_gemm.get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:119-158]().

`_configure_mega_moe_deep_gemm_num_sms` calculates physical counts to avoid compounding reservations since two-batch overlap and DSA indexers can reconfigure SMs process-wide [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:63-97]().

**Diagram: DeepGEMM MegaMoE buffer preparation and runtime budget**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Experts["_mega_moe_nvfp4_or_w4a4"]
    MmaType["_mega_moe_mma_type"]
    Shape["check_mega_moe_shapes"]
    Device["_mega_moe_max_num_sms"]
    Budget["_configure_mega_moe_deep_gemm_num_sms"]
    Cache["_MEGA_MOE_SYMM_BUFFER"]
    Buffer["deep_gemm.get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe"]
    Restore["RestoreDeepGemmSmsSetting"]
    Experts --> MmaType --> Shape
    Device --> Budget
    Shape --> Cache
    Budget --> Cache
    Cache -->|"cache_miss"| Buffer
    Buffer --> Restore
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:56-60](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:63-117](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:119-158]()

## Two-Batch Overlap (TBO) and Expert Parallelism Coordination

The MegaMoE module coordinates with two-batch overlap by accounting for process-wide SM reconfiguration. `FlashinferDispatcher` handles expert-parallel communication, routing top-k, expert counts, and runner backends, returning `FlashinferDispatchOutput` and accepting `FlashinferCombineInput`.

**Diagram: MoE routing and FlashInfer dispatch code entities bridging natural language and code entities**

```mermaid
    MoE["FusedMoERunner"]

    TopK --> Dispatcher
    Runner --> Dispatcher
    Dispatcher --> Dispatch
    Dispatch --> MoE
    MoE --> Combine
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:63-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py:31-38](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py:112-201]()

## Expert Specialization and Activation Fusion

The CUTLASS payload supports per-expert SwiGLU overrides through `swiglu_alpha`, `swiglu_beta`, and `swiglu_limit` tensors via `materialize_swiglu_params_for_cutlass`. `mega_gate.py` defines `MegaGateRouting` and enforces strict hardware, model, and forward-mode checks in `should_use_mega_gate` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:22-96]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:22-96](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py:170-194]()

## Optimization Techniques and Operational Checks

- **MegaMoE shape checks:** `check_mega_moe_shapes` validates scale groups and alignments based on `mma_type` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:100-117]().
- **MXFP4 CUTLASS padding:** `_pad_intermediate_size` pads local intermediate dimensions to 128-element boundaries.
- **DeepGEMM JIT pre-compilation:** `compile_utils.py` manages JIT compilation of kernels for various batch sizes, serialized across ranks using file locks (`_local_rank_compile_lock`) [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-147]().
- **DeepGEMM execution hooks:** `deep_gemm_execution_hook` ensures kernels are compiled for specific `(m, n, k, num_groups)` configurations prior to execution [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:150-184]().
- **Contiguous layout alignment:** `get_contiguous_layout_alignment` and `contiguous_layout_alignment_scope` manage layout alignment requirements in DeepGEMM [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:173-208]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:100-117](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:173-208]()

## Summary

SGLang provides robust MoE quantization and optimization pathways, integrating MXFP4/FP8 data structures, DeepGEMM symmetric buffers, FlashInfer/CUTLASS backends, JIT compilation utilities, and specialized expert routing mechanisms.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:1-7](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py:56-158](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-184]()

## Purpose and Scope

SGLang’s quantization system connects model quantization formats to layer-specific execution methods and hardware-optimized kernels. This parent page provides a high-level overview of how quantization configurations are resolved and dispatched across linear and MoE layers. Detailed configurations, scheme registries, and individual method implementations are covered in the designated child pages.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:51-56]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:135-182]()

## Quantization Configuration and Registry

Quantization methods implement common base classes such as `QuantizationConfig`, `LinearMethodBase`, and `FusedMoEMethodBase` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:51-56](). The configuration parser inspects model metadata (e.g., HuggingFace config or compressed-tensors dicts) to instantiate the correct scheme handler via factory methods like `get_quantization_config` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:135-182]().

## FP8 and ModelOpt Quantization

FP8 quantization relies on 8-bit floating-point types (`float8_e4m3fn` or `float8_e4m3fnuz`) defined in quantization kernel utilities [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py:97-112](). Execution paths leverage Triton scaled matrix multiplication, block-wise quantization scales, and DeepGEMM or AITER backend wrappers depending on the hardware architecture (e.g., Hopper or AMD MI300/MI350 series) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-33]().

**FP8 and ModelOpt method flow**

```mermaid

    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"

    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        Fp8Scheme["CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8"]
        KernelOps["scaled_fp8_quant"]
        DeepGemmWrapper["deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback"]
    end
    FP8Choice --> Fp8Scheme
    Fp8Scheme --> KernelOps

```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py:97-112]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-33]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:51-59]()

For details, see [FP8 and ModelOpt Quantization](#9.2).

---

## FP4 and MXFP4 Quantization

For modern hardware architectures supporting sub-byte or 4-bit micro-scaling formats (such as Blackwell GPUs or specialized MoE layers), SGLang provides MXFP4, NVFP4, and FP4 quantization support [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/marlin_utils_fp4.py:79-89](). These schemes handle micro-scaling factors, weight repacking, and custom Marlin kernel invocations (`apply_fp4_marlin_linear`) to maximize throughput [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/marlin_utils_fp4.py:79-89]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/marlin_utils_fp4.py:79-89]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:48-51]()

For details, see [FP4 and MXFP4 Quantization](#9.3).

---

## INT8 and Other Quantization Methods

In addition to FP8 and FP4, SGLang supports a wide variety of quantization formats including INT8, AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF, AutoRound, BitsAndBytes, and model-specific compression methods [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py:19-23](). Quantized KV cache options (such as FP8/FP4 KV cache scaling) are also integrated through these modules.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py:19-23]()

For details, see [INT8 and Other Quantization Methods](#9.4).

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the quantization configuration and registration layer located in SGLang’s `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/` package. It covers the `QuantizationConfig` base interface, the `get_quantization_config` factory and registry, compressed-tensors schemes, activation/weight quantization mappings, and how linear and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers query quantization methods [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:35-40]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:26-82]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:35-40](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:26-82]()

## Quantization Registry and Factory

The quantization registry maps checkpoint quantization metadata to concrete `QuantizationConfig` subclasses. The package-level factory inspects model configuration parameters to instantiate the appropriate configuration parser [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-158]().

| Quantization Family | Configuration Class / Module | Implementation References |
|---|---|---|
| `compressed_tensors` | `CompressedTensorsConfig` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-172]() |
| `fp8` | `Fp8Config` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py` |
| `quark` | Quark config classes | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py` |
| `nvfp4_online` | `NvFp4OnlineConfig` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/nvfp4_online.py` |
| Unquantized | `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:77-80]() |

## Configuration Class Hierarchy

Quantization configuration classes inherit from `QuantizationConfig`, while layer methods implement `QuantizeMethodBase`, `LinearMethodBase`, or `FusedMoEMethodBase` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/base_config.py:35-40](). For example, `CompressedTensorsConfig` maintains `target_scheme_map`, `ignore`, `quant_format`, `sparsity_scheme_map`, and `kv_cache_scheme` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-158]().

**Diagram: Quantization Class Hierarchy**

```mermaid
classDiagram
  class QuantizationConfig {
    +get_quant_method(layer, prefix)
    +get_name() str
  }
  class QuantizeMethodBase
  class LinearMethodBase
  class FusedMoEMethodBase
  class CompressedTensorsConfig {
    +target_scheme_map: Dict
    +ignore: List
    +get_linear_method()
  }
  class Fp8Config
  class NvFp4OnlineConfig {
    +is_nvfp4_online: bool
    +use_per_token_activation: bool
  }

  QuantizationConfig <|-- CompressedTensorsConfig
  QuantizationConfig <|-- Fp8Config
  QuantizationConfig <|-- NvFp4OnlineConfig
  QuantizeMethodBase <|-- LinearMethodBase
  QuantizeMethodBase <|-- FusedMoEMethodBase
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/base_config.py:35-40](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-158]()

## Compressed-Tensors Schemes and Layer Resolution

The `compressed-tensors` integration supports diverse quantization schemes across linear weights and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers. `CompressedTensorsConfig` resolves linear schemes via `get_linear_method()` and delegates MoE layers to specialized scheme handlers [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:41-67]().

Helper functions in `compressed_tensors/utils.py` govern layer inclusion and matching:
- `should_ignore_layer()` checks whether a layer name matches the `ignore` list or contains fused shard mappings where all shards share a consistent scheme [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:26-82]().
- `find_matched_target()` matches layer names, module class names, or fused component names against configuration group targets [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:109-155]().

### Method Dispatch and Layer Integration Mapping

The diagram below illustrates how configuration objects resolve specific linear and MoE methods through scheme registries during model loading.

```mermaid

  subgraph "Runtime Initialization"
    ModelLoad[""model_loader/loader.py""] --> GetConfig[""get_quantization_config()""]
  end

  subgraph "Configuration Object"
    GetConfig --> ConfigInstance[""CompressedTensorsConfig""]
  end

  subgraph "Layer Binding"
    ConfigInstance -->|get_quant_method()| LayerSelect[""LinearBase / FusedMoE""]

    LayerSelect --> MoEMethod[""CompressedTensorsMoEScheme""]
  end

  subgraph "Scheme Registry"

  end
```

## Summary

- `get_quantization_config` provides the core factory interface for resolving checkpoint quantization metadata into `QuantizationConfig` instances [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-172]().
- Base abstractions (`QuantizationConfig`, `LinearMethodBase`, `FusedMoEMethodBase`) decouple model architecture logic from low-level quantization kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/base_config.py:35-40]().
- `CompressedTensorsConfig` and utility helpers (`should_ignore_layer`, `find_matched_target`) manage fine-grained layer overrides, regex matching, and activation scaling semantics [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-158]() [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:26-155]().
- Scheme modules (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/`) implement specialized weight-only and weight-activation formats (WNA16, FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py:3-36]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:134-172](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/base_config.py:35-40](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py:26-155](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py:3-36]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes SGLang’s FP8 and NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization infrastructure, focusing on the `torch.float8_e4m3fn` (E4M3) representation, block-wise quantization, backend dispatch via Triton, CUTLASS, and AITER, and the DeepGEMM wrapper integration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and dense linear layers. It covers the system architecture, configuration parsing, weight loading via `ModelOptModelLoader`, and runtime environment controls.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:55-80](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:18-39](), [test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py:24-43]()

---

## System Overview

Quantization configuration and execution are split across dedicated modules within `sglang.srt.layers.quantization`:
- `fp8.py`: Defines `Fp8Config`, `Fp8LinearMethod`, and `Fp8MoEMethod` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:43]().
- `fp8_utils.py`: Houses scale conversion helpers, quantization primitives, and backend dispatchers (`dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`, `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:55-80]().
- `modelopt_quant.py`: Implements `ModelOptFp8Config`, `ModelOptFp4Config`, `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig`, and associated linear/MoE methods [test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py:29-35]().
- MoE Runners (`deep_gemm.py`, `flashinfer_trtllm.py`, etc.): Integrate quantization metadata into expert computation pipelines [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:25-34]().
