## FP8 Configuration and Data Flow

### FP8 Methods and Quantization Primitives

SGLang utilizes low-precision FP8 formats (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`) for weight-activations (W8A8) matrix multiplications. The quantization module imports primitives such as `scaled_fp8_quant`, `static_quant_fp8`, and `per_token_group_quant_fp8` from `sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.fp8_kernel` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:15-20](). 

At the utility tier, `fp8_utils.py` interfaces with GEMM backends including `triton_scaled_mm`, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_deepgemm`, and `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-15](). Platform-specific constraints—such as FNUZ formats (`is_fp8_fnuz()`) on specific AMD architectures—are checked dynamically during initialization [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:26]().

### Weight Loading and Parameter Structures

Weights and scales are stored using specialized parameter classes:
- `ModelWeightParameter`: Manages quantized model weights.
- `BlockQuantScaleParameter`: Handles block-wise quantization scales (e.g., $128 \times 128$ blocks).
- `PerTensorScaleParameter`: Manages per-tensor scaling factors [python/sglang/srt/layers/parameter.py:45-47]().

Title: FP8 Execution Primitive Mapping

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    fp8_dtype["fp8_dtype"] --> apply_fp8_linear["apply_fp8_linear"]
    is_fp8_fnuz["is_fp8_fnuz"] --> apply_fp8_linear
    scaled_fp8_quant["scaled_fp8_quant"] --> apply_fp8_linear
    per_token_group_quant_fp8["per_token_group_quant_fp8"] --> apply_fp8_linear
    apply_fp8_linear --> dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear["dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear"]
    dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear --> deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback["deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback"]
    deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback --> w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_deepgemm["w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_deepgemm"]
    deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback --> w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton["w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:15-20](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-27]()

---

## ModelOpt Integration

### Configuration and Parsing

NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization schemes (`modelopt_fp8`, `modelopt_fp4`, `modelopt`) are parsed through helper methods on `ModelConfig`. The configuration parser maps HuggingFace quantization algorithms (`quant_algo`) to SGLang internal method identifiers:

| Quantization Algorithm / Method | SGLang Internal Mapping |
|---|---|
| `modelopt` + `quant_algo: FP8` | `modelopt_fp8` |
| `modelopt` + `quant_algo: FP4` / `NVFP4` | `modelopt_fp4` |
| `quant_algo: MXFP8` | `mxfp8` |
| `quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION` | `w4afp8` |

Sources: [test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py:141-159]()

### FP4 Custom Operation Execution

For ModelOpt NVFP4 models, `modelopt_quant.py` registers a custom operation `fp4_gemm` (`@register_custom_op`) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py:134-144](). It attempts hardware dispatch via `try_qwen3x_nvfp4_gemm` before falling back to FlashInfer's `mm_fp4` or `mm_bf16_fp4` backed by `get_fp4_gemm_runner_backend()` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py:145-181]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py:134-181]()

---

## Per-Token and Block-Wise Quantization Kernels

### Granularity and Scale Layouts

Block-wise quantization divides weights and activations into blocks (typically $128 \times 128$) with independent scaling factors. The utility layer provides conversion functions such as `block_fp8_scale_to_e8m0_128`, `block_fp8_scale_to_mxfp8_e8m0`, and `requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm` to adapt scale representations between checkpoint formats and kernel input requirements [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:55-75]().

### DeepGEMM Memory Budgeting

In `deep_gemm.py`, `_estimate_masked_standard_layout_peak_bytes()` calculates dynamic memory overhead for MoE execution by factoring in activation dtypes, block sizes, and scale tensors (`uint8` packed UE8M0 vs. FP32 scales):
- Block size defaults to 128 if not specified in `quant_info.block_shape` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:160]().
- Peak row bytes aggregate input activation storage, input scales, down-projection inputs, down scales, and intermediate GEMM buffers multiplied by padded token counts (`padded_m`) per local expert [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:171-178]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:55-75](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:130-178]()

---

## Linear and MoE Implementations

### Linear Layers

Dense linear quantization is handled by `Fp8LinearMethod` and `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod`. During forward execution, they invoke `apply_fp8_linear`, which routes tensors through `dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` or per-tensor quantization routines depending on the configuration and hardware capability [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:68]().

### MoE Layers

MoE quantization is implemented via `Fp8MoEMethod` and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod`, integrated directly into `FusedMoE` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:59-71](). `_fuses_routed_scaling_factor_in_topk` inspects whether scaling factors are fused into top-k routing based on runner backends such as FlashInfer, TRT-LLM, or CUTLASS [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:108-130]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:68](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:59-71](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:108-130]()

---

## Hardware-Specific Features and Platform Distinctions

### ROCm and AITER Integration

When running on AMD ROCm hardware (`_is_hip`), SGLang supports AITER-accelerated GEMM kernels:
- `_use_aiter` enables AITER block-FP8 paths (except on `gfx1250` architectures where CK quant/GEMM kernels lack required MFMA/WMMA instructions) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:79-81]().
- For `gfx95` architectures, `_AITER_GFX95_CK_W8A8_MAX_SAFE_M` maps specific $(N, K)$ shapes to maximum safe $M$ thresholds to prevent numerical NaN occurrences in older ROCm runtimes prior to version 7.2 [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:96-101]().
- `set_dense_mxscale()` checks if the installed AITER library supports `get_mxscale_bpreshuffle_config` for e8m0 block scales before enabling dense MX-scale paths [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:157-176]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:79-101](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:157-176]()

---

## Environment Variables and Runtime Controls

| Environment Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_USE_AITER` | Enables AITER operator acceleration on supported AMD ROCm platforms. [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:79-81]() |
| `SGLANG_FORCE_CK_W8A8` | Forces the use of CUTLASS/AITER preshuffled W8A8 GEMMs. [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:118-120]() |
| `SGLANG_DSV4_DENSE_MXSCALE_SHAPES` | Configures the $(N, K)$ whitelist or `all` policy for dense MX-scale GEMMs. [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:182-186]() |
| `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT` | Forces conversion of MXFP8 weights to native block-FP8 (`[128, 128]`) format. [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:151-153]() |
| `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_MEMORY_BUDGET_FRACTION` | Sets the fraction of free non-static device memory allocated for DeepGEMM masked layout buffers. [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:129-135]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:79-186](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:151-153](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:129-135]()

## Purpose and Scope

This section documents SGLang’s FP4 and MXFP4 quantization paths, including MXFP4 microscaling, NVFP4 checkpoint detection, Quark W4A4 schemes, Blackwell (SM100) and Hopper (SM90) FlashInfer/CUTLASS MoE execution interfaces, and activation/weight preparation routines [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:1-65](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:1-65](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]()

---

## System Architecture Overview

The quantization configuration and execution path connects checkpoint metadata to a per-layer scheme, then to a dense-layer or MoE implementation. The codebase uses specialized detection utilities (`_detect_nvfp4_source`) to parse configuration dictionaries from ModelOpt or AMD Quark, mapping them to appropriate online quantization schemes, dequantization routines, or fused MoE runners [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:147-175]().

### High-Level Dataflow Mapping: Natural Language Space → Code Entity Space

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural_Language_Space"
        Checkpoint["Checkpoint quantization metadata"]
        LayerScheme["Per-layer W4A4 scheme"]
        Activations["MXFP4 activation preparation"]
        FusedExecution["Fused MoE execution"]
    end
    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        Detect["_detect_nvfp4_source"]
        QuarkScheme["QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE"]
        Prepare["_prepare_flashinfer_mxfp8_activations"]
        Runner["Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod"]
    end
    Checkpoint --> Detect
    Detect --> QuarkScheme
    LayerScheme --> QuarkScheme
    Activations --> Prepare
    Prepare --> Runner
    QuarkScheme --> Runner
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:147-175]()

### Execution Roles

| Code entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `_detect_nvfp4_source()` | Parses quantization configurations from ModelOpt or AMD Quark checkpoints to return an `Nvfp4SourceConfig` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](). |
| `QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE` | Implements the Fused MoE quantization scheme for W4A4 MXFP4 weights and activations, integrating with AITER or Triton backends [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:147-175](). |
| `_prepare_flashinfer_mxfp8_activations()` | Prepares and quantizes input activations into MXFP8/UE8M0 formats for FlashInfer/TRT-LLM MoE runners [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118](). |
| `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod` | Manages weight creation, sharding, and kernel dispatch for MXFP4 MoE layers on SM100 architectures [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:118-173](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:147-175](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:118-173]()

---

## NVFP4 and ModelOpt Source Detection

Checkpoints produced by ModelOpt or AMD Quark carry metadata specifying per-group FP4 weights (typically with group size 16 or 32) and per-tensor or per-block scaling factors (such as E8M0 or FP8 scale tensors) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](). `_detect_nvfp4_source()` inspects `quant_method`, `quant_algo`, and global quantization configurations to determine whether online re-quantization or direct weight loading is required [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]()

---

## MXFP4 Microscaling and Data Representation

MXFP4 representations pack two 4-bit values (`float4_e2m1`) into each `uint8` element. Microscaling factors (stored as E8M0 byte arrays) provide block-level exponents to maintain dynamic range across groups of elements (e.g., block size 16 or 32) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:121-161]().

### Packed Data and Scale Flow

| Stage | Representation or operation |
|---|---|
| Serialized weight | FP4 nibbles packed two per `uint8`; weight scales use E8M0 block layouts [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:142-161](). |
| Scale decoding | `e8m0_to_f32()` decodes raw byte values $b$ to $2^{b-127}$, handling NaN/Inf sentinels ($255$) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/utils.py:183-190](). |
| Dequantization fallback | `_dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16()` converts packed weights and scales into dense `bfloat16` tensors for hardware execution paths that lack native FP4 instruction support (such as certain consumer RDNA or non-native architectures) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:142-161](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:121-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/utils.py:183-190]()

### Activation Preparation Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input tensor x and hidden_size"] --> CheckShape["Check if x.shape[-1] matches hidden_size"]
    CheckShape -->|Match| RouteHandoff["Call route_quant_handoff or per_token_group_quant"]
    CheckShape -->|Mismatch/SM107| FlashinferQuant["Call flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize or per_token_group_quant"]
    RouteHandoff --> ReturnPrepared["Return x_quant and x_scale"]
    FlashinferQuant --> ReturnPrepared
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118]()

---

## SM100 and SM90 MoE Execution

Blackwell (SM100) and Hopper (SM90) architectures employ specialized FlashInfer and CUTLASS kernels for fused MoE execution with MXFP4/MXFP8 microscaling [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-39](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:121-143]().

- **SM100 Path**: Uses FlashInfer TRT-LLM / CuTe-DSL wrappers (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`, `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`) supporting block-scaled interleave operations [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-34]().
- **SM90 Path**: Uses CUTLASS mixed-input GEMM kernels with interleaved weights and scales, supporting both W4A16 and corrected Humming W4A8 execution modes [test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py:1-42]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-39](), [test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py:1-42]()

---

## Quark W4A4 Schemes and AITER Integration

AMD ROCm platforms integrate MXFP4 and W4A4 schemes via AITER (`aiter`) operators, supporting specialized shufflers, scale swizzlers (`moe_shuffle_scale`, `e8m0_shuffle`), and dynamic quantization routines (`dynamic_mxfp4_quant`) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:50-64](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:45-66]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:50-64](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py:45-66]()

---

## Summary Table: FP4 and MXFP4 Paths

| Path | Configuration or data shape | Execution details |
|---|---|---|
| ModelOpt / Quark NVFP4 Detection | `quant_method` in `modelopt`, `quark`, `nvfp4` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]() | Parsed via `_detect_nvfp4_source()` to configure online re-quantization or weight loading [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131]() |
| FlashInfer MXFP8 Activation Quant | Group size 32, scale format `e8m0` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:138-152]() | Prepared via `_prepare_flashinfer_mxfp8_activations()` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118]() |
| SM100 TRT-LLM MXFP4 MoE | Packed FP4 weights, E8M0 block scales [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-34]() | Executed via `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` and block scale interleave helpers [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-34]() |
| AITER / Quark W4A4 MoE | Per-group scales for weights and activations [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:162-170]() | Dispatched through AITER fused kernels and shuffle utilities on supported ROCm architectures [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:50-64]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:81-131](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:79-118](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:28-34](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py:50-170]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers INT8, AWQ, GPTQ, QServe, GGUF, AutoRound, Petit, ModelSlim, BitsAndBytes, and quantized KV cache formats (FP8/FP4 KV). It details quantization concepts, platform support, and implementation mechanics established across the SGLang codebase and documentation. SGLang distinguishes **offline quantization** (loading pre-quantized weights) from **online quantization** (computing quantization scales at runtime). For pre-quantized models, the serving engine advises against passing `--quantization` flags that trigger online parameter computation [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:6-17]().

Sources: [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:6-17]()

---

## Quantization Method Overview and Registry

The documentation and codebase support a wide variety of quantization methods and hardware backends. Quantization behavior depends heavily on the method, model checkpoint specification, and hardware target [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:23-25]().

| Method or family | Documented support and implementation notes |
|---|---|
| `blockwise_int8` | NVIDIA and AMD; Triton-based block quantization [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:67-71](). |
| `w8a8_int8` | NVIDIA and AMD [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:74-78](). |
| `awq` | NVIDIA, AMD, and Ascend; utilizes JIT-compiled CUDA kernels on NVIDIA, Triton dequantization on AMD, and CANN kernels on Ascend [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:88-92](). |
| `gptq` | Listed for Ascend and Intel CPUs with AMX; replaced by `gptq_marlin` on NVIDIA/AMD [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:95-100](). |
| `gguf` | NVIDIA and Ascend; NVIDIA uses CUDA kernels via `sgl-kernel`, while Ascend performs CPU pre-dequantization at load time [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:144-149](). |
| `auto-round` | Supported on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel, with partial Ascend CANN kernel support [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:116-120](). |
| `modelopt` | NVIDIA-only compatibility; requires Hopper/SM90+ architecture for FP8 and ModelOpt mixed formats [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:151-155](). |
| Other formats | Includes `compressed-tensors`, `quark`, `awq_marlin`, `gptq_marlin`, and BitsAndBytes 4-bit sharding [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:102-142](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:176-189](). |

### From method names to code entities

```mermaid
    end
```

## INT8 (W8A8) Quantization Implementation

`W8A8` specifies 8-bit quantization for both weights and activations. The compatibility matrix lists `w8a8_int8` for NVIDIA and AMD, with `blockwise_int8` implemented via Triton [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:67-78]().

For Ascend NPU ModelSlim checkpoints, the engine imports `ModelSlimW8A8Int8` and `ModelSlimW8A8Int8MoE` schemes [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:20-33](). `ModelSlimConfig` parses quantization parameters, maps aliases, and patches `RMSNorm` initialization and forward passes when bias addition is required [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:51-90,149-181]().

The `NPUW8A8Int8LinearMethod` class manages W8A8 INT8 linear layers on NPU. It invokes `prepare_w8a8_int8_linear_weights()` and instantiates `aclnn_input_scale`, `aclnn_input_scale_reciprocal`, and `aclnn_input_offset` parameters [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py:41-58](). Its `apply()` method quantizes activation tensors `x` to `torch.qint8` if necessary and invokes `torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul()` [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py:59-102]().

`NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod` implements dynamic quantization, utilizing `torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_quant()` or accepting pre-quantized inputs with per-token dynamic scales prior to calling `torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul()` [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py:105-130]().

**Diagram: Ascend W8A8 INT8 Linear Layer Data Path**

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["InputTensorX"] --> B{"IsXAlreadyINT8?"};
    B -- No --> C["torch.ops.npu.npu_quantize"];
    B -- Yes --> D["QuantizedX"];
    C --> D;
    D --> E["torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul"];
    F["LayerWeights"] --> E;
    G["LayerDequantScale"] --> E;
    H["LayerBias"] --> E;
    E --> I["OutputTensor"];

    subgraph NPUW8A8Int8LinearMethod.apply
        B; C; D; E; F; G; H;
    end
```

Sources: [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:67-78](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:20-33](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py:41-130]()

---

## AWQ, GPTQ, QServe, and GGUF Quantization

### AWQ
Supported across NVIDIA, AMD, and Ascend. NVIDIA executes JIT-compiled CUDA kernels, AMD uses Triton-based dequantization, and Ascend relies on native CANN operator bindings [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:88-92]().

### GPTQ
Legacy GPTQ on NVIDIA and AMD is deprecated in favor of `gptq_marlin`. GPTQ remains supported on Ascend via CANN kernels and on Intel CPUs with AMX acceleration [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:95-100]().

### QServe
Integrated into the broader quantization ecosystem and supported via specialized engine plugins and custom linear dispatch methods.

### GGUF
Supported on NVIDIA and Ascend backends. NVIDIA executes optimized CUDA kernels in `sgl-kernel`, while Ascend performs CPU pre-dequantization during model weight loading [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:144-149]().

Sources: [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:88-149]()

---

## AutoRound, Petit, ModelSlim, BitsAndBytes, and Other Methods

### AutoRound
Documented for NVIDIA and AMD with partial Ascend CANN support, alongside platform-agnostic Intel AutoRound execution [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:116-120]().

### Petit
Included in specialized NVFP4 and mixed-precision execution flows.

### ModelSlim
`ModelSlimConfig` administers NPU-specific offline quantization metadata [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:149-152](). It normalizes DeepSeek V4 parameter names (e.g., keys prefixed with `hc_head_`), inserts module aliases for `block_sparse_moe`, and wraps `RMSNorm` layers when quantization bias fusion is required [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:51-90,153-181](). Supported schemes span `ModelSlimW8A8Int8`, `ModelSlimW4A4Int4`, and diverse MXFP4/MXFP8 variants [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/schemes/__init__.py]().

### BitsAndBytes
BitsAndBytes 4-bit checkpoint sharding and tensor loading are handled via utility functions like `adjust_bitsandbytes_4bit_shard()`, which computes per-shard dimensions and tensor offsets relative to the parent model [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:176-189]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:176-189](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:51-90](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py:149-181]()

---

## MoE Quantization Data Flow and NPU Backend

The Ascend MoE execution path links quantization-aware routing with underlying block hardware runners. `_NPUMoEMethodBase` and associated subclasses configure dispatch dtypes and weight prefixes [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py:174-203](). For MXFP8/MXFP4 MoE layers, `w4a8_mxfp_gmm()` coordinates grouped matrix multiplication combining FP4 weights and FP8 activations via `torch.ops.npu.npu_grouped_matmul()` [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py:46-89]().

**Diagram: Quantization concepts mapped to Ascend MoE entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        INT8["W8A8INT8MoE"]
        MXFP8["MXFP8MoE"]
    end

    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        RUNNER_CORE["AscendRunnerCore"]
        INT8_ACT["NPUSwigluQuant"]
        MXFP8_METHOD["NPUMXFP8MoEMethod"]
        MXFP8_GMM["w4a8_mxfp_gmm"]
    end

    INT8 --> RUNNER_CORE
    MXFP8 --> RUNNER_CORE

    RUNNER_CORE -- if INT8 MoE --> INT8_ACT
    RUNNER_CORE -- if MXFP8 MoE --> MXFP8_METHOD
    MXFP8_METHOD --> MXFP8_GMM
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py:46-89](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py:174-203]()

---

## Quantized KV Cache (FP8 and FP4 KV)

Quantized KV cache formats (such as FP8 KV and FP4 KV) reduce memory consumption during long-context generation. In SGLang, KV cache scaling factors and dtypes are resolved during model loading and attention initialization. Specifically, weight loader utilities parse scaling factors from checkpoints and convert them into device-resident tensors attached to `RadixAttention` modules (`k_scale`, `v_scale`) for hardware-accelerated dequantization during attention forward passes [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/load_model_utils.py:164-185]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/load_model_utils.py:164-185]()

---

## Online and Offline Quantization

Offline quantization loads pre-quantized weights (such as GPTQ, AWQ, ModelSlim, and compressed-tensors checkpoints) produced through calibration datasets [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:6-17](). Online quantization computes scaling parameters dynamically at startup. SGLang recommends offline quantization for serving throughput and warns against combining online quantization flags with pre-quantized checkpoints [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:6-17](). On Ascend NPU, offline quantization configurations are parsed automatically from `quant_model_description.json` or `config.json` [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/quantization.mdx:6-8]().

Sources: [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:6-17](), [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/quantization.mdx:6-8]()

---

## Platform and Support Caveats

Quantization support varies across hardware backends. For example, AWQ spans NVIDIA, AMD, and Ascend with different kernel implementations, whereas `gptq_marlin` targets NVIDIA, and GGUF utilizes `sgl-kernel` on NVIDIA versus CPU pre-dequantization on Ascend [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:88-149](). Backend initialization routines configure hardware attention backends, memory allocations, and operator bindings [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py:76-216]().

Sources: [docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:88-149](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py:76-216]()

---

## Purpose and scope

This page gives a high-level map of SGLang’s model execution layers: reusable model-building components, hardware-specific implementations, distributed layer operations, and the layer boundary transition framework [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:1-60](). It introduces how these concerns connect and points to the child pages for implementation details. For model-family examples, the codebase includes architectures like LLaMA, Qwen2, and Gemma 3 text and multimodal models [python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:82-182](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:79-178](), [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3_mm.py:108-188]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:1-60](), [python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:82-182](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:79-178](), [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3_mm.py:108-188]()

## Overview

Model implementations assemble layer-level operations such as attention, normalization, and linear projections. For example, `LlamaAttention` and `LlamaMLP` use `QKVParallelLinear`, `MergedColumnParallelLinear`, and `RowParallelLinear` [python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:82-112](). These examples show how model code composes reusable layer APIs rather than implementing every operation inside a model class.

Layer implementations also connect model semantics to platform, distributed execution, and stage transitions managed by `sglang.srt.layers.layer_boundary` [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:40-65](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:70-118](). Backend files like `xpu_backend.py` provide hardware-specific attention implementations [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py:149-160]().

| Concern | Representative code entity | Where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Attention execution | `XPUAttentionBackend`, `FlashAttentionBackend` | [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py:149-160]() |
| Normalization | `RMSNorm`, fused normalization operators | [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:14-35]() |
| Parallel projections | `QKVParallelLinear`, `RowParallelLinear` | [python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:95-112]() |
| Stage boundaries | `StagePlan`, `StageBoundary` | [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:70-118]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:14-65](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py:149-160](), [python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:82-112](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:70-118]()

## Platform abstraction and distributed operations

Layer modules select or import implementations according to available platform support. In `layernorm.py`, platform checks include CUDA, HIP, NPU, CPU, XPU, MLU, and MUSA; optional paths include FlashInfer, AITER, sgl_kernel, and JIT-compiled norms [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:37-65](). Attention backends like `XPUAttentionBackend` handle platform-specific metadata and execution strategies [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py:149-160](). Additionally, layer boundary factories and contracts coordinate reduction strategies (`_resolve_ffn`) and multi-stage parallel topologies [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:132-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-54]().

```mermaid
    LayernormProviders --> LayernormFile["python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py"]

    XPUAttnBackend --> XPUBackendFile["python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py"]

    ResolveFFN --> FactoriesFile["python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py"]
```

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes how SGLang represents hardware platforms, selects a platform at runtime, and exposes seams for platform-specific runtime components. It also covers hardware-specific execution packages and operator dispatch. The implementation details cover NPU, XPU, and MLX packages, along with the custom-op registration framework [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-10]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-10]()

---

## Architecture Overview and Platform Detection

### Platform Detection and Resolution

`current_platform` is a lazy singleton: its active `SRTPlatform` is resolved on first access. `_resolve_platform()` checks `SGLANG_PLATFORM`. When set, it loads the selected plugin; an unknown name or an activation callback returning `None` raises an error. When unset, it activates discovered platform plugins and uses one active plugin, errors if multiple plugins activate, or falls back to an in-tree platform [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:1-10]().

The built-in fallback checks CPU opt-in first (`SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1`), then SAIL, CUDA, NPU, ROCm, XPU, MUSA, and MPS, before falling back to the base `SRTPlatform`. CUDA and ROCm are distinguished using `torch.version.hip`; NPU and XPU detection call respective PyTorch availability APIs [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:37-73]().

`DeviceMixin` provides common device identity and capability operations, while `SRTPlatform` adds runtime-specific capability declarations, lifecycle hooks, and subsystem factory methods. `PlatformCapabilities` declares conservative defaults for Triton, graph capture, piecewise graphs, HiCache device kernels, and PyNccl support [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:49-73]() [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:76-101]().

### Platform Selection: Natural Language to Code Entities

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        Request["Select active runtime platform"]
        Environment["Runtime environment variable"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Lazy["current_platform"]
        Resolve["_resolve_platform()"]
        Env["SGLANG_PLATFORM"]
        Plugins["PLATFORM_PLUGINS_GROUP"]
        Fallback["SRTPlatform subclass check"]
        NPU["NPUSRTPlatform"]
        XPU["XpuSRTPlatform"]
        CUDA["CudaSRTPlatform"]
        CPU["CpuSRTPlatform"]
        Active["SRTPlatform"]
    end

    Request --> Lazy
    Lazy --> Resolve
    Resolve --> Env
    Environment --> Env
    Env -->|"set"| Plugins
    Env -->|"unset"| Fallback
    Fallback --> NPU
    Fallback --> XPU
    Fallback --> CUDA
    Fallback --> CPU
    Plugins --> Active
    NPU --> Active
    XPU --> Active
    CUDA --> Active
    CPU --> Active
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:1-178]()

### Platform Interface and Dispatch Seams

`SRTPlatform` defines methods for choosing platform defaults and supplying runtime components. Its interface includes `get_default_attention_backend()`, `get_default_speculative_draft_attention_backend()`, `get_graph_runner_cls()`, `get_full_graph_backend_cls()`, `get_kv_pool_cls(kind=...)`, `get_paged_allocator_cls()`, and `get_compile_backend()` [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:103-179]().

`get_kv_pool_cls()` accepts `mha`, `mla`, and `dsa` pool kinds. A platform can return a specialized pool subclass or leave the choice to the in-tree implementation [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:39-45]() [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:130-147]().

Out-of-tree SRT platforms are discovered through the `sglang.srt.platforms` entry-point group and subclass `SRTPlatform` [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-10]() [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx:50-115]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:39-179]() [docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx:50-115]()

---

## Hardware Backend Packages: NPU, XPU, MLX

The platform interface and hardware backend code work at different levels. `SRTPlatform` provides selection and factory seams; backend-specific modules implement execution components such as KV pools, attention preparation, graph runners, and routing operations [python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:103-179]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:88-120]().

### 1. NPU Backend (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/`)

The NPU implementation imports `torch_npu` and uses NPU-specific operations alongside SGLang runtime abstractions. `NPUMHATokenToKVPool` subclasses `MHATokenToKVPool`, reads FIA and NPU cache configuration, and overrides buffer creation [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:1-25]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:88-120]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:134-178]().

`ascend_backend.py` defines NPU attention metadata and imports NPU-specific attention implementations, including `AscendTorchNativeAttnBackend`, sparse DCP attention, MLA cache gathering, and MLA preprocessing [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py:6-41]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py:86-126]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:1-178]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py:6-126]()

### 2. XPU and Intel AMX Backend (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`)

The platform discovery code includes `XpuSRTPlatform` as an in-tree platform and checks XPU availability through `torch.xpu.is_available()`. `IntelAMXAttnBackend` handles CPU/AMX-specific attention and decode/extend operations via `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.decode_attention_cpu` and `extend_attention_cpu`, managing KV cache and metadata buffers for CPU inference [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py:19-62]() [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:20-30]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py:19-62]() [python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:20-30]()

### 3. MLX Backend (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/`)

The MLX backend provides `MlxModelRunner` for Apple Silicon, which integrates with the scheduler's `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` and `RadixCache`. It manages attention KV from `MlxAttentionKVPool` and handles native auxiliary layer states [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py:1-24]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py:43-59]().

`MlxModelRunnerStub` is a lightweight `ModelRunner` that skips PyTorch weight loading and KV cache allocation, creating only CPU-side bookkeeping pools needed by the scheduler [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:1-5]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:43-48]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:97-103]().

`MlxTpModelWorker` routes inference through MLX, replacing the standard `ModelRunner` with `MlxModelRunnerStub` and delegating forward passes to `MlxModelRunner` [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/tp_worker.py:1-13]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/tp_worker.py:70-77]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py:1-59]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner_stub.py:1-103]() [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/tp_worker.py:1-77]()

## Custom Op and JIT Kernel Framework

SGLang utilizes a custom operator and JIT kernel framework to provide optimized implementations for various hardware platforms, supporting platform-specific dispatch and integration with `torch.compile`.

### Custom Operator Registration

The `sgl_kernel` library provides custom operators for various functionalities. For CPU and general backends, `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp` registers CPU-specific kernels, including activation functions, normalization layers, and attention operations [python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp:24-193]().

These operators are exposed through `torch.library.impl` and `torch.library.def` in C++ extensions, making them callable from Python via `torch.ops.sgl_kernel`.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp:24-193]()

### `torch.compile` Integration and Fake Ops

To support `torch.compile`, SGLang registers fake implementations for custom operators. `CPUGraphRunner` defines `register_cpu_compile_fake` and `register_fake_ops` to provide meta-implementations for `sgl_kernel` CPU operators [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:151-190]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:151-190]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents SGLang’s attention-layer interface, attention implementations (MHA, MLA, GQA, and Sparse Attention), and backend engines visible in the codebase (`FlashAttentionBackend`, `FlashInferAttnBackend`, `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend`, `AiterBackend`, `TritonAttnBackend`, `WaveAttnBackend`, `HybridAttnBackend`). It also details the attention registry, backend selection mechanics, and execution dispatch through `RadixAttention`.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:52-80](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py:10-15]()

---

## Attention Architecture Overview

`RadixAttention` serves as the primary model-layer interface for attention computations [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-108](). It manages per-layer properties such as query-head count, key/value head count, head dimensions, scaling factors, attention type, and sliding-window configuration. During the forward pass, it handles input reshaping and special graph paths before dispatching execution to `get_attn_backend().forward(...)` [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](). The backend supplies the underlying kernel implementations, while the layer handles model-specific parameter mapping.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-108](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176]()

**Diagram: Model attention layer to backend execution**

```mermaid
graph LR
    ModelLayer["ModelAttentionLayer"] --> RadixAttention["RadixAttention"]
    RadixAttention --> ForwardContext["get_attn_backend()"]
    ForwardContext --> AttentionBackend["AttentionBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> FlashAttentionBackend["FlashAttentionBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> FlashInferAttnBackend["FlashInferAttnBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> TritonAttnBackend["TritonAttnBackend"]
    FlashInferAttnBackend --> TRTLLMHAAttnBackend["TRTLLMHAAttnBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> AiterBackend["AiterBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> FlashInferMLAAttnBackend["FlashInferMLAAttnBackend"]
    AttentionBackend --> WaveAttnBackend["WaveAttnBackend"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:33-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-80](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:174-176](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py:36-155](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py:132-160](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py:32-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py:150-166](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py:32-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/wave_backend.py:1-35]()

---

## Attention Mechanisms

### Multi-Head Attention (MHA)

`RadixAttention` tracks the query-head count in `tp_q_head_num`, and the KV-head count in both `tp_k_head_num` and `tp_v_head_num` [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-108](). `head_dim`, `v_head_dim`, scaling, layer ID, attention type, and optional sliding-window size are maintained on the layer [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-132](). The forward path reshapes incoming key and value tensors using these head counts and dimensions before dispatching to the active backend.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-108](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-132]()

### Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)

Grouped-Query Attention is configured by setting `tp_q_head_num` differently from `tp_k_head_num` and `tp_v_head_num` within `RadixAttention` [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-87](). Sparse attention backends implement GQA-oriented kernel interfaces such as `sparse_gqa_fwd_interface_triton` and `sparse_gqa_packed_decode_triton` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:25-44]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:60-87](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:25-44]()

### Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)

MLA compresses keys and values into latent vectors to reduce memory footprint. It features dedicated execution paths across FlashInfer, TRTLLM, and AITER backends:
- **FlashInfer MLA:** Uses `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` and `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py:70-86]().
- **TRTLLM MLA:** Manages multi-CTA KV counter buffers and applies FP8 QKV quantization helpers [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py:104-158]().
- **AITER MLA:** Implements AMD-specific persistent MLA prefill and decode execution paths [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:47-69]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py:70-86](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py:104-158](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:47-69]()

### Sparse Attention (QSA & DSA)

Sparse attention mechanisms utilize indexers to select subset blocks of key/value caches (e.g., `QSAIndexer` in `qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py` and DeepSeek Sparse Attention). They construct metadata via indexers and dispatch to sparse kernel wrappers like `qsa_sparse_attention` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:25-44]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:1-44](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py:56-96]()

---

## Attention Backends

Backends inherit from `AttentionBackend` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py:85-106]() and implement metadata initialization (`init_forward_metadata_out_graph` / `init_forward_metadata_in_graph`) and forward passes.

- **FlashAttentionBackend:** Manages metadata via `FlashAttentionMetadata` storing sequence-length data, cumulative lengths, page tables, and window configurations [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py:74-148]().
- **FlashInferAttnBackend:** Utilizes FlashInfer paged and ragged prefill/decode wrappers with safe fallback mechanisms [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py:10-15](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py:76-113]().
- **TRTLLMHAAttnBackend:** Extends `FlashInferAttnBackend`, handling prefill dispatch by GPU architecture and decode via XQA or TRTLLM-GEN [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py:3-13](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py:174-175]().
- **TritonAttnBackend:** Implements custom Triton attention kernels for decode and extend operations with window rails [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py:125-184]().
- **AiterBackend:** Integrates AMD-specific MHA, MLA, paged-attention, and unified-attention kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:47-73]().
- **WaveAttnBackend:** Provides specialized attention kernel wrappers for optimized hardware targets [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/wave_backend.py:1-40]().
- **HybridAttnBackend:** Combines different backends for prefill and decode stages (e.g., mixing sparse/linear attention or distinct prefill/decode optimizations) [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_attn_backend.py:27-57]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py:85-106](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py:74-148](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py:10-113](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py:3-175](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py:125-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:47-73](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/wave_backend.py:1-40](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_attn_backend.py:27-57]()

---

## Backend Dispatch and Runtime Selection

`RadixAttention.forward` inspects the execution context and input tensors to determine whether to take a graph-cached path or dispatch directly to the active backend via `get_attn_backend()` [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:33-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](). Backend instances are retrieved dynamically from thread-local forward context set up during model runner initialization [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/attention_backend_setup.py:1-50]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:33-35](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py:114-176](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/attention_backend_setup.py:1-50]()

**Diagram: `RadixAttention.forward` execution path**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Inputs["q, k, v, ForwardBatch"] --> Reshape["RadixAttention.forward: reshape K and V"]
    Reshape --> GraphCheck{"extend in graph scope?"}
    GraphCheck -->|"yes"| Eager["_eager_attention"]
    GraphCheck -->|"no"| RealRows{"padded real-token path?"}
    RealRows -->|"yes"| Real["attention on real rows"]
    RealRows -->|"no"| Lookup["get_attn_backend()"]
    Lookup --> BackendForward["AttentionBackend.forward"]
    Eager --> Output["attention output"]
    Real --> Output
    BackendForward --> Output
```

## Purpose and scope

This page describes SGLang’s rotary positional embedding implementations: standard RoPE, YaRN scaling, multimodal RoPE (MRoPE), and additional variants exposed through the RoPE factory. It covers cache construction and reuse, position-to-cache data flow, and the hardware-specific paths visible in the codebase [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:11-30]()`

---

## 1. Overview

SGLang’s positional embedding code is organized around `RotaryEmbedding`, which precomputes cosine and sine values and stores them in a non-persistent `cos_sin_cache` buffer. Its constructor records the head and rotary dimensions, maximum position, frequency base, layout style, dtype, and position offset. It also sets up platform-dependent execution choices [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]().

Specialized implementations extend the available behavior: `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` changes frequency calculation and can extend its cache; `MRotaryEmbedding` assigns rotary lanes to temporal, height, and width axes; and `factory.py` imports multiple model- and scaling-specific variants for construction through `get_rope` [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:91-180](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:60-172](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:11-30]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:91-180]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:60-172]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:11-30]()`

### High-level data flow

`get_rope` accepts the embedding dimensions, position limit, frequency base, layout style, optional scaling configuration, dtype, partial rotary factor, and optional dual-chunk configuration. It normalizes list-valued configuration entries for use in its cache key, applies `partial_rotary_factor` to `rotary_dim` when below one, then checks the process-wide `_ROPE_DICT` before constructing an embedding [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:125-170]().

For standard RoPE, `RotaryEmbedding` computes its cache during initialization and registers it as a non-persistent buffer. The base class imports `apply_rotary_emb` as the wrapped implementation and chooses native or platform-specific paths according to platform and runtime conditions [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:10-28](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:110-165]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Request["Model requests positional embedding"]
    Factory["get_rope"]
    Key["Configuration cache key"]
    Cache["_ROPE_DICT"]
    Instance["RotaryEmbedding or selected variant"]
    CosSin["cos_sin_cache"]
    Apply["Rotary application path"]
    Output["Position-adjusted query and key"]

    Request --> Factory
    Factory --> Key
    Key --> Cache
    Cache -->|"live entry"| Instance
    Cache -->|"missing or invalid entry"| Instance
    Instance --> CosSin
    CosSin --> Apply
    Apply --> Output
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:90-170]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]()`

## 2. Core Architecture and Class Hierarchy

`RotaryEmbedding` is defined as a `BaseFusedOp` subclass. Its constructor saves configuration fields, computes the cosine/sine cache, and registers that cache as a non-persistent buffer. The cache is kept in FP32 for CUDA, HIP, XPU, or when `SGLANG_ROPE_CACHE_FP32` is enabled; otherwise, it is converted to the requested dtype [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-120](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:153-156]().

The constructor sets `use_fallback_kernel` and `fallback_rotary_embedding` under a platform- and head-size-dependent condition. It also sets `_supports_bf16_rope_store` only when several conditions hold, including CUDA, the exact `RotaryEmbedding` type, NeoX style, and no forced-native execution. The visible constructor sets `forward_native` as the selected method for forced-native execution or MUSA [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:110-165]().

| Field or mechanism | Role |
|---|---|
| `head_size`, `rotary_dim` | Record head width and the portion of each head designated for rotary embedding [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:92-109](). |
| `max_position_embeddings`, `base` | Configure the position range and frequency base used by the embedding [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:92-109](). |
| `is_neox_style` | Select the rotary layout style stored by the instance [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:92-109](). |
| `cos_sin_cache` | Non-persistent buffer populated from `_compute_cos_sin_cache()` [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:115-120](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:153-156](). |
| `_apply_rotary_emb_wrapped` | Initially references `apply_rotary_emb`; the forced-native/MUSA path wraps it with `torch.compile` [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:156-164](). |
| `_force_native` | Derived from runtime role and deterministic on-policy target state [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:110-114](). |

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]()`

## 3. Positional Embedding Types

### 3.1. Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)

`RotaryEmbedding` is the standard implementation. It computes the cache during initialization, registers it as a buffer, and keeps a reference to `apply_rotary_emb` for rotary application. The supplied code also shows CUDA, HIP, NPU, and XPU-specific imports or optional fast paths, alongside device-dependent fallback selection [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:44-86](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]().

The constructor’s FP32 cache policy is platform-aware: CUDA, HIP, and XPU retain the computed cache dtype, while other platforms convert it to the requested dtype unless `SGLANG_ROPE_CACHE_FP32` is enabled. NPU’s optional `fused_rope_qk_mqa` import is caught; if unavailable, the module logs a warning and records `None` for that kernel [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:47-70](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:115-120]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:44-86]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:86-165]()`

### 3.2. YaRN Scaling Rotary Embedding

`YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` extends `RotaryEmbedding`. Its constructor accepts a scaling factor, extrapolation and attention factors, `beta_fast`, `beta_slow`, truncation behavior, and optional magnitude-scaling parameters. It computes `mscale` from the supplied values or from `yarn_get_mscale_simple`, then passes the RoPE dimensions and layout to the base constructor [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:91-135]().

The frequency calculation blends interpolation and extrapolation frequencies. `yarn_find_correction_range` determines the blend range, and `yarn_linear_ramp_mask` forms the interpolation mask used in that blend. `_ensure_cos_sin_cache_length` calls `_extend_yarn_cache`; the helper returns the existing cache unchanged when it already covers the requested position, otherwise it aligns the new length using `SGLANG_ROPE_CACHE_ALIGN` and appends newly computed rows [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:14-51](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:66-88](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:137-180]().

| YaRN element | Implementation role |
|---|---|
| `yarn_find_correction_dim` and `yarn_find_correction_range` | Derive and clamp correction dimensions from rotation counts and embedding parameters [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:14-40](). |
| `yarn_linear_ramp_mask` | Produces a clamped linear ramp for frequency blending [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:43-51](). |
| `yarn_get_mscale_simple`, `yarn_get_mscale` | Compute magnitude-scaling values for scales above one [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:54-63](). |
| `_extend_yarn_cache` | Extends the cache to an aligned length and returns appended, uncast rows for auxiliary use [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:66-88](). |
| `_compute_inv_freq` | Blends interpolation and extrapolation inverse frequencies using the correction range and ramp mask [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:137-161](). |

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:14-88]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn.py:91-180]()`

### 3.3. Multimodal Rotary Embeddings (MRoPE)

`MRotaryEmbedding` subclasses `RotaryEmbedding` and accepts `mrope_section`, `mrope_interleaved`, and `mrope_interleaved_glm`. When sections are provided, their sum is checked against `rotary_dim // 2`; mismatches are corrected by rescaling the sections or distributing them across axes [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:60-109]().

`_build_axis_map` maps each rotary pair to one of three axes. In GLM interleaved mode it assigns lanes cyclically while respecting each section’s capacity; in the other interleaved mode it assigns lanes by a stepped pattern; otherwise, it assigns contiguous ranges by section. The resulting `axis_map` is registered as a non-persistent buffer [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:109-143]().

For one-dimensional positions, `get_cos_sin_with_position` delegates to the base implementation. For two-dimensional positions, it indexes `cos_sin_cache`, splits cosine and sine values, then rearranges sections. Interleaved MRoPE uses `apply_interleaved_rope_triton` when both prefill and decode backends support Triton; otherwise it uses `apply_interleaved_rope`. The resulting position cosine and sine tensors are repeated and reshaped for subsequent use [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:145-172]().

`apply_interleaved_rope` clones the first position-axis tensor and replaces selected lanes with values from the second and third axis tensors [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:53-57]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:53-172]()`

### 3.4. Other Rotary Embedding Variants

`factory.py` imports multiple alternatives, including `LinearScalingRotaryEmbedding`, `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`, `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding`, `DynamicNTKAlphaRotaryEmbedding`, `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding`, `FourierRotaryEmbedding`, `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`, `Llama3RotaryEmbedding`, and `Phi3LongRoPEScaledRotaryEmbedding`. The available factory excerpt shows that a non-`None` `dual_chunk_attention_config` selects `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding`, passing through `chunk_size` and `local_size` when present [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:11-30](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:172-190]().

The visible `Phi3LongRoPEScaledRotaryEmbedding` implementation requires NeoX style and constructs separate short- and long-context caches from their respective factor lists. Its forward path selects positions from a concatenated cache and rotates the configured portion of query and key while preserving the remaining dimensions [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/rope_variant.py:37-100](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/rope_variant.py:103-170]().

`FourierRotaryEmbedding` is identified in its class docstring as an extended Fourier rotary embedding; the provided excerpt shows its constructor parameters, including `fope_init_factor`, `fope_sep_head`, and `num_inv_freq` [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/rope_variant.py:173-200]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:11-30]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:172-190]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/rope_variant.py:37-200]()`

## 4. Factory Interface and Cache Invalidation Lifecycle

`get_rope` accepts the principal RoPE parameters and optional scaling and dual-chunk configuration. It defaults `dtype` to PyTorch’s default dtype, converts list-valued configuration entries to tuples for the cache key, and scales `rotary_dim` when `partial_rotary_factor < 1.0`. The key includes head size, effective rotary dimension, maximum position, base, layout style, scaling configuration, dual-chunk configuration, and dtype [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:125-167]().

The process-wide `_ROPE_DICT` stores embedding instances. `_get_live_rope_cache_entry` returns no cached instance when the current construction is not on the meta device and a cached buffer is meta-backed or has zero-byte storage; it removes that entry so the factory can rebuild it. During a meta-device construction pass, a meta entry is retained for sharing [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:90-122]().

The visible `get_rope` excerpt first checks for a live cached entry. If none is returned, it constructs `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding` when a dual-chunk configuration is provided, or `RotaryEmbedding` when scaling is absent [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:168-190]().

### Cache lookup and recovery

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as "Model initialization"
    participant Factory as "get_rope"
    participant Dict as "_ROPE_DICT"
    participant Checker as "_get_live_rope_cache_entry"
    participant Module as "RotaryEmbedding instance"

    Caller->>Factory: "Request embedding with configuration"
    Factory->>Dict: "Lookup configuration key"
    Dict-->>Factory: "Cached instance or no entry"
    Factory->>Checker: "Validate cached entry"
    alt "Entry is live"
        Checker-->>Factory: "Return cached module"
        Factory-->>Caller: "Return shared module"
    else "Entry is missing or invalid"
        Checker->>Dict: "Remove invalid entry when applicable"
        Checker-->>Factory: "Return no live entry"
        Factory->>Module: "Construct embedding"
        Module-->>Factory: "New module and cache buffer"
        Factory->>Dict: "Store module"
        Factory-->>Caller: "Return new module"
    end
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:90-122]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py:125-190]()`

The cache invalidation tests verify rebuilding after a module is moved to the meta device or its cache storage is released. They also verify that live entries are shared and that intentionally created meta-device entries remain shared during meta construction [test/registered/rotary/test_rope_cache_invalidation.py:23-77]().

Sources: `[test/registered/rotary/test_rope_cache_invalidation.py:23-77]()`

## 5. Hardware-Specific Integration and Optimization

`base.py` selects or imports platform-specific implementations at module load time. The NPU fused kernel is optional and falls back to the generic path when unavailable; the XPU fused kernel is also optional and emits a warning when it cannot be imported. HIP imports `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache`, and CUDA imports `apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace` [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:30-86]().

| HIP | `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache` | Imported when `_is_hip` is true [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:72-76](). |

| XPU | `fused_qk_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace` | Optional import; missing-kernel handling sets the symbol to `None` and logs a warning [python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:77-86](). |

## Purpose and scope

This page maps SGLang’s normalization and activation layer code to its roles in model execution. It covers the implementation evidence for RMSNorm, LayerNorm, SiLU, GELU, and fused operations (including FP8 quantization fusion, JIT activations, and batch-invariant variants). [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:14-47]()

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:14-47]()`

---

## Overview and architecture

`python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py` prepares normalization implementations by detecting the runtime platform and importing available providers. The file handles CUDA, HIP, MUSA, NPU, CPU, and XPU environments, conditionally importing FlashInfer, SGLang kernels (`sgl_kernel`), AITER, vLLM operators, and CUDA JIT kernels. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:49-57]()[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:61-107]()[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:111-177]()[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:183-194]()

### Layer roles mapped to code entities

**Diagram 1 — Normalization and activation names mapped to model-layer code entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    RMS["RMSNorm"] --> LNFILE["python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py"]
    GEMMA3["Gemma3RMSNorm"] --> LNFILE
    LAYER["LayerNorm"] --> LNFUNC["layernorm"]
    LNFUNC --> FLASH["flashinfer.norm.layernorm"]
    SWIGLU["SiluAndMul"] --> QWENMLP["Qwen2MLP"]
    SWIGLU --> LLAMAMLP["LlamaMLP"]
    GEGLU["GeluAndMul"] --> GEMMAMLP["Gemma3MLP"]
```

The model architecture files import the named normalization and activation entities shown: `Qwen2MLP` and `LlamaMLP` construct `SiluAndMul`; `Gemma3MLP` constructs `GeluAndMul`; and various causal models import `RMSNorm`. The `layernorm.py` module defines a custom `layernorm` operation binding to FlashInfer when available. [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:29-40]()[python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:32-42]()[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:81-87]()

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:81-87]()` `[python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:29-40]()` `[python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:32-42]()`

### Platform dispatch and provider setup

At module import, `layernorm.py` evaluates platform predicates and stores their results in module-level flags. On CUDA, XPU, or MUSA, it attempts to register a FlashInfer-backed `layernorm` custom operation. It separately checks for FlashInfer RMSNorm quantization operations (`fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` and `rmsnorm_quant`) and imports `sgl_kernel` RMSNorm functions. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:49-111]()

For HIP, the module selects AITER operators when `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is enabled, or falls back to vLLM RMSNorm operators. On CUDA, it attempts to import JIT-compiled RMSNorm family kernels (`_jit_rmsnorm`, `_jit_fused_add_rmsnorm`, `_jit_rmsnorm_quant`, etc.) tuned for SM100 architectures. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:112-177]()

**Diagram 2 — Platform setup bridged to normalization provider symbols**

```mermaid
graph TD
    PLATFORM["Runtime platform flags"] --> CUDA["is_cuda"]
    PLATFORM --> HIP["is_hip"]
    PLATFORM --> NPU["is_npu"]
    PLATFORM --> XPU["is_xpu"]
    CUDA --> FLASH["flashinfer.norm.layernorm"]
    CUDA --> SGL["sgl_kernel.rmsnorm"]
    CUDA --> JIT["_jit_rmsnorm"]
    CUDA --> FUSED["_jit_fused_add_rmsnorm"]
    HIP --> AITER["aiter.rmsnorm2d_fwd"]
    HIP --> VLLM["vllm._custom_ops.rms_norm"]
    NPU --> NPUGEMMA["npu_gemma_rms_norm"]
    XPU --> FLASH
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:49-111]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:112-177]`, `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:183-194]`

## RMSNorm (Root Mean Square Normalization)

`RMSNorm` is implemented in `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py` with multi-backend dispatch supporting PyTorch native fallback, `sgl_kernel`, FlashInfer, and JIT-compiled variants. It also supports batch-invariant execution paths via `rms_norm_batch_invariant` and `fused_add_rms_norm_batch_invariant` [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:25-29]().

### FP8 Quantization Fusion in RMSNorm

`RMSNorm` includes specialized methods for fused RMSNorm and per-tensor FP8 static quantization, such as `forward_with_per_tensor_quant_fusion` tested in `test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py` [test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py:46-88](). This path leverages FlashInfer's `rmsnorm_quant` and `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` to write directly into an FP8 tensor buffer while simultaneously returning the calculated or updated residual tensor.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:25-29]()`, `[test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py:46-88]()`

---

## LayerNorm

FlashInfer LayerNorm is exposed as a custom operation named `layernorm` decorated with `@register_custom_op`. It delegates directly to `flashinfer.norm.layernorm(input, gamma, beta, eps)` when available on CUDA, XPU, or MUSA backends [python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:61-87]().

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:61-87]()`

---

## Activation functions

### SiluAndMul (SwiGLU activation)

`SiluAndMul` is widely used across LLaMA, Qwen2, and other modern architectures. In `Qwen2MLP` (`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py`) and `LlamaMLP` (`python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py`), the gate and up projections are combined via `MergedColumnParallelLinear`. Their output is processed by `SiluAndMul()`, multiplying the swish-activated gate projection by the up projection [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:109-136]()[python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:117-135]().

Furthermore, custom activation JIT compilation utilities under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/activation.py` provide optimized implementations for SiLU, GELU, and GELU-tanh, including filtered execution paths for MoE and table-based rounding support [python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/activation.py:19-61]().

### GeluAndMul (GeGLU activation)

`Gemma3MLP` validates that the hidden activation is `"gelu_pytorch_tanh"` or equivalent and wraps it with `GeluAndMul()` to handle gated GELU projections.

**Diagram 3 — MLP activation pipeline dataflow**

```mermaid
graph LR
    IN["Hidden States x"] --> PROJ["MergedColumnParallelLinear (gate_up)"]
    PROJ --> ACT{"Activation Type"}
    ACT -->|SiluAndMul| SILU["Silu activation * up projection"]
    ACT -->|GeluAndMul| GELU["GELU tanh activation * up projection"]
    SILU --> DOWN["RowParallelLinear (down_proj)"]
    GELU --> DOWN
    DOWN --> OUT["Output Hidden States"]
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:109-136]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/models/llama.py:117-135]()`, `[python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/activation.py:19-61]()`

---

## Fused operations

Fused operations combine elementwise activation or quantization with normalization or linear layers to minimize memory bandwidth overhead. Examples include `SiluAndMul` combined with quantization (`DenseSiluAndMulQuant`), JIT-compiled elementwise activation kernels (`run_activation`), and fused RMSNorm with FP8 quantization.

### Summary table: normalization and activation layers

| Operation or entity | Evidence available in the codebase | Code pointer |
|---|---|---|
| `RMSNorm` | Multi-backend RMSNorm with JIT, FlashInfer, and batch-invariant support | `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:25-29]()` |
| `RMSNorm` FP8 Fusion | Fused RMSNorm + per-tensor FP8 static quantization via FlashInfer | `[test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py:46-88]()` |
| FlashInfer `layernorm` | Custom op registered via `@register_custom_op` | `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:61-87]()` |
| `SiluAndMul` | SwiGLU activation applied in LLaMA, Qwen2 MLPs | `[python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:109-136]()` |
| JIT Activation Module | Compiled activation module handling SiLU, GELU, and filtering | `[python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/activation.py:19-61]()` |

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:25-87]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py:109-136]()`, `[test/registered/layers/test_layernorm_fusion.py:46-88]()`, `[python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/activation.py:19-61]()`

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the linear-layer, distributed-communication, and layer-boundary interfaces implemented in SGLang. It covers parallel-group resolution in `python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-137](), the `layer_boundary` framework contracts and stage-plan construction [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-177](), and advanced communication fusion including the JIT custom all-reduce (v2) engine (`CustomAllReduceV2`) across decoupled storage planes (`PushPlane`, `PullPlane`) and FlashInfer-based communication fusions [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-38]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-137](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-177](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-38]()

## Linear Layers and Parallel-Group Resolution

`python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py` defines `ReplicatedParallelGroup` and the `LinearParallelGroup` type, which can name `tp`, `attn_tp`, `replicated`, and `shared_experts_tp` groups [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-78](). `resolve_linear_parallel_group()` returns the rank and size of the selected group [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:82-86]().

`_resolve_linear_group()` handles ordinary and replicated group selection [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:112-139](). A `ReplicatedParallelGroup` wraps a base group and derives an effective rank and world size by dividing both by `replica_size`; invalid replica sizes are rejected [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:69-74](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:115-121](). A group name of `"replicated"` resolves to no group [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:122-123]().

When distributed groups are not yet initialized, `_resolve_linear_group()` can construct a `_LogicalGroup` from the configured rank and size for groups larger than one [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:132-138](). The `shared_experts_tp` group is an exception: construction requires that group to exist already [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:133-134]().

| Entity | Role supported by the codebase |
|---|---|
| `ReplicatedParallelGroup` | Declares a base group (`tp` or `attn_tp`) and a replica size. [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:63-73]() |
| `LinearParallelGroup` | Names supported linear group choices, including `shared_experts_tp`. [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:76-79]() |
| `resolve_linear_parallel_group()` | Resolves a group to its rank and size. [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:82-86]() |
| `_LogicalGroup` | Represents a rank and world size before distributed communication is initialized. [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:89-94]() |
| `_ReplicatedGroup` | Exposes the effective rank and size after applying replication. [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:96-110]() |

### Linear layer parallel-group resolution

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Resolve["resolve_linear_parallel_group"] --> ResolveGroup["_resolve_linear_group"]
    ResolveGroup --> RepGroup["ReplicatedParallelGroup"]
    ResolveGroup --> GroupTP["tp"]
    ResolveGroup --> GroupAttnTP["attn_tp"]
    ResolveGroup --> GroupShared["shared_experts_tp"]
    ResolveGroup --> GroupRepl["replicated"]
    RepGroup --> RepGroupObj["_ReplicatedGroup"]
    GroupTP --> CoordOrLog["GroupCoordinator_or_LogicalGroup"]
    GroupAttnTP --> CoordOrLog
    GroupShared --> ExistRequired["ExistingGroupRequired"]
    RepGroupObj --> EffRank["EffectiveRankAndWorldSize"]
    CoordOrLog --> RankSize["RankAndWorldSize"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-139]()
