## Layer Boundaries: Contracts, Layouts, and Stage Plans

The `layer_boundary` framework manages transitions between compute stages. It completes outstanding reductions, moves token rows, applies the producer's residual update, and prepares the consumer's normalized or quantized input [docs/docs/developer_guide/layer_boundary.mdx:6-8]().

### Contracts and batch variants

`ProducerReduction` distinguishes an always-partial producer output from an exit-scoped reduction [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-42](). `ALWAYS_PARTIAL` is attention-only: the output is handed to the next stage’s input as a partial sum [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:34-35](). `EXIT_SCOPED` describes outputs whose sum is completed at the exit or carried to the next input [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:35-37]().

`InputContract` declares the consumer’s required token layout, any token axes the compute stage can gather itself, its residual read operation, and whether it consumes the whole sequence in token order [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:66-86](). `OutputContract` declares the producer’s layout, any outstanding sum group, permitted reduction handoffs, residual update, optional output transform, and custom sum implementation [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:88-131]().

`BatchVariant` identifies ordinary, context-parallel, input-scattered, sequence-parallel, and unpadded batch paths [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:56-64](). `StageContract` pairs one input contract with one output contract, while `EdgeContract` describes both sides of a boundary and the residual’s row movement [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:133-161]().

| Entity | Boundary responsibility |
|---|---|
| `InputContract` | Declares consumer rows, consumer-side gathers, and residual read behavior. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:66-86]() |
| `OutputContract` | Declares producer rows, reduction permissions, residual update, and optional transform. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:88-131]() |
| `StageContract` | Groups input and output contracts for a stage. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:133-143]() |
| `EdgeContract` | Describes producer and consumer contracts plus residual movement across the edge. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:145-161]() |
| `BatchVariant` | Selects a bound path for a supported batch configuration. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:56-64]() |
| `ProducerReduction` | Specifies whether reduction is always handed off or is scoped to the producer’s exit. [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-42]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:29-161]()

### Stage construction and binding

`StagePlan` binds reusable entry and exit paths from a stage’s resolved declarations [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-118](). It stores edge declarations by `BatchVariant`, tracks whether the stage enters the stack or is terminal, and constructs paths for the declared variants [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-177]().

`factories.py` selects active variants from runtime configuration [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:99-109](). The ordinary variant is always yielded; context-parallel, input-scattered, sequence-parallel, and unpadded variants are yielded when their associated configuration predicates hold [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:100-108]().

### Stage construction and forward-path binding

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    StageEdge["StageContractAndEdgeContract"] --> ActiveVariants["factories._active_variants"]
    ActiveVariants --> VariantOrdinary["BatchVariant.ORDINARY"]
    ActiveVariants --> VariantCP["BatchVariant.CONTEXT_PARALLEL"]
    ActiveVariants --> VariantScatter["BatchVariant.INPUT_SCATTERED"]
    ActiveVariants --> VariantSP["BatchVariant.SEQUENCE_PARALLEL"]
    ActiveVariants --> VariantUnpadded["BatchVariant.UNPADDED"]
    VariantEdges["VariantEdges"] --> StagePlan["StagePlan"]
    StagePlan --> BindEntry["bind_entry"]
    StagePlan --> BindExit["bind_exit"]
    StagePlan --> ReusablePaths["ReusableEntryAndExitPaths"]
    Stream["ForwardBatch.ResidualStream"] --> ResidualState["PerForwardResidualState"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/factories.py:99-109](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:70-177](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/boundary.py:23-30]()

## Distributed Communication and Comm Fusion

SGLang integrates high-performance custom device communication mechanisms, notably the JIT custom all-reduce engine (`CustomAllReduceV2`) and FlashInfer communication fusion primitives.

### JIT Custom All-Reduce (v2) Architecture

`CustomAllReduceV2` (`python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`) implements zero-filled symmetric push/pull planes over a decoupled storage architecture [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-29](). 
The CUDA kernel side (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh`) provides four core algorithms:
- `1shot_push`: Lamport-style push of local data to every peer's push workspace, followed by a local polling reduction (optimal for small sizes) [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-6]().
- `2shot_push`: Lamport push where each chunk goes to its owner rank, which reduces it and pushes the sum to all other ranks [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:6-8]().
- `1shot_pull`: Every rank reduces all peers' data from symmetric pull workspaces, a CUDA-graph pointer table, or a multicast address [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:9-11]().
- `2shot_pull`: Reduce-scatter fused with all-gather [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:11-13]().

### Custom All-Reduce Storage Planes and Dataflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InputTensor["InputTensor"] --> ChooseAlgo["choose_algo"]
    ChooseAlgo --> PushPlane["PushPlane_symm_workspace"]
    ChooseAlgo --> PullPlane["PullPlane_symm_workspace"]
    PushPlane --> Kernel1ShotPush["all_reduce_1shot_push_kernel"]
    PushPlane --> Kernel2ShotPush["2shot_push_kernels"]
    PullPlane --> Kernel1ShotPull["1shot_pull_kernels"]
    PullPlane --> Kernel2ShotPull["2shot_pull_kernels"]
    Kernel1ShotPush --> Output["ReducedOutput"]
    Kernel2ShotPush --> Output
    Kernel1ShotPull --> Output
    Kernel2ShotPull --> Output
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-38]()

## Summary

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py` handles parallel group naming, logical pre-initialization groups, and replicated group allocations [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-139]().
- The `layer_boundary` framework manages stage transitions, data layouts, and residual stream updates via `StagePlan` and `ForwardBatch.ResidualStream` [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:66-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-118]().
- `CustomAllReduceV2` provides JIT-compiled communication primitives over decoupled push/pull symmetric memory planes supporting push, pull, and multicast execution modes [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-38]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:62-139](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/contracts.py:66-161](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/construction.py:93-118](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py:1-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh:1-38]()

SGLang provides support for advanced attention architectures optimized for long contexts, including **hybrid attention** models that combine standard attention with linear or state-space mechanisms, and **linear attention** models featuring alternatives to quadratic complexity. This documents key implementations, data flows, kernel backends, and models such as Qwen3-Next, NemotronH, Qwen3.5, and Kimi-Linear [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:49-110](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py:38-42]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:49-110](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py:38-42]()

---

## Overview and Purpose

This section details SGLang’s modular design around hybrid and linear attention backends, providing:

- **Hybrid Backends**: Unified implementations combining standard softmax attention (`RadixAttention`) with linear or SSM-based layers, primarily managed by `MambaAttnBackendBase` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:32-49]().

- **Linear Attention Backends**: Implementations such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), Kernel Delta Attention (KDA), Flash Linear Attention (FLA) primitives, Lightning attention configs, and Mamba2-style state-space models, all orchestrated via the `LinearAttnBackends` enum and kernel backends [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/utils.py:38-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py:11-19]().

- **Model Implementations**: Hybrid and linear attention models like Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Kimi-Linear, and NemotronH that leverage these backends for scalable, efficient attention on long sequences [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:79-88](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:27-34]().

- **Kernel Dispatch and State Handling**: Usage of kernel dispatchers like `KDAKernelDispatcher`, FlashInfer kernels, Mamba metadata (`ForwardMetadata`, `Mamba2Metadata`), and memory pooling abstractions [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba2_metadata.py:28-86]().

- **Performance Optimizations**: Techniques such as Breakable CUDA Graphs, piecewise graph capture, and tightly fused kernels to accelerate linear and hybrid attention [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:24-27](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:13-18]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:32-155](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/utils.py:38-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py:11-19](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:24-27](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:13-18]()

---

## Hybrid Attention Backend

The **hybrid attention backend** integrates standard softmax attention with linear state-space mechanisms for models requiring both precision and efficiency on long sequences. At its core, the `MambaAttnBackendBase` class orchestrates this unified hybrid attention:

- **Pooling and Index Translation:** It relies on the `HybridReqToTokenPool` for managing request-to-token mappings specialized for hybrid use, including support for state pool views and slot ID translation to manage fused replay states and convolutional states used by the Mamba/linear kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:38-111]().

- **State Tracking and Metadata:** The backend maintains `ForwardMetadata` to track replay indices, track masks, convolution states, and fused accept states for breakable CUDA graph optimizations during decode and extend passes [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:112-141]().

- **Multi-Item Scoring (MIS) Support:** Hybrid backends validate MIS support via `validate_mis_support`, ensuring that decode and prefill phases have compatible attention kernels and coherent state management [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:64-75]().

### Key Classes and Data Flow

Title: "Hybrid Attention and Metadata Flow"

```mermaid
graph TD
    MR["ModelRunner"]
    HRTP["HybridReqToTokenPool"]
    MAB["MambaAttnBackendBase"]
    FM["ForwardMetadata"]
    MAM["MambaMixer2"]
    SSU["SelectiveStateUpdateAndCausalConvKernels"]

    MR -->|ProvidesPoolAndDevice| HRTP
    HRTP -->|VirtualToPhysicalSlotTranslation| MAB
    MAB -->|GeneratesAndUpdatesMetadata| FM
    FM -->|StateIndicesAndMasks| MAM
    MAM -->|InvokesKernelUpdates| SSU
```
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:49-110](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:7-10](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba2_metadata.py:28-86]()

---

## Linear Attention Backends

SGLang supports several state-of-the-art **linear attention backends**, including Gated Delta Network (GDN), Kernel Delta Attention (KDA), Flash Linear Attention (FLA), and Lightning attention.

### Gated Delta Network (GDN) and FLA Integration
- Implements recurrent linear attention models using fused gating and delta state updates via custom Triton and FlashInfer kernels, utilizing Flash Linear Attention (FLA) primitives (`fused_gdn_gating`, chunk delta kernels) [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:6-14]().
- Uses a specialized `GDNMISMetadata` structure carrying request-local token segmentations for multi-item scoring [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:87-96]().
- Supports fused projections and decode/prefill fusion with operators like `fused_qkvzba_causal_conv1d_update_contiguous` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:70-74]().
- Maintains compatibility with gated delta kernels on SM90 (Hopper) and SM100 (Blackwell) NVIDIA architectures [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:68-96]().

### Kernel Delta Attention (KDA)
- Implements delta-rule-based recurrent attention with fused updates across prefill, decode, and verify phases [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:101-158]().
- The central dispatcher `KDAKernelDispatcher` selects the appropriate kernel backend (`TritonKDAKernel`, `HelionKDAKernel`, `CuteDSLKDAKernel`, `FlashInferKDAKernel`) based on hardware, phase, and flags [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:101-166]().
- Supports packed decode with replay state scatter, fused accept state plan, and multi-item scoring with fused windows [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:13-20]().
- Advanced verification kernels and fallback paths manage replay correctness and enable breakable CUDA graph support [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:168-175]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:6-151](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:47-175]()

---

## State and Memory Management

Efficient state management is essential for linear and hybrid attention. SGLang provides:

- **MambaPool & BaseLinearStateParams:** Manage fixed-size convolutional and SSM states per request, including pre-calculated byte sizes for convolution and temporal state tensors, critical for efficient memory allocation [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:47-47](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:30-30]().

- **ForwardMetadata & Mamba2Metadata:** Structures that hold all transient metadata needed during forward and decode passes, including replay indices, forced flush flags for replay SSM, fused accept buffers for KDA, and multi-item speculation tokens [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba2_metadata.py:28-86]().

- **Verify Intermediate State Indices:** Functions such as `build_verify_intermediate_state_indices` maintain stable row mappings into speculative intermediate scratch buffers used during multi-step verification of speculative decoding in linear backends [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/utils.py:40-42]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba2_metadata.py:28-86](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/utils.py:40-42]()

---

## Model Implementations Leveraging Hybrid and Linear Attention

SGLang hosts multiple models that fully exploit these architectures:

- **Qwen3-Next:** A hybrid multi-head mixture-of-experts model using gated delta mechanics and sharded projection loaders (`mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader`) for tensor parallelism with precise head shard grouping [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:79-88]().

- **Qwen3.5:** Integrates gated delta network layers, fused projection views (`qwen3_5_gdn_prefill_projection_views`), and specialized RMSNorm gated primitives [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:27-34]().

- **Kimi-Linear:** Combines kernel delta attention with replicated gating, MoE routing with bias correction, and shared expert modules, optimized for multi-device tensor and pipeline parallelism.

- **NemotronH:** This model supports both attention and Mamba-based layers, allowing for hybrid configurations. Its architecture includes decoder layers that leverage `HybridLinearAttnBackend` or `Mamba2AttnBackend` depending on the configuration [python/sglang/srt/models/nemotron_h.py:33-36]().

- **Radix Linear Attention Wrapper:** Provides a unified interface (`RadixLinearAttention`) that manages data flow across linear attention backends, enabling dynamic sequence extensions, breakable CUDA graph capture, and integration with speculative decoding [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py:38-45]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:79-88](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py:38-45](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py:27-34]()

---

## Summary Table of Key Characteristics

| Feature | Mamba / Linear Attention Models | Standard Attention Models |
| :-------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| **State Storage** | Fixed-size `MambaPool` / SSM states | Growing KV cache pool |
| **Compute Complexity** | Linear time O(N) | Quadratic time O(N²) |
| **Tensor Parallel Support** | Sharded loaders like `mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader` | `QKVParallelLinear` and variants |
| **Backends & Kernels** | Triton, FlashInfer, CuTe DSL, FLA (GDN/KDA) | FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton |
| **Supported Models** | Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, NemotronH, Kimi-Linear | LLaMA, Qwen2, DeepSeek |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/mamba/mamba.py:79-88](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:38-43](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py:101-166]()

# Summary

This page documents the sophisticated hybrid and linear attention models in SGLang. The hybrid backends unify softmax and linear/SSM mechanisms for efficient long-context support, notably in Mamba, GDN, and KDA architectures. Linear attention backends such as GDN, KDA, and FLA-backed operations provide specialized recurrent kernels optimized for hardware platforms. Models like Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, NemotronH, and Kimi-Linear leverage these backends for scalable and performant deployments.

## Purpose and Scope

The `sglang.kernels` namespace provides a unified interface for kernel implementations and backend selection. Its metadata distinguishes an implementation’s provenance—such as `TRITON`, `JIT`, `AOT`, `FLASHINFER`, or `CUTE_DSL`—from the devices on which it can run; per-kernel `CapabilityRequirement` metadata expresses platform and, where applicable, CUDA architecture constraints [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:12-17](). Kernel implementations are loaded lazily, keeping the namespace lightweight until a kernel is called [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:1-10]().

This parent page outlines the library’s organization, dispatch model, and optimization themes. For implementation detail, see [Build System and Multi-Architecture Support](#11.1), [Kernel Categories and Implementations](#11.2), [Quantization Kernels](#11.3), [MoE Fused Kernels](#11.4), [Third-Party Library Integration](#11.5), and [CPU and JIT Kernel Support](#11.6).

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:1-17]()

---

## Package Structure and Build System

### High-Level Build Architecture

The kernel namespace describes multiple implementation backends, including pure PyTorch, Triton, JIT, AOT, CuTe DSL, FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, AITER, and `torch_npu`; the backend name describes implementation provenance, not device compatibility [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:29-54](). Device support is declared separately through capability requirements, including CUDA architecture bounds [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:125-162](). Build configuration and platform-specific compilation are covered in [Build System and Multi-Architecture Support](#11.1).

**Kernel metadata and dispatch concepts**

```mermaid
graph LR
    NL["Kernel implementation"] --> Spec["KernelSpec"]
    Spec --> Backend["KernelBackend"]
    Spec --> Capability["CapabilityRequirement"]
    Capability --> Platform["PlatformInfo"]
    Backend --> Selector["select_kernel"]
    Platform --> Selector
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:9-17](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:29-54](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:68-77](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:125-162]()

The build system’s CMake configuration, SM90/SM100 compilation, ROCm support, and platform-specific build paths are detailed in [Build System and Multi-Architecture Support](#11.1). This overview focuses on the runtime-facing distinction between kernel backend and device capability, rather than prescribing build steps [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:12-17]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:12-17]()

---

## Kernel Categories and Implementations

### Kernel Source Organization and Registration

The Python namespace groups kernels by operation family. For example, `sglang.kernels.ops.attention` registers Triton attention and metadata kernels, while `sglang.kernels.ops.gemm` registers GEMM operations and backend alternatives [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/__init__.py:25-73](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:78-149](). Activation operations can expose a pure-PyTorch reference and optimized AOT, JIT, or AITER implementations behind a shared fused-op interface [python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/__init__.py:28-48](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/__init__.py:50-106]().

`BaseFusedOp` provides the shared operator abstraction and dispatches among implementations according to explicit or forced backend selection, platform capability, and fallback behavior [python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:1-20](), [python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:23-44](). For category-specific inventory and PyTorch binding details, see [Kernel Categories and Implementations](#11.2).

**Operation families mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    Attention["Attention compute"] --> AttentionPkg["ops/attention"]
    AttentionPkg --> Decode["decode_attention_fwd"]
    AttentionPkg --> Prefill["context_attention_fwd"]
    GEMM["Matrix multiplication"] --> GemmPkg["ops/gemm"]
    GemmPkg --> ScaledMM["Fp8ScaledMMOp"]
    Activation["Fused activation"] --> ActivationPkg["ops/activation"]
    ActivationPkg --> Silu["SiluAndMulOp"]
    Silu --> Dispatch["forward_native / forward_aot / forward_jit"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/__init__.py:25-73](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:78-149](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/activation/__init__.py:28-80]()

---

## Quantization Kernels

Quantization-related operations are represented in the kernel namespace alongside their alternatives and eligibility conditions. For instance, `Fp8ScaledMMOp` exposes AOT and PyTorch paths for FP8 scaled matrix multiplication, with a shape- and platform-dependent eligibility check for the PyTorch route [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:30-76](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:78-147](). The `per_token_group_quant` kernel handles per-token, per-group quantization for various output types (FP8, INT8) and scale formats (FP32, UE8M0) [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-152](). This kernel can also fuse SiLU and multiplication operations [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:114-115](). The precise supported formats and implementations—including FP8, NVFP4, INT8, and AWQ—are covered in [Quantization Kernels](#11.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:30-76](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:78-147](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-152](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:114-115]()

---

## MoE Fused Kernels

Kernel operations support MoE-related paths as well as general-purpose compute. For example, the Muse Spark model imports specialized routing and GEMM operations from `sglang.kernels.ops` and uses different expert execution paths for BF16 and NVFP4 weights [python/sglang/srt/models/muse_spark.py:22-43](), [python/sglang/srt/models/muse_spark.py:74-75](). The `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant` kernel is used in MoE contexts for DeepSeek-V4, performing SiLU and multiplication followed by FP8 quantization on masked inputs [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant.cuh:39-61](). The MoE child page covers fused gating, expert selection, grouped GEMM, and alignment kernels in detail: [MoE Fused Kernels](#11.4).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/muse_spark.py:22-43](), [python/sglang/srt/models/muse_spark.py:74-75](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant.cuh:39-61]()

---

## Third-Party Library Integration

The backend vocabulary includes implementations associated with libraries such as FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, and AITER [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:40-54](). Operation registrations can point to a specific backend and target; GEMM registrations, for example, include FlashInfer and CuTe DSL targets [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:151-184](). DeepGEMM is integrated for various grouped GEMM operations, including FP8 and BF16 variants, with JIT compilation and pre-compilation support [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-171](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:160-184](). The `cutedsl_bf16_gemm` kernel provides low-latency Blackwell (SM10x) GEMM using CuTe DSL primitives [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:10-25](). See [Third-Party Library Integration](#11.5) for the integration details and supported libraries.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:40-54](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:151-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-171](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:160-184](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:10-25]()

---

## CPU and JIT Kernel Support

The dispatch model includes CPU as a device type and JIT as an implementation backend; those are separate dimensions, and device eligibility is determined by capability metadata [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:29-37](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:57-65](). The namespace is designed to avoid importing kernel backends until needed, and its metadata module does not import Torch or the JIT implementation at module import time [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:1-10](). DeepGEMM utilizes JIT compilation, with options for pre-compilation and fast warmup to optimize kernel loading [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-103](). See [CPU and JIT Kernel Support](#11.6) for CPU kernels, JIT infrastructure, and platform-specific optimizations.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:1-10](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:29-37](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:57-65](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:42-103]()

### Attention and Distributed Decode Concepts to Code Entities

Decode context parallelism (DCP) illustrates how a runtime operation can combine kernel code with communication code: `dcp_kernels.py` defines Triton routines for KV-index construction and attention-output correction, while `comm.py` coordinates gathered statistics and output merging across a `GroupCoordinator` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dcp_kernels.py:15-20](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/dcp/comm.py:45-53](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/dcp/comm.py:56-82](). Linear attention models like Jet Nemotron use fused recurrent kernels for gated delta rule operations [python/sglang/srt/models/jet_nemotron.py:8-10](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_recurrent.py:126-184]().

    KVIndex --> TritonModule["ops/attention/dcp_kernels.py"]

The `sglang.kernels` namespace organizes kernel implementations by operation and describes their backend and platform eligibility through registry metadata [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:12-17](), [python/sglang/kernels/spec.py:125-162](). Shared fused-op dispatch supports optimized implementations and fallbacks behind a common operator interface [python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:1-16](), [python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:23-44](). ## Purpose and Scope

This page details the build system, CMake configuration, multi-architecture compilation pathways (targeting SM90/SM100 for CUDA and `gfx942`/`gfx950`/`gfx1250` for ROCm), ROCm container builds via `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, and platform-specific wheel release automation workflows [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-124](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:1-115]().

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-124](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:1-115]()

---

## Build System Architecture Overview

The SGLang and `sgl-kernel` build architecture separates containerized environment definitions from compilation scripts and distribution packaging. CMake acts as the core native compilation driver for custom CUDA and ROCm extensions, while Python packaging tools (`setuptools`, `wheel`, `scikit-build-core`) handle wheel generation.

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping: Build Pipeline

| Build Concept | Code Entity | Evidenced Role |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm Image Flavor Selection | `GPU_ARCH` and `FROM ... AS gfx...` | Selects architecture- and ROCm-version-specific Docker build stages [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:65-124]() |
| AOT Kernel CMake Configuration | `CMakeLists.txt` | Configures host and device compilation standards, CUDA toolkits, and target architectures |
| AMD CI Dependency Installation | `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` | Resolves image GPU architectures and installs test-time python extras and dependencies [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]() |

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:65-124](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]()

### Build Flow Diagram

This diagram maps high-level build concepts to concrete code entities in the repository.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    sub5["CI and Build Workflows"]
    sub5 --> ROCM_DOCKER["rocm.Dockerfile"]
    sub5 --> KERNEL_CMAKE["CMakeLists.txt"]
    ROCM_DOCKER --> GPU_ARG["GPU_ARCH (gfx942 / gfx950)"]
    GPU_ARG --> STAGE_BUILD["Multi-stage ROCm Builders"]
    KERNEL_CMAKE --> CMAKE_BUILD["sgl-kernel CMake Driver"]
    CMAKE_BUILD --> WHEEL_INDEX["scikit-build-core / Wheel Packaging"]
```

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-124](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]()

## CMake Configuration and Multi-Architecture Compilation (SM90/SM100)

Custom operators and kernel extensions rely on CMake configuration files to compile device code targeting specific GPU microarchitectures. For NVIDIA CUDA platforms, compilation targets include SM90 (Hopper architectures) and SM100 (Blackwell architectures), ensuring that PTX and SASS instructions leverage architecture-specific tensor cores and asynchronous copy instructions.

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping: Architecture Targets

| Compilation Concept | Code Entity | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| SM90 Hopper Code Generation | `-gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90` | Enables Hopper-specific hardware instructions in CUDA flags |
| SM100 Blackwell Feature Flag | `SGL_KERNEL_ENABLE_SM100A` | Toggles compilation support for Blackwell architectures |
| Compilation Threads Limitation | `SGL_KERNEL_COMPILE_THREADS` | Restricts concurrent compilation tasks to avoid host out-of-memory errors (defaults to `32`) |

Sources: [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:1-50]()

### Multi-Architecture Compilation Flow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    sub1["Compilation Trigger"] --> CMAKE_CFG["CMake Configuration"]
    CMAKE_CFG --> ARCH_DETECT["Architecture Detection"]
    ARCH_DETECT -->|NVIDIA CUDA| CUDA_TARGET["SM90 Hopper / SM100 Blackwell"]
    ARCH_DETECT -->|AMD ROCm| ROCM_TARGET["gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx1250"]
    CUDA_TARGET --> PTXAS_BIN["PTX / SASS Assembly via gencode flags"]
    ROCM_TARGET --> HIPCC_BIN["LLVM / HIPCC Compilation via GPU_ARCH"]
```

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-124](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]()

## ROCm Build System and Docker Flavors

The ROCm build framework is centered around `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, which defines a modular set of target build stages corresponding to different AMD GPU architectures and ROCm software development kit versions [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-124]().

### Build Stage Configuration

Key build arguments and environment variables control optional components during image construction:
- `GPU_ARCH`: Specifies the target graphics architecture, defaulting to `gfx950` [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:65-66]().
- `BUILD_AITER_ALL`: Controls the inclusion of the AITER operator library (`1` to enable) [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:74]().
- `BUILD_MOONCAKE`: Enables Mooncake transfer backend compilation (`1` to enable) [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:75]().
- `PIP_CONSTRAINT`: Enforces specific ROCm-compatible PyTorch constraints in newer flavors (such as `gfx942-rocm724`) to prevent accidental PyPI CUDA package overrides [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:105-106]().

| ROCm Stage Flavor | Key Configuration / Environment |
|---|---|
| `gfx942` | Uses `BASE_IMAGE_942`; enables AITER and Mooncake; disables VLLM and Triton compilation passes [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:70-76]() |
| `gfx942-rocm720` | Uses ROCm 7.2 PyTorch base; pins Triton commit `42270451990532c67e69d753fbd026f28fcc4840` [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:80-87]() |
| `gfx942-rocm724` | Uses Python 3.12 / torch 2.11 stack; sets `PIP_CONSTRAINT` and enables `HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1` to mitigate IPC memory leaks [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:91-111]() |

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:70-111]()

### ROCm Build Flavor Selection Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    INPUT["Docker Build Argument GPU_ARCH"] --> SELECT_STAGE["Select Docker Stage"]
    SELECT_STAGE -->|gfx942| STAGE_942["gfx942 Base"]
    SELECT_STAGE -->|gfx950| STAGE_950["gfx950 Base"]
    SELECT_STAGE -->|gfx942-rocm720| STAGE_720["ROCm 7.2 / PyTorch 2.9"]
    SELECT_STAGE -->|gfx942-rocm724| STAGE_724["ROCm 7.2.4 / PyTorch 2.11 / Python 3.12"]
    STAGE_942 --> CONFIG_FLAGS["Set BUILD_AITER_ALL=1, BUILD_MOONCAKE=1"]
    STAGE_950 --> CONFIG_FLAGS
    STAGE_720 --> CONFIG_FLAGS
    STAGE_724 --> CONFIG_FLAGS
```

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:70-124]()

## Platform-Specific Builds and Environment Management

Platform-specific configurations and environment variable resolutions are managed dynamically via runtime tools and build scripts. For instance, runtime checks supply late-bound platform determinations to configure backend defaults without importing torch at module initialization time. Similarly, CI scripts like `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` detect host and container architectures via runner hostnames and printenv configurations to deploy matching python distribution extras [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]().

Sources: [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:43-108]()

## Purpose and scope

This page describes the organization, modular structure, and selection patterns visible in `python/sglang/kernels`, with emphasis on attention, GEMM, MoE, elementwise, and diffusion kernels. It details the PyTorch binding architecture, the PEP 562 lazy-resolution mechanism, kernel metadata registration via `KernelSpec`, and numerical quality gates [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:1-46](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-26]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:1-46](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-26]()

---

## Kernel organization overview

Kernel packages under `python/sglang/kernels` organize implementations by operator domain and register kernel metadata for inventory and selection. The structure separates operator domains into distinct packages and directories:

```
python/sglang/kernels/
  ops/
    attention/   # Attention kernels, indexers, sparse prefill utilities
    gemm/        # Scaled matrix multiplication and fused GEMM operations
    moe/         # Mixture of experts fused gates and grouped GEMM
    diffusion/   # Diffusion and DiT transformer block fused operators
    activation/  # Elementwise activation fusions (SiLU, GLU, GELU)
    quantization/# FP8, NVFP4, INT8, AWQ quantization primitives
  registry.py    # register_kernel decorator and KernelSpec definitions
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:11-19](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:27-48]()

**Diagram: Kernel domains mapped to package entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Attention["Attention compute"] --> AttentionPackage["python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention"]
    AttentionPackage --> Decode["decode_attention_fwd"]
    AttentionPackage --> Prefill["context_attention_fwd"]
    AttentionPackage --> Extend["extend_attention_fwd"]
    GEMM["GEMM and fused GEMM"] --> GemmPackage["python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm"]
    GemmPackage --> ScaledMM["Fp8ScaledMMOp"]
    Diffusion["Diffusion fused operators"] --> DiffusionPackage["python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion"]
    DiffusionPackage --> Norm["norm"]
    DiffusionPackage --> Rope["rope"]
    DiffusionPackage --> Layout["layout"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-189](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:27-48]()

---

## Attention kernels and indexers

The attention package registers Triton and JIT kernels for decode, extend, and prefill modes, along with support operations for merging attention state, padding sequences, and constructing KV indices or page tables [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py:14-116]().

Functions like `extend_attention_fwd` and `decode_attention_fwd` handle prefix caching, window constraints, and block-level parallelism across varying head dimensions (`Lq`, `Lv`) and hardware architectures (Hopper, Ampere, Blackwell, and CDNA) [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py:69-164]().

**Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space for Attention Execution**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Req["Request Prefill or Extend Chunk"] --> Metadata["SeqLens and qo_indptr Tensor"]
    Metadata --> BlockSizeGetter["_get_block_sizes_for_extend_attention"]
    BlockSizeGetter --> TileConfig["BLOCK_M & BLOCK_N Tiling Configuration"]
    TileConfig --> TritonLauncher["extend_attention_fwd / decode_attention_fwd"]
    TritonLauncher --> OutputBuffer["Output Tensor o"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py:69-164](), [test/registered/attention/test_triton_attention_kernels.py:8-22]()

---

## GEMM and fused matrix operations

The GEMM package defines scaled matrix multiplication operations, supporting both Ahead-Of-Time (AOT) compiled kernels and native PyTorch fallbacks depending on runtime layout and hardware capabilities [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-72]().

Additional registrations use `KernelSpec` to associate operation names and backends with target implementations, including FP8 rowwise operations, NVFP4 GEMM/SwiGLU fusions, and model-specific epilogues [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-72]().

**Diagram: GEMM and quantized execution path**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Caller["GEMM Caller"] --> ConfigCheck["QuantizationConfig & Shape Check"]
    ConfigCheck -->| "FP8 / NVFP4" | FusedQuant["fused_packed_swiglu_fp8_rowwise"]
    ConfigCheck -->| "Standard" | Unquantized["apply_unquantized_linear"]
    FusedQuant --> TritonKernel["Triton / CUTLASS Backend"]
    Unquantized --> PyTorchOp["torch.nn.functional.linear"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-72](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:76-83]()

---

## MoE kernels and routing

Diffusion and multimodal MoE architectures utilize expert selection and routing domains (e.g., `diffusion.fused_packed_swiglu_fp8_rowwise`) to execute grouped convolutions and sparse routing computations efficiently across parallel worker ranks [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-53](). These kernels manage token dispatch, expert alignment, and hierarchical expert selection.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:47-53](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:35-48]()

---

## Elementwise and activation operations

The kernel library includes an `activation` domain containing JIT-backed and Triton-backed operators such as `diffusion.gelu_tanh_cat` (`fused_gelu_tanh_cat`) [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:73-77](). Fused normalization and modulation operations (e.g., RMSNorm, LayerNorm, and GroupNorm with scale/shift epilogues) are grouped alongside domain-specific activation kernels [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:78-113]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:73-113](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:27-44]()

---

## Diffusion and multimodal-generation kernels

The diffusion kernel package (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion`) provides fused operations for DiT transformer blocks, VAE encoders/decoders, and sequence-parallel plumbing [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-5]().

### Numerical contracts and quality policy

Diffusion generation requires strict numerical contracts due to multi-step denoising error amplification:
- **Bit-exact (`torch.equal`)**: Mounted unconditionally when reproducing exact eager reduction trees (verified via `BitExactFusionGate`) [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:52-61]().
- **Quality-gated (`lossless` / `high`)**: Enabled selectively based on user-facing quality switches (`--quality lossless`) to balance precision and performance [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx:11-36]().

Model wrappers such as FLUX (`_flux_norm_modulate`), Qwen-Image (`_qwen_norm_out`), and FLUX.2 (`_flux2_single_qk_rope`) perform runtime checks before dispatching to these fused paths [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:159-181](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py:122-181](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:123-165]().

**Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space for Diffusion Fused Dispatch**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ModelBlock["QwenImageTransformerBlock"] --> FacadeModule["sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion"]
    FacadeModule --> RegistrySPECS["_SPECS Metadata Registry"]
    RegistrySPECS --> GateController["BitExactFusionGate"]
    GateController -->| "Verified / Lossless" | FusedKernelImpl["fused_layernorm_modulate_raw"]
    GateController -->| "Mismatch / Exact" | EagerReference["AdaLayerNormContinuous Reference Chain"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:21-46](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:159-181](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py:122-181]()

---

## Python binding and kernel-selection architecture

The Python packages use `register_kernel` to record `KernelSpec` metadata containing operation names, backends, targets, and capability requirements [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:32-34](). Model implementations query these specs via facades and specialized predicate functions (`can_use_*`) to determine eligibility prior to launching kernels [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:82-105](). Resolution is lazy (PEP 562) to avoid forcing heavy dependencies like Triton, CUTLASS, or FlyDSL at import time [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:21-26]().

**Diagram: Python kernel metadata mapped to runtime entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    OperationName["diffusion.rmsnorm_scale_shift"] --> KernelSpec["_SPECS KernelSpec Entry"]
    KernelSpec --> Backend["KernelBackend.TRITON"]
    Backend --> TargetModule["norm.rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact"]
    TargetModule --> RuntimeLaunch["fused_rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:32-132]()

---

## Summary

The kernel packages organize implementations around operator domains, exposing them via lazy-loading facades, metadata registries, and quality-gated invocation wrappers. Attention modules integrate advanced indexers and Triton-based decode/extend kernels, while GEMM and diffusion libraries provide heavily optimized fused paths for cutting-edge LLMs and multimodal DiT architectures.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:21-46](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py:69-164](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:27-75]()

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the quantization-kernel implementations in SGLang (`sgl-kernel` and SRT layers), covering per-token and per-token-group FP8/INT8 quantization, scale formatting and layouts, DeepGEMM grouped-GEMM wrappers, compressed-tensors integration, and fused activation-quantization pathways [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:20-22](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-66](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:57-84]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:20-22](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-66](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:57-84]()

---

## Quantization Kernel Taxonomy

The per-token-group API accepts BF16, FP16, or FP32 input, and produces FP8 E4M3 or INT8 output. Supported group sizes include 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:20-22]().

| Area | Code entities | Role |
|---|---|---|
| JIT quantization entrypoint | `_per_token_group_quant_custom_op`, `_jit_module` | Selects and launches a JIT kernel according to dtype, group size, scale format, layout, and optional fusion/layout flags [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184]() |
| Quantization math and stores | `WeightTrait`, `ScaleStoreArgs` | Defines FP8/INT8 conversion behavior and scale-output address/layout handling [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-63](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:65-142]() |
| Fused activation quantization | `fuse_silu_and_mul`, `silu_and_mul_mode` | Allows the quantization kernel to fuse SiLU-and-multiply under supported combinations [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:43-56](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:108-120]() |
| DeepGEMM grouped GEMM | `grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked`, `grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_contig` | Wraps DeepGEMM FP8 grouped matrix multiplication, including masked and contiguous layouts [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:132-159]() |
| FP8 & Compressed Tensors Integration | `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8`, `apply_fp8_linear` | Manages compressed-tensors parameters and dispatches linear layers to Triton or DeepGEMM kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:51-59](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:57-84]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:20-22](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-142](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:132-159](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:51-59](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:57-84]()

### Natural-Language Concepts Mapped to Code Entities

**Diagram: Activation Quantization Dispatch**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Input["Input activations"]
        GroupQuant["Per-group quantization"]
        Scale["Scale output layout"]
        FusedAct["Optional fused SiLU and multiply"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        CustomOp["_per_token_group_quant_custom_op"]
        JIT["_jit_module"]
        Trait["WeightTrait"]
        Store["ScaleStoreArgs"]
        ActFlag["fuse_silu_and_mul"]
    end
    Input --> CustomOp
    GroupQuant --> CustomOp
    CustomOp --> JIT
    JIT --> Trait
    Scale --> Store
    CustomOp --> Store
    FusedAct --> ActFlag
    ActFlag --> JIT
```

The custom-op wrapper derives layout and kernel specialization inputs, then calls the selected JIT module; the device-side implementation provides quantization traits and scale stores [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-66](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:65-142]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-66](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:65-142]()

---

## FP8 Quantization and Scaled GEMM

### Per-Token and Group Quantization Entrypoints

`_jit_module` validates input/output dtypes and group size, constructs specialization arguments, and loads the `per_token_group_quant` JIT source from `gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82]().

`_per_token_group_quant_custom_op` infers scale layout, selects the specialization, and invokes the JIT module with either masked-token metadata, sorted-token metadata, or a flat input. It includes fallbacks for specific configurations such as `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184]().

For FP8 E4M3, the CUDA trait uses the dtype's maximum value for conversion; the INT8 trait clamps to `[-128, 127]` and casts to `int8` [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-63]().

### Scale Formats and Layouts

The host wrapper recognizes FP32 scale buffers and INT32-packed buffers. INT32-packed scales require `scale_ue8m0=True`; their alignment is determined by whether the number of groups is divisible by four [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:85-101]().

`ScaleStoreArgs::store` handles row-major and column-major addressing. In the packed column-major UE8M0 layout, four scale bytes share an INT32 unit; when the group count is not divisible by four, tail bytes are zero-filled [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:65-142]().

Correctness tests employ a PyTorch reference for FP8 and INT8 group quantization, verifying bit-exact results for UE8M0 paths and scaled accuracy for FP32-scale paths [test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py:1-88]().

### Fused Activation Quantization

The JIT specialization supports a dense mode when SiLU-and-multiply fusion is enabled for BF16 or FP16 input, FP8 output, group size 128, and a non-sorted layout [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:43-56]().

**Diagram: From Quantization API to Grouped GEMM**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["BF16 FP16 or FP32 activations"] --> Op["_per_token_group_quant_custom_op"]
    Op --> Select["_infer_scale_layout"]
    Select --> JIT["_jit_module"]
    JIT --> Kernel["per_token_group_quant.cuh"]
    Kernel --> Quantized["FP8 E4M3 or INT8 output"]
    Kernel --> Scales["FP32 or packed UE8M0 scales"]
    Quantized --> Wrapper["grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked"]
    Scales --> Wrapper
    Wrapper --> DeepGEMM["deep_gemm.fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked"]
```

The quantization wrapper builds a JIT module and launches the selected layout; the DeepGEMM entrypoint accepts FP8 tensors with scales and calls the masked grouped GEMM implementation [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:85-101](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:85-101](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]()

### DeepGEMM Grouped GEMM Wrappers

`grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked` derives dimensions from tensor inputs, runs sanity checks, ensures FP8 input/scale pairs reside on CUDA, and enters `deep_gemm_execution_hook` before calling `deep_gemm.fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked` [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]().

The contiguous variant returns early when `m == 0`; otherwise, it invokes `deep_gemm.m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_contiguous` [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:132-159]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:132-159](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:113-123]()

---

## NVFP4, MXFP4, and FP4 GEMM

SGLang provides utilities for MXFP4/NVFP4 formats via `MXFP4QuantizeUtil` and compressed-tensors schemes (e.g. `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE`, `CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4`) [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:37-114](). Hardware acceleration paths dispatch to specialized Blackwell or SM100 routines when available.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/__init__.py](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:37-114]()

---

## INT8 and AWQ Quantization Methods

The per-token-group CUDA implementation supports INT8 activation output via `WeightTrait<int8_t>`, clamping values to `[-128, 127]` [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:52-63](). Compressed tensors W8A8 INT8 schemes (`CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8`) handle static/dynamic channelwise or blockwise INT8 quantization [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_int8.py](). AWQ and GPTQ linear methods are integrated via standard model weight loaders and layer wrappers.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:52-63](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_int8.py]()

---

## Summary of Quantization Data Flow

The data path begins with activation tensors and output buffers. The custom-op wrapper selects a JIT specialization using dtype, group size, scale representation, layout, and fusion metadata. Quantized values and scales are written to memory, subsequently consumed by scaled GEMM or DeepGEMM grouped-GEMM layers [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]().

**Diagram: Quantization Data Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Activation tensor"] --> CustomOp["_per_token_group_quant_custom_op"]
    CustomOp --> JIT["_jit_module"]
    JIT --> QuantKernel["PerTokenGroupQuant flat masked or sorted kernel"]
    QuantKernel --> Q["Quantized tensor"]
    QuantKernel --> S["Scale tensor"]
    Q --> GEMM["grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked"]
    S --> GEMM
    GEMM --> Result["BF16 GEMM output"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:70-184](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]()

---

## Key Code Entities

| Code entity | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `_jit_module` | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py` | Loads and caches JIT specializations for quantization options [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-82]() |
| `_per_token_group_quant_custom_op` | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py` | Dispatches to JIT kernels or fallback paths [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:104-184]() |
| `WeightTrait` | `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh` | Implements FP8 and INT8 output conversion traits [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-63]() |
| `ScaleStoreArgs` | `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh` | Computes scale stores for supported layouts, including packed UE8M0 [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:65-142]() |
| `grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py` | Invokes DeepGEMM's masked FP8 grouped-GEMM entrypoint [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97]() |
| `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` | Configures compressed-tensors FP8 linear weights and parameters [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:51-141]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/per_token_group_quant.py:25-184](), [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh:36-142](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:48-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:51-141]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the Mixture of Experts (MoE) routing and expert-computation kernels implemented in the SGLang codebase: the Triton gate in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:14-18](), hierarchical expert selection, grouped GEMM implementations and wrappers in the MoE Triton runner [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), and alignment metadata consumed by GEMM kernels [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-164]().

The primary data path handles scoring expert logits, selecting top-k routes, organizing token-route pairs into expert-aligned blocks via alignment kernels, executing expert projections with fused activations, and finally combining the routed contributions.

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:14-18](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-164]()

---

## Kernel Categories and Data Flow

The MoE kernel architecture cleanly separates routing/gating operations from grouped expert computation. Triton router kernels (`_router_triton_kernel`) evaluate token scores, while wrapper operations like `inplace_fused_experts` coordinate activation, gating, and quantization settings [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:98-144](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210]().

| Category | Role | Key Code Entities |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Gate and Route Selection | Score experts, apply routing options, and select per-token routes | `_router_triton_kernel`, `_SCORING_FUNC_MAP` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:14-18](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:98-144]() |
| Token Alignment | Produce token-order and expert-block metadata for tiled GEMM operations | `moe_align_block_size`, `sorted_token_ids`, `expert_ids`, `num_tokens_post_padded` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-164]() |
| Expert Computation | Execute expert projections over aligned token blocks | `inplace_fused_experts`, `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`, `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:18-23](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-164]() |
| Activation and Reduction | Apply fused activation and MoE reduction operations selected by the runner | `act_and_mul_triton`, `moe_sum_reduce_triton` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:18-23]() |

### Data Flow: Runtime Names to Code Entities

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input[""logits_and_ids""] --> Gate[""moe_fused_gate""]
    Gate --> RouterKernel[""_router_triton_kernel""]
    RouterKernel --> Weights[""topk_weights""]
    RouterKernel --> IDs[""topk_ids""]
    Weights --> Experts[""inplace_fused_experts""]
    IDs --> Experts
    Experts --> Align[""moe_align_block_size""]
    Align --> Sorted[""sorted_token_ids""]
    Align --> BlockExperts[""expert_ids""]
    Sorted --> GEMM[""fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq""]
    BlockExperts --> GEMM
    GEMM --> Output[""hidden_states""]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:98-144](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:18-23](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:163-210](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-164]()

---

## Gating and Hierarchical Expert Selection (`moe_fused_gate`)

### Gate Kernels and Scoring

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py` maps scoring names (`sigmoid`, `sqrtsoftplus`, `softmax`) to compile-time integer identifiers specified in `_SCORING_FUNC_MAP` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:14-18](). The general `_router_triton_kernel` processes a row tile of router scores with experts along the reduction axis, parameterized by expert count `N`, output top-k `K`, and routed top-k `K_ROUTED` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:98-144]().

The router loads scores as `float32`, supporting shared expert biases, token-specific alternate biases, and input IDs used for selective alternative bias application [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-108](). Padding is managed via `num_token_non_padded_ptr` to exclude padded rows from active mask evaluations [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-108]().

### Hierarchical and Grouped Selection

The general router kernel exposes parameters such as `N_GROUP`, `TOPK_GROUP`, and `EXPERTS_PER_GROUP` as compile-time constants for hierarchical or grouped expert selection, where `N_GROUP == 1` represents ungrouped routing [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-167](). 

### Gate Path Call Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Inputs[""scores_ptr, bias_ptr, input_ids_ptr""] --> GateCall[""moe_fused_gate""]
    GateCall --> Kernel[""_router_triton_kernel""]
    Kernel --> Scoring[""_SCORING_FUNC_MAP""]
    Scoring --> GateOutput[""out_weights_ptr, out_indices_ptr""]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:14-18](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-167]()

---

## Grouped GEMM Kernels for Expert Computation (`fused_moe`)

### Wrapper and Computation Stages

`inplace_fused_experts` is a registered custom operation that accepts hidden states, expert weights (`w1`, `w2`), routing weights, indices, activation types, and quantization configurations, delegating to `fused_experts_impl` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:170-210]().

### Grouped GEMM Metadata and Tiling

`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` implements fused expert calculations where token input `A` is multiplied by stacked expert weights `B` to produce output `C` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:83-164](). Routing metadata such as `sorted_token_ids` and `expert_ids` ensure that tokens are ordered and blocked per expert for efficient tensor core utilization [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:83-164](). If an expert ID equals `-1` (indicating padding or nonlocal routes), the kernel writes zeros to the output cache via `write_zeros_to_output` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:63-80](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:182-205]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:170-210](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:63-80](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:83-205]()

---

## Token Alignment and Dispatch (`moe_align`)

The MoE execution pipeline uses alignment utilities (such as `moe_align_block_size`) to organize tokens into blocks matching hardware tile requirements [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51]().

### Alignment Metadata Consumed by GEMM

```mermaid
graph LR
    Routes[""topk_ids""] --> Align[""moe_align_block_size""]
    Align --> TokenOrder[""sorted_token_ids""]
    Align --> BlockExperts[""expert_ids""]
    Align --> Count[""num_tokens_post_padded""]
    TokenOrder --> Kernel[""fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq""]
    BlockExperts --> Kernel
    Count --> Kernel
    Kernel --> ExpertOutput[""C_output""]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:93-108](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:140-164](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:184-205]()

---

## Summary Table: MoE Fused Kernel Components

| Component | Location | Role |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `_router_triton_kernel` | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py` | Implements row-tiled scoring and selection with grouped expert support [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-167]() |
| `inplace_fused_experts` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py` | Fused expert execution wrapper supporting quantization and activation [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:170-210]() |
| `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py` | Grouped GEMM kernel consuming sorted token IDs and expert metadata [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:83-164]() |
| `moe_align_block_size` | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/moe_align_block_size.py` | Aligns token counts and sorts tokens by expert blocks [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py:22-167](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:43-51](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:170-210](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:83-164]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page details how SGLang integrates external kernel, communication, and model optimization libraries—such as CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, FlashInfer, Flash-Attention, AITER, cuDNN, and TRT-LLM—into its runtime execution and compilation pipelines. It covers backend dispatch mechanisms, quantization adapters, MoE runner integrations, JIT compilation workflows, and communication runtimes.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:55-80](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:112-217](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:53-70]()

---

## 1. Integration Architecture and Backend Dispatch

SGLang manages third-party libraries through pluggable backend abstractions, dispatcher factories, and quantization-aware dispatchers. Backend identifiers are defined in configuration classes like `MoeRunnerBackend` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:112-217](), and integrated via specialized execution runners (e.g., `FlashinferDispatcher` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py:143-146](), `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:50-71]()).

### Integration Flow: Natural Language to Code Entities

**Diagram 1: Mapping third-party library roles to runtime classes and modules**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        DL["DeepGEMM FP8 GEMMs"]
        FI["FlashInfer MoE / A2A"]
        CL["CUTLASS Fused MoE"]
    end

    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        FP8["python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py"]
        DeepGemmModule["python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py"]
        FlashinferDispatcher["FlashinferDispatcher python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py"]
        CutlassRunner["FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py"]
    end

    DL --> FP8
    DL --> DeepGemmModule
    FI --> FlashinferDispatcher
    CL --> CutlassRunner
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:31-80](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py:143-146](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:50-71]()

---

## 2. CUTLASS Integration

CUTLASS kernels are integrated primarily through FlashInfer's fused MoE wrappers, CuTe DSL custom extensions, and specialized quantization methods. Classes like `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:50-71]() define the input/weight structures (BF16, FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4) passed to `cutlass_fused_moe`.

### Fused MoE, CuTe DSL, and SwiGLU Parameters
- `materialize_swiglu_params_for_cutlass` constructs per-expert SwiGLU parameters (`alpha`, `beta`, `limit`) required by CUTLASS kernels when activation clamping or custom scaling is active [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:73-110]().
- Low-latency Blackwell SM10x GEMM kernels leverage `TgvGemmCuteExtKernel` within `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` to implement warp-specialized 7-warp configurations, managing TMA loads and `tcgen05.mma` instructions directly via CuTe DSL primitives [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:96-156]().
- In the build system, `python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt` uses `FetchContent_Declare` to fetch and compile CUTLASS [python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:51-57]() with explicit compiler flags such as `-DCUTLASS_ENABLE_TENSOR_CORE_MMA=1` [python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:118]() and target SM architectures [python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:114]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py:50-110](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:96-156](), [python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:51-118]()

---

## 3. DeepGEMM Integration

DeepGEMM provides high-performance FP8 and MXFP8 block-scaled matrix multiplication primitives, managed through compilation utilities and JIT execution hooks.

- **JIT Compilation and Warmup**: `compile_utils.py` handles JIT caching via `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`, multi-rank compile locks using `_local_rank_compile_lock`, and fast-warmup M-list sampling via `update_deep_gemm_config` [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:59-147]().
- **Execution Wrappers**: `entrypoint.py` provides typed operations such as `grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked` and TMA-aligned tensor safety checks via `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor` [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:24-97]().
- **Kernel Types**: Operations are categorized using the `DeepGemmKernelType` enumeration spanning contiguous and masked FP8/BF16 grouped GEMMs [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:113-121]().

### DeepGEMM Pipeline: Natural Language to Code Entities

**Diagram 2: Mapping DeepGEMM concepts to runtime compilation and execution modules**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        JITComp["DeepGEMM JIT Pre-Compilation & Caching"]
        GroupedGEMM["Masked & Contiguous Grouped FP8 GEMMs"]
        TMA["TMA-Aligned Scale Layouts"]
    end

    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        CompileUtils["compile_utils.py python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py"]
        Entrypoint["entrypoint.py python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py"]
        KernelEnum["DeepGemmKernelType python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py"]
    end

    JITComp --> CompileUtils
    GroupedGEMM --> Entrypoint
    GroupedGEMM --> KernelEnum
    TMA --> Entrypoint
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py:59-147](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py:24-97](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:31-80]()

---

## 4. FlashInfer Integration

FlashInfer supplies accelerated operations for Attention, MoE All-to-All communication (`MoeAlltoAll`), block-scaled quantization (`fp4_quantize`), and communication fusion [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp4_utils.py:21-85](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py:121-138]().

### Communication Fusion and Backend Resolution
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` implements unified allreduce fusion via `flashinfer.comm.allreduce_fusion` and `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` [python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py:121-138]().
- `_resolve_backend` selects between `trtllm`, `mnnvl`, and `cutedsl` depending on hardware architecture (e.g., SM90 vs. Blackwell SM100) and multi-node topology [python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py:47-99](). A specialized `_FixedTorchDistBackend` subclass wraps FlashInfer's `TorchDistBackend` to resolve broadcasting ranks using global process group ranks and prevent interference with CUDA graph capture via GLOO cpu groups [python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py:156-181]().

### FP4 Quantization and MegaMoE Autotuning
- `fp4_quantize` integrates FlashInfer's FP4 quantization kernel into SGLang's custom op framework (`register_custom_op_from_extern`) supporting dynamic scale swizzling and layout options [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp4_utils.py:21-85]().
- `MegaMoeTunedForward` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe_autotune.py` manages startup profiling and capacity-based workspace partitioning for FlashInfer MegaMoE kernels, caching tuning records via FlashInfer's `AutoTuner` [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe_autotune.py:47-156]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py:47-181](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp4_utils.py:21-85](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe_autotune.py:47-156]()

---

## 5. Flash-Attention and Attention Library Backends

SGLang maintains an attention backend architecture that dispatches to Flash-Attention (FA3, FA4), FlashInfer, Triton, SDPA, or platform-specific custom kernels based on model configuration and hardware capabilities [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:62-69]().
- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v3.py` loads FA3 kernels either via community wheel caches or the `sgl-fa3` package (`_load_fa3_kernels`), implementing support checks (`_is_fa3_supported`) for Hopper (SM90) and Ampere (SM80) architectures [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v3.py:31-100]().
- Sizing contracts during speculative decoding (e.g., DSpark, EAGLE) ensure query widths match backend expectations for cumulative query metadata in FA3 and FA4 [test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashattention_graph_metadata.py:75-81]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v3.py:31-100](), [test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashattention_graph_metadata.py:75-81](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:62-69]()

---

## 6. AITER and Hardware-Specific Backends

For AMD ROCm environments, SGLang integrates with AITER (AMD AI Engine Toolkit) for optimized FP8 linear and MoE operations, governed by environment flags such as `SGLANG_USE_AITER` and architecture-specific checks. Similarly, Ascend NPU environments utilize `torch_npu` fused attention primitives and Ascend-specific operator configs [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:33]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py:33](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:71-78]()
