## Purpose and Scope
This page documents CPU-side kernel implementations, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) acceleration, NUMA-aware thread binding, CPU graph compilation infrastructure (`CPUGraphRunner`), C++ CPU custom operators (`sgl_kernel`), and the JIT/AOT kernel selection system. It details how SGLang executes optimized transformer layers, attention mechanisms, normalization, activation, and MoE routing on CPU platforms.

---

## 1. CPU Kernel Implementations and Thread/NUMA Management

CPU execution relies on a specialized C++ extension library (`sgl_kernel`) exposed via PyTorch custom operators, combined with Intel AMX and vector instruction optimizations, as well as NUMA-aware subprocess and thread binding configuration.

### 1.1 Intel AMX Attention Backend (`IntelAMXAttnBackend`)

The `IntelAMXAttnBackend` class manages attention execution for CPU architectures supporting AMX tile instructions. It binds token pools, layer routers, and dispatches directly to C++ optimized kernels `decode_attention_cpu` and `extend_attention_cpu`.

Title: IntelAMXAttnBackend Initialization and Metadata Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Init["IntelAMXAttnBackend.__init__"] --> LoadPools["Capture req_to_token_pool and token_to_kv_pool"]
    LoadPools --> BindOps["Bind torch.ops.sgl_kernel.decode_attention_cpu and extend_attention_cpu"]
    Init --> Meta["init_forward_metadata"]
    Meta --> CheckMode["ForwardMode check: decode, extend, or target_verify"]
    CheckMode --> BuildExtend["_build_extend_metadata (speculative token tree masks)"]
    BuildExtend --> SWA["_init_swa_forward_metadata (Sliding Window Attention)"]
```
Sources: `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`

### 1.2 CPU Graph Runner and `torch.compile` Infrastructure

The `CPUGraphRunner` optimizes CPU execution overhead by leveraging PyTorch's `torch.compile` infrastructure [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:14-115]().

- **Model Patching**: Re-entrant context managers and monkey-patching of layer boundary classes (`cpu_graph_patch_boundary_classes`) prevent Dynamo global guard failures and graph breaks during capture and replay [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:182-187]().
- **Dynamic Dimension Bounds**: Uses sentinel limits like `_DYNAMIC_DIM_MAX` for marked dynamic dimensions [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:81-85]().

Title: CPU Graph Runner Execution and Patching Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Runner["CPUGraphRunner.forward"] --> Patch["cpu_graph_patch_boundary_classes"]
    Patch --> Dynamo["torch.compile / Dynamo Replay"]
    Dynamo --> CheckDynamic["Evaluate _DYNAMIC_DIM_MAX bounds"]
    CheckDynamic --> ExecModel["Execute Compiled CPU Subgraph"]
```
Sources: `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py`

### 1.3 NUMA Affinity and Subprocess Configuration

In multi-socket Xeon environments (such as Sapphire Rapids SPR and Granite Rapids GNR CI runners), test suites partition execution across socket-pinned containers and NUMA nodes. Sizing of the KV cache pool respects container memory limits to prevent host RAM exhaustion.

The NUMA utils module provides `configure_subprocess` and `init_threads_binding` to bind processes and threads to correct NUMA nodes and physical cores [python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py:31-84](), [test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py:94-134]().

Title: NUMA Subprocess Configuration Flow (`configure_subprocess`)
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ConfigSub["configure_subprocess"] --> CheckEnv["Check SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2"]
    CheckEnv --> GetNode["get_numa_node_if_available"]
    GetNode --> NumactlArgs["_numactl_cpu_mem_args"]
    NumactlArgs --> Probe["_probe_numactl_args"]
    Probe --> Executable["_create_numactl_executable"]
    Executable --> Spawn["multiprocessing.spawn.set_executable"]
```
Sources: `python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py`, `.github/workflows/pr-test-xeon.yml`, `test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py`

---

## 2. C++ CPU Extension Operators and Layer-Level Dispatch

The C++ extension (`torch_extension_cpu.cpp`) implements a broad suite of custom operators optimized for CPU vector units.

### 2.1 Normalization, Activation, and RoPE CPU Kernels

CPU kernels are registered for various normalization, activation, and positional embedding layers:
- **Normalization**: `rmsnorm_cpu`, `gemma_rmsnorm_cpu`, `gemma3_rmsnorm_cpu`, `gemma4_rmsnorm_cpu`, `layernorm_cpu`, `fused_add_rmsnorm_cpu`, `fused_dual_residual_rmsnorm_cpu` [python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp:36-80]().
- **Activations**: `silu_and_mul_cpu`, `gelu_and_mul_cpu`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul_cpu`, `fused_sigmoid_mul_cpu` [python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp:23-32]().
- **Positional Embeddings**: `rotary_embedding_cpu`, `multimodal_rotary_embedding_cpu`, `fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu` [python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp:93-102]().

Title: Dispatch from Python Frontend to C++ CPU Extension Operators (`torch_extension_cpu.cpp`)
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TensorIn["Input Tensor x"] --> NormDispatch["torch.ops.sgl_kernel.rmsnorm_cpu"]
    TensorIn --> ActDispatch["torch.ops.sgl_kernel.silu_and_mul_cpu"]
    TensorIn --> RopeDispatch["torch.ops.sgl_kernel.multimodal_rotary_embedding_cpu"]
    NormDispatch --> CppNorm["rmsnorm_cpu"]
    ActDispatch --> CppAct["silu_and_mul_cpu"]
    RopeDispatch --> CppRope["multimodal_rotary_embedding_cpu"]
```

## 3. JIT Kernel Infrastructure and Platform Dispatch

Kernel selection utilizes a registry mapping operation names to backend specifications (`KernelSpec`) [python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py:7-16]().

### 3.1 Kernel Registry and `KernelSpec` Records

Operations register multiple backends (AOT, JIT, Torch native, FlashInfer) with conditional hardware requirements.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

```
Sources: `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py`

### 3.2 JIT Compilation and Operator Dispatch Logic

The selection framework evaluates platform information and capability constraints before resolving execution paths. Platform-specific execution environments maintain persistent, size-capped JIT and inductor compilation caches partitioned by device affinity to prevent stale artifact reuse [docker/xeon.Dockerfile:50-55]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page gives a high-level map of speculative decoding in SGLang: how draft proposals relate to target-model verification, which implementation families are represented in the codebase, and where scheduling and execution fit. As a parent page, it provides a high-level overview of EAGLE, N-gram, DFlash, DSpark, and Frozen-KV MTP implementations, leaving deep technical details to the respective child pages.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:92-114]()

## Architecture and Key Components

At a high level, a speculative worker proposes candidate tokens; the target model evaluates proposals, and the runtime represents proposal and verification inputs using algorithm-specific data structures. For EAGLE, the visible code includes `EagleDraftWorker`, `EagleDraftInput`, and `EagleVerifyInput` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42](). The N-gram worker (`NGRAMWorker`) sources its candidates from a corpus rather than a separate draft model.

**Diagram: Speculative-decoding concepts mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    CandidateProposal["CandidateProposal"] --> EagleWorker["EagleDraftWorker"]
    EagleWorker --> DraftInput["EagleDraftInput"]
    DraftInput --> VerifyInput["EagleVerifyInput"]
    VerifyInput --> TargetVerify["TargetModelVerification"]
    NgramProposal["CorpusProposal"] --> NgramWorker["NGRAMWorker"]
    NgramWorker --> NgramInput["NgramVerifyInput"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42]()

The code separates algorithm-specific workers and inputs from execution infrastructure. For example, EAGLE draft graph runners (`EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner`, `EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner`) subclass `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`, connecting speculative execution directly to the model executor runtime [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-102](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]().

**Diagram: Worker and execution code entities**

```mermaid
graph TB
    SpecWorker["BaseSpecWorker"] --> EAGLE["EagleDraftWorker"]
    SpecWorker --> NGRAM["NGRAMWorker"]
    SpecWorker --> MultiLayerEAGLE["MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker"]
    EAGLE --> DraftRunner["EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner"]
    EAGLE --> ExtendRunner["EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner"]
    DraftRunner --> DecodeRunner["DecodeCudaGraphRunner"]
    ExtendRunner --> DecodeRunner
    NGRAM --> Corpus["NgramCorpus"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-182](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-130](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-102](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]()

## Supported Algorithms

The following table identifies implementation families visible in the codebase:

| Family | High-level role | Code pointer |
|---|---|---|
| `EAGLE` | Draft-worker path with EAGLE-specific proposal and verification input structures. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42]() |
| Multi-layer EAGLE | Multi-layer draft worker with its own draft runner list and MTP steps. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-130](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:164-184]() |
| `NGRAM` | Candidate proposals sourced from an N-gram corpus rather than a draft model. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:92-114]() |
| DFlash | Speculative worker implementation with DFlash-specific utilities and inputs. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:47-63]() |
| DSpark | Referenced in acceptance-sampling imports; works with block verification. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:47-63]() |
| Frozen-KV MTP | Worker where the draft reads target KV read-only without owning a separate KV pool. | [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:47-63]() |

Algorithm names and draft configuration are handled by parameter resolution utilities, normalizing algorithm settings and alias handling.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-184](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:47-63]()

## EAGLE Algorithm and Architecture

EAGLE's worker is constructed with a target `TpModelWorker` and reads speculative settings such as top-k, step count, and draft-token count [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](). Its verification input carries draft tokens, positions, tree-retrieval metadata, and related shape information [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42](). The multi-layer worker is a separate implementation that configures a draft worker for multi-layer token generation [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-130]().

For details on EAGLE/EAGLE2/EAGLE3 architecture, draft-model construction, tree verification, and adaptive speculative decoding, see [EAGLE Algorithm and Architecture](#12.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-198](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-130]()

## Draft and Verification Flow

The common conceptual path is proposal followed by target verification, but the proposal source and input representation vary by algorithm [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-42](). EAGLE defines `EagleDraftInput` and `EagleVerifyInput` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-171](), while alternative workers reuse verify structures while managing state differently.

For details on draft token generation, tree construction, target verification, and alternative workers such as DFlash, DSpark, frozen-KV MTP, and standalone, see [Draft and Verification Flow](#12.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:18-171]()

## Integration with Scheduling

Speculative worker interfaces use runtime batch types such as `ScheduleBatch` and return generation-batch results [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:33-36](). The N-gram worker also reads scheduling configurations and maintains corpus state associated with decode batches [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:92-114]().

For details on scheduler and batch integration, including the N-gram worker and spec registry, see [Integration with Scheduling](#12.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:33-36](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:92-114]()

## Memory Management

Speculative execution uses cache-location and batch metadata alongside proposal inputs. The EAGLE verification input can carry cache allocation details [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:37-42](); workers obtain the target worker's request-to-token pool and KV-pool allocator after allocation occurs [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:137-149]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:37-42](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:137-149]()

## CUDA Graph Optimization

EAGLE has dedicated draft and draft-extend graph runners (`EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner`, `EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner`), both built on the `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` infrastructure [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-102](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24](). These runners handle fixed-shape capture and fast-path replay for speculative steps.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-102](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page explains the EAGLE speculative-decoding implementation in SGLang: how draft workers and target workers cooperate, how proposals are represented and verified as a tree, how multi-layer EAGLE (MTP) differs from the single-worker path, and where adaptive speculative runtime state and CUDA graph runners fit [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-201]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-178]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-60]().

## Architecture Overview

EAGLE’s runtime is organized around a target model worker (`TpModelWorker`) and a speculative draft worker (`EagleDraftWorker` or `MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker`). The worker reads speculative settings from runtime context and constructs draft execution support. `EagleVerifyInput` carries proposed tokens, attention masks, positions, and tree traversal metadata used during target verification [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-201]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-178]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-60]().

### EAGLE Family and Configuration

The worker reads `speculative_eagle_topk`, `speculative_num_steps`, `speculative_num_draft_tokens`, and `speculative_algorithm` from the speculative runtime context. The single-layer worker asserts `topk == 1` when rejection sampling is enabled. The multi-layer worker also reads rejection-sampling settings and requires `speculative_num_draft_tokens == speculative_num_steps + 1` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:199-201]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:136-151]().

| Setting or type | Role visible in the implementation |
|---|---|
| `speculative_eagle_topk` | Draft branching width; used as `topk` by the workers [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:200-201](). |
| `speculative_num_steps` | Number of configured speculative steps [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:137-137](). |
| `speculative_num_draft_tokens` | Draft-token width used by worker setup and input sizing [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:138-138](). |
| `speculative_algorithm` | Parsed into `SpeculativeAlgorithm` by each EAGLE worker [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:107-107]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:149-151](). |
| `speculative_use_rejection_sampling` | Enables rejection-sampling behavior; the single-layer worker constrains it to `topk == 1` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:201-201]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:143-148](). |
| `EagleVerifyInput` | Holds tree verification tensors and derives default per-request verification width from `draft_token_num` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-51](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:199-201]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:136-151]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-51]()

## Core Components and Data Flow

### `EagleDraftWorker`

`EagleDraftWorker` receives `ServerArgs`, device/communication parameters, and a target `TpModelWorker`. It stores those references, reads the runtime device and speculative settings, converts the configured algorithm to `SpeculativeAlgorithm`, and rebuilds top-k-one chain buffers [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-201]().

The worker file imports shared EAGLE preparation and verification functions (`prepare_for_draft`, `prepare_for_draft_extend`, `build_eagle_verify_input`, and `run_eagle_verify`) [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:97-105]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:97-105]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:176-201]()

### Draft and Verification Input Structures

`EagleDraftInput` includes top-k probabilities and token indices, optional draft proposal probabilities, optional hidden states, and a capture-hidden mode [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:171-175]().

`EagleVerifyInput` includes `draft_token`, `custom_mask`, token `positions`, tree retrieval arrays, step and top-k metadata, sequence-length data, and optional proposal distributions and cache-location planning data [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-41](). Its `__post_init__` sets the input type to `EAGLE_VERIFY`, fills a missing `num_tokens_per_req` from `draft_token_num`, and sets the per-request log-probability width to that draft-token count. `max_tree_depth` returns `spec_steps + 1`; `tree_topk` returns `topk` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:46-63]().

| Structure | Relevant fields | Purpose indicated by code |
|---|---|---|
| `EagleDraftInput` | `topk_p`, `topk_index`, `draft_probs`, `hidden_states`, `capture_hidden_mode` | Carries draft candidates, optional distributions, and optional hidden-state input [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:171-175](). |
| `EagleVerifyInput` | `draft_token`, `custom_mask`, `positions`, `retrieve_index`, `retrieve_next_token`, `retrieve_next_sibling`, `retrieve_cum_len` | Carries the draft tree and verification metadata [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-41](). |
| `EagleVerifyInput` sizing | `num_tokens_per_req`, `num_tokens_for_logprob_per_req`, `max_tree_depth`, `tree_topk` | Supplies verification-width and tree-shape information [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:46-63](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-63]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:171-175]()

## Draft Model and Tree Generation

### Draft Execution

`EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner` subclasses `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`. Its constructor selects the model runner from the EAGLE worker, sets the draft attention backend and capture mode, obtains capture batch sizes, and resolves a static capture width for the `draft_decode` phase [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-171]().

`EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` subclasses `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` for `ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`, resolving its static capture width for the `draft_extend` phase and keeping draft-extend-specific buffers [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-168]().

### Draft Results and Tree Assembly

`organize_draft_results` concatenates per-step scores and tokens, selects highest-scoring candidates, sorts selected indices, gathers corresponding tokens, and returns parent information, selected indices, and draft tokens [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py:162-185]().

`per_step_draft_out_cache_loc` checks cache-location buffer dimensions and reshapes/permutes it into per-step slices [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py:86-110]().

```mermaid
    end
```

## Verification and Acceptance

### Tree-Based Verification Input

`EagleVerifyInput` represents verification as a batch of draft tokens plus metadata for tree-shaped attention and path recovery (`retrieve_index`, `retrieve_next_token`, `retrieve_next_sibling`, `retrieve_cum_len`, `custom_mask`, and `positions`) [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-41]().

`generate_attn_arg_prefill` widens paged sequence lengths by `draft_token_num`, constructs cumulative KV lengths and query indptr values, allocates packed KV indices, and populates indices using `runner_ids.pack_read_stream` [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:91-167]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:16-41]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info.py:91-167]()

## CUDA Graph Optimizations

`DecodeCudaGraphRunner` supports decode, target verification, and DLLM extend under a configurable backend (`full`, `breakable`, or `tc_piecewise`) [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24](). EAGLE draft and draft-extend runners reuse this capture framework while overriding buffers and graph execution steps [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-101]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:14-24]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py:102-116]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:92-101]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:133-149]()

## Multi-Layer EAGLE (MTP)

`MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker` receives a target `TpModelWorker`, retains model configuration, and requires `speculative_num_draft_tokens == speculative_num_steps + 1`. It instantiates a draft `TpModelWorker` under draft-specific contexts [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-178]().

`MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` coordinates multi-layer draft-extend execution with shared persistent input buffers (`MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendInputBuffers`) [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:103-131]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:133-149]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py:114-178]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:103-131]() [python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:133-149]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the implementation of speculative decoding flows in SGLang, covering draft token generation, verification tree building, target model verification, and alternative worker architectures such as DFlash, DSpark, frozen-KV MTP, and standalone workers. It explains how candidate tokens are proposed by draft mechanisms (e.g., EAGLE, DFlash, DSpark), validated against the target model using specialized verification kernels and attention masks, and integrated back into the standard sequence generation and scheduling loops [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:155-195](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:88-126]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:155-195](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:88-126]()

---

## Architectural Position

A speculative worker wraps or coordinates alongside a target `TpModelWorker`. EAGLE-family workers initialize and manage model runners for both draft and target execution, while alternative workers like DFlash borrow the target's `lm_head` and layers or execute via specialized pipeline components [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181]().

The following diagram maps the logical request and generation states in Natural Language Space to their concrete implementations in Code Entity Space.

Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space (Speculative Workers)
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Prompt["Prompt and Decode Context"]
        Response["Accepted Output Tokens"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        TargetWorker["TpModelWorker"]
        DFlashWorker["DFlashWorkerV2"]
        DSparkWorker["DSparkWorkerV2"]
        VerifyInput["DFlashDraftInputV2"]
    end

    Prompt --> TargetWorker
    TargetWorker --> DFlashWorker
    TargetWorker --> DSparkWorker
    DFlashWorker --> VerifyInput
    DSparkWorker --> VerifyInput
    VerifyInput --> TargetWorker
    TargetWorker --> Response
```

Alternative workers like `DFlashWorkerV2` and `DSparkWorkerV2` manage candidate generation cycles, while structures like `DFlashDraftInputV2` handle data packing for verification [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:99-111](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:164-192]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:99-111](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:164-192]()

## Configuration and Algorithm Resolution

Speculative execution parameters are processed through `handle_speculative_decoding` and `_resolve_speculative_algorithm_alias`, which resolve algorithm aliases and validate hardware capabilities [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:88-167](). For instance, `NEXTN` aliases to `EAGLE`, while Gemma 4 assistant architectures automatically promote `NEXTN` or `EAGLE` to `FROZEN_KV_MTP` [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:119-126]().

| Setting or Concept | Role Evidenced by Implementation |
|---|---|
| `speculative_algorithm` | Selects the active draft and verification strategy (`EAGLE`, `DFLASH`, `DSPARK`, `FROZEN_KV_MTP`) [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:148-153](). |
| `speculative_use_block_verification` | Enables block-wise verification modes for EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py:186-191](). |

```mermaid
        DSpark["DSparkWorkerV2"]
    end

    Hook --> Alias

```

## Core Data Structures and Transitions

The data pipeline transitions between draft proposal structures and target verification objects:
* `DFlashDraftInputV2`: Encapsulates draft proposal state, bonus tokens, and new sequence lengths for DFlash and DSpark execution [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_info_v2.py]() (see also references in [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:99-111]()).
* `DFlashVerifyInput`: Carries verification-related inputs and adjustments for target models [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_info.py:98-98]().

Diagram: Draft-to-Verification Data Transition
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DraftOutput["Draft Proposals and Scores"]
    Organize["make_next_draft_input"]
    BuildTree["VerifyWindow"]
    VerifyInput["DFlashDraftInputV2"]
    Verify["TargetVerifyExecutor"]

    DraftOutput --> Organize
    Organize --> BuildTree
    BuildTree --> VerifyInput
    VerifyInput --> Verify
```

`make_next_draft_input` processes proposal tensors into flat token sequences and sequence length structures [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py:116-121]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_info_v2.py](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_info.py:98-98](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py:116-121]()

---

## Draft Token Generation and Tree Building

Draft generation occurs iteratively or via specialized neural heads:
1. **Proposal Projections**: Workers generate draft hidden states across multiple steps, evaluating candidate logits using either a dedicated draft model or target head sharing [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:55-84]().
2. **Markov Walks and Samplers**: `DsparkDraftSampler` and `MarkovWalker` handle fast step-by-step token sampling with temperature adjustments and greedy masks [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft_sampler.py:38-141]().
3. **Tree and Window Construction**: Components like `DSparkVerifyPlanner` and `VerifyWindow` assemble candidate tokens into a verification layout, producing custom attention structures that allow the target model to verify all candidate paths efficiently [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_planner.py:61-68]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:55-84](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft_sampler.py:38-141](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_planner.py:61-68]()

---

## Target Model Verification and Sampling

Target verification evaluates the proposal tree in parallel:
* The target model executes forward passes over the ragged verification batch using specialized verification executors (`TargetVerifyExecutor`) [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py:137-178]().
* Verification sampling and rejection kernels (`blockwise_rejection`, `accept_sampling`) compare target and draft probabilities to accept or reject candidate tokens [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py:11-38]().
* Accepted tokens and bonus tokens are committed to the KV cache, and state variables are updated for the next generation step [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py:179-184]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py:11-184]()

---

## Alternative Workers: DFlash and DSpark

SGLang supports several alternative speculative architectures optimized for specific hardware and model topologies:
* **DFlash**: Implemented via `DFlashWorkerV2`, DFlash performs capture-safe greedy argmax and candidate generation over the target `lm_head` weights without requiring a separate draft model instance [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181]().
* **DSpark**: Implemented via `DSparkWorkerV2`, DSpark coordinates a multi-stage architecture comprising `DraftBlockProposer`, `DSparkVerifyPlanner`, `TargetVerifyExecutor`, `DsparkVerifyEpilogue`, and `TargetHiddenKvInjector`. Non-last pipeline-parallel stages execute target-only workloads [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:55-84](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:155-192]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:137-181](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:55-84](), [python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:155-192]()

---

## End-to-End Entity Map

The end-to-end execution flow connects scheduling batches, draft workers, tree assembly, and target verification runners.

## Purpose and Scope

This page explains the code-visible boundary between speculative algorithms, scheduler batches, and overlap input resolution. It covers algorithm selection through `SpeculativeAlgorithm`, N-gram-specific sequence-length requirements, the `FutureMap` input path, prebuilt batches used by disaggregated decode, and the plugin-facing `CustomSpecAlgo` interface. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-65]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:113-154]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-29]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-55]`

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-65]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51,113-154]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-29]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-55]`

## Speculative Algorithm Registry and Configuration

The `spec` configuration namespace exposes `speculative_algorithm` as an optional string; its documented built-ins include `EAGLE`, `EAGLE3`, `NEXTN`, `STANDALONE`, `NGRAM`, `DFLASH`, `DSPARK`, and `UNO`. `[python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/spec.py:24-35]`

`SpeculativeAlgorithm.from_string()` maps `None` to `NONE`, resolves built-in enum names case-insensitively, maps reserved alias `NEXTN` to `EAGLE`, and otherwise looks up a plugin algorithm. Unknown names raise `ValueError`. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-65]`

Built-in algorithms and registered plugins share capability predicates such as `is_ngram()`, `supports_mixed_chunk()`, and `supports_grammar_overlap()`. These predicates let callers query algorithm behavior through a common interface rather than branching on the enum versus plugin type. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:93-100]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:132-172]`

`SpeculativeAlgorithm.register()` is the plugin-facing decorator. It delegates registration to the registry implementation and accepts options including `supports_overlap`, a server-argument validator, and a `CustomSpecAlgo` subclass. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:67-91]`

`CustomSpecAlgo` stores the plugin name, factory, overlap capability, and optional validator. Its default capability methods are conservative: it identifies itself as speculative, but does not claim built-in algorithm features. Its `create_worker()` checks the resolved overlap configuration and rejects an algorithm that does not support overlap when overlap scheduling is enabled. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-55]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:60-116]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:134-152]`

## Scheduler Integration and Overlap Dataflow

With overlap enabled, `resolve_forward_inputs(batch, future_map)` materializes the batch’s input tokens at forward entry. For prefill, it copies `prefill_input_ids_cpu` to the batch device. For a mixed batch, it gathers decode tokens from `future_map.output_tokens_buf` using `mix_running_indices` and concatenates them with the prefill tokens. For ordinary decode with no pre-supplied `input_ids`, it gathers from the same buffer using `req_pool_indices`. `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:113-148]`

When overlap is enabled and the batch uses a speculative algorithm, `resolve_forward_inputs()` also calls `future_map._resolve_spec_extras(batch)`. The code comments distinguish this overlap relay path from the synchronous non-overlap V2 path, which installs `next_draft_input` directly. `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:150-154]`

The CPU sequence-length mirror has an explicit scheduling dependency: `decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens()` returns true when two-batch overlap is enabled, because that path reads the mirror to split a batch. It also forces the mirror for N-gram because N-gram’s `USE_FULL_MASK` verification path uses per-request CPU sequence lengths to size its tree mask, regardless of attention backend preference. Otherwise, the decision is based on the configured attention backends’ `needs_cpu_seq_lens` declarations; an undeclared flag defaults to true. `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51]`


## Request Initialization, KV Bookkeeping, and Ownership Contracts

This integration path exposes specific batch fields used to prepare and relay inputs; the available implementation excerpts do not establish the broader KV ownership fields or commit rules described in some scheduler designs. In particular, this page does not assign ownership to fields such as `kv_committed_len` or `kv_allocated_len`. `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:113-154]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-109]`

For disaggregated prebuilt batches, `prepare_for_prebuilt()` sets `forward_mode` to `PREBUILT`, builds sequence-length and request-pool metadata, gathers output-cache locations for each request’s extend range, and creates `SamplingBatchInfo`. Its comments specify that a prebuilt batch does not enter a model forward to process the transferred prompt and does not copy every transferred prompt to the GPU only to discard it. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-29]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:31-109]`

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:113-154]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-109]`

## N-gram and Specialized Worker Integration

### N-gram Worker

N-gram is represented by the `NGRAM` built-in algorithm and is detected through `SpeculativeAlgorithm.is_ngram()`. Its scheduling-specific requirement visible here is the CPU sequence-length mirror: `decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens()` forces that mirror for N-gram’s `USE_FULL_MASK` verification path, even if an attention backend opts out. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-48]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:132-134]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51]`

The provided implementation excerpts do not show the `NGRAMWorker` definition or the structure and relay construction of `NgramVerifyInput`. Therefore, worker internals and N-gram relay payload fields are not specified here. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:22-29]`

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:22-29,32-48,132-134]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51]`

### Other Speculative Worker Families (DFlash, DSPark, and EAGLE)

`SpeculativeAlgorithm` exposes capability checks that affect scheduling and batch compatibility. For example, EAGLE-family algorithms, DFLASH, and DSPARK report support for mixed-chunk prefill; N-gram is excluded because its overlap relay does not provide the output-token buffer that mixed-input resolution reads. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:147-158]`

The same capability interface distinguishes algorithms that support ragged verification, grammar overlap, draft KV, and draft hidden-state transfer. The built-in predicates are algorithm-specific; `CustomSpecAlgo` defaults generally do not opt into these capabilities. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:160-183]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:72-116]`

For disaggregated prebuilt batches, `process_prebuilt()` collects each request’s last output token, calls `spec_algorithm.build_disagg_draft_input()`, and installs the result as `spec_info` when one is returned. If the algorithm returns no speculative input, it stashes the last token in `FutureMap` so the first decode can resolve it through the normal forward-input path. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:111-156]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:164-175]`

For EAGLE disaggregation, `build_eagle_disagg_draft_input()` creates `EagleDraftInput` from transferred top-k probabilities, token indices, hidden states, and last-token bonus inputs. In overlap mode it publishes the request indices and sequence lengths to the future map and stashes a relay payload derived from the draft input. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_disaggregation.py:50-78]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_disaggregation.py:124-147]`

### Speculative Feature Flags and Worker Behavior

The scheduler-facing capability methods express constraints without requiring generic scheduling code to know every worker implementation. Examples include `supports_mixed_chunk()`, `supports_ragged_verify()`, `supports_grammar_overlap()`, `has_draft_kv()`, and `carries_draft_hidden_states()`. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:147-183]`

For plugins, `CustomSpecAlgo` provides default implementations for these queries. A plugin that needs built-in-specific scheduler or model-runner branches can supply a subclass and override the relevant `is_*()` or `supports_*()` methods. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-42]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:60-116]`

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:147-183]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-42,60-116]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:111-156]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_disaggregation.py:50-78,124-147]`

## Batch Forward Modes and Caching Integration

`ScheduleBatchDisaggregationDecodeMixin.prepare_for_prebuilt()` prepares metadata for a `PREBUILT` batch without running a model forward over the transferred prompt. It sets request indices, sequence lengths, cache locations, extend metadata, multimodal inputs, and sampling information. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-29]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:31-109]`

`process_prebuilt()` then handles the per-request last output token, checkpoints the KV cache, updates grammar state when present, and builds algorithm-specific disaggregated draft input. A non-speculative result is routed through `FutureMap.stash()` instead. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:111-156]`

The available excerpts do not show general scheduler batch formation, `ForwardBatch` construction, or radix-cache prefix matching. The flow below is limited to the documented prebuilt-batch and speculative-input boundary. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-156]`

# Summary

Speculative scheduling integration is exposed through a shared algorithm interface, overlap-aware input resolution, and batch-specific hooks. `SpeculativeAlgorithm` resolves built-ins and plugins and provides capability predicates; `CustomSpecAlgo` supplies the plugin contract and worker factory checks. `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-91]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-55,134-152]`

For overlap execution, `resolve_forward_inputs()` gathers decode tokens from `FutureMap` or stages prefill inputs, and resolves speculative extras when appropriate. N-gram additionally forces publication of CPU sequence lengths for its full-mask verification path. `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51,113-154]`

For disaggregated decode, prebuilt batch preparation establishes batch metadata, while `process_prebuilt()` constructs algorithm-specific draft input or stashes a non-speculative last token for the first decode step. `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-109]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:111-156]`

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_info.py:32-91]`, `[python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_registry.py:26-55,134-152]`, `[python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py:26-51,113-154]`, `[python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py:22-109,111-156]`

## Purpose and scope

SGLang exposes multiple user-facing interfaces for model serving across programmatic Python applications, HTTP/OpenAI-compatible clients (including chat, completions, and `/v1/responses` endpoints), gRPC clients, Anthropic/Ollama compatibility layers, and chat-oriented frontends. This parent page provides a high-level overview of these entry points and maps them to their underlying serving, protocol, and formatting components. Detailed method signatures, parameter specifications, and wire formats are documented in the respective child pages.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:50-87](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-38](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]()

## Interface overview

The SGLang runtime (SRT) architecture organizes its external interfaces by communication channel. The Python Engine serves embedded applications, FastAPI powers the HTTP and OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints, and a Rust-backed gRPC server via PyO3 handles typed and pass-through RPCs. 

### Interface-to-code map

| User-facing Area | Code Entity | Role / File Location |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP FastAPI Server | `FastAPI` app | Implements REST routes and middleware |
| OpenAI Chat Serving | `OpenAIServingChat` | Handles chat completion routes and request translation [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:50-87]() |
| OpenAI Completion Serving | `OpenAIServingCompletion` | Converts text completion requests into `GenerateReqInput` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:49-75]() |
| OpenAI Responses Serving | `OpenAIServingResponses` | Handles `/v1/responses` requests and structured tool call pipelines [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]() |
| Python-gRPC Bridge | `RuntimeHandle` | Exposes synchronous methods called by Rust gRPC via PyO3 |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:50-87](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:49-75](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]()

## Python Engine API

The Python Engine API provides a direct programmatic interface to the SGLang runtime for embedded workflows, automated testing, and custom orchestration scripts. It wraps process managers, tokenization pipelines, and model execution loops into a unified class interface. 

For full documentation on the `Engine` class, `generate` and `async_generate` methods, session management, and weight update APIs, see [Python Engine API](#13.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_base.py:27-38]()

## HTTP Server and OpenAI-Compatible API

The HTTP server is built on FastAPI and uvicorn, exposing a comprehensive set of REST endpoints mirroring the OpenAI API specification (including `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, and `/v1/responses`), alongside extensions for Anthropic and Ollama compatibility. It manages request routing, JSON validation, streaming response serialization via `StreamingResponse`, and metrics middleware.

For detailed endpoint documentation, request/response formats, and third-party compatibility layers, see [HTTP Server and OpenAI-Compatible API](#13.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-38](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_base.py:79-142](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]()

## Chat Templates and Conversation Formatting

SGLang includes a robust chat template and formatting engine managed by model-specific encoding adapters and prompt segment renderers [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-30](). It automatically detects model metadata or uses explicit user configurations to apply correct chat templates (`tokenizer.apply_chat_template`), parsing multi-turn conversations and formatting system prompts.

For details on the template system, model-specific overrides, and conversation formatting rules, see [Chat Templates and Conversation Formatting](#13.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-59]()

## gRPC Server Interface

SGLang features a high-performance Rust-based gRPC frontend (`sglang-grpc`) integrated via PyO3. The service definitions are established via Protocol Buffers (`sglang.proto`), supporting both SGLang-native typed RPCs and OpenAI-compatible JSON pass-through RPCs. 

For detailed protobuf specifications, the gRPC request manager, and the Rust frontend pipeline, see [gRPC Server Interface](#13.4).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-38]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the Python entry point for the SGLang Runtime (SRT): `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:14-18](). It covers the `Engine` class, generation and asynchronous generation methods, session management mechanisms, and weight update APIs.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:14-18]()

---

## 1. Overview of the `Engine` Class and Architecture

`engine.py` implements the primary Python APIs for the SGLang inference engine [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:14-18](). It coordinates internal background managers such as `TokenizerManager`, `run_scheduler_process`, `run_detokenizer_process`, and data parallel controllers, communicating across process boundaries using ZMQ and structured message types defined in `io_struct.py` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:72-118]().

### Natural-Language to Code Entity Mapping: Engine Architecture

This diagram associates the high-level engine runtime roles with their concrete code entities.

**Diagram: Engine runtime roles and imported code entities**

```mermaid
graph TD
    PythonApp["Python application"] -->|Instantiates| EngineModule["Engine (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py)"]
    EngineModule -->|Launches| TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager (python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"]
    EngineModule -->|Launches process| Scheduler["run_scheduler_process (python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py)"]
    EngineModule -->|Launches process| Detokenizer["run_detokenizer_process (python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py)"]
    EngineModule -->|Launches controller| DPController["run_data_parallel_controller_process (python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py)"]
    EngineModule -->|Sends requests| IORequests["managers/io_struct.py request types"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:72-118]()

---

## 2. Engine Initialization and Configuration

The engine parses and handles arguments via `ServerArgs` and `PortArgs`, while managing runtime contexts using functions like `publish`, `snapshot_context`, and `restore_context` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:133-151](). It also instantiates tokenizer components and resolves prompt template parsers using `TemplateManager` and `resolve_auto_parsers` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:115-118]()[python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:129-132]().

```mermaid
    EngineModule --> TemplateManager["TemplateManager"]
```

## 3. Text Generation and Embedding APIs (`generate` and `async_generate`)

The engine provides text generation and embedding capabilities driven by request structures such as `GenerateReqInput` and `EmbeddingReqInput` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:79-87](). These methods coordinate batched prompt execution, sampling parameters, and asynchronous result streaming.

### Request Data Structures

| API Category | Imported Request/Response Symbols | Role in Engine |
|---|---|---|
| Generation | `GenerateReqInput` | Encapsulates input prompt, sampling parameters, and structured output constraints [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:85-85]() |
| Embeddings | `EmbeddingReqInput` | Encapsulates requests for extracting vector embeddings [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:83-83]() |
| RPC / Control | `RpcReqInput`, `RpcReqOutput` | Handles internal control messages and RPC request-response cycles [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:96-97]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:79-105]()

---

## 4. Session Management

Session management supports multi-turn conversations and cached state persistence across requests using `OpenSessionReqInput` and `CloseSessionReqInput` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:81-91](). On the scheduler side, `StreamingSession` and `SessionSlot` manage session-owned KV records and tree locks in conjunction with `UnifiedRadixCache` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-73]().

### Natural-Language to Code Entity Mapping: Session Management Flow

**Diagram: Session request types and streaming-session cache component**

```mermaid
graph LR
    EngineAPI["Engine Session APIs"] -->|Sends Request| OpenRequest["OpenSessionReqInput / CloseSessionReqInput (python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py)"]
    OpenRequest --> TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager"]
    TokenizerManager --> StreamingSession["StreamingSession (python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py)"]
    StreamingSession --> SessionSlot["SessionSlot"]
    SessionSlot --> KVRecord["ReqKvInfo & TreeLock"]
    SessionSlot --> UnifiedRadixCache["UnifiedRadixCache"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:79-105]()[python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-73]()

---

## 5. Weight Update and Advanced Operation APIs

The engine offers extensive support for dynamic weight updates, LoRA adapter management, profiling, and memory occupation control via specialized input request structures [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:79-105]().

### Weight Update Request Types

| Operation Category | Imported Request Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Update Lifecycle | `BeginWeightUpdateReqInput`, `EndWeightUpdateReqInput` | Initiates and concludes weight update transactions [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:80-84]() |
| Source Updates | `UpdateWeightFromDiskReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromIPCReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromDistributedReqInput` | Loads or updates model weights from disk, PyTorch tensors, IPC shared memory, or distributed ranks [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:99-102]() |
| LoRA Management | `LoadLoRAAdapterReqInput`, `UnloadLoRAAdapterReqInput`, `LoadLoRAAdapterFromTensorsReqInput` | Dynamically loads and unloads LoRA adapters [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:88-98]() |
| Memory Control | `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput`, `ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput` | Releases or restores GPU memory occupation for external tasks [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:94-95]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:79-105]()

---

## Summary

`engine.py` serves as the primary Python API entry point for SGLang Runtime. It connects user-facing applications to background execution managers through ZMQ IPC channels and structured request classes covering generation, embeddings, sessions, weight updates, LoRA adapters, and memory controls [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:14-118]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py:14-118]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the HTTP-facing API architecture and protocol translation layers implemented in SGLang Runtime (SRT). It covers FastAPI server initialization via `http_server.py`, OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, etc.), Anthropic Messages and Ollama compatibility layers, and request/response formatting protocols. It details how client-facing payloads are validated using Pydantic models in `protocol.py`, normalized, converted into internal engine requests (`GenerateReqInput`), and serialized back to JSON or Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:14-118](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-115](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-45](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ollama/serving.py:1-30]()

---

## FastAPI Server Architecture and Component Mapping

### Serving Classes and Endpoint Mapping

The HTTP server builds upon FastAPI and `uvicorn`, routing incoming requests to specialized serving handler classes responsible for protocol conversion, tokenization handling, and request execution.

| API Operation / Protocol | Serving Class / Module | Implementation Role |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions | `OpenAIServingChat` | Parses chat messages, manages tool calls, applies chat templates, handles tokenization and streaming chunks [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:24-87]() |
| OpenAI Text Completions | `OpenAIServingCompletion` | Validates prompt inputs, constructs sampling parameters, and builds `GenerateReqInput` structs [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:71-146]() |
| OpenAI Responses API | `OpenAIServingResponses` | Extends chat/completion serving to support advanced `/v1/responses` endpoints with structured output and tool servers [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:1-50]() |
| Anthropic Messages API | `AnthropicServing` | Translates Anthropic Messages format into OpenAI chat completion requests and converts SSE streams back [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-45]() |
| Ollama Compatibility | `OllamaServing` | Maps Ollama chat/generate requests to internal engine execution paths [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ollama/serving.py:1-30]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:74-125](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:24-87](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-45]()

## Request Processing Pipeline and Data Mapping

### Request Models and Validation

Incoming HTTP requests are validated against Pydantic models defined in `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-72](). For instance, `ChatCompletionRequest` validates message structures, tool choices, response formats, and sampling parameters (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:64-85](). 

`OpenAIServingCompletion._convert_to_internal_request` translates client payloads into `GenerateReqInput` objects, mapping options for streaming, logprobs, LoRA adapters, disaggregation bootstrap headers, and custom caching parameters [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:71-146](). These inputs are then passed to `TokenizerManager` for asynchronous tokenization and batch scheduling [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:92-121]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:14-85](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:71-146](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:92-121]()

### Chat Encoding and Normalization

Chat templates are resolved dynamically via `resolve_chat_encoding_spec`, supporting Hugging Face standard templates as well as specialized encoders for DeepSeek, Kimi, and Inkling [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:1-60](). The chat serving layer also normalizes tool message contents and assistant tool call arguments using `normalize_tool_content` and `normalize_assistant_tool_call_arguments` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:144-205]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:1-60](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:144-205]()

---

## Tool Calling, Reasoning, and Structured Outputs

### Tool Call and Reasoning Parsers

SGLang integrates specialized parsers to extract structured tool calls and reasoning segments from generated token streams:
- `FunctionCallParser` and `JsonArrayParser` handle structured tool arguments and execution results [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:103-112]().
- `ReasoningParser` and model-specific detectors (e.g., `Glm47MoeDetector`, `IQuestQ1ReasoningDetector`) manage thinking/reasoning blocks during generation [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:105-131]().
- Structured outputs leverage grammar backends (`xgrammar`) and JSON schema validators to constrain generation paths [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:48-49]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:48-137]()

---

## Response Formats, Streaming, and Usage Reporting

### Response Types and SSE Streaming

Non-streaming endpoints return responses serialized via `ORJSONResponse`, whereas streaming endpoints utilize FastAPI `StreamingResponse` wrapping Server-Sent Events (SSE) constructed via `build_sse_content` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:67-70](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/sse_utils.py:1-90]().

### Token Usage and Cache Reporting

Response payloads include `UsageInfo` detailing `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `total_tokens` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:200-230](). When cache reporting is enabled, `PromptTokensDetails` and `CachedTokensDetails` break down token consumption across device caches, host memory tiers, and external storage backends [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:206-227]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:67-70](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:200-230]()

---

## Anthropic Messages & Ollama Compatibility Layers

### Anthropic Messages API (`AnthropicServing`)

`AnthropicServing` acts as a protocol translation layer between Anthropic's `/v1/messages` endpoint and SGLang's OpenAI chat completion engine [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-45](). It converts `AnthropicMessagesRequest` into `ChatCompletionRequest`, processes execution via `OpenAIServingChat`, and maps output chunks and stop reasons (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `tool_use`) back to Anthropic SSE event types [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-180]().

### Ollama Compatibility (`OllamaServing`)

Ollama-compatible endpoints (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/api/tags`) map incoming requests to internal generation structures, providing seamless drop-in support for Ollama client libraries and CLI tools [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ollama/serving.py:1-30]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:1-180](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ollama/serving.py:1-30]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents SGLang's chat-template and conversation formatting infrastructure, covering template text representation, rule-based auto-detection of reasoning and tool-call parsers, streaming reasoning and format detection (`BaseReasoningFormatDetector`), tool parser dispatch (`FunctionCallParser`), and JSON schema normalization utilities.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:14-19](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:71-78]()

## Template Inputs and Responsibilities

A chat template is represented in the detection code as template text. `TemplateDetectionContext` carries that template text alongside an optional `ReasoningToggleConfig`, a `force_reasoning` flag, and a tokenizer vocabulary set. Its helper methods check for literal text (`has_text`), regular-expression matches (`has_pattern`), exact vocabulary tokens (`has_vocab`), and vocabulary tokens matching a pattern (`has_vocab_pattern`). 

Tokenizer loading and vocabulary inspection provide the substrate against which detection rules evaluate vocabulary tokens.

| Concern | Code entity | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Detection input | `TemplateDetectionContext` | Holds template text, reasoning configuration, force flag, and vocabulary; exposes text and vocabulary predicates. [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:38-58]() |
| Detection rule | `DetectionRule` | Associates a name and result value with a predicate over the context. [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:61-65]() |
| Reasoning configuration | `ReasoningToggleConfig` | Represents a toggle parameter, default state, special case, or effort keyword; `always_on` reflects the `"always"` special case. [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:67-77]() |
| Tokenizer vocabulary fixture | `_DummyTokenizer.get_vocab()` | Shows the vocabulary interface used in parser-detection unit tests. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:25-32]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:38-77](), [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:25-32]()

## Detection Flow: Template and Vocabulary to Parser Settings

Detection is rule-based: a `DetectionRule` predicate examines a `TemplateDetectionContext`. For reasoning toggles, `_has_toggle_default_assignment` parses the template using `jinja2.Environment` and examines `jinja2.nodes.Filter` nodes for the `default` or `d` alias. It recognizes a boolean default on the named parameter while excluding cases that do not implement a working toggle (such as `default(true, true)`). Parsing errors are caught and handled by returning `False`.

### Diagram: Natural-Language Inputs to Detection Entities

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Natural["Natural Language Space"]
        Template[""Raw chat template text""]
        Vocab[""Tokenizer vocabulary""]
        Toggle[""Jinja default toggle assignment""]
    end
    subgraph Code["Code Entity Space"]
        Context[""TemplateDetectionContext""]
        Predicate[""has_text / has_vocab / has_pattern""]
        ToggleParser[""_has_toggle_default_assignment""]
        Rule[""DetectionRule""]
        Result[""ReasoningToggleConfig""]
    end
    Template --> Context
    Vocab --> Context
    Context --> Predicate
    Toggle --> ToggleParser
    Context --> ToggleParser
    Predicate --> Rule
    ToggleParser --> Rule
    Rule --> Result
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:38-142]()

### Rule Ordering and Model-Specific Cases

Unit tests verify that specific template markers take precedence over broader fallback patterns. For instance, an IQuest template resolves to `iquest_q1`, and a GigaChat 3.5 GCML marker resolves to `gigachat35` even when the template also contains `<think>` tokens.

| Tested template signals | Tested result |
|---|---|
| `<|iquest_assistant|>` and IQuest tool markers | Reasoning and tool-call parser: `iquest_q1`. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:85-92]() |
| `<｜GCML｜tool_calls>` with `<think>` | Reasoning and tool-call parser: `gigachat35`. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:94-108]() |
| Qwen-style `enable_thinking` default and `<tool_call>` | Reasoning toggle default enabled; parser: `qwen3`. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:110-125]() |
| GLM-5.3 reasoning-effort header and compact tool format | Forced reasoning; reasoning parser: `glm45`; tool-call parser: `glm47`. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:162-176]() |

Sources: [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:62-176]()

Sources: [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:62-176]()

## Reasoning Configuration and Streaming Parsing

`BaseReasoningFormatDetector` handles parsing of reasoning sections in model outputs for both one-time (`detect_and_parse`) and streaming incremental (`parse_streaming_increment`) execution modes. It tracks state such as `_in_reasoning`, `_buffer`, and whether the think start token has been stripped. `StreamingParseResult` separates normal text from reasoning text.

Sources: [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:1-177]()

## Tool-Call Parser Dispatch and Detectors

`FunctionCallParser` maps parser-name strings to `BaseFormatDetector` subclasses via its `ToolCallParserEnum` dictionary. Supported names include `deepseekv32`, `qwen3_coder`, `glm47`, `gpt-oss`, and others defined in `TOOL_CALL_PARSER_NAMES`.

Detectors such as `Qwen3CoderDetector` and `DeepSeekV32Detector` inspect streamed or buffered tokens for sentinel tags (e.g., `<tool_call>`, `<function=...>`, or DSML tags) and parse arguments according to schema configurations.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:71-129](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/parser_names.py:10-57]()

### Diagram: Parser Name to Streaming Detector

```mermaid

    end

    end

    Stream --> Increment

```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:71-152]()

## Schema Normalization Utilities

Tool definitions often pass JSON schemas exported from database or ORM tooling that use non-standard type names (`varchar`, `text`, `int`, `float`, etc.). `normalize_json_schema_types` walks a JSON schema in-place and rewrites these non-standard types to standard JSON Schema primitives (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`) using `_JSON_SCHEMA_TYPE_ALIASES` and prefix matching rules.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:62-65]()

## Summary

- `TemplateDetectionContext` exposes template text and vocabulary predicates to rule-based parser detection. [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:38-58]()
- `_has_toggle_default_assignment` inspects Jinja AST filter nodes for working boolean defaults on reasoning toggles. [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:92-142]()
- `BaseReasoningFormatDetector` manages incremental stream parsing and separation of reasoning tokens. [test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py:1-177]()
- `FunctionCallParser` maps string identifiers to concrete format detectors for tool calls. [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:71-129]()
- `normalize_json_schema_types` normalizes non-standard type aliases in tool parameter schemas to standard JSON Schema primitives. [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:62-65]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:38-142](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:71-129](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:62-65]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the gRPC server architecture, protobuf definitions, the Python-to-Rust gRPC request bridge (`RuntimeHandle`), the Rust-based `sglang-grpc` extension integration, and the `sglang-server` Rust frontend pipeline embedded within the Python scheduler process.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:1-8](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-13](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:27-46]()

---

## Overview and Purpose

The SGLang gRPC server interface bridges high-performance gRPC clients with the embedded multi-threaded Rust frontend (`sglang-server`), which runs inside the Python scheduler process alongside the `TokenizerManager` and `DetokenizerManager` threads.

The Rust frontend exposes a PyO3 module (`sglang.srt.rust_extensions._server`) that handles HTTP/gRPC transports via `tonic` and `axum`, while Python's `RuntimeHandle` orchestrates asynchronous request submission, tokenization dispatch, and backpressure management.

| Concern | Code entity | Established role |
|---|---|---|
| Python gRPC Bridge | `RuntimeHandle` | Synchronous-to-asynchronous bridge invoked by Rust gRPC handlers, managing request submission and chunk callbacks. [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-100]() |
| Rust gRPC/HTTP Server | `sglang_server::Server` | Multi-threaded Rust runtime driving tokio transports and managing IPC channel flow. [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:8-12](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-16]() |
| gRPC Port Configuration | `ServerArgs.grpc_port`, `RustServerServerArgs.grpc_addr` | Optional gRPC listener configuration slots. [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:27-46](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:117-122]() |
| Shared Request Core | `CoreHandle` | Cloneable capability for queuing requests and handling cancellations in the core runtime. [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/handle.rs:95-117]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-100](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:8-12](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-16](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:27-46]()

### Natural-Language-to-Code Map

**Diagram: gRPC Frontend to Scheduler Data Pipeline (`Runtime` & `Server`)**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["gRPC Client"] --> GRPCServer["sglang_server gRPC Service (rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/grpc/service.rs)"]
    GRPCServer --> RuntimeHandle["RuntimeHandle (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py)"]
    RuntimeHandle --> TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager (python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"]
    TokenizerManager --> Scheduler["Scheduler Process (python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py)"]
    Scheduler --> ModelRunner["ModelRunner (python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py)"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-100](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12]()

---

## Architectural Data Flow

Requests arriving over gRPC are decoded in Rust and passed to Python via PyO3 boundaries or shared memory (`ShmBuffer`). `RuntimeHandle` translates these into asynchronous tasks submitted to `TokenizerManager`, using thread-safe event loop scheduling (`asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`) and backpressure monitoring (`_send_with_backpressure`).

**Diagram: Request Flow from gRPC to TokenizerManager (`_safe_callback`)**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Request["gRPC Request"] --> Service["tonic gRPC Service (rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/grpc/service.rs)"]
    Service --> PyO3["PyO3 Call (rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs)"]
    PyO3 --> RuntimeHandle["RuntimeHandle._safe_callback (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py)"]
    RuntimeHandle --> Backpressure["RuntimeHandle._send_with_backpressure (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py)"]
    Backpressure --> TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager.generate (python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py)"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-176](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:45-91]()

---

## Protobuf Definitions (`proto/`)

Protobuf contracts define the gRPC runtime and API services under `proto/sglang/runtime/v1/` and `proto/sglang/api/v1/`. These definitions specify the service interfaces, request/response message structures, streaming endpoints, and metadata fields consumed by both the Rust `tonic` gRPC server and external clients.

Sources: [proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto](), [proto/sglang/api/v1/common.proto]()

---

## Python-Rust Request Manager (`RuntimeHandle`)

The Python-side bridge (`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py`) implements `RuntimeHandle`, which exposes synchronous methods (`submit_*`, `abort`) callable from Rust via PyO3 while executing underlying generation logic asynchronously on the `TokenizerManager` event loop.

Key mechanisms implemented in `RuntimeHandle`:
- **Chunk Callbacks**: Invokes Rust-side PyO3 callback objects (`chunk_callback`) with `(payload, finished, error)` tuples [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-119]().
- **Backpressure Handling**: Manages `_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT_S` via `_send_with_backpressure` and `asyncio.Event` readiness triggers to prevent queue overflow when streaming responses outpace consumer consumption [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:121-176]().
- **Request Abatement**: Routes cancellation signals back to `TokenizerManager.abort_request` across single or batched request IDs [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:131-137]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-197]()

---

## Rust `sglang-grpc` Extension and `sglang-server` Frontend Pipeline

The `sglang-server` crate builds both a `cdylib` and an `rlib`, registering `sglang.srt.rust_extensions._server` as its PyO3 module [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:8-18](). It bundles `tonic` for gRPC support, `axum` for HTTP, and `tokio` for asynchronous execution [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:25-40]().

The embedded runtime initializes worker threads for tokenization, detokenization, and core state management, providing zero-copy buffer passing (`IngressRequest` and `ShmBuffer`) to integrate efficiently with Python NumPy arrays and shared memory segments [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:45-91](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-16]().

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:8-40](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:45-91](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-16]()

---

## gRPC Configuration and Startup

Server configuration is unified through `ServerArgs` and `RustServerServerArgs` [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:27-122](). The Python-side configuration builder `_build_server_args` resolves the gRPC port, conditionally enabling or disabling gRPC transport depending on legacy mode flags (`smg_grpc_mode`, `grpc_mode`) and serving configuration [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/config.py:64-75]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/config.py:64-75](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:27-122]()

---

| Runtime Pipeline | `Runtime` in `rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs` | Manages tokio runtimes, worker thread pools, and IPC channel rings. [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-16]() |
