## Purpose and Scope

SGLang’s environment and configuration mechanisms supply runtime settings and connect platform metadata to execution entities. The environment variable subsystem manages process environment values via typed fields and singletons, while platform detection mechanisms inspect hardware capabilities (such as CUDA, ROCm/HIP, and NPU) to drive runtime dispatch and optimization strategies. 

For detailed information, see the child pages:
- [Environment Variables System](#14.1)
- [Hardware Detection and Platform Configuration](#14.2)

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-124]()

## 14.1 Environment Variables System

The environment variable subsystem centers around `EnvField` and its typed subclasses in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`. These classes handle retrieving, parsing, validating, and temporarily overriding environment configurations (such as cache directories, timeout thresholds, and feature flags). The singleton pattern ensures unified access across modules, and deprecated aliases provide backward compatibility with warnings.

For details, see [Environment Variables System](#14.1).

**Diagram: Configuration flow from environment variables to runtime components**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    OS["os.environ"] --> FIELD["EnvField.get()"]
    FIELD --> PARSE["EnvBool / EnvInt / EnvStr / EnvJSON / EnvTuple"]
    PARSE --> ENV["envs"]
    ENV --> ARGS["ServerArgs"]
    ARGS --> CONTEXT["RuntimeContext"]
    CONTEXT --> SCHEDULER["Scheduler"]
```
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-124](), [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:125-211]()

## 14.2 Hardware Detection and Platform Configuration

Hardware detection utilities inspect the underlying device architecture (e.g., checking `is_cuda`, `is_hip`, `is_npu`, or device capability versions) to initialize appropriate backend kernels, memory pools, and execution modes. These capabilities interface with `RuntimeContext` and `ServerArgs` to configure model runners and attention backends accordingly.

For details, see [Hardware Detection and Platform Configuration](#14.2).

**Diagram: Platform detection and hardware dispatch routing**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CHECKS["is_cpu / is_hip / is_npu / is_xpu"] --> UTILS["sglang.srt.utils"]
    UTILS --> PARALLEL["parallel_state.py"]
    UTILS --> BATCH["ForwardBatch"]
    ENV["envs"] --> ARGS["ServerArgs"]
    ARGS --> CONTEXT["RuntimeContext"]
    CONTEXT --> RUNNER["ModelRunner"]
    CONTEXT --> SCHEDULER["Scheduler"]
```
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:11-26](), [python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:50-58](), [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-23]()

## Summary

Environment variables and hardware platform checks work in tandem to establish the operating bounds of an SGLang deployment. Configuration inputs feed into `ServerArgs` and runtime singletons, while platform checks dictate which hardware-specific optimizations and attention kernels are activated. 

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-124](), [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-23]()

## Purpose and Scope

SGLang’s environment-variable interface provides typed `EnvField` objects implemented in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` featuring parsing, default value resolution, warnings, aliases, and scoped overrides [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-123](). Runtime modules access configuration through `envs.<NAME>.get()`. This page covers the field implementation and environment configuration; hardware detection and platform configuration are covered in section 14.2.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-123](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37]()

---

## System Architecture

`EnvField.get()` reads the field’s named value from the process environment using `os.getenv()`, resolves a default when the variable is unset, or parses the value when set [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-86](). A runtime consumer imports `envs` and invokes `.get()` to obtain the typed value; for example, `handle_moe_kernel_config()` reads `envs.SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION.get()` when validating backend and quantization combinations [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]().

### Environment Variable Data Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    OSEnv["os.getenv(name)"] --> Get["EnvField.get()"]
    Get --> Parse["EnvField.parse(value)"]
    Parse --> Typed["typed value"]
    Get --> Default["_resolve_default()"]
    Default --> Typed
    Typed --> Consumer["handle_moe_kernel_config()"]
    Consumer --> Field["envs.SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION.get()"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-86](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:69-90](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]()

---

## Core Components

### EnvField Descriptor System

`EnvField` stores a default value, a `secret` flag, and a marker (`_set_to_none`) indicating whether the environment variable is explicitly set to Python `None` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-54](). Its `__set_name__()` method records the field name used as the environment key and asserts against prohibited descriptor-usage patterns [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:55-58](). Subclasses implement custom `parse()` routines [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:59-60]().

`get()` reads the named variable using `os.getenv()` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:68](). An explicitly marked `None` returns `None` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:70-73](); an unset variable resolves to its default via `_resolve_default()` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:76-77](); and a set variable is parsed [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:79-80](). If parsing raises `ValueError`, `get()` emits a warning and returns the resolved default [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:81-86](). Callable defaults are evaluated lazily only when needed [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-65]().

`set()` writes `str(value)` to `os.environ` and tracks whether the value was Python `None` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:91-93](). `override()` saves the prior environment value and marker, applies the temporary value, and restores the saved state after the context block [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:95-108](). `clear()` removes the variable and resets the marker [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:110-112]().

Implicit truth-value and length checks are explicitly prohibited: `__bool__()` and `__len__()` raise `RuntimeError`, directing callers to use `.get()` explicitly [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:114-123]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-123]()

### EnvField Read and Override Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["EnvField.get()"] --> CheckNone["_set_to_none?"]
    CheckNone -->|"yes"| ReturnNone["return None"]
    CheckNone -->|"no"| Read["os.getenv(name)"]
    Read --> Unset["value unset?"]
    Unset -->|"yes"| Default["_resolve_default()"]
    Unset -->|"no"| Parse["parse(value)"]
    Parse -->|"success"| Result["return parsed value"]
    Parse -->|"ValueError"| Warn["warnings.warn()"]
    Warn --> Fallback["_resolve_default()"]
    Fallback --> Result
    Override["EnvField.override(value)"] --> Save["save prior environment state"]
    Save --> Set["EnvField.set(value)"]
    Set --> Yield["yield to scoped caller"]
    Yield --> Restore["restore prior environment state"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-112]()

### Type-Specific EnvField Classes

| Class | Parsing Behavior | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `EnvTuple` | Splits comma-separated strings, strips whitespace, discards empty entries, and returns a tuple of strings. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:125-128]() |
| `EnvStr` | Returns the input string unchanged. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:130-133]() |
| `EnvJSON` | Returns `None` for empty inputs; otherwise loads JSON from a file path if it exists, or parses inline JSON strings. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:135-143]() |
| `EnvBool` | Accepts case-insensitive `true`, `1`, `yes`, `y` as `True` and `false`, `0`, `no`, `n` as `False`; raises `ValueError` otherwise. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:145-153]() |
| `EnvInt` | Converts the input to an integer, raising `ValueError` on failure. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:155-161]() |
| `EnvFloat` | Converts the input to a float, raising `ValueError` on failure. | [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:204-209]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:125-161](), [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:204-209]()

### Deprecated Variable Fallbacks

`_DeprecatedEnvFallback` provides a mixin that adds deprecated-name lookup to `EnvField` subclasses [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:163-169](). If the canonical environment variable is unset and the deprecated variable is set, `get()` emits a `FutureWarning`, copies the deprecated value into the canonical environment key, and proceeds with parsing [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:175-189](). Concrete subclasses include `EnvBoolWithAlias`, `EnvIntWithAlias`, and `EnvStrWithAlias` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:192-201]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:163-201]()

## Environment Variable Domains and Examples

SGLang environment variables use the `SGLANG_` prefix for canonical configuration, though some vendor integrations retain upstream prefixes [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:6-8](). General configuration options include model sourcing, network binding, logging, and caching [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:26-85]().

| Environment Variable | Documented Role | Code / Doc Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE` | Enables loading models from ModelScope (`false` by default). | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:26-29]() |
| `SGLANG_HOST_IP` | Specifies server host IP address (`0.0.0.0` by default). | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:31-34]() |
| `SGLANG_PORT` | Configures server port (auto-detected by default). | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:36-39]() |
| `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` | Root cache directory for weights and kernel compiler outputs (`~/.cache/sglang` by default). | [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:82-85]() |
| `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION` | Controls per-token activation formatting for FlashInfer NVFP4 kernels. | [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]() |

The environment module also provides lazy default helpers: `_default_hip()` defers PyTorch HIP detection until needed [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:11-25](), `_default_cache_subdir()` derives paths beneath `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:31-38](), and `_default_on_in_ci()` checks `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:40-43]().

Sources: [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:6-8](), [docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx:26-85](), [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:11-43](), [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-65]()

## Usage Patterns and Integration

### Accessing Environment Variables

Runtime components import `envs` from `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` and call `.get()` to retrieve configurations [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37](). For instance, `handle_moe_kernel_config()` reads `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION` during MoE backend configuration checks [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]().

### Temporary Overrides for Scoped Configuration

`EnvField.override(value)` serves as a context manager that modifies the process environment temporarily and restores the prior state upon exiting [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:95-108](). Callers must access field values via `.get()` rather than evaluating descriptor objects directly [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:114-123]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:95-123](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]()

## Summary

`EnvField` provides centralized mechanisms for parsing environment variables, resolving defaults, emitting validation warnings, and managing scoped overrides [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-123](). Typed subclasses handle parsing for booleans, integers, floats, strings, tuples, and JSON structures [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:125-209](). Runtime modules access these fields through `envs.<NAME>.get()`, enabling robust configuration control across SGLang [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:62-86](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/environ.py:45-209](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:31-37](), [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py:119-135]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes how SGLang detects hardware backends, resolves platforms via lazy singletons and entry-point plugins, represents platform capabilities, and exposes platform-specific configuration and dispatch hooks. The implementation distinguishes backend-presence checks and device identity queries in `DeviceMixin` from the `SRTPlatform` abstraction, which declares capabilities and provides subsystem factories `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-10]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:1-26]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:1-10]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:1-26]()`

---

## Platform Detection and Resolution (`current_platform`)

SGLang manages hardware platforms using a module-level lazy singleton named `current_platform` located in `python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py`. On first access, `_resolve_platform()` discovers platform plugins via Python's `setuptools` entry points under the `sglang.srt.platforms` group or falls back to built-in platform implementations `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:4-10]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:76-110]()`.

### Discovery and Resolution Flow

The resolution logic branches based on whether the environment variable `SGLANG_PLATFORM` is explicitly set:

1. **Explicit Selection (`SGLANG_PLATFORM` set)**:
   - Enumerates entry points without importing unrelated plugin modules (front-loading filter).
   - Loads and activates only the named plugin. If the name is not found or `activate()` returns `None`, a `RuntimeError` is raised `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:110-139]()`.

2. **Automatic Discovery (`SGLANG_PLATFORM` unset)**:
   - Imports and activates all discovered plugins under `sglang.srt.platforms`.
   - If zero plugins activate, it falls back sequentially through built-in checks:
     - `_is_cpu_available()` (`SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE == "1"`) → `CpuSRTPlatform` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:46-48]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:155-157]()`
     - `is_sail_available()` → `SailSRTPlatform` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:158-162]()`
     - `_is_cuda_available()` (CUDA available and HIP absent) → `CudaSRTPlatform` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:38-40]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:163-167]()`
     - `_is_npu_available()` → `NPUSRTPlatform` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:50-52]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:168-170]()`
     - `_is_rocm_available()` (CUDA available and HIP present) → `RocmSRTPlatform` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:42-44]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:171-175]()`
     - Other platforms (`XPU`, `MUSA`, `MPS`, `MLU`, or base `SRTPlatform`) `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:54-74]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:176-178]()`.

### Platform Resolution Pipeline Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Access["Access current_platform"] --> CheckEnv["SGLang_Platform_Set_Check"]
    CheckEnv -->|Yes| FilterPlugins["Enumerate entry_points and load named plugin"]
    CheckEnv -->|No| AutoDiscover["Activate all registered platform plugins"]
    AutoDiscover --> CountActivated["Active plugins count check"]
    CountActivated -->|0| FallbackChain["Check built-in availability: CPU -> SAIL -> CUDA -> NPU -> ROCm -> XPU -> MUSA -> MPS -> MLU"]
    CountActivated -->|1| UsePlugin["Use activated plugin"]
    CountActivated -->|N > 1| RaiseError["Raise RuntimeError (ambiguous plugins)"]
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:76-178]()`

---

## Device Identity and Platform Abstraction (`DeviceMixin` and `SRTPlatform`)

Base device identity queries—such as `is_cuda()`, `is_hip()`, `is_npu()`, `is_cpu()`, `is_xpu()`, `is_musa()`, and `is_mlu()`—are provided by `DeviceMixin` in `python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:69-80](), while SRT-specific subsystem factory methods and capabilities are defined by `SRTPlatform` in `python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:100-112]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:78-88]()`.

### `PlatformEnum` and Identity Queries

`PlatformEnum` enumerates known platforms including `CUDA`, `ROCM`, `CPU`, `XPU`, `MUSA`, `NPU`, `MLU`, `TPU`, `MPS`, `SAIL`, `OOT` (out-of-tree), and `UNSPECIFIED` `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:41-60]()`.

`DeviceMixin` provides methods such as `is_cuda()`, `is_rocm()`, `is_cpu()`, `is_npu()`, and `is_cuda_alike()` (which returns `True` for CUDA, ROCm, MUSA, and SAIL) `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:117-155]()`, `[python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:69-80]()`.

### `PlatformCapabilities`

`PlatformCapabilities` is a frozen `msgspec.Struct` that declares what operations a platform supports. Core reads these flags prior to component construction `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-76]()`:

| Capability Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `supports_triton` | `False` | Triton kernels can launch on this device. If `False`, core falls back to torch-native allocators `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:71]` |
| `graph_capture` | `False` | Enables the decode graph runner (`get_graph_runner_cls()`) `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:72]` |
| `piecewise_graph` | `False` | Enables the prefill piecewise compilation backend `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:73]` |
| `hicache_device_kernels` | `False` | Enables `sgl_kernel` HiCache transfer and write-back kernels `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:74]` |
| `supports_pynccl` | `False` | Enables PyNccl communicator creation for model-parallel groups `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:75]` |

### Platform Abstraction and Capabilities Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DeviceMixin["DeviceMixin (_enum, device_name, device_type)"] --> SRTPlatform["SRTPlatform"]
    SRTPlatform --> PlatformCapabilities["PlatformCapabilities"]
    PlatformCapabilities --> SupportsTriton["supports_triton"]
    PlatformCapabilities --> GraphCapture["graph_capture"]
    PlatformCapabilities --> PiecewiseGraph["piecewise_graph"]
    PlatformCapabilities --> HiCacheKernels["hicache_device_kernels"]
    PlatformCapabilities --> SupportsPyNccl["supports_pynccl"]
    SRTPlatform --> SubsystemFactories["Subsystem Factories (Attention, Graph Runner, KV Pool, MoE Expert Executor)"]
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-76]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:78-88]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:41-60]`, `[python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:69-80]()`

---

## Configuration Lifecycle and Subsystem Factories

`SRTPlatform` defines configuration lifecycle hooks and factory methods that concrete platforms (such as `CudaSRTPlatform` and `NPUSRTPlatform`) override `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:90-165]()`:

- `apply_server_args_defaults(server_args)`: Applies platform-specific default values to `ServerArgs` after parsing `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:98-103]()`.
- `get_default_attention_backend()`: Returns the default attention backend name (e.g., `"ascend"` for NPU) `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:119-121]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/npu.py:79-80]()`.
- `get_graph_runner_cls()`: Returns the graph runner class or `None` for in-tree defaults `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:127-136]()`.
- `get_moe_expert_executor_cls(context)`: Allows platforms or models (such as Gemma4) to provide custom MoE expert executors while preserving the `FusedMoE` parameter ABI `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:142-161]()`.

### Hardware and Platform Subsystem Dispatch Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CurrentPlatform["current_platform singleton"] --> Resolve["_resolve_platform()"]
    Resolve --> CudaPlatform["CudaSRTPlatform"]
    Resolve --> NpuPlatform["NPUSRTPlatform"]
    Resolve --> CpuPlatform["CpuSRTPlatform"]
    Resolve --> OotPlatform["Out-of-Tree Platform Plugin"]
    CudaPlatform --> CudaCaps["Cuda Capabilities & Subsystems"]
    NpuPlatform --> NpuCaps["Npu Capabilities & Subsystems"]
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:76-178]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:90-165]`

---

## Summary

SGLang abstracts hardware detection and platform configuration through lazy singleton resolution (`current_platform`), the `DeviceMixin` identity hierarchy, and `SRTPlatform` subsystem factories. Platform capabilities are explicitly declared using `PlatformCapabilities` to inform core compilation and runtime execution paths across CUDA, ROCm, NPU, XPU, CPU, and out-of-tree vendor plugins `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:4-10]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-88]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:100-112]()`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py:4-10]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/interface.py:51-88]`, `[python/sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py:100-112]()`

## Purpose and scope

This parent page maps SGLang’s testing and development topics to the main workflows and code entities visible in the repository. The GitHub Actions configuration includes pull-request, scheduled, rerun, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation test paths [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-14](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:1-21](), [.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml:1-19](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml:1-11](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:1-15](). Details of test orchestration, benchmarking, test runners, debugging tools, and the simulator belong on the designated child pages [.agents/skills/ci-workflow-guide/SKILL.md:1-12](), [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:38-79]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-14](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:1-21](), [.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml:1-19](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml:1-11](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:1-15](), [.agents/skills/ci-workflow-guide/SKILL.md:1-12](), [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:38-79]()

## CI pipeline and orchestration code mapping

The main PR workflow starts with change detection and can invoke extra test workflows or gate checks; reusable stage workflows receive test partitions and runner configuration [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:72-88](), [.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml:1-35](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:77-108](). Scheduled and parallel test dispatches use similar reusable patterns [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:10-48](), while change filters dynamically size partitions via backend registration utils [python/sglang/test/ci/ci_utils.py:1-25](), [scripts/ci/utils/compute_partitions.py:1-15]().

**Diagram: Pull-request testing concepts mapped to workflow entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        PR["Pull request test request"]
        Changes["Change detection"]
        Stage["Runner-specific test stage"]
        Suite["Test suite execution"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntities["Code Entity Space"]
        PRYML[".github/workflows/pr-test.yml"]
        ChangesYML[".github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml"]
        StageYML[".github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml"]
        SuiteRunner["test/run_suite.py"]
    end
    PR --> Changes --> Stage --> Suite
    PR -.-> PRYML
    Changes -.-> ChangesYML
    Stage -.-> StageYML
    Suite -.-> SuiteRunner
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:72-88](), [.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml:1-35](), [python/sglang/test/ci/ci_utils.py:1-25](), [scripts/ci/utils/compute_partitions.py:1-15]()

| Change detection and partitioning | `_pr-test-check-changes.yml`, `compute_partitions.py` | Pipeline filtering overview [.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml:1-35](), [scripts/ci/utils/compute_partitions.py:1-15]() |

## Test infrastructure and CI/CD

The PR workflow supports pull requests, scheduled runs, and manual dispatch [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:10-47](). Its change-detection job is followed by conditional test workflows and gating checks [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:72-88](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:77-108](). The reusable stage workflow defines runner configuration, partition inputs, and timeout values [.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml:10-35](). Dependency installation and environment configuration are managed by dedicated scripts like `ci_install_dependency.sh` [scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh:1-35]().

For details on test orchestration, CI registration, platform workflows, permissions, and monitoring, see [Test Infrastructure and CI/CD](#15.1).

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:10-47](), [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:72-88](), [.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml:10-35](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:77-108](), [scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh:1-35]()

## Benchmarking and performance measurement

The workflow excerpts include JIT-kernel test matrices with benchmark-named suites as well as dedicated scripts for diffusion and serving benchmarks [.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml:47-81](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:141-153](). These pipelines collect performance telemetry during test suite execution.

For benchmarking tools, profiling utilities, and the `benchmark/` directory, see [Benchmarking and Performance Measurement](#15.2).

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml:47-81](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:141-153]()

## Test runners and model comparison

Model testing utilizes specialized test harnesses and evaluation tools to ensure accuracy across engine revisions [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:85-103](). Evaluation scripts interface directly with running SGLang servers to check output correctness against known benchmarks [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:85-97]().

For `HFRunner` vs `SRTRunner`, accuracy testing, test kits, and output comparison, see [Test Runners and Model Comparison](#15.3).

**Diagram: Model evaluation concepts mapped to test entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        ServerTest["Server-backed model test"]
        Evaluation["Model evaluation"]
        Result["Metrics and assertions"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntities["Code Entity Space"]
        TestClass["DefaultServerBase"]
        EvalCall["run_sgl_eval"]
        ScoreCheck["gsm8k"]
    end
    ServerTest --> Evaluation --> Result
    ServerTest -.-> TestClass
    Evaluation -.-> EvalCall
    Result -.-> ScoreCheck
```

Sources: [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:85-97]()

## Development tools and debugging

The PR, rerun, and multimodal generation workflows configure environment variables such as `SGLANG_CUDA_COREDUMP` to capture debugging information [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:57-64](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:41-47](). Pre-commit hooks (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`) enforce formatting, linting, and structural rules across code and workflow files [.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-45]().

For tensor dumps, dump comparison, debugging utilities, and internal playbooks, see [Development Tools and Debugging](#15.4).

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:57-64](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml:41-47](), [.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-45]()

## SGLang Simulator (`tools/sglang-simulator`)

The simulator is tested through dedicated CPU and GPU workflows defined in extra test pipelines [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:143-153](). It reuses SGLang's scheduler and cache logic while replacing model forward passes with latency predictors [.agents/skills/ci-workflow-guide/SKILL.md:1-12]().

For simulator architecture, trace replay, workload generation, predictor modes, and metrics, see [SGLang Simulator (tools/sglang-simulator)](#15.5).

**Diagram: Simulator CI concept mapped to workflow entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        SimulatorCheck["Simulator test job"]
        CPUPath["CPU workflow path"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntities["Code Entity Space"]
        ExtraWorkflow[".github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml"]
        SimulatorJob["simulator-test-cpu"]
        SimulatorWorkflow[".github/workflows/_pr-test-simulator-cpu.yml"]
    end
    SimulatorCheck --> CPUPath
    SimulatorCheck -.-> ExtraWorkflow
    SimulatorCheck -.-> SimulatorJob
    CPUPath -.-> SimulatorWorkflow
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-14](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-extra.yml:143-153](), [.agents/skills/ci-workflow-guide/SKILL.md:1-12]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the test infrastructure, suite orchestration, CI registry systems, and workflow automation of SGLang. It details how `test/run_suite.py` orchestrates test execution [test/run_suite.py:1-17](), how GitHub Actions workflows (`pr-test.yml`, `pr-test-amd.yml`, `pr-test-npu.yml`, and `rerun-test.yml`) manage cross-platform CI pipelines [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-80](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml:6-98](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:1-47](), [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:1-63](), and how permissions and gate mechanisms (`CODEOWNERS`, `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, and `slash_command_handler.py`) govern contributions and CI operations [.github/CODEOWNERS:1-15](), [.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:1-18](), [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:43-160]().

Sources: [test/run_suite.py:1-17](), [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-80](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml:6-98](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:1-47](), [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:1-63](), [.github/CODEOWNERS:1-15](), [.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:1-18](), [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:43-160]()

## 1. Test Suite Organization and Registration

### Test Registration System

SGLang manages test suites through a modular registration framework. `test/run_suite.py` imports `CIRegistry`, `HWBackend`, `auto_partition`, and `collect_tests` from `sglang.test.ci.ci_register`, and `run_unittest_files` from `sglang.test.ci.ci_utils` [test/run_suite.py:11-17](). 

The `HW_MAPPING` dictionary maps string identifiers to `HWBackend` enum members across supported hardware accelerators and platforms [test/run_suite.py:19-30]().

| Platform Key | Registry Backend |
|---|---|
| `cpu` | `HWBackend.CPU` [test/run_suite.py:20-20]() |
| `cuda` | `HWBackend.CUDA` [test/run_suite.py:21-21]() |
| `amd` | `HWBackend.AMD` [test/run_suite.py:22-22]() |
| `musa` | `HWBackend.MUSA` [test/run_suite.py:23-23]() |
| `npu` | `HWBackend.NPU` [test/run_suite.py:24-24]() |
| `xpu` | `HWBackend.XPU` [test/run_suite.py:25-25]() |
| `mlx` | `HWBackend.MLX` [test/run_suite.py:26-26]() |
| `mps` | `HWBackend.MPS` [test/run_suite.py:27-27]() |
| `ppu` | `HWBackend.PPU` [test/run_suite.py:28-28]() |
| `mlu` | `HWBackend.MLU` [test/run_suite.py:29-29]() |

Sources: [test/run_suite.py:11-30]()

### Per-Commit and Nightly Suites

Test suites are categorized into `PER_COMMIT_SUITES` and `NIGHTLY_SUITES`, structured as mappings from `HWBackend` to lists of named suite identifiers [test/run_suite.py:31-151](), [test/run_suite.py:153-181](). 

- **Per-Commit Suites (`PER_COMMIT_SUITES`)**: Execute during Pull Requests and pushes. For CUDA, they include base tiers (`base-a-test-1-gpu-small`, `base-b-test-1-gpu-small`, `base-b-test-1-gpu-large`, `base-b-test-2-gpu-large`, `base-c-test-4-gpu-h100`) and label-gated extra tiers (`extra-a-test-1-gpu-small`, `extra-b-test-4-gpu-h100`) [test/run_suite.py:77-115](). AMD and other backends similarly partition tests into small, large, and multi-GPU configurations [test/run_suite.py:36-76]().
- **Nightly Suites (`NIGHTLY_SUITES`)**: Executed on scheduled cadences for exhaustive validation across complex topologies (e.g., `nightly-test-8-gpu-h200`, `nightly-test-8-gpu-b200`, model-specific accuracy and performance matrices) [test/run_suite.py:150-181]().

Sources: [test/run_suite.py:31-151](), [test/run_suite.py:153-181]()

```mermaid
    end

```

Sources: [test/run_suite.py:11-35](), [test/run_suite.py:153-158]()

## 2. Test Orchestration (`run_suite.py`)

### Orchestration Workflow

`test/run_suite.py` serves as the CLI and orchestration entry point for running registered test suites locally or within containerized CI runners. It maps command-line arguments (such as `--hw` and `--suite`) to registered backend enums, invokes `collect_tests` to discover test cases, and applies `auto_partition` to divide test loads across parallel execution shards [test/run_suite.py:1-17](). Execution is delegated to `run_unittest_files`, which executes files directly with configured fail-fast and error reporting semantics [test/run_suite.py:17-17](), [docs/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.mdx:43-46]().

### Data Flow and Code-Entity Map

Diagram: "Orchestration Data Flow in test/run_suite.py"

```mermaid
flowchart TB
        CLIInput["CLI Arguments: --hw, --suite"] --> run_suite["test/run_suite.py"]
        run_suite --> ResolveBackend["Resolve HWBackend via HW_MAPPING"]
        ResolveBackend --> LookupSuite["Lookup suite in PER_COMMIT_SUITES or NIGHTLY_SUITES"]
        LookupSuite --> Collect["collect_tests(suite_name)"]
        Collect --> Partition["auto_partition(tests)"]
        Partition --> Execute["run_unittest_files(shard_files)"]
        Execute --> CIUtils["sglang.test.ci.ci_utils: run_unittest_files"]
```

Sources: [test/run_suite.py:1-35](), [test/run_suite.py:153-158]()

## 3. CI/CD Workflow Architecture Across Platforms

SGLang utilizes GitHub Actions workflows to automate multi-platform testing across NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and Huawei NPU hardware backends.

### NVIDIA CUDA (`pr-test.yml`)
- **Triggers**: Pull requests, scheduled cron triggers (2x daily), manual workflow dispatch, and reusable workflow calls [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:10-48]().
- **Change Detection**: Delegates path filtering to `_pr-test-check-changes.yml` via the `check-changes` job [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:74-80]().
- **Sequential Execution**: Manages dependent gates (`wait-for-base-a`, `wait-for-base-b`) via the `wait-for-jobs` action and matrix partition counts [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:90-156]().

### AMD ROCm (`pr-test-amd.yml` & `nightly-test-amd.yml`)
- **Triggers**: Pull requests on core paths, scheduled rotations (`rocm10`, `rocm724`, `rocm720`), and manual dispatches supporting version selection and stage overriding [.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml:6-98]().
- **Concurrency**: Groups runs by branch or explicit run ID to cancel stale PR pushes while isolating scheduled and manual executions [.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml:154-158]().

### Huawei NPU (`pr-test-npu.yml`)
- **Triggers**: Scheduled daily runs, pull requests targeting `main` or NPU branches, and manual dispatch with optional coverage instrumentation [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:3-34]().
- **Path Filtering**: Evaluates changes against `python/sglang/` packages, NPU pyproject configurations, and test suites using `dorny/paths-filter` [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:73-103](). Includes CPU-hosted stub tests (`extra-a-test-npu`) for faster PR feedback [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:126-135]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:10-88](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml:6-98](), [.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd.yml:3-27](), [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml:3-47]()

Sources: [.github/CODEOWNERS:1-35](), [.github/CODEOWNERS:86-95]()

### CI Permissions Registry (`CI_PERMISSIONS.json`)
`.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json` defines user-specific authorization flags for triggering and managing CI actions [.*github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:1-18]()**:
- `can_tag_run_ci_label`: Authorizes applying label triggers (e.g., `run-ci-npu-extra`) [.*github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:3-3]().
- `can_rerun_failed_ci`: Authorizes re-running failed workflows [.*github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:4-4]().
- `cooldown_interval_minutes`: Rate-limiting window between dispatches [.*github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:5-5]().

### Maintenance and Rebase Gate
`_check_rebase_gate()` in `scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py` enforces pre-dispatch validation by checking maintenance issue `#21065` and verifying whether PRs meet required base commit hashes (`MIN_BASE_SHA`) [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:58-79](). PRs carrying the `bypass-maintenance` label bypass these restrictions [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:124-130]().

Sources: [.github/CODEOWNERS:1-15](), [.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:1-18](), [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:58-130]()

## 5. CI Monitoring, Rerun Infrastructure, and Slash-Command Handling

### Rerun Workflow (`rerun-test.yml`)
`.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml` allows manual execution of specific test commands across modes (`cuda`, `multimodal_gen`, `cpu`, `npu`, `amd`) [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:1-16](). 
- The `prepare-partitions` job runs `scripts/ci/partition_rerun_tests.py` to dynamically partition test commands into execution matrices [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:100-140]().
- Worker jobs check out trusted CI templates alongside the target PR head commit to execute tests securely [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:166-175]().

### Slash-Command Dispatch and Monitoring Flow
Diagram: "Slash-Command and Rerun Execution Pipeline"

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UserComment["GitHub PR Comment / Slash Command"] --> SlashHandler["scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py"]
    SlashHandler --> CheckPerms["Verify CI_PERMISSIONS.json"]
    CheckPerms --> CheckGate["_check_rebase_gate() (Issue #21065)"]
    CheckGate --> Dispatch["Dispatch rerun-test.yml / Workflow Run"]
    Dispatch --> PreparePartitions["prepare-partitions job"]
    PreparePartitions --> PartitionScript["scripts/ci/partition_rerun_tests.py"]
    PartitionScript --> Matrix["Execution Matrix"]
    Matrix --> TestExecution["Runner execution with environment isolation"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml:1-175](), [.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json:1-18](), [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:58-130](), [scripts/ci/partition_rerun_tests.py:1-10]()

## Summary

SGLang's test infrastructure and CI/CD pipeline combine structured Python test registries (`test/run_suite.py`), multi-platform GitHub Actions workflows (CUDA, AMD ROCm, NPU), and robust gating mechanisms (`CODEOWNERS`, `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, and `slash_command_handler.py`). Together, they provide automated test partitioning, selective path-based execution, maintenance enforcement, and flexible manual rerun capabilities. [test/run_suite.py:1-35](), [.github/workflows/pr-test.yml:1-88](), [.github/CODEOWNERS:1-15](), [scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py:58-130]()

## Purpose and scope

This page documents the benchmarking tools, online serving measurement (`sglang.benchmark.serving`) [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-13](), single-batch server measurement (`sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`), offline throughput benchmarking (`sglang.benchmark.offline_throughput`), runtime profiling (`SchedulerProfilerManager`, `ProfileManager`) [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py:53-103](), [python/sglang/srt/utils/profile_utils.py:73-90](), CI disaggregation test harnesses [scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh:1-12](), [scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml:1-20](), and evaluation utilities within the `benchmark/` directory.

Sources: [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-58](), [scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh:1-12](), [scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml:1-20]()

## 1. Overview of SGLang Benchmarking Architecture

The SGLang codebase establishes multiple performance measurement and stress-testing execution paths:

- `sglang.benchmark.serving` provides an online benchmark client for dynamic HTTP requests supporting TTFT, ITL, goodput, and reasoning stream token accounting [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-13](), [test/registered/bench_fn/test_bench_serving_reasoning_stream.py:1-9](). The legacy `sglang.bench_serving` module re-exports this implementation.
- `sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server` measures single-batch execution performance through a server's HTTP interface.
- `sglang.benchmark.offline_throughput` measures offline throughput using `Engine` and `Runtime` backends.
- CI Slurm test orchestration (`scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh` and `nightly-configs.yaml`) automates multi-node disaggregated benchmarking (prefill and decode over MORI or custom transport layers) with integrated accuracy gates [scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh:1-12](), [scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml:48-66]().

Sources: [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-13](), [scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh:1-12](), [scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml:48-66]()

## 2. The Benchmarking Tools Suite

| Tool or Component | Implementation | Measurement Boundary | Evidence in Codebase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online Serving Benchmark | `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py` | Dynamic requests sent to an HTTP backend | Module documentation describes online serving with dynamic requests [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-13](). |
| Single-Batch Server Benchmark | `python/sglang/benchmark/one_batch_server.py` | One batch through server HTTP interface | CLI examples accept batch size, sequence lengths, profiling, and output paths. |

| CI Disaggregation Harness | `scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh` | Multi-node disaggregated serving sweep | Launches prefill/decode servers and executes concurrency sweeps [scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh:1-12](). |
| Runtime Profiling | `SchedulerProfilerManager`, `ProfileManager` | Scheduler forward steps and stage transitions | Configures profiling triggers based on `ForwardMode` [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py:53-103](), [python/sglang/srt/utils/profile_utils.py:73-90](). |

## 3. Online Serving Benchmark (`bench_serving`) and Reasoning Streams

`sglang.benchmark.serving` implements the online benchmark CLI, importing asynchronous HTTP support (`_create_bench_client_session`), dataset selection, goodput calculations, and endpoint resolution helpers [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-58]().

### Request and Result Records

- `RequestFuncInput`: Stores prompt data, API URL, lengths, model/LoRA names, image data, and extra request fields [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:90-102]().
- `RequestFuncOutput`: Records generated text, success flag, total latency, TTFT (`ttft`), TPOT (`tpot`), inter-token latencies (`itl`), cached token counts, and speculative decoding acceptance metrics [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:104-128]().

### Reasoning Models Streaming Support

Modern reasoning models (such as DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3 reasoning, or Kimi-K2) stream chain-of-thought tokens via specialized payload fields like `delta.reasoning_content` or `delta.reasoning` [test/registered/bench_fn/test_bench_serving_reasoning_stream.py:1-9](). Helper functions such as `_combine_openai_chat_content()` aggregate reasoning chunks with standard content so TTFT, ITL, and generated token counts remain accurate during benchmarking [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:149-156]().

### Serving Benchmark Data Flow

Title: Serving Benchmark Data Flow
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CLI["CLIParser"] --> Dataset["get_dataset"]
    Dataset --> Input["RequestFuncInput"]
    Input --> Backend["ASYNC_REQUEST_FUNCS"]
    Backend --> HTTP["HttpEndpoint"]
    HTTP --> Response["StreamedResponse"]
    Response --> Output["RequestFuncOutput"]
    Output --> Metrics["GoodputAndLatencyMetrics"]
```
Sources: [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:6-156](), [test/registered/bench_fn/test_bench_serving_reasoning_stream.py:1-9]()

## 4. Workload Datasets and Distribution Management

Workloads are managed through `DatasetRow` and `get_dataset()` [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:44-45](), [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/common.py:21-40](). Supported datasets include random, ShareGPT, OpenAI, image, MMMU, Mooncake, custom, agentic trace, and generated shared-prefix workloads.

- **Generated Shared Prefix:** `GeneratedSharedPrefixDataset.from_args()` configures group distributions (`uniform` or `zipf`), prompt lengths, and cache paths under `~/.cache/sglang/benchmark` [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/generated_shared_prefix.py:40-163](). `_zipf_group_probs()` builds rank-based Zipf probability vectors [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/generated_shared_prefix.py:24-37]().
- **Image & Multimodal Datasets:** `ImageDataset.load()` initializes processors and samples image requests with flexible resolution bounds (`parse_image_resolution`, `parse_random_image_resolution`) [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/image.py:22-127]().

Sources: [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/common.py:21-40](), [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/generated_shared_prefix.py:24-163](), [python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/image.py:22-127]()

## 5. Profiling Utilities and Server Diagnostics

### `SchedulerProfilerManager` and `ProfileManager`

`SchedulerProfilerManager` coordinates scheduler-side profiling. It integrates with `ProfileManager` using `_StageBasedTrigger` to start or stop PyTorch profiling based on `ForwardMode` transitions (`prefill`, `decode`) [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py:53-103](), [python/sglang/srt/utils/profile_utils.py:73-90]().

### CUDA Graph Capture Traces

`export_cuda_graph_capture_trace()` exports Chrome-compatible traces when `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE` is set [python/sglang/srt/utils/profile_utils.py:37-70]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the test runner infrastructure, model comparison utilities, accuracy test runners, test kits, output verification mechanisms, and evaluation scripts used across the SGLang test suite [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:1-53](). It covers the architectural contrast between Hugging Face baseline runners (`HFRunner`) and SGLang Runtime runners (`SRTRunner`), how integration test servers are launched and managed, how accuracy and correctness are verified via numerical tolerances and metadata assertions, how attention method unittests and end-to-end evaluation scripts (`run_sgl_eval`, `run_eval`, and Evalscope integration) are structured, and how modular test kits validate correctness, log probabilities, and structured outputs [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:38-55](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:183-211]().

Sources: [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:1-55](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:183-211]()

---

## 1. Test Runner Architecture: HFRunner vs SRTRunner

SGLang regression and correctness tests frequently rely on side-by-side execution models to verify that SGLang's serving optimizations (such as RadixAttention, custom kernels, and distributed parallelisms) produce identical outputs to reference implementations [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:1-53](). This comparison is typically structured around two primary runner abstractions:

- **`HFRunner`**: Instantiates a standard Hugging Face `PreTrainedModel` (or `AutoModelForCausalLM`) in native PyTorch. It acts as the ground-truth numerical reference for exact logits, hidden states, and token generation sequences without custom serving engine overhead.
- **`SRTRunner`**: Initializes the SGLang Runtime engine or spawns a background SGLang serving daemon (`sglang.launch_server`) via `popen_launch_server`, handling tokenization, batch scheduling, KV cache allocation, and distributed model execution [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:38-43](), [test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_moe_backend.py:25-44]().

### Runner Process Model and Fixture Lifecycles

Complex architectures such as disaggregated serving, multi-node expert parallelism, and NPU multi-node clusters rely on specialized test fixtures to manage multi-process coordination (e.g., separate worker instances linked via bootstrap ports, NCCL rendezvous ports, and Kubernetes pods) [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_performance_utils.py:16-37]().

The test runner orchestrates server bootstrapping through a structured lifecycle:

| Phase | Observable Behavior | Code Entity / Implementation |

| Teardown | Terminates process trees and cleans up temporary IPC channels. | `kill_process_tree()` [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_performance_utils.py:16]() |

## 2. Accuracy Test Runner and Evaluation Framework

Evaluation runners execute standardized benchmark tasks (such as `gsm8k`, `gpqa_diamond`, `aime25`, `mmlu`) against a running SGLang server instance to verify end-to-end correctness under different parallelization and serving topologies [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:55-66]().

### Evaluation Scripts, Evalscope, and Tolerances

Evaluation utilities like `run_eval`, `run_sgl_eval`, and `run_evalscope` accept parameters governing evaluation configurations, datasets, batch sizes, and timeouts [python/sglang/test/ascend/test_ascend_utils.py:24](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:183-211](). 

Threshold calculations factor in dataset-specific fluctuation tolerances rather than flat percentage drops. For instance, `get_accuracy_threshold` computes acceptable score floors based on absolute question count tolerances for datasets like `gpqa_diamond` or `aime25` [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:83-94]().

```python
def get_accuracy_threshold(datasets, baseline_accuracy):
    dataset = datasets[0] if datasets else None
    if dataset in DATASET_FLUCTUATION and dataset in DATASET_QUESTION_COUNTS:
        fluctuation = DATASET_FLUCTUATION[dataset] / DATASET_QUESTION_COUNTS[dataset]
        return baseline_accuracy - fluctuation
    return baseline_accuracy * ACCURACY_TOLERANCE
```

Sources: [python/sglang/test/ascend/test_ascend_utils.py:24](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:83-94]()

Sources: [python/sglang/test/ascend/test_ascend_utils.py:24](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:83-211]()

## 3. Modular Test Kits and Attention Method Unittests

SGLang structures its test suite around reusable test structures and configuration parameters (`test/kits/`, `test/registered/`) that inject specific testing capabilities into test case classes without code duplication.

### Key Test Categories and Frameworks

- **Attention Method Unittests (`test/kits/attention_unittest/`)**: Validates individual attention mechanisms across platforms and backends by feeding controlled tensors and comparing outputs against reference implementations (e.g., `dense_attention.py`, `dsa_attention.py`, `dsv4_attention.py`, `gdn_attention.py`) [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py:70-81](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsa_attention.py:64-66](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsv4_attention.py:73-86](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/gdn_attention.py:49-62]().
- **Quantization and Loader Test Suites (`test/registered/unit/model_loader/`)**: Validates weight loading, checkpoint quantization parsing, and online quantization conversion [test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_moe_backend.py:18-44]().
- **Backend Conformance Suites (`test/registered/backends/`)**: Tests specialized MoE and attention backends like `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`, DeepEP, and Triton kernels [test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_moe_backend.py:18-44]().

Sources: [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py:70-81](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsa_attention.py:64-66](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsv4_attention.py:73-86](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/gdn_attention.py:49-62](), [test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_moe_backend.py:18-44]()

## 4. Output Comparison, Tolerances, and Metadata Verification

Verification scripts and attention method tests compare execution outputs against reference implementations or ground truth using numerical tolerances and metadata assertions [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:38-55]().

### Numerical Tolerances and Attention Backends

Different attention backends and quantization regimes (such as FP8, MXFP4, and sparse kernels) specify explicit absolute (`atol`) and relative (`rtol`) tolerances to account for hardware accumulation differences across microarchitectures [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py:35-36](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsa_attention.py:52-61](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsv4_attention.py:62-69](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/gdn_attention.py:44-46]().

| Attention Method / Kernel | Typical ATOL | Typical RTOL | Notes / Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dense MHA / MLA | `3e-2` | `3e-2` | Standard half/bfloat16 precision comparison [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py:35-36]() |
| DSA Sparse Prefill | `1.6e-1` to `2.0e-1` | `1.6e-1` to `2.0e-1` | FP8 KV cache quantization noise absorption [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsa_attention.py:52-61]() |
| DSV4 SWA | `8e-2` to `1e-1` | `8e-2` to `1e-1` | FlashMLA sliding window attention with sink scaling [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsv4_attention.py:62-69]() |
| GDNAttn / KDA | `3e-2` to `5e-2` | `3e-2` to `5e-2` | Linear attention and gated delta net states [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/gdn_attention.py:44-46]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py:35-36](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsa_attention.py:52-61](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dsv4_attention.py:62-69](), [python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/gdn_attention.py:44-46]()

### Logprob and Metadata Validation

Output verification inspects internal request metadata structures generated during batch processing. For instance, evaluation assertion checks validate score thresholds and internal metrics such as average speculative acceptance length (`accept_rate`) or throughput [test/registered/npu/performance/deepseek_v4_flash/test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_8p_in8k_out1k_50ms.py:129-130]().

# Summary

The SGLang test infrastructure combines robust process launchers (`popen_launch_server`), runner comparisons (`HFRunner` vs `SRTRunner`), modular test classes, attention unittests with explicit numerical tolerances, and automated evaluation runners (`run_eval`, `run_sgl_eval`, `run_evalscope`) to guarantee correctness across complex multi-node, disaggregated, and quantized deployments [python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:1-55](), [python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py:183-211](), [test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_trtllm_gen_moe_backend.py:18-64]().

## Tensor Dumper System

The tensor dumper is exposed through `DumperConfig` and `_Dumper` in `python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py`. The implementation provides configuration parsing and validation; its unit tests exercise these behaviors and import additional dumper helpers. [python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:33-70]()[python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:136-190]()[test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py:17-40]()

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py`, `test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py`

### Dumper Configuration (`DumperConfig`)

`DumperConfig` is a frozen dataclass whose fields control dumping enablement, filtering, output directory and destinations, value/grad capture, experiment naming and cleanup, collective timeout, server port, source patching, grafting, and parallel-rank filename tags. Defaults include `enable=False`, `dir="/tmp/dumper"`, `collective_timeout=60`, and `server_port="-1"`. [python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:136-169]()

Configuration values are type-checked by `_BaseConfig._verify_types`. `from_env()` derives environment variable names from the config prefix and field names (`DUMPER_` prefix). Empty or whitespace-only environment values use field defaults, booleans recognize `"true"` and `"1"`, and integer defaults trigger integer parsing. `from_kv_pairs()` parses `key=value` entries, rejecting unknown keys and ensuring correct type coercion. [python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:36-70]()[python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:81-130]()[python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:171-175]()

`with_defaults()` applies code-provided defaults only when the corresponding environment variable is unset. Tests verify environment parsing, type errors, whitespace handling, and explicit overrides. [python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:72-79]()[test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py:74-142]()

| Configuration Area | Fields Shown in `DumperConfig` |
|---|---|
| Enablement and Selection | `enable`, `filter` |
| Output | `dir`, `enable_output_file`, `enable_output_console`, `exp_name`, `cleanup_previous` |
| Captured Data | `enable_value`, `enable_grad`, `enable_model_value`, `enable_model_grad` |
| Distributed Operation | `collective_timeout`, `include_parallel_rank_in_filename` |
| Runtime Control and Patching | `server_port`, `non_intrusive_mode`, `source_patcher_config` |
| Grafting | `grafter_enable`, `grafter_role`, `grafter_b2t_filter`, `grafter_t2b_filter`, `grafter_master_address`, `grafter_master_port`, world sizes, backend, group, timeout, and transform path |

[python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:136-169]()

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py`, `test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py`

### `_Dumper`, Dumping, and Source-Patched Capture

The dumper module imports PyTorch, distributed PyTorch, ZeroMQ, HTTP server support, and runtime context accessors like `get_parallel`, `get_server_args`, and `get_serving`. Serialization and value-handling helpers include `_torch_save`, `_materialize_value`, `_map_tensor`, and `_deepcopy_or_clone`. [python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py:1-31]()[test/registered/debug_utils/test_dumper.py:17-40]()

End-to-end tests document YAML source-patch configurations that insert `dumper.dump(...)` calls into selected model forward methods (such as Qwen3 MoE forward paths), enabling numerical consistency checks across parallel configurations. [test/registered/debug_utils/test_engine_dumper_comparator_e2e.py:1-14]()

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/dumper.py`, `test/registered/debug_utils/test_engine_dumper_comparator_e2e.py`

## Dump Comparator and Weight Checker

### `WeightChecker` and `ComparableWeight` Framework

SGLang provides rigorous weight verification and comparison tools via `WeightChecker` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py`) and `ComparableWeight` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py`). These components validate model weights, compute checksums across distributed ranks, and compare weight states (useful for RL training workflows and distributed parameter verification). [python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py:110-152]()[python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:30-51]()

`WeightChecker` supports actions such as `snapshot`, `reset_tensors`, `compare`, `checksum`, and `raw_checksum`. Non-persistent buffers (such as rotary embedding cosine/sine caches) are filtered out via `_is_skip_weight_check()` to prevent false positives in weight comparison and checksum calculations. [python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py:60-80]()[python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py:126-152]()

`ComparableWeight` subclasses handle precision-specific comparison logic:
- `RawComparable`: Performs bitwise-equal comparisons on standard raw tensors using chunked streaming (`CHUNK_NUMEL = 64 * 1024 * 1024`) to limit peak GPU memory usage [python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:20-21]()[python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:123-140]().
- `Fp8BlockComparable`: Handles DeepSeek-style block-quantized FP8 weights (`float8_e4m3fn` with block scales), un-shuffling weights when necessary and performing dequantization chunks for tolerance-aware numerical comparisons [python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:52-122]().

`compare_weights()` computes `CompareResult` (equality status, maximum absolute error, mean absolute error, and number of elements exceeding combined per-side tolerance based on ULP) across chunks [python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:23-28]()[python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:141-172]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py`, `python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py`

### Weight Checking and Comparison Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B1["WeightChecker.handle()"] -->|action=snapshot| B2["_snapshot()"]
    B1 -->|action=compare| B3["_compare()"]
    B1 -->|action=checksum| B4["_compute_checksum()"]
    B3 --> B5["_build_check_entries()"]
    B5 --> B6["select_comparable_weight()"]
    B6 -->|FP8 block quant| B7["Fp8BlockComparable"]
    B6 -->|Raw / Standard| B8["RawComparable"]
    B7 --> B9["compare_weights()"]
    B8 --> B9
    B9 --> B10["CompareResult"]
```
Sources: `python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker.py:110-204`, `python/sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py:30-172`

## Debug Utilities and CUDA Coredump Handling

### Request-Time Instrumentation

`req_time_stats.py` defines request-stage names and configuration (tokenizer, API dispatch, request processing, prefill, decode, multimodal encode, disaggregation, speculative decoding, and CPU batch execution stages). Each `RequestStageConfig` carries a stage name, trace hierarchy level, and timing flags [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:88-227]().

Wall-clock and performance-counter offsets are calibrated to convert performance counters into realtime timestamps across threaded boundaries [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:56-85](). Unit tests ensure that sentinel timestamps (`0.0`) remain unchanged upon serialization and that latency attributes are appropriately derived [test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py:1-134]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py`, `test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py`

### Server Crash-Dump Test

`test_crash_dump.py` exercises the server `--crash-dump-folder` option by launching a server, simulating a crash condition, and inspecting output pickle files (`*/crash_dump_*.pkl`) containing `server_args` and active request state [test/registered/debug_utils/test_crash_dump.py:24-115]().

Sources: `test/registered/debug_utils/test_crash_dump.py`

## Purpose and Scope

The simulator located under `tools/sglang-simulator` evaluates LLM serving performance, scheduling efficiency, and memory management without executing actual model forward passes. It reuses SGLang's core `Scheduler`, prefix caching, and memory management subsystems while substituting the model forward execution step with a latency predictor. Its functional scope covers trace replay, synthetic workloads, multiple predictor modes, and the generation of serving-compatible performance metrics. 

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py`

## Architecture and Component Integration

The simulator bridges workload generation with SGLang's production scheduling components. In the live runtime, requests flow through `Scheduler`, populating `ScheduleBatch` structures which are subsequently lowered into `ForwardBatch` objects for `ModelRunner` execution [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-76](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48](). The simulator intercepts this pipeline at the model execution boundary, querying a latency predictor instead of invoking tensor-parallel GPU kernels.

### Component Overview

- **Workload Input:** Parses trace logs or generates synthetic request streams with configurable arrival distributions.
- **Scheduling Engine (`Scheduler`):** Manages waiting queues, prefill/decode scheduling phases, and request state transitions [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-76]().
- **Batch Representation (`ScheduleBatch` & `ForwardBatch`):** Encapsulates token allocations, prompt lengths, and batch metadata [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().
- **Latency Predictor:** Replaces the GPU forward pass by estimating duration based on batch size, input lengths, and decoding step counts.
- **Prefix Cache (`UnifiedRadixCache` / `BasePrefixCache`):** Reuses SGLang's prefix matching and cache management logic to simulate hit rates and memory reclamation [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:136-186]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `python/sglang/mem_cache/common.py`

### High-Level Dataflow

**Diagram 1: Workload-to-simulation flow and runtime boundary**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Workload["TraceReplayWorkload"] --> Requests["RequestArrivals"]
    Requests --> Scheduler["Scheduler"]
    Scheduler --> ScheduleBatch["ScheduleBatch"]
    ScheduleBatch --> ForwardBatch["ForwardBatch"]
    ForwardBatch --> Predictor["LatencyPredictor"]
    Predictor --> SimTime["SimulatedElapsedDuration"]
    SimTime --> Metrics["ServingCompatibleMetrics"]
    Scheduler --> Cache["RadixCachePrefixMatcher"]
    Cache --> Scheduler
```

This dataflow outlines how workload inputs leverage production scheduling structures while redirecting execution flow through a latency predictor.

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`

## Core Components and Data Structures

### Scheduler and ScheduleBatch

The `Scheduler` class manages request admission, chunked prefill chunking limits, and dispatch queues [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-76](). `ScheduleBatch` stores the high-level scheduling metadata on the CPU, tracking active requests, token counts, and completion states [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().

### ForwardBatch and ModelRunner

`ForwardBatch` holds tensor-level batch data constructed via `ForwardBatch.init_new` [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48](). In the simulator, the tensor execution managed by `ModelRunner` is bypassed or mocked using predicted delays.

### Memory Pools and Prefix Caches

The simulator integrates with SGLang's memory subsystem, utilizing functions such as `match_kv_cache`, `free_kv_row_segments`, and allocator interfaces to accurately simulate cache hits, prefix sharing, and memory pressure [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:63-134]().

**Diagram 2: Natural-language simulator roles mapped to runtime code entities (`Scheduler`, `ScheduleBatch`, `ForwardBatch`, `ModelRunner`)**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    SimInput[""Workload Request Input""] --> Sched["Scheduler"]
    Sched --> SchedBatch["ScheduleBatch"]
    SchedBatch --> FwdBatch["ForwardBatch"]
    FwdBatch --> ModelExec["ModelRunner Execution"]
    FwdBatch --> SimPredictor["Latency Predictor Module"]
    SchedBatch --> CacheOps["BasePrefixCache match_kv_cache and Allocators"]
    CacheOps --> SchedBatch
```

This diagram associates conceptual simulator roles with specific codebase entities (`Scheduler`, `ScheduleBatch`, `ForwardBatch`, `ModelRunner`, `BasePrefixCache`) [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-76](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py`

## Predictor Modes and Workload Generation

The simulator supports various operational modes to analyze performance under different conditions:
- **Trace Replay:** Reads historical request timestamps, prompt lengths, and output lengths from datasets [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:77-128]().
- **Synthetic Workloads:** Generates requests following Poisson arrival processes and configurable distributions for input/output token counts.
- **Predictor Modes:** Ranges from analytical formula-based predictors (modeling FLOPs and memory bandwidth limits) to empirical lookup tables calibrated against real hardware runs.

Sources: `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py`

## Serving-Compatible Metrics

The simulator collects and reports serving metrics identical to production SGLang endpoints:
- **Time to First Token (TTFT):** Measures queue waiting time plus prefill execution/prediction duration.
- **Time per Output Token (TPOT) / Inter-Token Latency (ITL):** Evaluates decode step durations across batch sizes.
- **Request Latency and Throughput:** Summarizes end-to-end request turnaround times and completed tokens per second.
- **Cache Hit Rate:** Tracks prefix sharing effectiveness via radix caches [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:136-186]().

**Diagram 3: Metrics boundary mapping natural execution phases to code-level measurement collectors (`SchedulerReqTimeStats`, `SchedulerMetricsCollector`)**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Arrivals["Client Request Arrivals"] --> Schedule["Scheduler and ScheduleBatch"]
    Schedule --> Estimate["LatencyPredictor Estimation"]
    Estimate --> RequestTiming["Simulated Request Timing and SchedulerReqTimeStats"]
    Schedule --> CacheState["BasePrefixCache and SchedulerMetricsCollector"]
    CacheState --> CacheMetric["Cache Measurement"]
    RequestTiming --> Output["Simulator Metrics Output"]
    CacheMetric --> Output
```

This diagram bridges the natural-space metric collection steps to specific code classes like `SchedulerReqTimeStats` and `SchedulerMetricsCollector` [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:139-148]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py`

## Summary and References

The SGLang simulator provides a fast, hardware-independent environment for evaluating scheduling policies, memory management, and prefix caching by replacing model execution with latency estimation.

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py` — Scheduler process and dispatch loop implementation [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:13-76]().
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py` — ScheduleBatch and ForwardBatch batch management structures [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py` — Cache matching, retraction, and prefix key helpers [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:63-186]().
- `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py` — Serving benchmark workload generation and client session management [python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py:77-128]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py`, `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py`

## Purpose and scope

This parent page provides a high-level overview of the release automation and deployment pipelines for Python wheels, deep-extension packages (such as DeepGEMM), and Docker images within SGLang. The infrastructure relies on GitHub Actions workflows—such as [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml]()—and container specifications to package custom kernels, core runtimes, and optimized execution environments.

For installation and local deployment procedures, see [Installation and Deployment](#2).

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-45](), [docker/Dockerfile:1-35]()

---

## Overview

Release automation separates artifact compilation from publishing. Build workflows compile target-specific binaries across architecture and Python version matrices (such as `x86_64` and `aarch64` architectures), run validation test suites on specialized GPU runners via jobs like `test-cu130`, and upload verified artifacts to PyPI or GitHub release assets.

Container deployment pipelines complement wheel automation by building multi-stage Docker images tailored for specific hardware configurations using tools like `uv` for isolated package environments.

### Release Architecture Overview
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    WorkflowTrigger["WorkflowDispatch"] --> KernelWorkflow[".github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml"]
    KernelWorkflow --> BuildMatrix["build-cu130-matrix"]
    BuildMatrix --> BuildScript["build_sgl_deep_gemm.sh"]
    BuildMatrix --> TestJob["test-cu130"]
    TestJob --> PyPIUpload["PyPIAndGitHubRelease"]
```
Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-105]()

---

## Wheel Build and Release Pipeline

SGLang builds and releases multiple wheel packages, including the core framework (`sglang`), `sgl-kernel`, and extension packages like `sgl-deep-gemm`. The build scripts handle compiler flags, architecture targeting (e.g., `sm90`, `sm100`), and PyTorch ABI linking as defined in configuration files like `python/pyproject.toml` [python/pyproject.toml:1-10]().

For detailed documentation on the sgl-kernel wheel builds, platform matrices, and release workflows, see [Wheel Build and Release Pipeline](#16.1).

| Configuration / Script | Target Component | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `python/pyproject.toml` | Core `sglang` | Metadata, project dependencies, and build-system definitions [python/pyproject.toml:1-15]() |
| `.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml` | `sgl-deep-gemm` | Compilation and test-gated release workflow for DeepGEMM custom CUDA kernels [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-50]() |

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:1-15](), [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-50]()

---

## Docker Build and Release Pipeline

Container image generation uses multi-stage Dockerfiles to isolate build toolchains from runtime environments. These pipelines ensure that dependencies such as `torch`, `flashinfer`, and custom kernels are correctly pinned and compiled against matching CUDA driver versions, leveraging BuildKit parallel builder stages.

For detailed documentation on container variants, multi-stage build scripts, and cross-platform publishing, see [Docker Build and Release Pipeline](#16.2).

### Docker Build Pipeline Scope
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DockerContext["ContainerSource"] --> DockerBase["docker/Dockerfile"]
    DockerBase --> ParallelStages["ParallelBuilderStages"]
    ParallelStages --> RuntimeArtifact["RuntimeContainerImage"]
```
Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:1-40]()

---

## Version Management

Version synchronization across packages relies on centralized version configuration and release coordination scripts. For extension modules and core packages, version strings are dynamically derived or updated during branch cutting and tagging operations (e.g., writing target versions into files like `DeepGEMM/sgl_deep_gemm/VERSION`) [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:81-85]().

For detailed explanations of version numbering schemes, branch cutting policies, and update scripts, see [Version Management](#16.3).

### Version Coordination Flow
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    GitTag["GitVersionTag"] --> VersionScript["VersionUpdateScript"]
    VersionScript --> VersionFile["VersionMetadataFiles"]
    VersionFile --> PackageRelease["PackageDistribution"]
```
Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:11-15](), [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:81-85]()

---

## Summary

Release and deployment automation coordinates multi-architecture wheel compilation, rigorous GPU-backed test gating, multi-stage Docker image builds, and version lifecycle management. 

For deep dives into each subsystem, refer to the child pages:
- [Wheel Build and Release Pipeline](#16.1)
