## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the wheel-related build, testing, and release validation workflows for SGLang and its tightly coupled extension packages (`sgl-kernel`, `sgl-deep-gemm`). It covers the platform matrices, CI artifact distribution, and GitHub Actions / PyPI release pipelines.

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-180](), [python/pyproject.toml:1-105]()

---

## Package Ecosystem and Distribution Mapping

The release infrastructure manages separate packages that share a coordinated release cadence or follow independent versioning schemas. The core `sglang` package, `sgl-kernel`, and `sgl-deep-gemm` are built, packaged, and tested via specialized workflows.

| Distribution or component | Workflow-visible source or artifact location | Role supported by the codebase |
|---|---|---|
| `sglang` | Repository checkout (`python/`) | Main project package, containerizing SRT (SGLang Runtime), CLI, and Python entrypoints [python/pyproject.toml:11-16]() |
| `sgl-kernel` | `python/sglang/kernels/aot/dist/` | Custom CUDA/ROCm operator kernel wheels downloaded during CI/CD test phases [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-42]() |
| `sgl-deep-gemm` | `DeepGEMM/sgl_deep_gemm/` and `DeepGEMM/dist/` | Independently versioned DeepSeek GEMM kernel package built and validated against specific Torch ABIs [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:68-103]() |

**Diagram: Package Names Mapped to Workflow Entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Repo["Repository checkout"] --> SGLANG["sglang"]
  Repo --> AOT["python/sglang/kernels/aot/dist/"]
  AOT --> KERNEL["sgl-kernel wheel artifact"]
  DeepGEMM["DeepGEMM checkout"] --> VERSION["sgl_deep_gemm/VERSION"]
  DeepGEMM --> DIST["DeepGEMM/dist/"]
  DIST --> DEEPWHEEL["sgl-deep-gemm wheel artifact"]
  KERNEL --> DIFFUSION["release-whl-deepgemm.yml"]
  DEEPWHEEL --> DEEPTEST["test-cu130"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:68-103](), [python/pyproject.toml:11-105]()

---

## sgl-deep-gemm Build and Release Automation

The `Release sgl-deep-gemm` workflow (`release-whl-deepgemm.yml`) is manually triggered via `workflow_dispatch` and accepts a target version, build target (`all` or `cu130`), source branch, validation flags, and test bypass flags. The workflow explicitly pins `TORCH_VER` to `2.14.1` because the precompiled `_C.so` dynamic library links against this specific Torch ABI [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-42]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:1-42]()

### Build Matrix and Execution Environment

The build job executes only inside the `sgl-project/sglang` repository when the target parameter is `all` or `cu130`. The matrix targets Python `3.12`, CUDA `13.0`, and architectures `x86_64` and `aarch64`, mapped to runner nodes `x64-kernel-build-node` and `arm-kernel-build-node` respectively.

| Matrix dimension | Values shown | Build mapping |
|---|---|---|
| Python Version | `3.12` | Consistent across build matrix legs [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:49-52]() |
| CUDA Version | `13.0` | Bound to `cu130` toolchain containers [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:45-53]() |
| Architecture | `x86_64`, `aarch64` | Routed to `x64-kernel-build-node` / `arm-kernel-build-node` [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:53-59]() |
| Version String | User input | Written directly into `DeepGEMM/sgl_deep_gemm/VERSION` [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:81-84]() |

**Diagram: DeepGEMM Build Jobs and Artifact Handoff**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISPATCH["workflow_dispatch: release-whl-deepgemm.yml"] --> MATRIX["build-cu130-matrix"]
  MATRIX --> X64["x86_64: x64-kernel-build-node"]
  MATRIX --> ARM["aarch64: arm-kernel-build-node"]
  X64 --> CHECKOUT["Checkout DeepGEMM submodule"]
  ARM --> CHECKOUT
  CHECKOUT --> SETVERSION["Write sgl_deep_gemm/VERSION"]
  SETVERSION --> BUILDSCRIPT["scripts/build_sgl_deep_gemm.sh"]
  BUILDSCRIPT --> DIST["DeepGEMM/dist/*.whl"]
  BUILDSCRIPT --> PYPI_DIST["DeepGEMM/dist-pypi/*.whl"]
  DIST --> ARTIFACT["Upload wheel artifacts"]
  PYPI_DIST --> ARTIFACT
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:44-103]()

### Post-Build Hardware Validation

Unless `skip_tests` is enabled, the `test-cu130` job depends on the build matrix output, fetching the architecture-specific wheels. The test matrix runs on high-performance runners matching compute capabilities (`sm90`, `sm100`, etc.).

| Test target | Runner | Wheel architecture | Timeout (min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sm90` | `8-gpu-h200` | `x86_64` | 60 |
| `sm100` | `8-gpu-b200` | `x86_64` | 180 |
| `sm100-aarch64` | `4-gpu-gb300` | `aarch64` | 180 |

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:104-128]()

**Diagram: Artifact Validation Path**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  BUILD["build-cu130-matrix"] --> WHEELS["deepgemm-wheel-cuda13.0 artifacts"]
  WHEELS --> TEST["test-cu130"]
  TEST --> X86["x86_64 wheel tests"]
  TEST --> ARM["aarch64 wheel tests"]
  X86 --> SM90["sm90: 8-gpu-h200"]
  X86 --> SM100["sm100: 8-gpu-b200"]
  ARM --> GB300["sm100-aarch64: 4-gpu-gb300"]
  TEST --> ABI["TORCH_VER=2.14.1 and cu130 dependencies"]
  TEST --> BIND["LD_BIND_NOW=1 symbol validation"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:104-180]()

## sgl-kernel Wheel Build Pipeline and Platform Matrix

The `sgl-kernel` package handles performance-critical operators. Its build jobs are triggered during PR evaluation and release pipelines, compiling custom CUDA extensions across architectures (e.g., `SM90`, `SM100`). In pipeline executions, prebuilt kernel wheels matching `wheel-python3.11-cuda*` are downloaded directly into `python/sglang/kernels/aot/dist/` [python/pyproject.toml:1-105]().

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:1-105]()

### Platform Constraints and Pyproject Configurations

Dependency resolution varies depending on the target platform. Standard CUDA builds use `python/pyproject.toml`, while alternate platforms employ dedicated configuration files (e.g., `pyproject_xpu.toml` for Intel XPU, `pyproject_other.toml` for CPU or specialized hardware backends) [python/pyproject.toml:1-105](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:1-100]().

**Diagram: `sgl-kernel` CI Artifact Consumption**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CHANGE["check-changes: sgl_kernel"] --> BUILD["PR Test Extra: sgl-kernel-build-wheels"]
  BUILD --> BUILDER["x64-kernel-build-node"]
  ARTIFACT["wheel-python3.11-cuda* artifact"] --> DOWNLOAD["release-whl-deepgemm.yml"]
  DOWNLOAD --> DESTINATION["python/sglang/kernels/aot/dist/"]
  DESTINATION --> INSTALL["ci_install_dependency.sh diffusion"]
  INSTALL --> TEST["Diffusion test suite"]
```

Sources: [python/pyproject.toml:1-105](), [python/pyproject_xpu.toml:1-100]()

## GitHub Release and PyPI Publication Workflow

Releases are serialized through GitHub Actions workflows that handle version stamping, tag validation, artifact collection, and PyPI publication. Concurrency locks (e.g., `group: release-sgl-deepgemm-${{ github.ref }}`) are enforced to cancel redundant in-progress releases on the same ref [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:34-36]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:3-36]()

**Diagram: Release Workflow Boundaries**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  INPUT["workflow_dispatch inputs"] --> BUILD["build-cu130-matrix"]
  BUILD --> ARTIFACTS["Upload DeepGEMM wheel artifacts"]
  ARTIFACTS --> TEST["test-cu130, unless skip_tests"]
  TEST --> GATE["release-cu130 test gate"]
  GATE -.-> PUBLISH["PyPI publication step"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:3-32](), [.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml:86-106]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the Docker image build processes, multi-stage builds, platform variants (AMD ROCm and Ascend NPU), release automation workflows, and container runtime startup orchestration. It details how Docker images are parameterized across GPU architectures (`GPU_ARCH`), how versioning and setuptools_scm pretend versions are injected during builds, and how nightly and tagged release pipelines publish and mirror images across registries. [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-115](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml:1-120](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:1-128]()

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-115](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml:1-120](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:1-128]()

---

## Docker Image Build Architecture and Variants

The `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` file establishes a flexible multi-stage build architecture where specific ROCm versions, PyTorch stacks, and hardware targets are selected via build arguments (`GPU_ARCH`). [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-115]()

| Image Variant / Stage | Base Image / Flavor Source | Notable Configuration & Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm `gfx942` | `BASE_IMAGE_942` (default `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904`) | Sets `BUILD_AITER_ALL=1`, `BUILD_MOONCAKE=1`, and pins `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`. [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:50-77]() |
| ROCm `gfx942-rocm720` | `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM720` (ROCm 7.2 PyTorch release) | Sets `BUILD_TRITON=1`, pins `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` and older `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`. [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:79-90]() |
| ROCm `gfx942-rocm724` | `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM724` (Python 3.12 + torch 2.11 stack) | Configures persistent `PIP_CONSTRAINT="/etc/sglang/constraints/torch-rocm.txt"` and enables `HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1` for ROCm IPC leak workarounds. [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:93-114]() |
| ROCm 10.0 / 10.1 flavors | `rocm1000-base` (built from `ubuntu:24.04`) | Pulls stable AMD ROCm wheel channels, supports `gfx942`, `gfx950`, and `gfx1250` bring-up. [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:17-27](), [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:57-64]() |

Optional build arguments also enable specialized integration features: `ENABLE_MORI=1` for MoRI multi-node transport, `ENABLE_NIXL=1` for prefill/decode disaggregation transfer backends, and `BUILD_UTLX=1` for SGLang TLX kernel compilation [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:29-48]().

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-115]()

---

## Multi-Stage Parallel Build Topology

The build pipeline leverages Docker BuildKit and named build stages corresponding to target architectures and software stacks. 

**Diagram: ROCm and Release Pipeline Build Architecture**
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subcode ["Workflow & Build Automation"]
    Rel1["release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml"]
    Rel2["release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml"]
    Script["amd_ci_start_container.sh"]
  end
  subcode2 ["Docker Build & Stages"]
    DockerFile["docker/rocm.Dockerfile"]
    Stage942["gfx942-rocm1000"]
    Stage950["gfx950-rocm1000"]
    Stage724["gfx942-rocm724"]
  end
  Rel1 -->|"docker build -f docker/rocm.Dockerfile"| DockerFile
  Rel2 -->|"build-arg GPU_ARCH"| DockerFile
  DockerFile --> Stage942
  DockerFile --> Stage950
  DockerFile --> Stage724
  Script -->|"docker run --device /dev/dri"| Stage942
```

Sources: [docker/rocm.Dockerfile:1-115](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml:107-118](), [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh:30-118]()

## Release Automation and Nightly Pipelines

Docker image publishing is automated through GitHub Actions workflows such as `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml` and `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml`. [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml:1-40](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:1-45]()

1. **Version Extraction**: Workflows execute `python3 scripts/release/get_version_tag.py --tag-only` to fetch semantic version tags from git history [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:69-74]().
2. **Pretend Version Injection**: To satisfy `setuptools_scm` during container builds without requiring full git shallow clone tag depth inside the container, a pretend version string (`PRETEND_VERSION="${VERSION}.dev${DATE}+g${COMMIT_HASH}"`) is passed via `--build-arg SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:80-90]().
3. **Registry Push & Mirroring**: Images are initially built and pushed to `rocm/sgl-dev` and subsequently tagged and mirrored to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` for public consumption [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:97-160]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml:64-136](), [.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml:69-160](), [scripts/release/get_version_tag.py:1-25]()

---

## Container Startup and CI Execution Environment

The script `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh` manages container startup for testing and CI pipelines. It detects GPU architecture (`mi30x` or `mi35x`) from Kubernetes hostnames or environment overrides (`AMD_CI_GPU_ARCH`), configures ROCm render device passthrough (`/dev/dri`), authenticates with Docker Hub using `retry_with_backoff`, and locates cached or remote images [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh:74-171]().

**Diagram: Container Startup and CI Execution Flow**
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subcode3 ["Container Runtime Startup"]
    StartScript["scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh"]
    FindImg["find_latest_image()"]
    LoginFn["retry_with_backoff()"]
    DevFlag["AMD_CI_RENDER_DEVICES"]
  end
  subcode4 ["CI Execution & Testing"]
    ExecScript["scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_exec.sh"]
    RunSuite["test/run_suite.py"]
    NightlyAMD[".github/workflows/nightly-test-amd.yml"]
  end
  StartScript --> FindImg
  StartScript --> LoginFn
  StartScript --> DevFlag
  StartScript -->|"Executes container"| ExecScript
  ExecScript --> RunSuite
  NightlyAMD -->|"Dispatches job"| StartScript
```

Sources: [scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh:1-171](), [test/run_suite.py:1-40](), [.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd.yml:1-50]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the version-management and release-coordination mechanisms visible in the codebase configuration: the manually dispatched SGLang version-bump workflow, release-branch creation, documentation-reference updates, and the test workflows coordinated around those operations [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:1-87`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:1-176`]().

Sources: [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:1-87`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:1-176`]()

## 1. Version Inputs and What the Workflows Establish

The `Bot Bump SGLang Version` workflow is manually dispatched with a required `new_version` string input. Its input description gives `0.5.3` and `0.5.3rc0` as examples [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:1-9`]().

The workflow passes the input to `scripts/release/bump_sglang_version.py`, then invokes `scripts/release/commit_and_pr.sh` with the product name, requested version, and generated branch name [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:42-50`]().

| Concern | What the supplied workflow shows |
|---|---|
| Input | Required `new_version` string; examples include `0.5.3` and `0.5.3rc0` [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:4-9`](). |
| Version update | Calls `python scripts/release/bump_sglang_version.py` with the input [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:42-45`](). |
| Branch | Creates a generated branch named with the `bot/bump-sglang-version-` prefix, the requested version, and a random suffix [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:31-40`](). |
| PR handoff | Calls `scripts/release/commit_and_pr.sh` with `SGLang`, the requested version, and the generated branch [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:46-50`](). |

Sources: [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:1-50`]()

## 2. Automated Version Bump and Test Coordination

The version-bump workflow checks out the repository, configures Git with the `sglang-bot` identity, generates a unique branch suffix, and exports the branch name for later workflow steps [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:21-50`]().

After the bump job, the workflow fans out to platform test workflows. NVIDIA, AMD, and NPU nightly workflows receive the generated branch through their `ref` input; AMD is explicitly asked to use `rocm10` [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:52-87`]().

```mermaid
    B --> E["branch_name output"]
    E --> F["nightly-test-nvidia.yml:ref"]
    E --> G["nightly-test-amd.yml:ref,rocm_version=rocm10"]
    E --> H["nightly-test-npu.yml:ref"]
    E --> I["pr-test-xeon.yml:ref"]
    E --> J["pr-test-xpu.yml:ref"]
```

## 3. Release Branch Cutting

The `Release Branch Cut` workflow is triggered manually. It requires `branch_name` and accepts an optional `commit_sha`; if no SHA is provided, the workflow uses the checked-out latest `main` commit [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:1-14`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:22-36`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:54-63`]().

The branch-name check requires a nonempty value. A name that does not start with `release/` produces a warning about the `release/vX.Y.Z` convention [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:38-52`]().

For the selected commit, the workflow verifies that the object exists and that it is an ancestor of `main`. It then checks whether the requested branch already exists remotely. If it does not, the workflow creates the branch from the validated commit, updates two documentation files, and pushes the branch [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:54-105`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:107-133`]().

| Stage | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Inputs | Required `branch_name`; optional `commit_sha` [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:3-14`](). |
| Commit selection and validation | Defaults to the checked-out `main` commit; rejects a missing Git object or a commit not on `main` [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:54-78`](). |
| Existing-branch handling | Checks remote heads and records whether the branch already exists [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:80-91`](). |
| Branch creation | Creates the branch from the validated commit when the branch is absent [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:93-105`](). |
| Documentation references | Extracts the version from the branch name and updates Git clone references in the installation and AMD platform documentation [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:107-125`](). |
| Push and handoff | Pushes a newly created branch and emits the requested branch name as a job output [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:127-138`](). |

Sources: [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:1-138`]()

### Documentation Update Behavior and Rerun Implications

For a new branch, the workflow derives `VERSION` by removing the `release/` prefix from the branch name. It applies `sed` substitutions to `docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx` and `docs/docs/hardware-platforms/amd_gpu.mdx`, replacing matching Git clone version references with that value [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:107-125`]().

Sources: [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:80-125`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:140-164`]()

The branch-cut workflow emits `branch_name` from the `cut-release-branch` job. Two reusable workflow jobs depend on that job: `run-pr-tests-nvidia` calls `pr-test.yml`, and `run-pr-tests-amd` calls `pr-test-amd.yml` [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:22-29`](), [`.github/workflows/release-branch-cut.yml:166-176`]().

```mermaid
    C --> D["Check remote release branch"]
    D -->| "missing" | E["Create branch from validated commit"]
    E --> F["Update docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx"]
    E --> G["Update docs/docs/hardware-platforms/amd_gpu.mdx"]

    G --> H
    D -->| "exists" | I["Skip branch creation and conditional updates"]

```

The version-bump and release-branch workflows serve distinct purposes. The bump workflow accepts a version string, runs the version-update and PR helper scripts, then passes its generated branch to a set of platform nightly and PR-test workflows [`.github/workflows/bot-bump-sglang-version.yml:1-87`]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page introduces how SGLang represents generation settings and how those settings relate to token selection, output limits, stopping behavior, and constrained decoding. It is a parent-page overview: detailed parameter semantics, logits processing, algorithms, and penalties are covered in the child pages. The request-level `SamplingParams` definition includes distribution settings, stop conditions, penalties, output limits, grammar constraints, and related options [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-165]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-165]()

---

## Overview

At a high level, generation settings travel with a request and guide how the runtime selects and stops output tokens. `SamplingParams` carries both sampling-distribution controls—such as `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, and `min_p`—and controls for output length, stop conditions, penalties, and structured constraints [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:125-158](). The runtime orchestrates batched sampling via `SamplingBatchInfo` and executes token selection through classes like `Sampler` [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-134](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-142](). This page does not specify the complete runtime execution order or individual sampling kernels; see [Logits Processing Pipeline](#17.2) and [Sampling Algorithms](#17.3) for those details.

Structured generation settings such as `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` connect request configuration to grammar-guided decoding. `GrammarManager` checks for these settings and obtains a grammar backend when one is configured [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:30-44](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-171](). The grammar backend represents token constraints using vocabulary masks that can be applied to logits [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:79-106](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-145]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:125-158](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-134](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-142](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:30-44](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-171](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:79-106](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-145]()

```mermaid
    end

```

## Subtopic Overviews and Links

### 17.1 Sampling Parameters and Configuration

`SamplingParams` is the request-level structure for controls including `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `max_new_tokens`, stop criteria, `n`, and `beam_width`. It also carries penalty fields, grammar constraint fields, logit bias, a sampling seed, custom parameters, and watermark configuration [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-165](). For parameter normalization, validation, and configuration details, see [Sampling Parameters and Configuration](#17.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-165]()

### 17.2 Logits Processing Pipeline

Logits processing is the bridge between model scores and the request’s sampling and constraint settings, managed centrally via `Sampler` and batched structures like `SamplingBatchInfo` [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-142](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-134](). Custom logit processors and sanitization utilities handle fine-grained adjustments before sampling [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:143-150](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/custom_logit_processor.py:31-45](). Grammar objects provide vocabulary-mask interfaces, and `XGrammarGrammar` applies a filled mask to logits [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:79-106](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:148-158](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-145](). For the processing stages, custom processors, and logprob computation, see [Logits Processing Pipeline](#17.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-150](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-134](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/custom_logit_processor.py:31-45](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:79-106](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:148-158](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-145]()

### 17.3 Sampling Algorithms

The request structure exposes distribution controls such as temperature, top-p, top-k, and min-p [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:134-138](). Their algorithmic behavior—including greedy decoding, probability renormalization policies via `sampling_renorm.py`, filtering, and fused implementations—is intentionally left to the child page [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:41-54](). For details, see [Sampling Algorithms](#17.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:134-138](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:41-54]()

### 17.4 Penalties and Constraints

`SamplingParams` includes frequency, presence, and repetition penalties, as well as `min_new_tokens` and stop-related fields [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:125-141](). Grammar constraints are represented separately in the same request structure and are handled through `GrammarManager` and grammar backends [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:146-149](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-171](). For penalty behavior and length constraints, see [Penalties and Constraints](#17.4).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:125-149](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-171]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the request-level `SamplingParams` schema, the visible initialization behavior, parameter validation evidence, and how grammar-related settings connect to constrained decoding. It focuses on configuration and transport; sampling algorithms and logits processing are covered on their respective pages. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-183]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-183]()

---

## Overview: Sampling Parameter Flow

`SamplingParams` is a typed request object. Its fields cover token selection, output limits, stopping, penalties, structured-output constraints, and related request options. The request schema also includes internal fields used to hold stop-condition aliases and normalization state. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-166]()

The available code shows a grammar-specific path from request sampling parameters to `GrammarManager`: when a request has a non-`None` grammar constraint, the manager selects a grammar key and uses its configured backend. The diagram shows this path and the typed parameter object; it does not imply an unshown path to sampler kernels. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-172]()

**Diagram: "Sampling Parameters and Grammar Request Path"**

```mermaid
graph TD
    "Client" --> "Params"
    "Params" --> "Req"
    "Req" --> "Manager"
    "Manager" --> "Backend"
    "Backend" --> "Constraint"

    sub5["Client Request Sampling Parameters"] --> Client
    sub4["SamplingParams"] --> Params
    sub3["Req.sampling_params"] --> Req
    sub2["GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar"] --> Manager
    sub1["BaseGrammarBackend.get_request_grammar_key"] --> Backend
    sub0["json_schema, regex, ebnf, structural_tag"] --> Constraint
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:117-166](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:145-172]()

|---|---|---|

| Reasoning-aware grammar wrapper | `ReasonerGrammarObject` | Wraps grammar behavior and tracks a reasoning terminator sequence. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:148-167]() |

## SamplingParams Class Structure

`SamplingParams` is defined as a `msgspec.Struct` with keyword-only construction and an array-like representation. Its fields are divided in the source into API parameters and internal fields populated during initialization or normalization. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:140-185]()

```mermaid
    "Params" --> "Other"

    sub5["temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p"] --> Distribution

    sub2["stop, stop_token_ids, stop_regex"] --> Stops

```

## Core Sampling Parameters and Initialization Logic

`SamplingParams.__post_init__` checks parameters upon instantiation. The initialization tests document these specific conversions:

- **Near-zero temperature:** A temperature strictly less than `_SAMPLING_EPS` (`1e-6`) is converted to `top_k = 1` and `temperature = 1.0`. A value exactly equal to `1e-6` does not trigger that conversion. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:42-43](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:31-49]()
- **Top-k sentinel:** `top_k = -1` becomes `TOP_K_ALL`; an explicit positive top-k value is preserved. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:42-43](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:56-64]()
- **Stop token IDs:** A nonempty input is converted to a set of integer values, filtering `None`; an empty or absent input becomes `None`. [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:66-80]()
- **Empty grammar strings:** Tests verify that empty values for `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` become `None`. [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:82-90]()

The tests also show that negative temperature is retained at construction and rejected by `verify()`; they separately check that NaN and infinity are rejected. For `top_p`, the tests establish that zero, negative values, and values above one are rejected, while `1.0` and a small positive value are valid. [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:51-54](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:135-175]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:42-43](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:31-90](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:135-175]()

## Structured Output Configuration and Grammar Management

`json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` are request fields used by `GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar()`. The manager checks whether any of them is non-`None`; if so, it either aborts the request when no grammar backend is configured or selects a grammar key for the specified constraint. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:169-172](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:154-172]()

**Diagram: "Grammar Constraint Mapping to Code Entities"**

```mermaid
graph TD
    "Params" --> "Req"
    "Req" --> "Manager"
    "Manager" --> "Key"
    "Key" --> "Backend"
    "Backend" --> "XGrammar"
    "Manager" --> "Reasoner"

    sub5["SamplingParams.json_schema_regex_ebnf_structural_tag"] --> Params
    sub4["Req.sampling_params"] --> Req
    sub3["GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar"] --> Manager
    sub2["BaseGrammarBackend.get_request_grammar_key"] --> Key
    sub1["BaseGrammarBackend"] --> Backend
    sub0["XGrammarGrammar"] --> XGrammar
    sub_reasoner["ReasonerGrammarObject"] --> Reasoner
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:169-172](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:154-172](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:58-109](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-95](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75]()

`GrammarManager` creates a grammar backend from scheduler configuration, tokenizer, vocabulary size, EOS token ID, and model reasoning terminator IDs when tokenizer initialization is enabled. If tokenizer initialization is skipped, it sets the backend to `None`. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:35-50]()

`XGrammarGrammar` stores its matcher and compiled grammar context. It fills a vocabulary mask from the matcher and applies that mask to logits using device-specific paths. The base grammar interfaces define corresponding mask operations and token acceptance/rollback hooks. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-95](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-147](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:58-107]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:169-172](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:35-50](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:154-172](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:58-107](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-95](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:118-147]()

### Reasoning End Token IDs and Thinking Budget

The private key `__sglang_reasoning_end_token_ids` transports a request-selected reasoning terminator through `custom_params`. `set_request_reasoning_end_token_ids()` adds a nonempty list of nonnegative integer IDs to that mapping. `get_request_reasoning_end_token_ids()` checks the value’s type, length, nonnegative IDs, optional vocabulary bound, and—when supplied—membership in the allowed sequences. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:51-65](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:67-98](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:101-115]()

`GrammarManager._apply_request_reasoning_config()` applies an allowed request-selected terminator to a `ReasonerGrammarObject` and reads an integer `thinking_budget` from `custom_params` to set `max_think_tokens`. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:135-153]()

`ReasonerGrammarObject` tracks the configured end-token sequence and reasoning state. Its `accept_token()` delegates accepted tokens to the wrapped grammar only after the reasoning terminator has moved it into generation state. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:97-121](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:154-167]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:51-65](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:67-115](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:135-153](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:97-121](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:154-167]()

## Stop Conditions, Custom Parameters, and Serialization

- **Stop strings and regexes:** The public `stop` and `stop_regex` fields are documented as API aliases copied to `stop_strs` and `stop_regex_strs` and cleared during normalization. The parameter module defines limits of 32 stop strings, 256 characters per stop regex, and 32 stop regexes. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:42-46](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:150-156](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:184-185]()
- **Stop token IDs:** Initialization filters `None` values, converts the remaining IDs to integers, and stores the result as a set; an empty result is represented as `None`. [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:66-80]()
- **Custom parameters:** `CustomParamValue` permits JSON-safe scalar values, lists of scalars, or string-keyed dictionaries of scalars. The source comment states these values must survive msgpack IPC without `PickleWrapper`. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:33-40]()
- **Rust representation:** The Rust `SamplingParams` is described as a typed port of the Python class. Its visible declaration uses serde deserialization, rejects unknown fields, and defines sampling defaults including temperature and top-p at `1.0`, top-k at the all-vocabulary sentinel, and min-p and penalties at `0.0`. [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:1-4](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:115-120](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:136-176]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:33-46](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:150-156](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:184-185](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:1-4](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:115-120](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:136-176]()

---

## Summary

`SamplingParams` is the typed request configuration for sampling, output limits, stop conditions, penalties, structured-output constraints, and related generation options. Its initialization normalizes selected inputs, including near-zero temperature, `top_k = -1`, stop token IDs, and empty grammar strings. Tests cover important validation boundaries for temperature and `top_p`. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:140-185](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:31-90](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:135-175]()

Grammar constraints flow from `SamplingParams` into `GrammarManager`, which dispatches constraint types to its grammar backend. Request-selected reasoning terminators and thinking budgets are conveyed through `custom_params` and applied to reasoning-aware grammar objects. [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:135-172](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:51-115]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:140-185](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:31-90](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:135-175](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:135-172]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the logits processing pipeline in SGLang, covering the LM-head quantization-method eligibility gate, the `LogitsProcessor` execution flow, logprob computation helpers, soft-capping operations, custom logit processors, and logits modification mechanics [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:14-75](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:31-50]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:14-75](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:31-50]()

---

## LogitsProcessor and LM Head

The `logits_processor.py` module manages the transformation of hidden states from the model backbone into raw token logits via the language model head (`lm_head`), applying quantization methods, soft-capping, and integration with logprob extraction [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:16-75](). 

The module implements runtime optimizations and integration hooks for sharded vocabulary execution, sharded verification, and custom logit processors that manipulate logits before sampling [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:114-122]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:16-122]()

---

## LM-Head Quantization Eligibility

The eligibility gate verifies whether an LM head can execute using a specialized quantization kernel rather than standard unquantized GEMM or fallback routines [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:83-153](). Unquantized methods such as `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, and `PackWeightMethod` are explicitly excluded from quantized kernel execution [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:100-104]().

### Quantization-method decision path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["should_apply_lm_head_quant_method"] --> Basic["CheckMethodWeightAndApply"]
    Basic -->|"Invalid"| Reject["ReturnFalse"]
    Basic -->|"Valid"| Unquantized{"IsExcludedUnquantizedClass"}
    Unquantized -->|"Yes"| Reject
    Unquantized -->|"No"| ModelOpt{"RecognizedModelOptMethod"}
    ModelOpt -->|"FP4_or_NVFP4"| Layout["CheckDtypeAndRequiredRuntimeAttributes"]
    ModelOpt -->|"FP8"| FP8["CheckFloat8E4m3fnAndScaleAttributes"]
    ModelOpt -->|"Other_method"| Accept["ReturnTrue"]
    Layout --> Decision["ReturnLayoutCheckResult"]
    FP8 --> Decision
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:83-196]()

---

## Logprob Computation

Logprob computation relies on modules imported from `sglang.srt.layers.logprob_processor`, including `InputLogprobProcessor`, `LogprobStage`, `get_token_ids_logprobs_raw`, and `get_top_logprobs_raw` [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:55-60](). These utilities extract token-level log probabilities and top-k logprob distributions during prefill and generation steps [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:31-144]().

| Imported Entity | Role and Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `InputLogprobProcessor` | Handles input-token logprob calculations for prompt evaluation phases [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:55-60](). |
| `LogprobStage` | Defines execution stages (`PREFILL`, `DECODE`) for logprob processing pipelines [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:31-35](). |
| `get_token_ids_logprobs_raw` | Computes raw logprobs corresponding to specific target token IDs [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:146-183](). |
| `get_top_logprobs_raw` | Extracts top-k log probabilities from raw logits tensors [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:98-130](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:55-60](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py:31-183]()

## Logit Modification and Soft-Capping

Logits can be modified in-place or transformed using soft-capping operations to prevent extreme logit growth in architectures like Gemma and newer transformer variants [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:26-36](). The pipeline incorporates operations such as `softcap_inplace_logits` (aliased as `fused_softcap`), `cast_to_float32_logits`, `gathered_softcap_logits`, `softcap_to_float32_logits`, and `softcap_row_argmax` [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:26-39]().

### Logits-related symbols in the pipeline

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| `fused_softcap` | In-place soft-capping operation on logits tensors [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:30-32](). |
| `cast_to_float32_logits` | Casts logits to single-precision float for numerical stability [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:26-29](). |
| `gathered_softcap_logits` | Applies soft-capping on gathered logit slices [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:26-29](). |
| `softcap_row_argmax` | Computes row-wise argmax over soft-capped logits [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:36-39](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py:26-39]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the implementation of sampling algorithms and supporting components within SGLang's sampling subsystem. It covers batched sampling parameters, sampler preprocessing, backend-related imports (FlashInfer, `sgl_kernel`, AITER, Ascend), probability renormalization policies for tensor parallelism, greedy decoding, top-k/top-p/min-p sampling, temperature scaling, and custom logit processors. [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:9-82](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-132]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:9-82](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-132]()

## Architecture Overview

`SamplingBatchInfo` manages per-request runtime sampling metadata, storing temperatures, top-p thresholds, top-k limits, and min-p values as batched tensors alongside boolean flags indicating batch-wide or partial greedy eligibility, grammar masking, and custom logit processor registrations. Its `from_schedule_batch()` constructor initializes these structures from request `sampling_params` and asynchronously transfers them to the execution device. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-132](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:133-179]()

`Sampler` inherits from `nn.Module` and coordinates logit preparation, logprob calculation, and token selection. Its `forward()` method accepts `LogitsProcessorOutput`, `SamplingBatchInfo`, logprob configurations, token positions, and optional pre-watermark logits. Prior to token selection, `_preprocess_logits()` evaluates custom logit processors and sanitizes non-finite logits via `sanitize_nan_logits()`. [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-150](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:152-176]()

### Diagram: Sampling Inputs and Visible Sampler Preprocessing

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ScheduleBatch["ScheduleBatch"] -->|"from_schedule_batch"| SamplingBatchInfo["SamplingBatchInfo"]
    SamplingBatchInfo -->|"temperatures top_ps top_ks min_ps"| SamplerForward["Sampler.forward"]
    LogitsProcessorOutput["LogitsProcessorOutput"] -->|"next_token_logits"| SamplerForward
    SamplerForward -->|"custom processors when present"| ApplyCustom["apply_custom_logit_processor"]
    ApplyCustom -->|"sanitize non-finite logits"| Sanitize["sanitize_nan_logits"]
    Sanitize -->|"preprocessed logits"| SamplingContinuation["Sampling implementation"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-179](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-176]()

## The `Sampler` Class and Execution Flow

`Sampler.__init__()` configures device synchronization groups (`tp_sync_group` and optional `cp_sync_group`) based on tensor-parallel, context-parallel, and data-parallel attention configurations. It reads execution context settings regarding deterministic inference and sampling backends, and instantiates an `OutputLogprobProcessor`. [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-142]()

The `_SamplingMaskCapture` `NamedTuple` constructs compact post-filter weights, optional token IDs, selected weights, and original batch-row mappings for grammar-guided structured generation and support-logprob streaming. [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:102-109]()

```mermaid
    RuntimeExec["get_exec"] -->|"deterministic and kernel settings"| SamplerInit
    LogitsOutput["LogitsProcessorOutput"] -->|"forward input"| SamplerForward["Sampler.forward"]
    SamplingInfo["SamplingBatchInfo"] -->|"forward input"| SamplerForward
    SamplerForward -->|"preprocessing"| Preprocess["_preprocess_logits"]
    Preprocess -->|"optional"| CustomProcessor["apply_custom_logit_processor"]
    Preprocess -->|"always"| NanSanitize["sanitize_nan_logits"]
    SamplerForward -->|"mask capture representation"| Capture["_SamplingMaskCapture"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:120-150](), [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py]()

## Sampling Backends and Renormalization Policy

The sampler module binds optimized operations including `sampler_softmax` and `sampler_argmax` from `sglang.kernels.ops.sampling`. On CUDA environments, it leverages FlashInfer routines (`min_p_sampling_from_probs`, `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs`) alongside custom probability renormalization kernels (`top_k_renorm_prob`, `top_p_renorm_prob`) from `sglang.srt.layers.sampling_renorm`. On MUSA, XPU, and NPU platforms, corresponding primitives are dispatched from `sgl_kernel` or `torch_npu`. [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:9-82](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:1-44]()

### Renormalization Determinism (`sampling_renorm.py`)

High-performance renormalization kernels use floating-point atomic reductions across thread blocks. Across multiple Tensor Parallel (TP) ranks, this introduces minor rounding variances. If a distributed random seed encounters values in this floating-point boundary, ranks can select diverging tokens, causing execution hangs during subsequent collective communication primitives.

To maintain cross-rank determinism, renormalization enforces deterministic accumulation flags when `tp_size > 1` or when explicit deterministic inference flags are enabled, reverting to optimized non-deterministic execution paths only under single-rank conditions (`tp_size == 1`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:1-85]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:9-82](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:1-85]()

## Sampling Algorithms

### Greedy Decoding

`SamplingBatchInfo` evaluates `is_all_greedy` and `is_any_greedy` flags to bypass stochastic filtering pipelines when requests demand deterministic argmax selection (`temperature == 0.0` or `top_k == 1`). On ROCm platforms, AITER's `greedy_sample` kernel can be activated, with fallback handling to `torch.argmax` to prevent out-of-range token indices on all-NaN or all-negative-infinity logit rows. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-70](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:65-79]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-70](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:65-79]()

### Top-k, Top-p, and Min-p Sampling

`SamplingBatchInfo` houses batched `top_ks`, `top_ps`, and `min_ps` tensors along with activation flags (`need_top_k_sampling`, `need_top_p_sampling`, `need_min_p_sampling`) populated via `from_schedule_batch()` [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-78](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:133-163]().

- **Top-k**: Truncates candidate pools to the $k$ highest scoring tokens, renormalized via `top_k_renorm_prob` [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:41-44]().
- **Top-p (Nucleus)**: Selects the minimal subset of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds probability threshold $p$, renormalized via `top_p_renorm_prob` [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:41-44]().
- **Min-p**: Eliminates tokens whose probabilities fall below a fraction (`min_p`) of the top candidate's probability.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:58-78](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:133-163](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py:41-44]()

### Temperature Sampling and Fused Temperature Softmax

Temperature parameters scale logit vectors prior to normalization: $\text{logits}_i / T$. `SamplingBatchInfo` stores temperatures in a broadcast-compatible shape `(-1, 1)` to align with batched vocabulary projections [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:60](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:140-148](). Softmax execution uses optimized operator bindings from `sampler_softmax` [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:11]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:60](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py:140-148](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py:11]()

## System Overview

`SamplingParams` defines request-facing penalty fields (`frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `repetition_penalty`), length constraints (`min_new_tokens`, `max_new_tokens`), stop conditions (`stop`, `stop_token_ids`, `stop_regex`), and structured output constraints (`json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, `structural_tag`) [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:153-187]().

The `GrammarManager` processes constrained requests by inspecting these fields, resolving or compiling the constraint via `create_grammar_backend`, and dispatching vocabulary masks [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:36-51]().

## Penalty Types

### Frequency and Presence Penalties

`SamplingParams.frequency_penalty` and `SamplingParams.presence_penalty` are floating-point request parameters defaulting to `0.0` [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:174-175](). They discourage repetitive token generation by penalizing logits proportionally to how often a token has already appeared (frequency) or whether it has appeared at all (presence).

### Repetition Penalty

`SamplingParams.repetition_penalty` scales logits for previously generated tokens. It defaults to `1.0` (no penalty) [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:176](). Values greater than `1.0` penalize repetition, while values below `1.0` encourage it.

### Minimum New Tokens and Stop-Token Penalization

`BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer` enforces `min_new_tokens` by adding `-inf` penalties to stop and EOS token IDs via tensor scattering (`scatter_add_`) during early decode steps where output length is below the minimum threshold [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-94](). Using `torch.where` instead of boolean-mask indexing avoids device-to-host synchronization during decode steps [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:88-93]().

### Penalty Field Reference

| Field | Type and Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `frequency_penalty` | `float`, `0.0` | Penalizes tokens based on their cumulative count in the generated text. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:174]() |
| `presence_penalty` | `float`, `0.0` | Penalizes tokens if they have appeared at least once in the generated text. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:175]() |
| `repetition_penalty` | `float`, `1.0` | Multiplicatively scales logits of previously generated tokens. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:176]() |
| `min_new_tokens` | `int`, `0` | Enforces a minimum generation length by suppressing stop/EOS tokens. [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:177]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:153-185](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-115]()

---

## Grammar Constraints

### Request Fields and Grammar Selection

`GrammarManager` supports grammar-guided constrained decoding via backends like `XGrammarGrammarBackend` and `ReasonerGrammarBackend` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:36-51](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75](). `GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar` inspects `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` fields [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:155-174](). If a constraint is present but `--grammar-backend none` was passed (`self.grammar_backend is None`), the request is aborted with an error message [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:163-167]().

### Reasoner Grammar Integration

`ReasonerGrammarObject` wraps underlying grammar objects to defer structural constraints until after the reasoning/thinking block completes (e.g., following `</think>` tokens) [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75](). It tracks token state transitions, reasoning token budgets, and strict thinking filters.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:36-174](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:58-136](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75]()

---

## Length and Stop Constraints

### Output-Length Fields

- `max_new_tokens`: Limits the maximum number of generated tokens. Defaults to `128` in Python and Rust [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:162](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:90-91](). An explicit `null` indicates no limit.
- `min_new_tokens`: Enforces a minimum generation length before EOS or stop triggers are evaluated [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:177](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-15]().

### Stop Tokens, Strings, and Regular Expressions

- `stop_token_ids`: A set of integer token IDs that immediately terminate generation when emitted [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:166]().
- `stop` / `stop_strs`: Stop strings normalized into internal representation during request initialization [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:163-165]().
- `stop_regex` / `stop_regex_strs`: Regular expression patterns validated for scheduler safety and pattern limits [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:167-169](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:18-27]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:162-177](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-94](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/sampling.rs:18-27]()

---

## Summary

- Frequency, presence, and repetition penalties modify token selection probabilities based on prior token history [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:174-176]().
- Length constraints (`min_new_tokens`, `max_new_tokens`) and stop criteria (`stop`, `stop_token_ids`, `stop_regex`) control generation boundaries [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:162-177](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-94]().
- Structured generation is orchestrated by `GrammarManager` and executed via backend engines and reasoner wrappers [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:36-174](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:140-185](), [python/sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/min_new_tokens.py:7-115](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:36-174](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-75]()

## Purpose and scope

This parent page gives a high-level overview of SGLang’s vision-language model (VLM) support and multimodal request path. It connects model-side vision components to media preprocessing and feature transport, and points to child pages for implementation details. The processor output types include image, video, and audio data, while model implementations connect vision components to multimodal embedding utilities [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107]() [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]().

For details, see [Vision-Language Model Architecture](#18.1), [Multimodal Input Processing](#18.2), and [Supported Vision-Language Models](#18.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]()

## Overview and high-level architecture

Multimodal requests add media preprocessing and model-specific visual processing to the language-model serving path. `BaseMultiModalProcessor` represents normalized processor output with text, optional token IDs, and image, video, and audio collections. Model-side utilities such as `general_mm_embed_routine` and `materialize_multimodal_features` connect those inputs to model execution [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107]() [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]().

The diagram links user-facing concepts to concrete code entities. It is a high-level map, not a complete request-lifecycle trace.

### Diagram: Multimodal request concepts mapped to code entities

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        A["PromptWithMedia"] --> B["PreprocessMedia"]
        B --> C["RunVLMInference"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        D["BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput"] --> E["organize_results"]
        E --> F["Modality.IMAGE / VIDEO / AUDIO"]
        G["general_mm_embed_routine"] --> H["Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration"]
        H --> I["VisionAttention"]
    end

    A --> D
    B --> E
    C --> G
    F --> G
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]()

For the model structure and vision attention, see [Vision-Language Model Architecture](#18.1). For media preprocessing and feature flow, see [Multimodal Input Processing](#18.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39]()

## Vision-language model architecture

VLM implementations combine a vision encoder with model-specific components and a language model. For example, Qwen3-VL imports `VisionAttention`, defines vision patch embedding components, and uses multimodal embedding utilities; Kimi-K2.5 also uses `VisionAttention` in its encoder layers [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39]() [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:176-181]() [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:28-31]().

The shared names in these implementations are useful entry points, but individual models may differ in vision tower, positional processing, and feature integration. For details, see [Vision-Language Model Architecture](#18.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:176-181](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:28-31]()

## Multimodal input processing

`BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput` groups text and optional media collections, and `organize_results()` labels image, video, and audio values with their corresponding `Modality`. Processor configuration can be provided by modality: unit tests cover `image`, `video`, and `audio` entries in `mm_process_config` and verify extraction into processor configuration [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107]() [test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_process_config.py:38-46]() [test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_process_config.py:125-135]().

Feature transport is a separate concern from media decoding and model execution. The model path includes `materialize_multimodal_features`, and the transport tests exercise `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy` reconstruction and cleanup through `MultimodalInputs.from_processor_output`. EVS and the details of encoding, transport, embedding merging, and image/video/audio handling belong in [Multimodal Input Processing](#18.2) [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:77-89]() [test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_vl_feature_materialization.py:14-22]().

```mermaid
        B --> C["SendFeaturesToInference"]
        C --> D["MergeMediaFeaturesWithPrompt"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        E["BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput"] --> F["organize_results"]
        F --> G["Modality.IMAGE / VIDEO / AUDIO"]
        H["CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy"] --> I["MultimodalInputs.from_processor_output"]

        J --> K["general_mm_embed_routine"]

```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:77-89]()

For details, see [Multimodal Input Processing](#18.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-107](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]()

## Supported vision-language models

The codebase includes implementations and processor integrations for several VLM families. Qwen-VL processor code imports Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, and additional conditional-generation model classes; Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL-MoE have dedicated model implementations. Kimi-K2.5 and Kimi-K3 are also represented in model and processor code [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:26-36]() [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:15-16]() [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py:1-37]() [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:27-31]() [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:24-27]().

The available file excerpts also identify InternS2-Mobius as a model implementation and show it referenced by the Qwen-VL processor module. This parent page does not attempt to provide a complete support matrix; see [Supported Vision-Language Models](#18.3) for the model-by-model reference [python/sglang/srt/models/interns2_mobius.py:1-2]() [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:22-25]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:26-36](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:15-16](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py:1-37](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:27-31](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:24-27](), [python/sglang/srt/models/interns2_mobius.py:1-2]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the Vision-Language Model (VLM) architecture implemented in SGLang. It covers multimodal processor outputs, model-side vision components, `VisionAttention` metadata preparation and backend selection, vision transformer graph runners across platforms (CUDA and NPU), and stream-ordered feature transport mechanisms. Concrete architectural examples are drawn from Qwen3-VL and Kimi K2.5.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:73-106](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:17-53](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:1-180]()

---

## Multimodal Data Structures and Transport

### Multimodal Processor Output

`BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput` records expanded `input_text`, optional pre-tokenized `input_ids`, and modality-specific `images`, `videos`, and `audios`. Its `organize_results()` method produces a sequence of `(Modality, data)` pairs, ordered as images, videos, then audio. `MultimodalSpecialTokens` holds modality token strings and IDs, builds regular expressions for identifying those tokens, and maps recognized token strings back to a modality. 

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:73-106](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:109-173](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:175-202]()

The processor module imports several model implementations, and derives its processor class from the shared `BaseMultimodalProcessor`. Similarly, Kimi K2.5 implements GPU-accelerated image preprocessing (such as NaViT resize configuration and bicubic interpolation on CUDA tensors) to optimize throughput before token embedding.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k25.py:34-75](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k25.py:151-178]()

### Feature Transport and Memory Pools

Multimodal features are transported across processes and streams using bounded stream-ordered GPU memory pools (`StreamOrderedMmFeaturePool`) defined in [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/transport/memory_pool.py:163-208](). These pools use generation-safe producer/consumer leases alongside CUDA driver wait/write primitives (`cuStreamWaitValue32` and `cuStreamWriteValue32`) to synchronize cross-rank feature ingestion without host-device synchronization overhead.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/transport/memory_pool.py:39-161](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/transport/memory_pool.py:163-208]()

## Top-Level VLM Architecture

The source modules import base model layers alongside multimodal input structures, embedding helpers, vision-attention components, and multimodal feature utilities. For instance, Kimi K2.5 imports `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `VisionAttention`, and `MLP2`, and defines `MoonViTEncoderLayer` using `VisionAttention` and `MLP2`.

| Kimi K2.5 | `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `VisionAttention`, `MLP2`, `MoonViTEncoderLayer` | Includes self-attention, normalization, residual additions, and an MLP. |

## Vision Encoder Architecture and Encoder Layers

### Qwen3-VL Vision Components

The Qwen3-VL module defines `Qwen3_VisionMLP`. It resolves a linear parallel group, creates a `ColumnParallelLinear` layer followed by an activation, and applies a `RowParallelLinear` layer. Its `forward()` method returns the second linear layer’s output.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:30-41](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:131-181]()

### Kimi K2.5 `MoonViTEncoderLayer`

`MoonViTEncoderLayer` initializes `norm0`, `norm1`, an `MLP2`, and a `VisionAttention` configured with QKV parallelism and a custom position-embedding applier (`apply_rope`). During `forward()`, it normalizes hidden states, applies attention with cumulative sequence lengths and optional position/forward metadata, adds residuals, and passes through the MLP.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:59-160]()

## `VisionAttention` Module and Backend Selection

### Attention Metadata

`VisionAttentionMetadata` holds cumulative sequence lengths, per-sequence lengths, and a maximum sequence length. `prepare_vision_attention_metadata()` moves `cu_seqlens` to the requested device as `int32`, computes each sequence length from adjacent cumulative offsets, and derives the maximum when not provided.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:140-180]()

`prepare_flashinfer_cudnn_vision_attention_metadata()` pads batch sizes to configured bucket sizes (`BATCH_BUCKETS`), computes element-based packed indptrs, selects sequence-length buckets (`FLASHINFER_MAX_SEQLEN_BUCKETS`), and delegates to `prepare_vision_attention_metadata()`.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:107-120](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:183-208]()

### Backend Context

The `vision.py` module conditionally imports platform-specific attention functions. CUDA paths use FlashAttention wrappers (`flash_attn_func`, `flash_attn_varlen_func`) and lazy imports of FlashInfer cuDNN prefill functions, while CPU, MUSA, NPU, and XPU maintain separate integration hooks and fallback routines.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py:44-100]()

---

## Vision Transformer Graph Runners

Vision Transformers support CUDA and NPU graph capture and replay via graph runner abstractions. These runners capture the transformer blocks, feature mergers, and optional deepstack merger lists into static execution graphs for identical batch shapes and sequence layouts.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/vit_cuda_graph_runner.py:30-43](), [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/vit_npu_graph_runner.py:32-41]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the multimodal input path within SGLang, covering modality-aware processor output representation (`BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput`), special-token parsing (`MultimodalSpecialTokens`), media preprocessing implementations (such as Qwen-VL and Kimi K2.5/K3 helpers), inter-process feature transport via CUDA IPC (`TransportProxyTensor`), embedding merging and scheduling (`DataEmbeddingFunc`, `get_embedding_chunk`), Efficient Video Sampling (EVS), and preprocess caching mechanisms [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-95]() [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:58-181]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:152-162]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-95](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:58-181](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:152-162]()

---

## Overview

The multimodal ingestion architecture bridges raw media streams (images, videos, audios) and textual prompts into sequence-aligned hidden states consumed by vision-language models. Requests entering the tokenizer or manager pass through modality-specific processors before being scheduled via `mm_schedule.py` and dispatched to the `ModelRunner` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:26-60]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:1-25]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:26-60](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:1-25]()

---

## Data Structures and Special Token Handling

The core data containers for raw and processed multimodal payloads are defined in `base_processor.py` and `mm_schedule.py`:

* `BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput`: Encapsulates `input_text`, pre-tokenized `input_ids`, and lists of `images`, `videos`, and `audios`. Its `organize_results()` method yields tuples mapping each media artifact to its corresponding `Modality` enum (`Modality.IMAGE`, `Modality.VIDEO`, `Modality.AUDIO`) [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-95]().
* `MultimodalSpecialTokens`: Manages token strings, IDs, and compiled regular expressions (`image_token_regex`, `video_token_regex`, `audio_token_regex`, and a `combined_regex`) used to segment prompt text around media placeholders [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:99-192]().
* `MultimodalDataItem`: Represents individual media items during scheduling, carrying cache hashes, offsets, and precomputed features [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:10-14]().

```mermaid
    end
```

## Image, Video, and Audio Preprocessing

Processors implement normalization, resizing, and patching routines tailored to individual model architectures:

* **Qwen-VL Resizing**: `smart_resize()` enforces scale constraints, boundary divisibility by `IMAGE_FACTOR` (28), and pixel bounds (`MIN_PIXELS`, `MAX_PIXELS`), rejecting aspect ratios above `MAX_RATIO` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:58-67]() [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:150-181](). Video preprocessing configurations filter out specific config keys via `_get_processor_video_config()` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:125-132]().
* **Kimi K2.5/K3 Processing**: Computes NaViT-style resize configurations using `navit_resize_config()` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:62-68](), expands token placeholder counts with `_expand_k3_image_prompt_token_ids()` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:85-131](), converts PIL images to CHW tensors, and applies bicubic antialiasing (`_resize_bicubic_if_needed()`) [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k25.py:67-70]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:58-181](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:62-131](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k25.py:67-70]()

---

## Feature Transport and CUDA IPC

To transfer heavy vision features between asynchronous tokenizer/processor processes and model workers with minimal overhead, SGLang utilizes `TransportProxyTensor` (`mm_utils.py`) and CUDA IPC mechanisms [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:123-213]().

* `TransportProxyTensor`: A `torch.Tensor` subclass carrying metadata such as `transport_mode` and `fields` [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:123-153]().
* **Pickling / IPC Serialization (`__getstate__`)**: When `transport_mode == "cuda_ipc"`, it extracts a shared CUDA storage handle (`_share_cuda_()`) along with shape, stride, and storage offsets, avoiding CPU-host memory copies [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:155-188](). If IPC handle creation fails, it falls back to standard tensor pickling [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:180-186]().
* **Unpickling (`__setstate__`)**: Reconstructs shared CUDA storage on the target device index using `torch.UntypedStorage._new_shared_cuda` [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:191-213]().

### Diagram: Tensor metadata and transport entities

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        EncodedFeatures["RawMediaTensorFeatures"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Proxy["TransportProxyTensor"]
        Meta["MetadataDict"]
        GetState["__getstate__()"]
        CudaIpc["CudaIpcStorageHandle"]
        Fallback["DefaultTensorSerialization"]
        SetState["__setstate__()"]
        TargetTensor["TargetDeviceTensor"]
    end

    EncodedFeatures --> Proxy
    Proxy --> Meta

    GetState --> CudaIpc
    GetState --> Fallback
    CudaIpc --> SetState
    Fallback --> SetState
    SetState --> TargetTensor
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:123-213]()

## Multimodal Embedding Merging and Scheduling

Embedding execution and chunking are orchestrated via `mm_schedule.py`:

* `DataEmbeddingFunc`: A callable signature receiving a list of `MultimodalDataItem` objects, returning either a concatenated tensor, a list of per-item tensors, or an `EVSEmbeddingResult` [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:152-162]().
* `get_embedding_chunk()`: Extracts embedding slices corresponding to a specific prefill chunk window (`extend_prefix_len` and `extend_seq_len`) based on item offset ranges (`items_offset`) [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:33-75]().
* `_get_precomputed_embedding()`: Retrieves cached or precomputed embeddings across batch items, enforcing device consistency and handling cache lookups [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:78-149]().

### Diagram: Prompt offsets to scheduled embedding chunks

```mermaid
    end

        Encoder["DataEmbeddingFunc"]
        Offsets["item.offsets"]
        ExtractChunk["get_embedding_chunk()"]
        Precomp["_get_precomputed_embedding()"]
        StaticCache["MultiModalStaticCache"]
    end

    PromptText --> DataItem
    DataItem --> Encoder

```

---

## Efficient Video Sampling (EVS)

EVS integrates specialized video sampling results into the SGLang embedding scheduling pipeline. `EVSEmbeddingResult` is imported and supported as a valid return type for `DataEmbeddingFunc`, enabling dynamic frame selection and embedding reduction policies during video processing [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:12-12]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:152-162]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:12-12](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:152-162]()

---

## Caching, Fingerprinting, and Feature Buffering

To accelerate repeated media inputs, SGLang employs fingerprinting and static caches:

* **Preprocess Caching**: Utilizes `MultimodalPreprocessCache`, `PreprocessFingerprintProvider`, and `build_processor_fingerprint()` to avoid redundant media decoding [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:27-31]().
* **GPU Feature Buffering**: `init_feature_buffer(device)` preallocates a contiguous float32 GPU buffer (`_GPU_FEATURE_BUFFER`), and `try_add_to_buffer(tensor)` sub-allocates views into this buffer to reduce fragmentation and allocation latency during high-throughput multimodal serving [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:74-121]().

| Component | Role / Definition |
|---|---|
| `MultimodalPreprocessCache` | Caches preprocessed media artifacts. [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:27-31]() |
| `build_processor_fingerprint` | Generates unique content/config fingerprints for media inputs. [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:27-31]() |
| `init_feature_buffer()` | Preallocates device memory for feature transport buffering. [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:74-91]() |
| `try_add_to_buffer()` | Copies tensors into the preallocated buffer view. [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:105-121]() |
| `init_mm_embedding_cache()` | Initializes the static embedding cache instance. [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:28-31]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:27-31](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py:74-121](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py:28-31]()
