## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the supported vision-language model (VLM) families and multimodal architectures in SGLang, detailing their end-to-end data processing pipelines, model runner integration, processor classes, and hardware execution backends. It maps high-level multimodal specifications (such as Qwen-VL, Kimi-VL/K2.5/K3, InternVL, Gemma, GLM, Llama4, and MiniCPM-V) to concrete SGLang codebase entities, configuration classes, and custom operators.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:30-98](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-57](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:17-53](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-35]()

---

## Overview and Multimodal Runtime Dataflow

SGLang manages multimodal inputs through a unified pipeline consisting of client request ingestion, asynchronous media preprocessing (`BaseMultimodalProcessor`), feature transport over CUDA IPC or VMM proxies, embedding materialization (`materialize_multimodal_features`), and dispatch to model-specific vision towers and text backbones.

The abstract data container `BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput` holds the expanded input text, raw token IDs, and lists of images, videos, and audios, which are organized via `organize_results()` into `Modality`-tagged items [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:62-107]().

**Diagram: End-to-end multimodal request dataflow**

```mermaid
graph TD
    ClientRequest["ClientHTTPRequest"] --> BaseProcessor["BaseMultimodalProcessor"]
    BaseProcessor --> ProcessorOutput["BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput"]
    ProcessorOutput --> Organize["organize_results"]
    Organize --> Transport["CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy"]
    Transport --> Materialize["materialize_multimodal_features"]
    Materialize --> VisionTower["VisionTower"]
    VisionTower --> Projections["MultimodalProjector"]
    Projections --> TokenEmbedding["TokenAndVisionEmbeddings"]
    TokenEmbedding --> Scheduler["SchedulerAndModelRunner"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:62-107](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:41-48](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:62-89]()

---

## Model Architecture Detection and Registry Integration

Vision-language models in SGLang are instantiated by matching HuggingFace configuration architecture fields against registered multimodal model classes. The tokenizer manager and model loader coordinate to identify whether a model requires multimodal processor workers, CUDA IPC feature transfer, or multi-modal rotary embedding (`MRoPE`) handling.

### Visible Model and Processor Relationships

**Diagram: Natural language family names to internal code classes**

```mermaid
graph LR
    Qwen3VL["Qwen3-VL Family"] --> QwenProc["sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.qwen_vl"]
    QwenProc --> QwenGen["Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration"]
    Qwen3VL --> QwenFile["python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py"]
    KimiK3["Kimi-K3 Family"] --> KimiProc["sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.kimi_k3"]
    KimiProc --> KimiGen["KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration"]
    KimiK3 --> MoonViT["KimiK3VisionTower"]
    GemmaSeries["Gemma3/4"] --> GemmaCausal["sglang.srt.models.gemma4_causal"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-50](), [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:15-39](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-133]()

## Supported Model Families

### Qwen-VL Family

The Qwen-VL family includes Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3.5, and Qwen3 Omni integration [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-39](). 
- **Qwen3-VL Implementation:** Relies on `Qwen3VLVisionPatchEmbed` for patch extraction, `Qwen3_VisionMLP` for vision feed-forward transformations with column/row parallel linear layers, and `VisionAttention` combined with `ViTCudaGraphRunner` for optimized vision execution [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-188]().
- **Preprocessing:** Utilizes `smart_resize()` to constrain aspect ratios, image factors, and pixel boundaries (`MIN_PIXELS`, `MAX_PIXELS`), alongside `VideoDecoderWrapper` for video processing [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:59-181]().

**Diagram: Qwen3-VL component hierarchy**

```mermaid
graph TD
    QwenModel["Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration"] --> PatchEmbed["Qwen3VLVisionPatchEmbed"]
    QwenModel --> VisionEnc["VisionAttention"]
    QwenModel --> VisionMLP["Qwen3_VisionMLP"]
    VisionMLP --> ColLinear["ColumnParallelLinear"]
    VisionMLP --> RowLinear["RowParallelLinear"]
    QwenModel --> EmbedUtils["materialize_multimodal_features"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-188](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:59-181]()

---

### Kimi-VL / K2.5 / K3 Family

The Kimi multimodal family features advanced hybrid architectures, notably Kimi K2.5 and the 2.8T-parameter Kimi-K3 hybrid Mixture-of-Experts vision-language model combining Kimi Linear attention, MoonViT3d vision towers, and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-8](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:17-53]().
- **Kimi K2.5 / MoonViT:** Implements `MoonViTEncoderLayer` utilizing `VisionAttention` with custom complex RoPE application and MLP blocks [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:61-160](). The processor implements `navit_resize_config()` for NaViT dynamic resolution scaling and token budgeting [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k25.py:34-74]().
- **Kimi K3:** Implements `KimiK3MultiModalProjector` and `KimiK3VisionTower` paired with the KimiLinear text backbone supporting Attention Residuals (`attn_res_block_size`), Latent MoE (`routed_expert_hidden_size`), and MLA output gates [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-133]().

**Diagram: Kimi K3 vision and preprocessing pipeline**

```mermaid
graph LR
    InputImg["InputImage"] --> NavitResize["navit_resize_config"]
    NavitResize --> Placeholder["_expand_k3_image_prompt_token_ids"]
    Placeholder --> MoonViT["KimiK3VisionTower"]
    MoonViT --> Projector["KimiK3MultiModalProjector"]
    Projector --> Backbone["KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-133](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/kimi_k3.py:1-130]()

---

### InternVL, Gemma, GLM-4V, and MiniCPM-V Families

- **InternVL Family:** Integrated via processor imports for `InternS2MobiusForConditionalGeneration` and `InternS2PreviewForConditionalGeneration` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-28]().
- **Gemma Family (Gemma3/4):** Text backbones include `Gemma3MLP`, `Gemma3TextScaledWordEmbedding`, and `Gemma4Router`, integrated with shared SGLang attention and FusedMoE layers [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py:55-194](), and `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` for multimodal generation [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py:120-198]().
- **GLM-4V & MiniCPM-V:** Supported via architecture configurations and test harness definitions on Ascend NPU and CUDA backends [python/sglang/test/ascend/test_ascend_utils.py:84-93]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-28](), [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py:55-194](), [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py:120-198]()

---

## Vision-Language Model Components & Attention Backends

Vision encoders rely on specialized attention layers and high-performance transport mechanisms:
- **VisionAttention:** Handles batched multi-head attention across variable-sized image/video patches with cumulative sequence lengths (`cu_seqlens`) [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:19-23]().
- **CUDA IPC & VMM Transport:** `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy` and memory pool managers handle zero-copy or fast cross-process transport of precomputed image/video features from tokenizer/processor worker processes to GPU model runner workers [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/transport/cuda_ipc.py:80-87](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:41-48]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py:32-39](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:19-23](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/transport/cuda_ipc.py:80-87]()

---

| **Kimi K2.5 / K3** | `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`, `MoonViT3d`, `KimiK3VisionTower` [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1-133](), [python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py:89-160]() | NaViT dynamic resolution, KimiLinear backbone, Latent MoE, MLA |
| **InternVL** | `InternS2MobiusForConditionalGeneration`, `InternS2PreviewForConditionalGeneration` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py:24-28]() | Multi-scale tile encoding, integrated via Qwen processor bridge |
| **Gemma 3/4** | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, `Gemma4Router` [python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py:120-198]() | Scaled word embeddings, FusedMoE, RadixAttention |

## Feature-Specific Overviews

### LoRA Adapter Support

`LoRAManager` is initialized with a base model, a maximum number of adapters per batch, server arguments, and a backend name. It creates the selected backend through `get_backend_from_name` and initializes its state. `LoRAMemoryPool` manages adapter-module memory, while `BaseLayerWithLoRA` provides a wrapper layer that consults backend batch metadata to determine whether LoRA execution is active. For details, see [LoRA Adapter Support](#19.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:68-81](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:132-150](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-149](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:45-88]()

### Constrained and Structured Output

This component handles grammar-guided and schema-constrained decoding via backends like `XGrammarBackend` and `GuidanceGrammar`, implementing vocabulary masking through `BaseGrammarObject` and `BaseGrammarBackend`. It also integrates reasoning parsers (`BaseReasoningFormatDetector`) to govern thinking phases and structural constraints. See [Constrained and Structured Output](#19.2) for details.

## LoRA and MoE

The LoRA manager records MoE-related settings, including the MoE runner backend and whether virtual experts are enabled. `LoRAMemoryPool` determines whether expert IDs are local or global based on the MoE parallel context and runner behavior. `StandardDispatcher` checks for compatible expert-ID conventions when LoRA is used with expert parallelism. ## Purpose and scope

This page documents SGLang’s LoRA adapter support: adapter management, memory-pool responsibilities, per-batch routing metadata, execution backends, eviction-policy selection, asynchronous overlap loading, and MoE LoRA integration. The implementation identifies S-LoRA and Punica as inspirations for the serving design [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:15-16]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:15-16]()

---

## 1. Architecture and component overview

The LoRA path connects adapter management to model layers and kernels. `LoRAManager` is initialized with the base model, model configuration, batch capacity, loading configuration, server arguments, backend name, and optional rank, target-module, and adapter-path settings. It selects a backend through `get_backend_from_name`, constructs it, and initializes manager state [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:68-81](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:132-150]().

`LoRAMemoryPool` owns adapter-buffer management and records model, rank, target-module, parallelism, eviction-policy, and loading-related configuration. `BaseLayerWithLoRA` wraps a base layer and holds the selected backend; its `lora_active` property uses backend batch metadata and capture state to decide whether LoRA kernels should run [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-163](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:45-86]().

| Responsibility | Code entity | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinate LoRA setup and backend selection | `LoRAManager` | Receives model and LoRA configuration, selects a backend, and initializes its state [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:68-81](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:132-150]() |
| Manage adapter weight storage | `LoRAMemoryPool` | Holds pool configuration, including capacity, target modules, rank, eviction policy, and overlap-loading configuration [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-163]() |
| Wrap a model layer | `BaseLayerWithLoRA` | Keeps the base layer and backend; determines whether the current batch should execute LoRA kernels [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:45-86]() |
| Represent dense-LoRA batch routing | `LoRABatchInfo` | Carries segment boundaries, adapter indices, ranks, scaling values, and activity metadata [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:51-104]() |
| Represent MoE-LoRA routing | `MoELoRABatchInfo` | Carries request segments, per-request adapter indices, enabled-adapter mask, and token-to-adapter mapping [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:35-49]() |

### Natural-Language-to-Code Mapping

This diagram maps the serving concepts used on this page to the implementation entities that implement them.

```mermaid

    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]

        BatchRouting["Per-batch adapter routing"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntity["Code Entity Space"]
        LoRAManager["LoRAManager"]
        LoRAMemoryPool["LoRAMemoryPool"]
        BaseLayerWithLoRA["BaseLayerWithLoRA"]

        MoELoRABatchInfo["MoELoRABatchInfo"]
    end

    AdapterManagement --> LoRAManager
    AdapterStorage --> LoRAMemoryPool
    LayerExecution --> BaseLayerWithLoRA
    BatchRouting --> LoRABatchInfo
    BatchRouting --> MoELoRABatchInfo
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:68-81](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-163](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:45-86](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:35-104]()

### Initialization and Component Wiring

`LoRAManager` chooses its dense LoRA backend by name and passes the configured maximum adapters per batch, device, and server arguments to the backend constructor. It also reads LoRA runtime settings such as eviction policy, overlap loading, strict loading, and virtual-expert behavior from runtime configuration [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:95-130](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:132-150]().

```mermaid
    Backend["BaseLoRABackend implementation"]
    State["LoRAManager.init_state"]
    Pool["LoRAMemoryPool"]

    Inputs --> Manager
    Manager --> BackendLookup
    BackendLookup --> Backend
    Manager --> State
    State --> Pool
```

## 2. Memory management and LoRA memory pool

`LoRAMemoryPool` is constructed with the base model and configuration, maximum adapters per batch, dtype, maximum LoRA rank, target modules, eviction policy, added-token capacity, and flags for shared outer MoE LoRAs, strict loading, and overlap loading [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-163](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:165-188](). It records tensor-parallel context and queries MoE expert-parallel and MoE tensor-parallel context for MoE weight handling.

The pool’s EP handling distinguishes runner backends that retain global expert IDs from paths that use local expert IDs. The pool detects whether the MoE runner preserves global IDs and, when applicable, determines whether LoRA buffers should use local expert IDs. It also obtains `moe_tp_size` and `moe_tp_rank` separately from the outer TP context because MoE expert weights can be sharded differently from attention weights [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:92-129](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:165-188]().

| Pool concern | Implementation detail |
|---|---|
| Capacity and layout configuration | The constructor accepts `max_loras_per_batch`, `max_lora_rank`, `target_modules`, and dtype [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:136-163](). |
| Parallel layout | The pool records TP size and rank, then obtains separate MoE EP and MoE TP context [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:154-163](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:165-188](). |
| Expert-ID convention | `_moe_runner_keeps_global_expert_ids()` recognizes selected FlashInfer and HPC runner variants; the result informs `moe_use_local_expert_ids` [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:113-129](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:172-178](). |
| Eviction policy | The pool constructor receives an `eviction_policy`; `LoRAManager` reads the configured policy from LoRA runtime settings [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:136-149](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:119-123](). |
| Overlap-loading compatibility | The pool records `enable_lora_overlap_loading`; the manager rejects the configuration when DP attention is enabled and the pool class does not advertise overlap-loading support [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:134-149](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:95-108](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:92-149](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:154-188](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:95-123]()

---

## 3. Multi-LoRA serving lifecycle and overlap loading

### Adapter configuration and batch routing

The manager accepts optional `lora_paths`, target modules, and maximum rank as initialization inputs, then calls `init_state` with those values [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:68-81](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:145-150]().

At execution time, dense-LoRA routing is represented by `LoRABatchInfo`. It includes segment boundaries (`seg_indptr`), adapter indices (`weight_indices`), per-adapter ranks and scalings, optional segment lengths, and a `has_active_lora` flag. Separate request-level segment pointers and adapter indices are available for MoE virtual-expert routing [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:51-104]().

The Triton backend includes helpers for constructing routing metadata for an explicit token order. `build_token_lora_batch_info` creates one-token segments from `weight_indices`; if MoE LoRA metadata is required, it constructs `MoELoRABatchInfo` with corresponding request and token adapter mappings [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:33-70]().

### Asynchronous Overlap Loading (`LoRAOverlapLoader`)

To overlap host-to-device weight transfers with execution, SGLang provides `LoRAOverlapLoader` [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:21-98](). It maintains a dedicated CUDA/device stream (`load_stream`) [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:25-28]() and tracks asynchronous loading events via `LoRAOverlapLoadStatus` (which can be `LOADED`, `LOADING`, or `NOT_LOADED`) [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:15-18](). 

`try_overlap_load_lora` drains completed loads [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:40-42](), evaluates load status [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:44](), and initiates asynchronous fetches into the adapter memory pool when capacity permits [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:51-53]().

### Overlap-loading constraints

The manager reads `enable_lora_overlap_loading` from runtime context. When DP attention is enabled, initialization raises an error if overlap loading is enabled but the selected `LoRAMemoryPool` class does not support DP-attention overlap loading. The pool base class shown here declares `supports_dp_attention_overlap_loading = False` [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:95-108](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:131-135]().

### Routing and execution flow

Diagram: Routing Sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Request as "Request batch"
    participant Metadata as "LoRABatchInfo"
    participant Manager as "LoRAManager"
    participant Layer as "BaseLayerWithLoRA"
    participant Backend as "BaseLoRABackend"

    Request->>Metadata: "Provide weight_indices and segment metadata"
    Metadata->>Layer: "Backend exposes current batch info"
    Layer->>Layer: "Evaluate lora_active"
    alt "LoRA active"
        Layer->>Backend: "Run LoRA kernel path"
    else "LoRA inactive"
        Layer->>Layer: "Use base_layer.forward"
    end
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:51-104](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:66-86](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:88-97](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:21-98]()

---

## 4. Model execution, backends, and kernels

### LoRA layer abstraction

`BaseLayerWithLoRA` stores a reference to the wrapped base layer and a `BaseLoRABackend`. Its default `forward` delegates to the base layer. The `lora_active` property checks whether LoRA has been enabled on the wrapper and whether the backend has batch metadata; it then accounts for backend skip-inactive settings and CUDA graph capture [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:45-86]().

Layer-specific wrappers and methods use the backend to compute LoRA contributions. For example, `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA` stores embedding buffers and uses the backend’s LoRA-B operation after producing LoRA-A embedding outputs [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:99-158](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:160-173]().

### Execution backends

`LoRAManager` resolves the configured backend name through `get_backend_from_name` and creates the backend with the batch-capacity, device, and server-argument context [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:132-143](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:17-30](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/chunked_backend.py:15-41](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/ascend_backend.py:1-22]().

| Backend | Implementation and behavior shown |
|---|---|
| Triton | `triton_backend.py` imports dense LoRA kernels for embedding, SGEMM, QKV, and gate-up operations and provides token-routing helpers [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:1-30](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:33-70](). |
| Chunked SGMV (`csgmv`) | `ChunkedSgmvLoRABackend` uses segmented matrix-vector multiplication and chunks sequences to reduce excessive kernel launches when adapter distribution is skewed. It declares prefill CUDA graph support [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/chunked_backend.py:27-41](). |
| Ascend | `AscendLoRABackend` implements embedding, shrink, and expand operations; its shown methods call NPU operations for dense LoRA computation [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/ascend_backend.py:13-22](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/ascend_backend.py:24-85](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/ascend_backend.py:87-116](). |
| Torch backend | `TorchNativeLoRABackend` provides PyTorch-native fallback operations for LoRA processing [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/torch_backend.py:34-43](). |

The Triton backend also contains DP-attention routing helpers. They gather DP-local adapter indices into a global token layout and construct global batch metadata for TP-global model sections [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:73-104](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/triton_backend.py:107-159]().

## 5. Special LoRA types

### Embedding LoRA

`VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA` implements embedding-specific LoRA handling. It stores embedding dimensions and vocabulary information, accepts embedding buffers through `set_lora_info`, and describes the embedding delta as an LoRA-A lookup followed by an LoRA-B projection [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:99-158](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:160-173]().

The wrapper documents that, with TP greater than one, embedding LoRA weights are replicated rather than sharded. It also asserts against the combination of TP greater than one and input-scattered attention context because the replicated embedding-LoRA approach is not mathematically correct in that mode [python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:118-133]().

### MoE LoRA

The MoE LoRA implementation injects LoRA deltas at two stages: after the gate-up projection and before activation, and after the down projection and before the final reduction. It uses hook closures so MoE backends can call into LoRA without requiring a separate LoRA runner subclass for every backend [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:15-23](). 

Furthermore, `FusedMoEWithLoRA` explicitly disables in-place execution (`inplace=False`) on the shared runner configuration object to prevent race conditions during decode graph replay where shared experts read inputs asynchronously [test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_moe_inplace_unit.py:1-6](), [test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_moe_inplace_unit.py:53-62]().

`LoRAInfo` carries the MoE LoRA weights, segment pointers, request-to-adapter mapping, rank and enabled-adapter metadata, token-to-adapter mapping, expert count, and options such as shared outer LoRAs and virtual experts [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:149-188]().

For small batches, `_naive_moe_lora_align_block_size` constructs token/expert alignment on CPU and transfers the resulting tensors to the target device [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:66-84](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:85-146]().

`StandardDispatcher` records the runner’s expert-ID convention. It rejects an EP configuration where the dispatcher’s global-versus-local expert-ID convention disagrees with the MoE runner convention while LoRA is enabled or adapter paths are configured [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py:105-145]().

`LoRAMemoryPool` uses the MoE EP context, runner convention, and MoE TP context to decide how per-expert LoRA buffers are represented and sized [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:165-188]().

Diagram: MoE LoRA Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RequestSegments["MoE request segments"]
    BatchRouting["MoELoRABatchInfo"]
    Dispatcher["StandardDispatcher"]
    ExpertRouting["topk expert routing"]
    Hooks["LoRAHooks"]
    GateUp["LoRA delta after gate_up projection"]
    Down["LoRA delta after down projection"]
    Reduction["Final expert reduction"]

    RequestSegments --> BatchRouting
    BatchRouting --> Dispatcher
    Dispatcher --> ExpertRouting
    ExpertRouting --> Hooks
    Hooks --> GateUp
    GateUp --> Down
    Down --> Reduction
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:15-23](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py:149-188](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py:105-145](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:35-49](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py:165-188](), [test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_moe_inplace_unit.py:1-6](), [python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_overlap_loader.py:21-98]()

## Purpose and scope

SGLang accepts per-request grammar constraints for structured generation, including JSON Schema, regular expressions, EBNF, and structural tags [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:182-186](). The scheduler's `GrammarManager` connects these request settings to a pluggable grammar backend (`BaseGrammarBackend`), which tracks grammar state and produces vocabulary masks that exclude disallowed next tokens via backends like `xgrammar`, `llguidance`, and `outlines` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:37-50](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:36-38](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-83](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:89-96](). This page describes the request parameters, the `GrammarManager` dispatch path, backend contracts, and mask generation flows.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:182-186](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:37-50](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:36-38](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-83](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:89-96]()

---

## Request constraints and supported forms

`SamplingParams` carries structured-output parameters: `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:182-186](). These parameters control grammar-guided generation, which is distinct from simple stopping criteria such as `stop` or `stop_regex` [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:164-170]().

| Constraint Field | Input Type | Grammar-Manager Dispatch Key |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | JSON Schema string | `"json"` |
| `regex` | Regular expression string | `"regex"` |
| `ebnf` | EBNF string | `"ebnf"` (or `"full_assistant_ebnf"` when `ebnf_full_assistant` is enabled) |
| `structural_tag` | Structural tag definition string | `"structural_tag"` |

The dispatch keys and fallback handling are evaluated inside `GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:157-171](). Empty strings provided for any of these fields are normalized to `None` rather than treated as restrictive empty constraints [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:86-94]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:164-186](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:157-171](), [test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_params.py:86-94]()

## Request-to-Code Bridge: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space

This diagram bridges user-facing structured output requests to the underlying codebase entities, mapping fields from `SamplingParams` directly to the `GrammarManager` dispatch logic.

**Diagram: Request mapping bridge to code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    NLReq[""UserStructuredOutputRequest""] --> SP[""SamplingParams (sampling_params.py)""]
    SP --> JS[""json_schema""]
    SP --> RG[""regex""]
    SP --> EB[""ebnf""]
    SP --> ST[""structural_tag""]
    
    JS --> GM[""GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar (grammar_manager.py)""]
    RG --> GM
    EB --> GM
    ST --> GM
    
    GM --> KJson[""key = ('json', json_schema)""]
    GM --> KRegex[""key = ('regex', regex)""]
    GM --> KEbnf[""key = ('ebnf' or 'full_assistant_ebnf', ebnf)""]
    GM --> KTag[""key = ('structural_tag', structural_tag)""]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:182-186](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:157-171]()

## GrammarManager lifecycle and execution flow

`GrammarManager` initializes with a scheduler reference, extracts `ServerArgs`, and instantiates a grammar backend via `create_grammar_backend` using the scheduler's tokenizer, vocabulary size, EOS token ID, and thinking-end IDs [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:37-50](). It maintains a `grammar_queue` implemented via `IndexedReqList` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:41-41]().

When a request arrives with a grammar constraint, `process_req_with_grammar` checks for an active `grammar_backend`. If the backend is missing (e.g., launched with `--grammar-backend none`), the request is aborted with an error message [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:165-168](). Otherwise, it constructs the grammar key and queues asynchronous compilation via the backend executor [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:183-188]().

**Diagram: GrammarManager request flow and PP synchronization**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Req as "Req"
    participant GM as "GrammarManager"
    participant GB as "BaseGrammarBackend"
    participant Q as "IndexedReqList (grammar_queue)"
    participant PP as "PP Group"

    Req->>GM: "process_req_with_grammar(req)"
    GM->>GB: "get_cached_or_future_value(key)"
    alt Cache Miss
        GB--->GM: "Future (Async Compilation)"
        GM->>Q: "Add to grammar_queue"
    else Cache Hit
        GB--->GM: "BaseGrammarObject (Copy)"
    end
    GM->>PP: "_pp_sync_ready_failed(ready_req_idxs, failed_req_idxs)"
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:37-120](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:183-188]()

---

## Backend contract, cache, and asynchronous compilation

`BaseGrammarObject` establishes the abstract interface for constrained decoding [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:58-128](). `BaseGrammarBackend` manages caching and asynchronous compilation tasks via a `ThreadPoolExecutor` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:183-188]().

| Contract Method / Property | Code Entity & Role |
|---|---|
| `accept_token(token)` | Updates internal matcher state with a newly generated token [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:72-76]() |
| `rollback(k)` | Reverts grammar state by `k` tokens [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:78-79]() |
| `fill_vocab_mask(mask, row)` | Populates the vocabulary mask tensor for a specific batch row [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:89-92]() |
| `apply_vocab_mask(logits, mask)` | Applies the filled bitmask to logit tensors prior to sampling [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:115-116]() |
| `copy()` | Clones a request-specific grammar object from a cached prototype [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:118-119]() |

`GrammarStats` tracks compilation metrics, including `compilation_time`, `schema_count`, `ebnf_size`, `is_cache_hit`, and `tree_traversal_time` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:40-49]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:38-128](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:183-188]()

---

## Grammar Backends: xgrammar, llguidance, and outlines

SGLang supports multiple compiler backends for parsing structural outputs and generating token bitmasks:

1. **xgrammar (`XGrammarGrammar`)**: Integrates `xgrammar`'s `GrammarMatcher` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-89](). Vocabulary masks are allocated as token bitmasks (`_allocate_token_bitmask`), populated via `fill_next_token_bitmask`, and applied using Triton or CUDA operations [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:66-75](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:140-152]().
2. **llguidance (`GuidanceGrammar`)**: Utilizes `llguidance`'s `LLMatcher` and `LLExecutor` for fast batch mask population (`fill_token_bitmask_batched`) [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:50-62](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:89-110]().
3. **outlines**: Supported via compatibility layers registered in `GRAMMAR_BACKEND_REGISTRY` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:36-36]().

## Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space: Backend Dispatch & Execution

This second bridge diagram maps high-level backend configuration structures down to specific execution classes and token filtering kernel implementations.

**Diagram: Backend dispatch and execution code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Args[""ServerArgs.grammar_backend""] --> Factory[""create_grammar_backend (base_grammar_backend.py)""]
    Factory --> XGBackend[""XGrammarGrammar (xgrammar_backend.py)""]
    Factory --> LLBackend[""GuidanceGrammar (llguidance_backend.py)""]
    
    XGBackend --> XMatch[""GrammarMatcher.fill_next_token_bitmask""]
    LLBackend --> LLMatch[""LLMatcher / fill_token_bitmask_batched""]
    
    XMatch --> TritonOp[""apply_token_bitmask_inplace_triton""]
    LLMatch --> TorchOp[""apply_token_bitmask_inplace""]
    
    TritonOp --> Logits[""Logits Tensor Modification""]
    TorchOp --> Logits
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:36-36](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:66-152](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:50-110]()

## Reasoning-aware constraints

`ReasonerGrammarObject` wraps an underlying grammar object to separate internal reasoning phases (such as chain-of-thought blocks) from structured output generation [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-85](). It tracks reasoning terminators and respects `max_think_tokens` budgets [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:62-72]().

`GrammarManager` applies request-level reasoning configurations, validating terminator sequences against model capabilities and wiring thinking budgets from `custom_params["thinking_budget"]` [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:138-156]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-85](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:138-156]()

---

## Grammar statistics and monitoring

`GrammarStats` collects telemetry during grammar compilation and mask generation, allowing operators to monitor compilation latency, cache hit rates, and schema complexities [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:40-49]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py:40-49]()

## Purpose and scope

This page documents the observability surfaces implemented in the codebase: scheduler and runtime metrics collection, Prometheus endpoint exposition, OpenTelemetry tracing integration, request time statistics, production metric categories, and timing mechanisms. The core entities include `SchedulerStats` and `SchedulerMetricsCollector` in `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py`, request stage configurations in `python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py`, and the `SchedulerMetricsReporter` in `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py`.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:59-177](), [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:28-45](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:19-30]()

## Overview and Metrics Collection Architecture

The observability architecture separates scheduler-level metrics tracking from request-level timing and tracing. `SchedulerStats` defines the structured state for queues, throughput, cache hit rates, KV-pool usages, speculative decoding performance, and disaggregation statistics [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:79-177](). `SchedulerMetricsReporter` consumes this data model alongside `SchedulerMetricsCollector`, maintaining time-windowed cache hit rates via `_CacheHitRateWindow` and deriving prefill metrics via `PrefillStats` [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:19-160]().

`ReqTimeStats` manages request-level latencies, integrating with tokenizer, encoder, and scheduler metric collectors as well as synchronous and asynchronous tracing contexts [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:26-45](). Integration tests validate this collection pipeline by launching a server with `--enable-metrics` and parsing Prometheus responses [test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py:104-175]().

The metric model distinguishes queue counts from per-priority queue breakdowns: `QueueCount.from_reqs` populates priority counters when priority scheduling is enabled [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:59-76](). `SchedulerStats` aggregates queue lengths, token usage ratios across full, SWA, and Mamba pools, and absolute token availability counts [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:79-130]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:59-130](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:19-30]()

## Prometheus Integration and Production Metrics

SGLang exposes metrics via a Prometheus-compatible endpoint when started with `--enable-metrics` [test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py:104-175](). Integration tests verify metric families such as `sglang:num_running_reqs`, `sglang:num_used_tokens`, `sglang:token_usage`, `sglang:gen_throughput`, `sglang:num_queue_reqs`, `sglang:num_grammar_queue_reqs`, and `sglang:cache_hit_rate` [test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py:178-187]().

Additional metrics cover device timers, data parallelism cooperation token totals, scheduled attention pairs, imbalance metrics, and synchronization wait times [test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py:70-123]().

### Production Metric Groups

| Group | Code Entities and Values Represented |
|---|---|
| Scheduler Queues | `QueueCount`, running/queued request counts, grammar queue count, and priority breakdowns [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:59-81](). |
| Throughput and Cache | Generation throughput (`gen_throughput`) and sliding window cache hit rate (`cache_hit_rate`) [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:82-83](). |
| KV and Memory Pools | `SchedulerStats` usage ratios (`token_usage`, `full_token_usage`, `window_token_usage`, `swa_token_usage`, `mamba_usage`) and absolute counts (`kv_available_tokens`, `kv_evictable_tokens`, `kv_used_tokens`) [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:86-130](). |
| Speculative Decoding | Acceptance length (`spec_accept_length`), acceptance rate (`spec_accept_rate`), block acceptance length, step count, and draft token count [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:131-139](). |
| Disaggregation | Prefill/decode queue counts, KV transfer speed (`kv_transfer_speed_gb_s`), latency, and preallocated token usage [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:144-162](). |

`SchedulerStats` computes pool usage ratios as `used / total`, where used capacity excludes available and evictable slots [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:86-102](). 

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py:59-177](), [test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py:70-187]()

### Collector Customization

Unit tests verify dependency-injection for metric collectors via `resolve_collector_class`, which selects registered subclasses for roles like `scheduler`, `tokenizer`, `storage`, `radix_cache`, and `expert_dispatch` [test/registered/unit/observability/test_stat_loggers_di.py:93-138](). The default collector path utilizes `prometheus_client` metric types [test/registered/unit/observability/test_stat_loggers_di.py:141-151]().

Sources: [test/registered/unit/observability/test_stat_loggers_di.py:93-151]()

## Request Time Stats and Pipeline Tracing

Request lifecycle tracking is managed through `RequestStageConfig` and `RequestStage` definitions in `python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py`, where stages are assigned hierarchical trace levels and per-stage latency observation flags [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:88-104](). Stages span tokenization (`TOKENIZE`), API dispatch (`API_SERVER_DISPATCH`), request processing (`REQUEST_PROCESS`), prefill (`PREFILL_FORWARD`, `PREFILL_CHUNKED_FORWARD`), decode (`DECODE_FORWARD`, `DECODE_LOOP`), speculative execution, and disaggregation steps [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:106-226]().

Time conversion helpers calibrate the offset between wall-clock time (`time.time()`) and monotonic time (`time.perf_counter()`) to avoid NTP skew during request latency calculations [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:56-85]().

## OpenTelemetry Tracing

OpenTelemetry integration leverages `SpanAttributes`, `TraceNullContext`, `TraceReqContext`, `TraceSliceContext`, and asynchronous tracing wrappers (`TraceReqContextAsync`) [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:33-45](). Unit tests confirm that `set_finished_time` correctly computes prefill, time-to-first-token (TTFT), end-to-end, and decode latencies, passing these attributes to the active trace context [test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py:104-151]().

Furthermore, `ReqTimeStatsBase.__setstate__` handles timestamp rebasing during inter-process serialization, re-anchoring monotonic timestamps to the receiving process's clock while preserving unset `0.0` sentinels [test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py:1-47]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:33-45](), [test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py:1-47](), [test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py:104-151]()

## Scheduler Timing and Forward-Pass Measurements

`SchedulerMetricsReporter` integrates with `DeviceTimer`, `ScheduledRequestMetrics`, `WelfordAccumulator`, and `wrap_forward_with_fpm` to measure forward-pass durations [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:19-46](). It tracks a one-second scheduler time-accounting interval and employs `_CacheHitRateWindow` to expire cache hit samples past the configured window [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:65-100](). Prefill batch metrics are summarized via `PrefillStats.from_adder` [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:121-160]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:19-160]()

| `SGLANG_RECORD_STEP_TIME` | Controls step-time recording behavior [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:61](). |
| `SGLANG_LOG_FORWARD_ITERS` | Controls forward iteration logging frequency [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:62](). |
| `SGLANG_TEST_REQUEST_TIME_STATS` | Enables request time statistics testing hooks [python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py:53](). |

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the session-related KV-cache behavior visible in SGLang’s streaming-session implementation: how a streaming turn can borrow persistent KV state, how finished turns return it to a session slot, and how aborts affect that state. The runtime session and cache integration manage multi-turn streaming conversations and context persistence via `StreamingSession` and `SessionSlot` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:29-63]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:29-63]()

## 1. Overview and Architecture

`StreamingSession` manages session slots for `UnifiedRadixCache`. A slot combines a `ReqKvInfo` record with a tree lock on the session’s tree-owned prefix; it also has a virtual-node sentinel and a flag used when the first turn is publishing its prompt [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:23-45]().

The cache imports `StreamingSession` and `is_virtual_node`, and `UnifiedRadixCache.__init__` records session-related cache settings [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:50-74]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:71-74]().

| Entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `StreamingSession` | Stores session slots and provides try-handle methods for active-session lookup, prefix matching, and finished-request handling [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:59-67]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-94]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172](). |
| `SessionSlot` | Holds the session’s `ReqKvInfo`, optional `TreeLock`, virtual node, and prompt-publication flag [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49](). |
| `_VirtualNode` | Sentinel lock target for session-owned KV; locking it is described as a no-op [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:26-30](). |
| `ReqKvInfo` | Per-request KV record stored in the slot; the session code reads its committed length and protected-cache length [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:41-41](). |
| `UnifiedRadixCache` | Cache associated with the session manager; it is passed to `StreamingSession` at construction [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:71-74](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:23-67]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:71-94]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

### Mapping Natural Language to Code Entities: Ownership and Cache Integration

A session slot owns the persistent record and tree lock between turns; a request borrows the record while its turn is processed [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:59-67]().

## 2. Session Lifecycle and Data Flow

### Flow Description

The implementation supports a lifecycle where a streaming request finds an active slot, borrows its KV record during prefix matching, and returns the record to the slot when the turn finishes or is retracted. An aborted turn removes the slot entry and returns its lock to the request [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-93]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]().

**Diagram: Streaming Session Turn Lifecycle**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Request as "Req"
    participant Session as "StreamingSession"
    participant Slot as "SessionSlot"
    participant Cache as "UnifiedRadixCache"

    Request->>Session: "find_active_slot(req)"
    Session->>Slot: "lookup by session_id"
    Session-->>Request: "active SessionSlot or None"
    Request->>Session: "try_match_prefix(params)"
    Session->>Slot: "lend slot.kv to req.kv"
    Session-->>Request: "MatchResult with session prefix"
    Note over Session,Slot: "Finished or retracted turn keeps its record in the slot"
    Request->>Session: "try_cache_finished_req(req)"
    Session->>Slot: "retain session record"
    Note over Session,Cache: "Abort path returns lock to request and removes slot entry"
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-93]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

### Active Slot Lookup and Pre-Abort Handling

`find_active_slot(req)` applies only when the request has a session and that session is marked streaming [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:55-56]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-87](). If `req.to_finish` is set, lookup releases multimodal inputs, calls `req.session.abort_req()`, detaches the request by setting `req.session = None`, and returns `None` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:88-92]().

`will_lend_record(req)` returns true for a streaming request not marked to finish whose session slot exists and holds KV [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:95-101]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:55-56]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-101]()

### Prefix Matching and KV Reuse

`try_match_prefix(params)` returns `None` when no active session slot is found. When a slot matches, `slot.kv` is lent to `req.kv`, and the reusable prefix is calculated as the minimum of committed KV length and request key length [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-114]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:133-138]().

Streaming sessions are append-only; an assertion ensures the prefix does not shrink below `cache_protected_len` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:141-145](). For page sizes greater than 1, alignment rules apply on NPU or when evicted sequence length exceeds the prefix length [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:117-129]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:148-154]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]()

### Finished Turns and Abort Behavior

`try_cache_finished_req(req)` verifies streaming state. On abort, it deletes the slot from `slots`, transfers the lock back to the request, releases multimodal inputs, and returns `False` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

---

## 3. Cache Management and Memory Entities

### Session Slot and KV Cache Persistence

A `SessionSlot` groups the persistent KV record (`kv`) with an optional tree lock (`lock`), a `_VirtualNode` instance, and a `publishes_prompt` flag [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49](). `StreamingSession.slots` indexes slots by session ID [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:73-73]().

**Diagram: Session Memory Classes**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class StreamingSession {
        +cache: UnifiedRadixCache
        +slots: Dict[str, SessionSlot]
        +any_holding_kv() bool
        +find_active_slot(req) Optional~SessionSlot~
        +will_lend_record(req) bool
        +try_match_prefix(params) Optional~MatchResult~
        +try_cache_finished_req(req) bool
    }

    class SessionSlot {
        +virtual_node: _VirtualNode
        +kv: ReqKvInfo
        +lock: Optional~TreeLock~
        +publishes_prompt: bool
    }

    class ReqKvInfo {
        +holds_kv
        +kv_committed_len
        +cache_protected_len
        +max_evicted_seqlen
    }

    class Req {
        +session
        +kv: ReqKvInfo
        +to_finish
        +finished_reason
    }

    StreamingSession *-- SessionSlot : "stores by session_id"
    SessionSlot *-- ReqKvInfo : "owns between turns"
    StreamingSession ..> Req : "checks and borrows"
    SessionSlot --> TreeLock : "protects tree-owned prefix"
    SessionSlot --> _VirtualNode : "session lock target"
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:26-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:59-73]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-101]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

### Multi-Turn Context Persistence

When a streaming request matches an active session, `try_match_prefix` assigns `slot.kv` to `req.kv` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:133-134](). Unit tests confirm that finished turns preserve metadata such as `mamba_next_track_idx` and component-specific evicted sequence lengths in the slot record [test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_streaming_session_unit.py:141-150]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:133-134]() [test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_streaming_session_unit.py:141-150]()

---

## 4. Observability and State Validation

The session implementation exposes `any_holding_kv()` to track whether any slot holds active KV allocations [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:75-76](). Unit tests cover slot retention after finished turns and safe detachment on pre-aborts [test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_streaming_session_unit.py:138-202]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:75-76]() [test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_streaming_session_unit.py:138-202]()

## 5. Session State Reference

| Field or method | Meaning in the session implementation |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | Key used to find a session slot in `StreamingSession.slots` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-86](). |
| `streaming` | Session flag checked by `_is_streaming(req)` [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:55-56](). |
| `SessionSlot.kv` | The `ReqKvInfo` record retained by the slot [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:133-134](). |
| `kv_committed_len` | Upper bound on session prefix length considered for reuse [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:135-139](). |
| `cache_protected_len` | Lower bound enforced by append-only prefix checks [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:141-145](). |
| `SessionSlot.lock` | Optional tree lock held with the session prefix [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172](). |
| `SessionSlot.virtual_node` | Sentinel used as node anchor in session match results [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:26-30]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:158-164](). |
| `find_active_slot(req)` | Looks up active slot and handles pre-aborts [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-93](). |
| `will_lend_record(req)` | Tests whether request can borrow a slot record [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:95-101](). |
| `try_match_prefix(params)` | Attempts session-specific prefix reuse [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-114](). |
| `try_cache_finished_req(req)` | Handles finished streaming requests and aborts [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:26-56]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:59-101]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

---

## Summary

SGLang’s streaming-session implementation maintains persistent `ReqKvInfo` records and tree locks inside `SessionSlot` instances. Active streaming requests borrow these records across conversation turns, subject to committed-length and alignment constraints. Aborted turns cleanly detach and return locks, while completed turns preserve state for subsequent interaction rounds [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-101]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:32-49]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:80-101]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:103-165]() [python/sglang/srt/session/streaming_session.py:166-172]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes SGLang’s function-call parsing and reasoning-parsing components: the parser and detector roles, model-specific detectors registered in `FunctionCallParser`, incremental parsing, tool-call formats, JSON schema normalization utilities, and how reasoning text is separated from ordinary output. It focuses on parsing, response formatting, and constrained decoding integration rather than tool execution [test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py:8-41](), [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:50-63](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:113-175]().

Sources: [test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py:8-41](), [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:50-63](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:113-175]()

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

Function-call parsing converts model-generated text or token-derived text into ordinary response text plus structured tool-call data. The core entry point is `FunctionCallParser`, which instantiates model-specific detectors via its `ToolCallParserEnum` mapping [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:70-128]().

The reasoning parser operates independently through `BaseReasoningFormatDetector`, whose `StreamingParseResult` holds `normal_text` and `reasoning_text` [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:54-64](). Constrained decoding backends such as `XGrammarGrammar` and `GuidanceGrammar` work alongside `ReasonerGrammarObject` to enforce schema compliance across token generation boundaries [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-114](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:89-136](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-97]().

### Key Components

| Entity | Role | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `FunctionCallParser` | Central manager for tool-call extraction and parser selection. | [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:70-128]() |
| `BaseFormatDetector` | Base detector interface implemented by model-specific tool detectors. | [python/sglang/srt/function_call/base_format_detector.py:1-15]() |
| `StreamingParseResult` (Function Call) | Holds parsed tool call items and normal text during incremental processing. | [python/sglang/srt/function_call/core_types.py:1-30]() |
| `BaseReasoningFormatDetector` | Base class for reasoning-format detectors, with one-time and incremental parsing interfaces. | [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:66-83]() |
| `StreamingParseResult` (Reasoning) | Contains `normal_text` and `reasoning_text`, defaulting missing values to empty strings. | [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:54-64]() |
| `ReasonerGrammarObject` | Defers structural/grammar constraints until reasoning termination or tool invocation. | [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-97]() |


## 3. Streaming and Incremental Parsing

Incremental parsing handles chunked text streams. For example, `Qwen3CoderDetector`, `DeepSeekV32Detector`, and `Glm47MoeDetector` maintain internal buffer positions and state flags (such as `StreamState` in `Glm47MoeDetector`) to parse XML-to-JSON tool invocations and parameters incrementally as chunks arrive from the generation engine [python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py:23-58](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/deepseekv32_detector.py:21-105](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm47_moe_detector.py:39-48]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py:23-58](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/deepseekv32_detector.py:21-105](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm47_moe_detector.py:39-48]()

---

## 4. Reasoning Parser and Toggle Configuration

`BaseReasoningFormatDetector` manages reasoning boundaries via `detect_and_parse()` and incremental streaming updates [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:66-158](). It tracks whether generation is inside a `<think>` block, strips opening tokens, and checks for tool-start interruptions.

Template detection rules (`REASONING_MODE_RULES` in `python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py`) analyze chat templates via `TemplateDetectionContext` and `ReasoningToggleConfig` to automatically resolve reasoning toggles, such as `enable_thinking`, effort arguments, or model-specific thinking behaviors [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:40-78](), [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:149-175]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:66-183](), [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:40-78](), [python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py:149-175]()

---

## 5. Tool Call Formats, JSON Schema Normalization, and Coercion

Tool arguments frequently rely on non-standard database types or custom schemas. SGLang provides schema validation and type resolution helpers (such as `_argument_types` and `get_argument_type` in `Glm47MoeDetector`) alongside JSON schema constraint generators [python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm47_moe_detector.py:88-174](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:113-175]().

Additionally, constrained decoding backends (`XGrammarGrammar` and `GuidanceGrammar`) integrate these constraints with `ReasonerGrammarObject` to pause structural validation until reasoning blocks terminate or tool markers appear [python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py:78-114](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/llguidance_backend.py:89-136](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-97]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm47_moe_detector.py:88-174](), [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:113-175](), [python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:43-97]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents SGLang’s discrete diffusion LLM (DLLM) support: its configuration and scheduler integration, request-state handling, and iterative denoising flow for masked language models such as LLaDA2 and SDAR [python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py:1-25](), [python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py:1-20](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158](). DLLMs refine masked token sequences through repeated model evaluations rather than generating only one token at a time.

The topics covered are `DllmConfig`, `SchedulerDllmMixin`, request phases, FDFO scheduling, and the data flow that coordinates repeated denoising passes [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14](), [python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py:1-25](), [python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py:1-20]()

---

## Architecture Overview

DLLM support adds diffusion-specific configuration, request lifecycle state, and scheduling behavior to the serving runtime. The scheduler coordinates repeated denoising passes and tracks tokens that are accepted or still unresolved [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158]().

### Key Components

| Name | Role | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `DllmConfig` | Stores DLLM decoding configuration, including algorithm and block-related settings. | [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `SchedulerDllmMixin` | Provides DLLM-specific scheduler behavior, including request staging, batch creation, and batch-result processing. | [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158]() |
| `DllmReqPhase` | Represents DLLM request lifecycle phases. | [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14]() |
| `DllmAlgorithm` | Defines the denoising-algorithm interface used to refine tokens and determine block progress. | [python/sglang/srt/dllm/algorithm/base.py:1-30]() |
| `ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND` | Identifies a DLLM forward pass in the scheduling and execution path. | [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-67]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158]()

### DLLM Request Dataflow

This diagram bridges the user-visible task of refining a masked prompt with the runtime entities that carry out DLLM serving. The scheduler’s DLLM path repeatedly forms batches and processes results, while request state preserves progress between denoising passes [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14]().

**Diagram: Masked-prompt refinement mapped to runtime entities**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Prompt["User_prompt_with_masked_positions"]
        Refined["Refined_generated_sequence"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Config["DllmConfig"]
        Req["Req_and_DllmReqPhase"]
        Scheduler["SchedulerDllmMixin"]
        Batch["ScheduleBatch"]
        Forward["ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND"]
        Algorithm["DllmAlgorithm"]
        Result["process_batch_result_dllm"]
    end

    Prompt --> Req
    Config --> Scheduler
    Req --> Scheduler
    Scheduler --> Batch
    Batch --> Forward
    Forward --> Algorithm
    Algorithm --> Result
    Result --> Req
    Result --> Refined
```

## Scheduling and Execution Details

DLLM requests require multiple refinement passes. `SchedulerDllmMixin` integrates DLLM-specific queueing, batch construction, and result processing into the scheduler so that requests can progress through those passes while retaining their per-request state [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-158]().

### First-Done-First-Out (FDFO) Scheduling

The DLLM scheduler supports FDFO behavior to let requests or blocks that make progress move forward without requiring every request in a batch to complete at the same rate. The mixin processes per-request acceptance results and maintains unresolved token and algorithm state for future passes [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]().

At a high level:

- The denoising algorithm returns an `accept_length` indicating how many tokens in a request’s current block can be accepted [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150]().
- Accepted tokens advance the request’s committed sequence state [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150]().
- Unresolved token IDs and algorithm state are retained for subsequent processing [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:113-119]().
- The configuration can enable or tune FDFO-related behavior [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150]()

### Iterative Denoising Loop

The scheduler mixin provides the DLLM-specific operations that participate in the iterative loop. These include initialization, fetching waiting requests, constructing a DLLM batch, and processing the completed batch result [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-170]().

1. **Initialize DLLM scheduling.** `init_diffusion_llm()` initializes DLLM-specific manager and state [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-67]().
2. **Fetch requests.** `_fetch_waiting_reqs()` moves eligible waiting requests into the running DLLM pool, subject to the configured concurrency limit [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-82]().
3. **Build a batch.** `get_new_batch_dllm()` constructs a batch for DLLM work [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-82]().
4. **Execute a DLLM forward pass.** The batch uses `ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND` for the diffusion-specific execution path [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-67]().
5. **Process results and continue or finish.** `process_batch_result_dllm()` updates accepted tokens, preserves unresolved state, and handles output streaming [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:22-170]()

---

### DLLM Batch Result Processing Flow

The result-processing path branches on whether a request made progress in its current denoising step. Accepted work updates request sequence state; unfinished work keeps its incomplete IDs and algorithm state available for a later pass [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150]().

**Diagram: Batch results mapped to scheduler actions**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Execution Space"
        Finished["DLLM_batch_forward_finished"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Process["SchedulerDllmMixin.process_batch_result_dllm"]
        Iterate["Process_each_request_result"]
        Check{"accept_length_greater_than_zero"}
        Commit["Update_accepted_token_and_sequence_state"]
        Stash["Preserve_dllm_incomplete_ids_and_dllm_algo_state"]
        Stream["output_streamer.stream_output"]
    end

    Finished --> Process
    Process --> Iterate
    Iterate --> Check
    Check -->|Yes| Commit
    Check -->|No| Stash
    Commit --> Stream
    Stash --> Stream
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:83-150](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14]()

---

## Denoising Algorithms and States

The algorithm abstraction separates token refinement from scheduler bookkeeping. The scheduler coordinates repeated execution and retains per-request state, while the selected denoising algorithm determines how logits are used to produce token updates [python/sglang/srt/dllm/algorithm/base.py:1-30](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:113-119]().

| Concept | Description | Code entity |
|---|---|---|
| Denoising algorithm | Interface for converting model outputs into token updates and reporting block progress. | `DllmAlgorithm` [python/sglang/srt/dllm/algorithm/base.py:1-30]() |
| Algorithm state | Per-request state retained between denoising rounds. | `dllm_algo_state` [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:113-119]() |
| Incomplete token IDs | Token IDs that have not yet been accepted and must be available for continued refinement. | `dllm_incomplete_ids` [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:113-119]() |
| Request phase | DLLM-specific lifecycle phase tracked for a request. | `DllmReqPhase` [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/algorithm/base.py:1-30](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/req.py:8-14](), [python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:113-119]()

---

## Configuration and Supported Models

### DLLM Configuration (`DllmConfig`)

`DllmConfig` is the central DLLM configuration object. Its settings describe the denoising algorithm and the token-block and masking behavior used by DLLM execution [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]().

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `algorithm` | Selects a denoising algorithm, such as `low_confidence` or `joint_threshold`. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `block_size` | Sets the number of tokens handled in a denoising block. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `mask_id` | Identifies the token used to represent masked positions. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `joint_threshold_joint_length` | Supplies a tuning parameter for joint-threshold decoding. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `joint_threshold_token_ratio` | Supplies a token-ratio tuning parameter for joint-threshold decoding. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `emulate_mlm` | Controls the configured MLM-emulation behavior. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |
| `fdfo_enabled` | Controls whether FDFO scheduling is enabled. [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]()

### Supported DLLM Architectures

- **LLaDA2:** The runtime includes the `LLaDA2ForCausalLM` model implementation [python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py:1-25]().
- **SDAR:** The runtime includes an SDAR model implementation and DLLM-specific support [python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py:1-20]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py:1-25](), [python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py:1-20]()

### Runtime Configuration and Flags

DLLM runtime behavior is controlled through `DllmConfig` and its algorithm, block, masking, and FDFO settings. The available configuration fields are defined in `python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py`; consult that definition for the current configuration surface [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/dllm/config.py:7-78]()
