This page documents SGLang's engine capabilities and integration pathways designed for Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems, post-training workflows, and advanced engine control. Topics covered include online weight synchronization and refitting, checkpoint integrity verification, engine sleep/wake lifecycle management, partial rollouts with cached-prefix replay, deterministic inference state handling, and integration with post-training frameworks.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

## Overview and Purpose

SGLang provides specialized runtime control features to support Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and iterative post-training pipelines where actor models require frequent weight updates, deterministic rollouts, prompt prefix reuse, and memory saving modes. The primary runtime components involved are `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager`, `WeightUpdater`, `WeightChecker`, and encoder-SWA replay mechanisms. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

## Weight Synchronization and Refitting

The weight-update path is organized around `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager` and per-runner `WeightUpdater` objects. The manager selects target and/or draft runners, invokes runner-specific update methods, records a supplied weight version after successful disk updates, and can request a cache flush after the target runner changes. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:71-79](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:87-103](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-163]()

### Dynamic Weight Updates

`SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager` accepts update request structures for disk, distributed, IPC, and tensor sources. Its constructor receives the target worker, draft worker, cache-flush callback, idle-state callback, and optional scheduler and metrics collector. It also captures a TP CPU group during initialization. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:87-103]()

For disk updates, `update_weights_from_disk` iterates the selected runners and delegates to each runner’s `weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk`. On success it records the requested weight version. If the target runner was updated, it applies the requested cache-flush policy; a refused flush returns a failure response explaining that requests remain active or queued. Weight-load duration is observed with a source label, here `"disk"`. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:105-118](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-163]()

Runner selection supports `"target"`, `"draft"`, and `"all"`; `"all"` selects both target and draft roles, while other values are rejected. A weight-update session records the selector chosen at begin time so that end-of-update handling can finalize the same runner set. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:71-85]()

| Concern | Code entity | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Update request types | `UpdateWeightFromDiskReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromDistributedReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromIPCReqInput`, `UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput` | [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]() |
| Runner selection | `_parse_runner_selector` | [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:71-79]() |
| Disk update orchestration | `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager.update_weights_from_disk` | [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:138-163]() |
| Cache flush after target update | `flush_cache_after_weight_update` | [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-133]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:71-163]()

### Update Safety and Cache Consistency

The model-side updater rejects online mutations when derived-weight caches may remain stale. `_unsupported_derived_weight_cache_error` checks for compensated weight splits and constraints whose cached split would retain old weights. The updater also rejects weight mutation while the CUDA IPC weight cache is active: in that mode, parameter data is shared from a master daemon copy. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-133]()

After a target weight update, `flush_cache_after_weight_update` calls the injected flush callback only when requested. If the callback refuses due to active or queued requests, the update call fails. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-133]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:120-133]()

## Weight Verification and Checkpoint Integrity

`WeightChecker` provides actions through `handle`: snapshot, reset tensors, compare, and checksum. Snapshot copies model state into views backed by an mmap arena; comparison checks the current model against that snapshot and releases the snapshot references after the check. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:64-64]()

The checker uses shared skip rules for reset and comparison, excluding non-persistent buffers and tensors marked `_skip_weight_check`. The overall checksum is computed across sorted tensor names and checksum strings. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:64-64]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:64-64]()

## Engine Lifecycle: Sleep and Wake

The scheduler weight-updater module imports `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput` and `ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput` and their corresponding output structures. The available excerpt does not show the request handlers or establish which resources are released or restored. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

The manager constructor includes a `memory_saver_adapter` field to participate in release or resume operations. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:87-100]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:87-100]()

## Partial Rollout and Cached-Prefix Replay

Cached-prefix replay during extend processing folds cached-prefix replay into an extend batch when request windows exist and the batch is an extend without speculative decoding. It resets eligible request windows, collects cached-prefix hits, and folds replay rows into the extend batch. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

## Deterministic Inference and State Capture

Deterministic inference configurations and state capturer classes are part of advanced rollout harnesses. Their implementation details depend on backend tensor synchronization and execution flags.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

## Post-Training Framework Integrations

Post-training framework integrations involve synchronizing model weights between training actor engines and inference rollout engines via custom process groups and weight update request structures.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py:20-46]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the advanced retrieval and attention subsystems implemented in SGLang: the **Engram** n-gram lookup and embedding hash memory subsystem, the **HiSparse** hierarchical sparse attention and KV cache staging engine, and the **Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA)** / **DeepSeek TopK** indexing and routing mechanisms. These features optimize memory utilization and computational throughput for large context lengths, mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers, and specialized architectures.

---

## 1. Engram N-gram Lookup and Embedding Subsystem

The Engram subsystem provides a gated n-gram hash memory added directly to the hyperconnection (`hc`) residual stream [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:1-5](). It helps models recall frequent n-gram combinations without allocating large sequence lengths in the primary KV cache.

### Token Normalization and Compressed Maps
To prevent spelling variants, case discrepancies, and punctuation differences from fragmenting embedding lookups, token sequences are first normalized. The `build_compressed_token_map` function constructs a mapping from tokenizer token IDs to compressed IDs based on NFKC/NFD normalization, case folding, and whitespace collapsing [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:136-171](). 

```python
# Conceptual flow inside build_compressed_token_map
lookup, compressed_vocab_size = build_compressed_token_map(tokenizer)
```
*Cited from [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:136-171]().*

### Hash Multipliers and Layouts
Hash multipliers are generated per layer using a deterministic random number generator bounded to fit within 64-bit integer limits [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:174-188](). The `EngramLayout` struct records `max_ngram_size`, layer IDs, embedding sizes, and prime table layouts [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:191-198](). Configuration parameters such as placement (`cpu` vs GPU resident) and lookup strategy (`peer_read`) are governed by `EngramConfig` [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/engram_config.py:44-50]().

### Execution Kernels
During forward passes, n-gram hash IDs are computed via `engram_hash_ids` or `engram_hash_ids_and_commit` [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:34-42](). Rows are gathered using `engram_gather` or peer communication helpers (`engram_gather_peer`), and combined with the residual stream via `fused_engram_gate` [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:27-33]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Natural Language / Token IDs"] --> norm["build_compressed_token_map()"]
    norm --> hash["engram_hash_ids() / engram_hash_ids_and_commit()"]
    hash --> gather["engram_gather() / engram_gather_peer()"]
    gather --> gate["fused_engram_gate()"]
    gate --> residual["Hyperconnection Residual Stream"]
```
*Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space for Engram Retrieval.*

**Sources:**
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py:1-202]()
- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/engram_config.py` [python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/engram_config.py:44-50]()

---

## 2. HiSparse Hierarchical Sparse Attention

HiSparse provides hierarchical sparse KV cache management, dividing storage between high-bandwidth GPU memory (HBM) and host DRAM or external tiers to serve ultra-long context windows.

### Coordinator and Prefetch Planning
The `HiSparseCoordinator` manages block allocations, swap queues, and staging events [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:159-168](). For models featuring shared attention index layers (such as DeepSeek DSA architectures), `resolve_shared_index_layers` evaluates whether adjacent layers can reuse previous top-k routing decisions [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:97-131]().

Consecutive skip layers are grouped under anchor compute layers using `_build_prefetch_groups`:
```python
groups, slot = _build_prefetch_groups(is_shared_index_layer)
```
*Cited from [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:134-156]().*

### Speculative Swap Management
`HiSparseSpecSwapManager` coordinates speculative execution paths with sparse cache lookups, handling multi-step scratch capacities and metadata tracking for draft tokens [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:159-199]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    req["Req / ScheduleBatch"] --> coord["HiSparseCoordinator"]
    coord --> resolve["resolve_shared_index_layers()"]
    resolve --> groups["_build_prefetch_groups()"]
    groups --> spec["HiSparseSpecSwapManager"]
    spec --> alloc["HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator / HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool"]
    alloc --> swap["Swap-in / Host-to-Device Transfer"]
```
*Diagram: Request Staging Flow to HiSparse Code Entities.*

**Sources:**
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py` [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:1-199]()
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py` [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py:1-61]()

---

## 3. Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) and DeepSeek TopK Transforms

Sparse attention mechanisms utilize dynamic indexers to select relevant token subsets or key-value blocks, drastically lowering attention compute complexity.

### QSA Indexer
The `QSAIndexer` class implements weight-free or project-based sparse-attention indexing for models like Qwen [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py:56-66](). It validates configuration parameters including `indexer_budget`, `indexer_compress_ratio`, and `indexer_kv_heads` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py:100-132](). Fused preparation kernels are dispatched conditionally based on tensor device properties and rotary embedding configurations [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py:134-148]().

The backend integration is handled by `QwenSparseAttnBackend`, which bridges sparse indices with paged or varlen attention implementations across Triton, FlashAttention, and custom kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:1-115]().

### DeepSeek TopK Transforms (v2)
DeepSeek-V4 and related sparse models rely on specialized top-k selection and page table transformation kernels defined in `topk_v2.cuh` and wrapped in `top.py` [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh:1-120](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/topk.py:34-83]().

The selection pipeline supports three distinct exactness modes configured via `SGLANG_TOPK_V2_MODE`:
1. **FAST (`0`)**: Employs coarse histograms and threshold bins, keeping arbitrary members on overflow [python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/topk_impl.cuh:74-80]().
2. **EXACT (`1`)**: Matches `torch.topk` multiset selection [python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/topk_impl.cuh:74-80]().
3. **DETERMINISTIC (`2`)**: Enforces stable tie-breaking across runs using index-ordered keys [python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/topk_impl.cuh:74-83]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    scores["Scores Tensor / Ragged Seq Lens"] --> plan["plan_topk_v2()"]
    plan --> transform["topk_transform_paged_v2() / topk_transform_ragged_v2()"]
    transform --> exactness{Exactness Mode}
    exactness -->|0: FAST| fast_mode["Coarse Histogram Binning"]
    exactness -->|1: EXACT| exact_mode["Exact Boundary Collect"]
    exactness -->|2: DETERMINISTIC| det_mode["Index-Ordered Tie-Breaking"]
    fast_mode --> indices["Page Table Transformed Indices"]
    exact_mode --> indices
    det_mode --> indices
```
*Diagram: TopK Execution and Exactness Routing in DeepSeek Indices.*

**Sources:**
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:1-163]()
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py` [python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/qsa_indexer.py:56-166]()
- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh` [python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh:48-120]()

## Purpose and Scope

This parent page provides a high-level overview of the Rust-based router ecosystem for SGLang (`sgl-router`), which operates as a slim, KV-aware proxy layer managing worker discovery, state synchronization, and request routing across distributed inference workers [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/main.rs:1-40](). Detailed technical specifications for cache-aware routing policies, Kubernetes discovery, and the gRPC/tool pipeline are covered in the child pages [sgl-router/REFERENCE.md:1-20]().

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/main.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/REFERENCE.md:1-20]()

---

## System Overview and Architecture

The `sgl-router` crate is designed as an independent HTTP and gRPC proxy that accepts client inference requests (such as OpenAI-compatible chat completions or native `/generate` calls) and dispatches them to backend SGLang worker nodes [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:129-155](), [sgl-router/src/proxy/grpc.rs:1-30](). It coordinates state via `AppContext` and manages worker registries, health checks, and load distribution policies [sgl-router/src/server/app_context.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:1-30]().

### 1. Client Request to Router Route Handlers

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client["ClientRequest"]
    ChatRoute["chat_completions"]
    MessagesRoute["messages"]
    GenerateRoute["generate"]
    ProxyLayer["proxy::forward_request"]

    Client --> ChatRoute
    Client --> MessagesRoute
    Client --> GenerateRoute
    ChatRoute --> ProxyLayer
    MessagesRoute --> ProxyLayer
    GenerateRoute --> ProxyLayer
```

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:129-155](), [sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs:37-58]()

### 2. Core Server and State Components

The router runtime relies on centralized state containers to track worker endpoints, policies, and tokenizers [sgl-router/src/server/app_context.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs:1-40]().

```mermaid
graph LR
    Ctx["AppContext"]
    Registry["WorkerRegistry"]
    Config["Config"]
    Tokenizers["TokenizerRegistry"]
    Proxy["Proxy"]

    Ctx --> Registry
    Ctx --> Config
    Ctx --> Tokenizers
    Ctx --> Proxy
```

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/app_context.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs:1-40]()

---

## Core Runtime Components

- **HTTP/gRPC Proxy Layer**: Exposes standard endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/generate`) using Axum and Tonic frameworks, translating incoming payloads into internal representations [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:129-175](), [sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs:37-60]().
- **Worker Management**: Tracks backend engine instances via `WorkerRegistry`, monitoring health, active requests, and reported loads [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs:1-30]().
- **KV-Aware Routing**: Evaluates prefix matching and cache states to route requests to workers with matching prefix segments, minimizing prefill overhead [sgl-router/src/policies/selection.rs:1-30]().

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:129-175](), [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/src/policies/selection.rs:1-30]()

## Purpose and scope

This page documents the `sgl-router` Rust crate: its slim routing role, KV-event-driven cache-aware routing, worker discovery, load-balancing policies, and Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation support. The router is described as a component for directing requests to SGLang workers, rather than as the model-serving runtime itself [sgl-router/src/main.rs:1-30]().

Sources: [sgl-router/src/main.rs:1-30]()

---

## 1. Slim architecture and application context

The router’s request path brings together runtime configuration, tokenizer and worker registries, routing policies, and proxy clients. HTTP handlers inspect and prepare requests before forwarding them [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:1-50]().

### High-level request dataflow

**Diagram: Request path from ingress to code entities**

```mermaid
graph TD
    ClientRequest["ClientHTTPRequest"] --> AxumServer["axum::Server\nsgl-router/src/server/app.rs"]
    AxumServer --> EndpointRoute["chat_completions\nsgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs"]
    EndpointRoute --> PrepareReq["prepare_chat_request\nsgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/preparation.rs"]
    PrepareReq --> TokenizerReg["TokenizerManager\nsgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs"]
    TokenizerReg --> ModelRouting["ModelRoutingLookup\nsgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/forward.rs"]
    ModelRouting --> PolicyEngine["select_worker\nsgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs"]
    PolicyEngine --> WorkerReg["WorkerRegistry\nsgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs"]
    WorkerReg --> ProxyClient["proxy_forward\nsgl-router/src/proxy/grpc.rs"]
    ProxyClient --> WorkerNodes["SGLangWorkerNodes"]
```

The request preparation path can tokenize prompt prefixes used for cache-aware routing. Forwarding supports cleartext HTTP/2 (`h2c`) or HTTP/1.1, depending on upstream capabilities [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:1-50]().

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:1-40]()

---

## 2. KV-event-driven cache-aware routing and advanced features

The router can use worker-reported KV-cache events to prefer workers that already hold blocks for a request’s prompt prefix. The KV event index maintains a radix-tree index populated from engine events received over subscriptions [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:10-60]().

### Cache-aware routing components and mechanisms

| Mechanism | Role |
|---|---|
| KV event index | Tracks KV block hashes in a radix tree, using worker KV events received over subscriptions [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:10-60](). |
| KV-event gap repair | Uses engine replay mechanisms to recover skipped event sequence gaps [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:15-65](). |
| Pending prefixes | Temporarily credits workers with prompt prefixes, using a configurable TTL, to reduce duplicate prefill work during parallel sampling or agent fan-out [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:20-70](). |
| Kubernetes peer bootstrap | Allows a starting replica to retrieve radix-tree snapshots from warm peers through internal endpoints [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:25-75](). |
| LoRA cache identity | Derives adapter-aware cache lookup identity from inputs such as model names or lora paths [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:20-50](). |

### Admission control

Cache ownership is combined with queue-based admission controls. If an owner worker’s queue exceeds limits, it is gated; if all prefix owners are gated, saturation floor settings can relax the constraint so routing can make progress [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:30-80]().

### Cache-aware routing dataflow

**Diagram: Prefix lookup, admission, and worker selection**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    IncomingRequest["IncomingRequest"] --> TokenizePrompt["tokenize_prompt\nsgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/preparation.rs"]
    TokenizePrompt --> ComputePrefix["compute_prefix_hashes\nsgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs"]
    ComputePrefix --> AdmissionGate{"queue_gate_check\nmax_queue_limit"}
    AdmissionGate -->|"OwnersAvailable"| WorkerSelect["select_cache_affine_worker\nsgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs"]
    AdmissionGate -->|"AllOwnersQueued"| SaturationFloor{"saturation_floor\nqueue_floor_config"}
    SaturationFloor -->|"Saturated"| AllQueuedDecision["record_all_queued_decision"]
    SaturationFloor -->|"Unsaturated"| CacheMissFallback["cache_miss_fallback"]
    WorkerSelect --> ProxyForward["proxy_forward\nsgl-router/src/proxy/grpc.rs"]
    AllQueuedDecision --> ProxyForward
    CacheMissFallback --> ProxyForward
```

Sources: [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:10-80](), [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs:20-50]()

---

## 3. Worker discovery, static pools, and Kubernetes EndpointSlice

The router supports worker-discovery modes including static URL lists and Kubernetes EndpointSlice discovery using label selectors. Static mode suits fixed worker topologies; EndpointSlice discovery is intended for dynamically changing Kubernetes worker sets [sgl-router/src/config/cli.rs:1-40]().

| Discovery mode | Configuration and role |
|---|---|
| Static URL list | Supply worker URLs through configuration parameters [sgl-router/src/config/cli.rs:1-40](). |
| Kubernetes EndpointSlice | Discover worker pods by watching EndpointSlices with label selectors [sgl-router/src/config/cli.rs:15-50](). |

Worker health and reliability use per-worker circuit breakers. The proxy tracks errors, timeouts, and backpressure responses—including service unavailable and too many requests statuses—to avoid repeatedly routing to unhealthy or overloaded workers [sgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs:1-50]().

Sources: [sgl-router/src/config/cli.rs:1-50](), [sgl-router/src/workers/worker.rs:1-50]()

---

## 4. Load-balancing policies and selection ladders

The policy framework defines policies for general worker selection and decode-worker selection [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30]().

| Policy | Selection behavior |
|---|---|
| `round_robin` | Selects healthy workers sequentially [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |
| `random` | Selects a worker uniformly at random [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |
| `power_of_two` | Samples two workers and chooses the less-loaded one [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |
| `load_based` | Selects the least-loaded worker [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |
| `cache_aware` | Prefers workers that cache prompt-token prefixes [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |
| `sticky` | Pins requests using routing keys or headers [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30](). |

Sources: [sgl-router/src/policies/dp_rank.rs:1-30]()

---

## 5. Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation support

The router supports distinct prefill and decode worker pools. Pool resolvers handle version-group labels and selectors. In the forwarding path, the router sends a request to a prefill worker and injects decoding hints for the selected decode peer [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/forward.rs:1-40]().

### PD routing flow

**Diagram: Prefill routing and decode-peer assignment**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as "Client"
    participant Router as "sgl-router\nsgl-router/src/server/app.rs"
    participant Resolver as "PdPoolResolver\nsgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs"
    participant PrefillWorker as "PrefillWorker"
    participant DecodeWorker as "DecodeWorker"
    Client->>Router: "post_chat_completions"
    Router->>Resolver: "resolve_prefill_candidates"
    Resolver-->>Router: "prefill_worker_list"
    Router->>PrefillWorker: "forward_request_with_decode_url_hint"
    PrefillWorker->>DecodeWorker: "kv_cache_transfer"
    DecodeWorker-->>Router: "stream_generated_tokens"
    Router-->>Client: "stream_response"
```

Sources: [sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/forward.rs:1-40](), [sgl-router/src/workers/manager.rs:1-40]()

---

## 6. Observability and Prometheus metrics

The router exposes a Prometheus metrics endpoint backed by metrics registry collections. The metrics surface includes request and response counters, worker request outcomes, cache-aware decisions, and worker active-load gauges [sgl-router/src/server/app.rs:30-70]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the gRPC-facing pipeline, Python-Rust gRPC bridge architecture via PyO3, request normalization in Rust, streaming response handling with backpressure, chat/messages route handlers, and tool/reasoning parsing components. The Rust server exposes HTTP and gRPC transport adapters over a shared runtime core, while `RuntimeHandle` in Python bridges the Rust gRPC server to `TokenizerManager` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:1-7]() [rust/sglang-grpc/src/server.rs:1-25]().

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:1-7`; `rust/sglang-grpc/src/server.rs:1-25`

---

## gRPC-Facing Pipeline Architecture and Python Bridge

The gRPC server layer interacts with Python's runtime via `RuntimeHandle` defined in `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py`. `RuntimeHandle` exposes synchronous methods that Rust calls through PyO3 with a brief GIL acquisition [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:1-7](). 

Each generation or request submission receives a Rust-side `chunk_callback` (a PyO3 callback object) invoked with `(chunk_dict, finished, error)` for every response chunk produced by `TokenizerManager` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-83]().

**Diagram: Transport-to-runtime entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RustGRPC["RustGRPCServer"] -->|"PyO3Call"| RuntimeHandle["RuntimeHandle"]
    RuntimeHandle --> TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager"]
    TokenizerManager --> Scheduler["Scheduler"]
    Scheduler --> TokenizerManager
    TokenizerManager -->|"ChunkCallback"| RustGRPC
```
Sources: `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:1-83`

### Request and Runtime Flow

Protobuf definitions (`proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto`) declare typed RPC services such as `TextGenerate`, `Generate`, `ChatComplete`, and `Complete`, alongside administrative and OpenAI-compatible pass-through endpoints [proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto:6-38](). Incoming requests are fanned out and validated by Rust request parsers (`rust/sglang-grpc/src/utils/request_utils.rs`) before entering the core dispatch pipeline [rust/sglang-grpc/src/utils/request_utils.rs:19-128]().

**Diagram: Transport to Runtime Entities Mapping**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["GRPCClient"] --> ProtoService["SglangService"]
    ProtoService --> RustAdapter["RustGRPCServer"]
    RustAdapter --> IntoRequests["sampling_params_to_map"]
    IntoRequests --> Core["RuntimeHandle"]
    Core --> TokenizerManager["TokenizerManager"]
    TokenizerManager --> PythonScheduler["SchedulerProcess"]
```

Sources: `proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto:6-38`; `rust/sglang-grpc/src/utils/request_utils.rs:19-128`; `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-95`

## Request Normalization, Chat Routes, and Messages API

Incoming batch requests parsed through `/v1/messages` or gRPC handlers undergo strict structural normalization. In the Rust router layer, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` are converted to chat completions via `sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs` [sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs:4-57](). The `parse` function validates incoming Axum request bodies and maps them into internal chat formats [sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs:94-102]().

On the Python side, `AnthropicServing` in `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py` translates Anthropic Messages API structures into OpenAI-compatible `ChatCompletionRequest` payloads, handling inline system message merging and tool conversions [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:184-205]() [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py:1-132]().

Sources: `sgl-router/src/server/routes/messages.rs:4-102`; `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:184-205`; `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py:1-132`

---

## Tool-Call Parsing and Format Detectors

### Parser Boundary and Format-Specific Detectors

Tool-call and reasoning parsing in SGLang are handled via modular format detectors and parsers [python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py:1-48]() [python/sglang/srt/function_call/inkling_detector.py:1-50](). These components process raw token or text streams to separate thinking/reasoning blocks from visible model output and structured tool invocations.

Schema normalization utilities (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py`) map non-standard database/ORM schema types to standard JSON Schema primitives before prompt rendering and validation [python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py:28-110]().

### Incremental Parsing and Stream State

Streaming response processing uses incremental state machines to handle partial markers (such as tool start tags or reasoning delimiters) across chunks without breaking downstream protocol frames [python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py:50-125]().

## Streaming Response Handling and Backpressure

### Backpressure Management in `RuntimeHandle`

When streaming responses back through the gRPC bridge, `RuntimeHandle` manages asynchronous backpressure via `_send_with_backpressure` [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:138-177](). It monitors chunk callback return statuses (such as `Pending` or `Closed`) and enforces a configurable timeout (`_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0`) to avoid unbounded queue growth if a gRPC client stops reading from the stream [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:121-177]().

**Diagram: Streamed gRPC response flow**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as "GRPCClient"
    participant Server as "RustGRPCServer"
    participant Bridge as "RuntimeHandle"
    participant TM as "TokenizerManager"
    Client->>Server: "Generate / TextGenerate RPC"
    Server->>Bridge: "Invoke generation task"
    Bridge->>TM: "Generate request stream"
    TM-->>Bridge: "Response chunk"
    Bridge->>Server: "_send_with_backpressure (chunk_callback)"
    alt Status is Pending
        Bridge->>Bridge: "Wait on ready_event with timeout"
    end
    Server-->>Client: "gRPC Stream Chunk"
```

Sources: `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_bridge.py:75-197`; `rust/sglang-grpc/src/server.rs:1-195`

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides an overview of the workspace crates located in the `rust/` directory of the SGLang repository and explains how they bind into the Python runtime (`python/sglang/srt/rust_server/`) via PyO3 and native extensions [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py:1-10](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](). The Rust workspace contains high-performance components for HTTP/gRPC serving, tokenization and chat template processing, radix tree prefix caching, multimodal tensor pipelines, and API type definitions.

As a parent page, this section outlines the high-level crate architecture and integration mechanisms. For deep technical details on individual crates, see the child pages.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py:1-10](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12]()

## Rust Workspace Crates Overview

The `rust/` workspace is structured into several modular crates, each handling specific performance-critical aspects of the serving engine. These crates communicate via typed Rust message passing and expose targeted bindings to Python.

*   `sglang-server`: The multi-threaded Rust frontend (HTTP/gRPC server, tokenizer/detokenizer management, and `CoreHandle` integration) embedded directly inside the Python scheduler process [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12]().
*   `sglang-processor`: Handles tokenization, chat template rendering, and text processing pipelines [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:46-46]().
*   `sglang-api-types`: Defines shared API types, request/response models, and codegen parity definitions [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:82-82]().
*   `sglang-radix-tree`: Implements the native unified radix tree core with PyO3 bindings for prefix caching and memory indexing.
*   `sglang-grpc`: Provides gRPC transport definitions, protocol buffers (`proto/`), and gRPC request management.
*   `sglang-mm`: The pure-Rust core of the multimodal processing pipeline for handling image, video, and audio feature extraction [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:72-75]().
*   `sglang-bench`: Benchmarking tools and load testing utilities implemented in Rust.

**Diagram: Workspace crate dependencies and Python binding architecture**

```mermaid
graph TD
    PythonRuntime["PythonRuntime"] --> PyO3Bindings["PyO3Extensions"]
    PyO3Bindings --> SglangServer["sglang-server"]
    SglangServer --> SglangProcessor["sglang-processor"]
    SglangServer --> SglangMm["sglang-mm"]
    SglangServer --> SglangApiTypes["sglang-api-types"]
    SglangServer --> SglangRadixTree["sglang-radix-tree"]
    SglangServer --> SglangGrpc["sglang-grpc"]
```

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](), [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:46-82]()

## Python Runtime Integration and PyO3 Bindings

The integration between Python and Rust relies on PyO3 (`cdylib`), allowing the Python scheduler process to spin up the embedded Rust server threads [rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml:15-19](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-17](). Configuration objects such as `ServerArgs` and `ModelConfig` are constructed via keyword arguments from Python and validated strictly against Rust structs at boot time [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:105-112](), [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/config.py:65-81]().

Data transfer across the FFI boundary utilizes zero-copy techniques where possible, such as mapping incoming request text and token ID buffers directly into NumPy arrays or POSIX shared memory segments (`ShmBuffer`) [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:69-97]().

**Diagram: Natural language to code mapping for native runtime components**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        EmbeddedRustServer["Embedded Rust Server Lifecycle"]
        TypedServerConfiguration["Typed Server Configuration"]
        SharedMemoryBufferTransfer["Shared Memory Buffer Transfer"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        RustServerModule["RustServer"]
        ServerArgsStruct["ServerArgs"]
        ShmBufferClass["ShmBuffer"]
    end

    EmbeddedRustServer --> RustServerModule
    TypedServerConfiguration --> ServerArgsStruct
    SharedMemoryBufferTransfer --> ShmBufferClass
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py:1-10](), [python/sglang/srt/rust_server/config.py:65-81](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:69-97](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:105-112]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the `sglang-server` crate, its multi-threaded Rust frontend architecture (HTTP/gRPC `api_server`, `tokenizer_manager`, message types, and shared request-submission handle `CoreHandle`), the `sglang-api-types` codegen package, protobuf definitions (`proto/`), and runtime parity test suites. The crate replaces the Python `api-server` + `TokenizerManager` + `DetokenizerManager` stack, running them as pinned Rust threads embedded inside the Python scheduler process to handle request ingestion, tokenization, serialization, and transport management [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-15]().

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-15]()

---

## Core Crate Structure and Boundaries

The `sglang-server` crate exposes a clean PyO3 boundary (`_server`) to the Python scheduler process via `lib.rs` [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](). Python hands down typed configuration objects like [`ServerArgs`] (defined in `message::config`) which are validated at startup [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:105-115](). Once booted, request ingestion, payload rendering, tokenization, and streaming are executed entirely in native Rust without crossing the PyO3 boundary per token [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12]().

The codebase is organized into primary modules:
- `api_server/`: Axum HTTP routers, gRPC services, data-plane handlers, and hooks (`CoreHandle`, `AppState`) [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs:1-15](), [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/grpc/service.rs]().
- `tokenizer_manager/`: Tokenization, detokenization, channel pipelines, and scheduler event loops [rust/sglang-server/src/tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler.rs]().
- `message/`: Wire structures, request parsing, sampling parameters, and runtime configuration (`ServerArgs`, `RuntimeConfig`) [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:1-20](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/request.rs:1-15]().
- `multi_modality/`: Multimodal processing workers, shm buffer management, and feature transformers [rust/sglang-server/src/multi_modality/worker.rs:1-15]().

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-12](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:1-20](), [rust/sglang-server/src/tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler.rs]()

---

## HTTP and gRPC API Server Architecture

The API server layer abstracts transport protocols behind `CoreHandle`, allowing HTTP (Axum) and gRPC endpoints to share identical request processing logic [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs:1-15](), [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/grpc/service.rs](). `AppState` maintains reference-counted access to configuration, metrics, and the core handle [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs:10-25](). Endpoints like `/generate`, `/health`, and `/health_generate` process generation tasks by registering state and submitting through intake channels managed by `CoreInner` [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs:1-30]().

### Control Plane and API Routing: Natural Language to Code Entities

Diagram Title: "ApiServerControlPlaneArchitecture"

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client["ClientRequest"] --> HTTP["HttpAdapter: api_server::http"]
    Client --> GRPC["GrpcAdapter: api_server::grpc::service"]
    HTTP --> State["AppState: api_server::http::app::AppState"]
    GRPC --> Core["CoreHandle: api_server::handlers::CoreHandle"]
    State --> Core
    Core --> Intake["CoreInner.intake_tx: api_server::core"]
    Core --> Abort["CoreInner.abort_tx: api_server::core"]
    Intake --> Runtime["RuntimePipeline: api_server::core"]
```

The diagram maps transport-facing concepts to specific code entities, illustrating how requests received via Axum or Tonic flow into `CoreHandle` and `CoreInner`.

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-21](), [rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs:1-15](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:44-68]()

---

## TokenizerManager and Bounded Worker Pipeline

Computationally intensive tasks are offloaded from the asynchronous Tokio executor onto dedicated, pinned OS threads [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-17](). The runtime spawns worker pools for tokenization, detokenization, and multimodal preprocessing (`start_mm_workers`) [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154](). Communication between these stages occurs over bounded `flume` channels (`to_scheduler_cap`, `from_scheduler_cap`, `stage_channel_cap`), providing backpressure under heavy traffic [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:33-53](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154]().

| Runtime Role | Code Entity / Mechanism | Description |
|---|---|---|
| API Transports | `api_server` | Tokio/Axum multi-threaded runtime handling HTTP and gRPC traffic. [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:5-12]() |
| Runtime Handle | `Runtime` | Manages channels, worker thread joins, and lifecycle states. [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:44-68]() |
| Tokenizer / Detokenizer | Worker Pools | Dedicated OS threads performing CPU-bound text encoding/decoding. [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:5-15]() |
| Multimodal Workers | `start_mm_workers` / `spawn_mm_pool` | Dynamically spawned worker pool for multimodal preprocessing. [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154]() |

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-17](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:44-68](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154]()

### Request and Worker-Stage Flow: Natural Language to Code Entities

Diagram Title: "WorkerStagePipelineFlow"

```mermaid
graph LR
    HTTP["HttpRoutes: api_server::http"]
    GRPC["GrpcRoutes: api_server::grpc::service"]
    CORE["CoreHandle: api_server::handlers"]
    INTAKE["CoreInner.intake_tx: api_server::core"]
    TM["TokenizerManager: tokenizer_manager"]
    TOKEN["TokenizerWorker: tokenizer_manager::tokenizer"]
    MM["MmWorker: multi_modality::worker"]
    DETOK["DetokenizerWorkerChannels: tokenizer_manager::detokenizer"]
    SCHED["PythonSchedulerBoundary: rust_server::server"]

    HTTP --> CORE
    GRPC --> CORE
    CORE --> INTAKE
    INTAKE --> TM
    TM --> TOKEN
    TOKEN --> MM
    SCHED --> DETOK
```

The diagram illustrates data routing from web routers through tokenizer and multimodal worker stages prior to reaching the Python scheduler boundary via `IngressRequest`.

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-21](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:40-47](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154]()

## Message Types and Configuration Schema

The `message/` module defines types shared across the API server, request normalizers, and configuration loaders [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:1-20](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/request.rs:1-15](). 
- `ServerArgs`: Mirrors Python's server configuration and is constructed via PyO3 keyword arguments, ensuring startup failure if parameters drift [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:105-115]().
- `GenerateRequest`: Parsed and validated from incoming HTTP bodies via `into_requests`, enforcing batch size limits (`SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ`) and data validation policies [rust/sglang-server/src/message/request.rs:30-95]().
- `SamplingParams`: Defines decoding configurations, top-p, top-k, temperature, and penalty fields matching Python specifications.

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/message/config.rs:105-115](), [rust/sglang-server/src/message/request.rs:30-95]()

---

## sglang-api-types, Proto Definitions, and Parity Tests

The `sglang-api-types` crate manages data type parity between Python and Rust components, generated from protobuf definitions residing in `proto/sglang/api/v1/` [proto/sglang/api/v1/service.proto](), [rust/sglang-api-types/tests/json_contract.rs]().
- **Protobuf Definitions**: `service.proto` and `generate.proto` specify gRPC service contracts and message payload structures [proto/sglang/api/v1/service.proto]().
- **Code Generation**: Rust structs and Serde serialization code are generated automatically (e.g. `sglang.api.v1.rs` and `sglang.api.v1.serde.rs`) [rust/sglang-api-types/src/generated/sglang.api.v1.rs](), [rust/sglang-api-types/src/generated/sglang.api.v1.serde.rs]().
- **JSON Contract & Parity Tests**: Tests in `rust/sglang-api-types/tests/json_contract.rs` and Python counterpart tests (`test_json_contract.py`, `test_parity.py`) validate that Rust serialization matches Python `api_types.py` schemas precisely, preventing contract drift [rust/sglang-api-types/tests/json_contract.rs](), [python/sglang/api/v1/api_types.py]().

Sources: [proto/sglang/api/v1/service.proto](), [rust/sglang-api-types/tests/json_contract.rs](), [python/sglang/api/v1/api_types.py]()

---

## Server Lifecycle and Teardown

The server lifecycle follows a deterministic bootstrap and termination flow coordinated by `runtime::start` and `Runtime::request_shutdown` [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-15]().

Diagram Title: "ServerLifecycleSequence"

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Boot as "runtime::start"
    participant RT as "Runtime: utils::runtime::Runtime"
    participant Server as "http::serve"
    participant Core as "CoreHandle: api_server::core"
    participant Shutdown as "Runtime::request_shutdown"

    Boot->>RT: "Initialize channels & spawn threads"
    RT->>Server: "Bind TCP listener & start Axum"
    Server->>Core: "Execute startup warmup"
    Core-->>Server: "Warmup completed / mark ready"
    Shutdown->>RT: "Drop shutdown sender"
    RT->>Server: "Signal listener shutdown"
    RT->>RT: "Join worker threads with timeout"
```

The sequence diagram depicts the initialization of runtime channels, execution of warmups, active API request handling, and bounded thread joins during shutdown.

Sources: [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:1-15](), [rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs:128-154](), [rust/sglang-server/src/lib.rs:1-21]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the Rust-native components within the SGLang monorepo workspace, focusing on three primary crates: `sglang-radix-tree`, which provides a high-performance unified prefix tree core and its PyO3 Python bindings; `sglang-processor`, which handles fast tokenization, chat template processing, and message formatting; and `sglang-mm`, which supports multimodal input processing and feature transformations.

Sources: [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:1-35](), [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-26](), [rust/sglang-processor/src/openai/chat.rs:1-10]()

---

## 1. sglang-radix-tree: Unified Tree Core and PyO3 Bindings

The `sglang-radix-tree` crate implements the core radix prefix tree used for KV cache prefix sharing, supporting multiple memory components (`FULL`, `SWA` for sliding window attention, and `Mamba` state components) [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:1-18](). It manages node arenas, reference counting, locking, and eviction strategies (such as joint LRU) natively in Rust to minimize garbage collection overhead and lock contention.

### Core Data Structures and Tree Architecture

The tree is anchored by `UnifiedTreeCore`, which coordinates node creation, key matching, component size bookkeeping, and locking receipts [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:57-170](). Nodes are stored in a dense `NodeArena` to ensure cache locality [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:19-25]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    RootNode["UnifiedTreeCore"] -->|ManagesArena| NodeArena["NodeArena"]
    NodeArena -->|Stores| TreeNode["Node"]
    TreeNode -->|HasChildren| ChildMap["HashMap ChildKeyType NodeId"]
    TreeNode -->|HoldsComponentData| CompSet["ComponentSet"]
    CompSet --> FullComp["FullComponent"]
    CompSet --> SwaComp["SwaComponent"]
    CompSet --> MambaComp["MambaComponent"]
```
Sources: [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:1-30](), [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-26]()

### PyO3 Bindings and Python Adapter Bridge

To expose the native Rust radix tree to the Python SRT runtime, `sglang-radix-tree` provides PyO3 bindings in `python_bindings.rs` [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-25](). The Python-side `RustUnifiedTreeCore` adapter wraps `RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding` and conforms to the `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` protocol [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py:1-79]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
class UnifiedTreeCoreInterface {
    <<protocol>>
    +match_prefix() MatchResult
    +begin_insert() InsertStepResult
    +inc_lock_ref() IncLockRefResult
    +dec_lock_ref() DecLockRefResult
}

class RustUnifiedTreeCore {
    +RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding binding
    +match_prefix() MatchResult
    +collect_full_device_indices() Tensor
}

class RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding {
    +new() RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding
    +begin_insert() InsertStepResult
    +inc_lock_ref() IncLockRefResult
}

UnifiedTreeCoreInterface <|-- RustUnifiedTreeCore : "implements"
RustUnifiedTreeCore --> RustUnifiedTreeCoreBinding : "delegates to"
```
Sources: [rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs:1-25](), [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py:1-79]()

---

## 2. sglang-processor: Tokenizer and Chat Processing

The `sglang-processor` crate is responsible for high-throughput text tokenization, chat template application, and message formatting. By performing these operations in Rust, SGLang avoids Python GIL bottlenecks during high-concurrency request ingestion.

### Tokenization and Chat Template Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RawInput["OpenAIChatRequest"] --> ChatParser["chat::parse_messages"]
    ChatParser --> TemplateEngine["ChatTemplateFormatter"]
    TemplateEngine --> TokenizerCore["TokenizeEngine"]
    TokenizerCore --> OutputTokens["Vec i64 Token IDs"]
```
Sources: [rust/sglang-processor/src/openai/chat.rs:1-30]()

---

## 3. sglang-mm: Multimodal Crate

The `sglang-mm` crate provides supporting data structures and utilities for multimodal processing (images, video frames, and audio features). It coordinates tensor packaging, padding, and alignment requirements before payloads are dispatched to the multimodal embedding pipeline.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/req_types.mm_utils]()

---

## 4. Summary of Rust Crates and Components

| Crate Name | Primary Responsibility | Key Files and Bindings |

## Purpose and Scope

SGLang’s `multimodal_gen` package provides a high-throughput serving and generation runtime for diffusion pipelines, focusing on DiT (Diffusion Transformer) models for image and video synthesis. This parent page outlines the high-level architecture, request execution flow, pipeline configurations, and major components of the diffusion framework. Detailed descriptions of runtime execution, model architectures, API specifications, loading pipelines, and testing suites live in the child pages. One-off generation tasks and persistent HTTP serving coordinate through entry points like `http_server.py` and scheduler clients [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/http_server.py:14-50](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/diffusion_generator.py:102-135]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/http_server.py:14-50](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/diffusion_generator.py:102-135]()

## System Architecture Overview

Generation requests enter through OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (`http_server.py`), are translated into configuration classes like `ServerArgs` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:5-20](), and are scheduled by the `Scheduler` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:126-136](). The scheduler delegates model execution to `GPUWorker` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-88](), which builds components and runs iterative generation loops via core pipelines and stages [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py:4-15]().

## 22.1 Diffusion Runtime Architecture

The diffusion runtime coordinates asynchronous requests through `Scheduler` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:126-136]() and executes pipelines using GPU workers (`GPUWorker`) [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-88](). Workers instantiate modular pipelines and drive multi-step diffusion via pipeline stages [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py:4-15](). Component residency and layerwise offload managers handle memory efficiency across constrained device pools.

For complete details on the worker lifecycle, pipeline composition, memory managers, and platform support, see [Diffusion Runtime Architecture](#22.1).

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:126-136](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-88](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py:4-15]()

---

## 22.2 Supported Diffusion Models and DiT Architectures

SGLang supports a wide variety of state-of-the-art diffusion models—including Flux, WanVideo, Qwen-Image, HunyuanVideo, Z-Image, LTX-2, MoVA, Cosmos3, and MiniMax-H3. Each model family defines tailored pipeline configurations, architecture settings, and dedicated loading rules.

For detailed breakdowns of supported model families, their DiT implementations, layer structures, and attention backends, see [Supported Diffusion Models and DiT Architectures](#22.2).

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/__init__.py]()

---

## 22.3 Diffusion API, Loading, and LoRA Support

The serving layer provides OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints under `/v1/images` and `/v1/videos` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/http_server.py:14-50]() and CLI tools [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/cli.mdx:45-65](). Model configurations, FSDP integration, component loading, quantization options, and LoRA adapter merging are managed via `ServerArgs` and dedicated loaders.

For comprehensive documentation on API request/response structures, weight loading pipelines, quantization schemes, and LoRA support, see [Diffusion API, Loading, and LoRA Support](#22.3).

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/http_server.py:14-50](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/cli.mdx:45-65]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the `multimodal_gen` runtime’s request coordination, GPU execution, composed pipeline and stage structure, memory-residency mechanisms, and platform abstraction. It focuses on how the named runtime components fit together; it does not document individual model architectures [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:110-135](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-90](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/base.py]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:110-135](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-90]()

---

## System Overview

The runtime separates request coordination from model execution. `Scheduler` runs the event loop for a rank-0 worker, receives requests through ZMQ, and coordinates worker execution [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:124-135](). It constructs a `GPUWorker` on accelerator platforms and a `CPUWorker` on CPU platforms [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:165-178](). The worker imports identify `ComposedPipelineBase`, `build_pipeline`, `Req`, and `OutputBatch` as pipeline and request types used by the execution layer [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-90]().

`ServerArgs` is the runtime configuration type passed to the scheduler and worker. It imports pipeline configuration, platform selection, component-residency handling, layerwise-offload configuration, and disaggregation-role definitions, linking those concerns in a common configuration surface [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:107-108](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:22-48]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:124-178](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-108]()

---

## Runtime Components: Natural-Language Roles and Code Entities

This map connects runtime roles to identifiers visible in the implementation. The scheduler chooses `CPUWorker` or `GPUWorker` based on `current_platform.is_cpu()`, and initializes the selected worker with rank, port, and `ServerArgs` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:165-175]().

Diagram: Runtime roles mapped to implementation entities
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Entrypoints["Generation entrypoints"]
        CLI["sglang_generate_or_serve"]
        IMG["image_api.py"]
        VIDEO["video_api.py"]
    end
    subgraph Coordination["Request coordination"]
        SCHED["Scheduler"]
        ROUTER["ZMQ_ROUTER_receiver"]
        CTRL["Control_Requests"]
    end
    subgraph Execution["Execution"]
        SELECT["current_platform.is_cpu()"]
        CPU["CPUWorker"]
        GPU["GPUWorker"]
        BUILD["build_pipeline"]
        PIPE["ComposedPipelineBase"]
        REQ["Req"]
        OUT["OutputBatch"]
    end
    CLI --> SCHED
    IMG --> SCHED
    VIDEO --> SCHED
    ROUTER --> SCHED
    SCHED --> CTRL
    SCHED --> SELECT
    SELECT --> CPU
    SELECT --> GPU
    GPU --> BUILD
    BUILD --> PIPE
    PIPE --> REQ
    PIPE --> OUT
```

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:124-186](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-89](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/openai/image_api.py:55-61]()

---

## Request Coordination and Scheduler

`Scheduler` is declared with `Pi05SegmentSchedulerMixin`, `SchedulerWarmupMixin`, `SchedulerPostTrainingMixin`, and `SchedulerDisaggMixin` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:124-130](). Its class documentation identifies it as the main event loop for the rank-0 worker: it listens for external requests over ZMQ and coordinates with other workers, but does not manage worker processes [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:130-135]().

During initialization, the scheduler stores `ServerArgs` and `PortArgs`, sets global server arguments, and calculates the number of GPUs per data-parallel replica [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:141-163](). The first GPU rank in each replica binds a ZMQ `ROUTER` socket at that replica’s scheduler endpoint; other ranks in the replica do not create a receiver [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:165-181]().

The scheduler selects `CPUWorker` when `current_platform.is_cpu()` is true and otherwise selects `GPUWorker` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:165-178](). It initializes that worker with `local_rank`, the master port, the global rank, and `ServerArgs` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:141-178]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/scheduler.py:124-181]()

---

## DiffGenerator and Generation Entrypoints

The diffusion CLI and entrypoints provide endpoints for image and video generation. The image API defines an `/v1/images` router with request/response protocol types, request preparation utilities, and `async_scheduler_client` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/openai/image_api.py:11-62](). The video API (`video_api.py`) defines `/v1/videos` routers, background video job management via `_start_video_job` and `shutdown_video_jobs`, and multipart parameter processing [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/openai/video_api.py:11-107](). `DiffGenerator` encapsulates high-level programmatic generation workflows.

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/openai/image_api.py:11-62](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/openai/video_api.py:11-107]()

---

## GPU Worker and Execution Boundary

`GPUWorker` imports distributed initialization and parallel-state helpers, including tensor-parallel and sequence-parallel group accessors [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:28-52](). It also imports `ComposedPipelineBase`, `LoRAPipeline`, `Req`, `build_pipeline`, and `OutputBatch`, which identify the worker’s principal execution-facing types [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-89]().

The worker module imports component-residency management, layerwise-offload configuration via `configure_layerwise_offload_modules`, and `MemoryOccupationController` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:60-73]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:28-89]()

---

## Composed Pipeline and Stage Architecture

The worker imports `build_pipeline` and `ComposedPipelineBase` from `pipelines_core`, alongside request and output types [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-89](). `DenoisingStage` is a core pipeline-stage implementation in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py`. Its module imports `PipelineStage`, `Req`, `ServerArgs`, `ComponentUse`, component-loading helpers, and layerwise-offload interfaces.

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:78-89]()

---

## Memory Management and Layerwise Offload

`layerwise_offload.py` defines `compute_streamed_layers(num_layers, resident_layers, policy)` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:67-69](). It validates the policy against `RESIDENCY_POLICIES`, clamps the resident-layer count to the valid range, and returns no streamed layers when all layers are resident [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:94-103](). For `leading`, it streams the tail after the resident prefix; for `strided`, it spreads streamed layers evenly across the whole step [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:105-114]().

The module also implements `_host_resident_tables` which scans modules for declared `host_resident_table_names`, resolves candidate submodules, and filters out invalid weights, tensor-parallel-sharded tables, and tables below `HOST_RESIDENT_TABLE_MIN_BYTES` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:139-168]().

| Mechanism | Code identifier | Established role |
|---|---|---|
| Layer selection | `compute_streamed_layers` | Determine streamed layer indices for `leading` or `strided` residency policies [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:67-114]() |
| Host resident tables | `_host_resident_tables` | Identify large vocab tables suitable for host-side lookups rather than device residency [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:139-168]() |
| Layerwise module setup | `configure_layerwise_offload_modules` | Worker integration point for configuring layerwise-offloaded modules [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:68-70]() |
| Component residency | `get_global_component_residency_manager` | Global component-residency manager accessor [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:64-67]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/layerwise_offload.py:67-168](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py:60-73]()

---

## Platform Support and Attention Selection

`ServerArgs` imports `AttentionBackendEnum` and `current_platform` from the platform package [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:70-73](). The CUDA platform module (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py`) defines resolvers for attention backends including AITER, Torch SDPA, cuDNN SDPA, sparse linear attention, sliding-tile attention, and SageAttention [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py:85-170](). 

The CUDA module ensures that code assumes CUDA without eagerly initializing a CUDA context [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py:5-7]() and disables PyTorch's cuDNN SDPA backend by default to prevent stability issues [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py:43-45]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py:5-45](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py:85-170]()

---

This diagram links user-facing diffusion entrypoints to the runtime entities implemented in the codebase.

```mermaid
flowchart TB

    subgraph RoutingSpace["Routing & Coordination Space"]
        CLIENT["async_scheduler_client"]
        ROUTER["ZMQ_ROUTER_socket"]
        SCHED["Scheduler"]
    end
    subgraph ExecutionSpace["Execution & Worker Space"]
        REQ["Req"]
        CPU["CPUWorker"]
        GPU["GPUWorker"]
        BUILD["build_pipeline"]
        PIPE["ComposedPipelineBase"]
        STAGE["DenoisingStage"]
        OUT["OutputBatch"]
    end
    USER --> CLI
    USER --> IMG
    USER --> VIDEO
    IMG --> CLIENT
    VIDEO --> CLIENT
    CLIENT --> ROUTER
    ROUTER --> SCHED
    SCHED --> REQ
    SCHED --> CPU
    SCHED --> GPU
    GPU --> BUILD
    BUILD --> PIPE
    PIPE --> STAGE
    STAGE --> OUT
```

## Configuration and Operational Context

`ServerArgs` integrates pipeline configuration, platform selection, component residency, and memory offload settings [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:22-48](). Sampling parameters such as `SamplingParams` and `SkipSoftmaxParams` manage request-level generation attributes, quality levels (`exact`, `lossless`, `high`), and threshold configurations [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/sample/sampling_params.py:56-146]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:22-48](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/sample/sampling_params.py:56-146]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page maps the supported diffusion model families to their respective Diffusion Transformer (DiT) implementation files and runtime layer abstractions within the `multimodal_gen` package. It focuses on implementation boundaries, data flow, attention backend selection, and model-specific fused operations. The supported models cover Flux, Flux.2, WanVideo, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-2.1, HunyuanVideo, Z-Image, GLM-Image, LTX-2, MoVA, Cosmos3, and MiniMax-H3, leveraging shared runtime layers, attention backends, and optimized diffusion kernels [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:17-44](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:2-7](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:14-60](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:2-6]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:17-44](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:2-7](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:14-60](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:2-6]()

## Architectural Overview

The diffusion model implementations sit within `multimodal_gen`: model-specific DiT modules use common runtime layers, attention abstractions, and diffusion-kernel operations. The kernel package serves as the supported import facade for diffusion operators; its registry records operator names, backend choices, and capability requirements, while resolving implementations lazily [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:21-45]().

The codebase illustrates three primary integration patterns across model families:
- DiT modules inherit from base classes such as `CachableDiT` or `BaseDiT`; for instance, Flux, Qwen-Image, and LTX-2 inherit from `CachableDiT`, whereas MiniMax-H3 inherits from `BaseDiT` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:84-89](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:57-60](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:96-97]().
- Attention mechanisms are exposed through shared layers like `USPAttention` and `LocalAttention`, which delegate backend selection to `get_attn_backend` and helper functions [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:59-60](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:42-47](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/layer.py:43-56]().
- Model-specific wrappers validate whether a fused operator is compatible with the active tensor layout, precision, and hardware capabilities before falling back to eager execution paths [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:105-181](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py:10-21](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:20-23]().

Sources: [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:21-45](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:59-89](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:42-60](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:96-97](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/layer.py:43-56](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:20-23]()

## Supported Models and Implementations

### Flux and Flux.2

`flux.py` and `flux_2.py` provide distinct implementation pipelines. The Flux implementation imports `USPAttention`, tensor-parallel linear layers, `FluxPosEmbed`, and `CachableDiT`; Flux.2 imports `USPAttention`, `Flux2PosEmbed`, model-parallel linear layers, and `CachableDiT` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:59-89]().

The Flux normalization wrapper `_flux_norm_modulate` executes the model's normalization-and-modulation operation. It first attempts fused layer normalization modulation; if unavailable, it uses the request-mounted fused affine path or falls back to eager execution [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:105-181]().

Flux.2's `_flux2_single_qk_rope` provides a specialized strided Q/K norm-plus-RoPE path, inspecting dimensions, normalization classes, epsilon values, and runtime flags prior to launching strided Q/K-norm operations [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:123-165]().

| Concern | Implementation Detail |
|---|---|
| Shared attention layer | `USPAttention` is utilized across both Flux implementations [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:59-60]() |
| Positional embedding | `FluxPosEmbed` and `Flux2PosEmbed` handle multidimensional position encodings [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:77-79]() |
| Flux normalization fusion | `_flux_norm_modulate` dispatches between verified kernel fusions and eager paths [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:105-181]() |
| Flux.2 Q/K and RoPE fusion | `_flux2_single_qk_rope` verifies constraints before dispatching to specialized kernels [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:123-165]() |
| Quantization integration | Flux.2 integrates ModelOpt FP4/FP8 linear methods and NVFP4 GEMM primitives [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:73-83]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:59-89](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py:105-181](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:63-90](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py:123-165]()

### WanVideo

`wanvideo.py` implements the WanVideo DiT, integrating with Wan-specific diffusion-kernel operations such as RMSNorm-silu activations, VAE optimizations, and temporal/spatial attention routing through `USPAttention` and `UlyssesAttention_VSA` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py:10-35](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py:103-140]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py:10-35](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py:103-140]()

### Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-2.1

`qwen_image.py` and `qwen_image21.py` define the Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-2.1 DiT architectures, importing parallel linear layers, normalization layers, and quantization methods. The normalization and output wrappers handle final LayerNorm plus adaLN scale/shift fusion [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py:52-57]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py:52-57]()

### HunyuanVideo

`hunyuanvideo.py` implements HunyuanVideo with specialized QKV packing, normalization, and rotary embedding pack utilities.

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/hunyuanvideo.py:1-1]()

### Z-Image

`zimage.py` provides the Z-Image DiT architecture with model-specific normalization bindings and integration into the diffusion testing framework.

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/zimage.py:1-1]()

### GLM-Image

`glm_image.py` implements GLM-Image, featuring helper functions that manage its unique adaLN layout and Q/K normalization requirements.

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/glm_image.py:1-1]()

### LTX-2

`ltx_2.py` imports local attention modules, RMSNorm modules, model-parallel linear layers, and configuration classes. It defines prompt KV projection helpers and sequence conditioning [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:31-60]().

`_ltx2_try_fused_qknorm_split_rope` attempts CUDA kernel fusion for Q/K normalization and split rotary embeddings under single-TP constraints [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py:76-135]().

### MoVA

`mova_video_dit.py` and `mova.py` implement the MoVA multimodal video DiT architecture, coordinating cross-modal conditioning and specialized attention routing paths [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py:1-1]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py:1-1]()

### Cosmos3

`Cosmos3OmniTransformer` (`cosmos3video.py`) implements a dual-pathway DiT: an Understanding (UND) pathway runs causal self-attention over text tokens once and caches its K/V, while a Generation (GEN) pathway cross-attends from noisy visual tokens to that cache at every denoising step [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:2-7](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:62-65]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:2-7](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/cosmos3video.py:62-65]()

### MiniMax-H3

`MiniMaxH3DiT` (`minimax_h3.py`) implements the MiniMax H3 audio-video DiT with packed inference keyword arguments and logits. It integrates `MiniMaxH3VDNHybridAttention`, Ulysses/ring parallelism, and checkpoint conversion helpers [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:2-6](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:138-140]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:2-6](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:138-140]()

## Attention Layer and Backend Selection

The shared attention layer imports FlashAttention's variable-length function, backend selectors, and distributed sequence-parallel primitives. `_resolve_sp_attention_mode` dispatches between Ulysses exchange and K/V gather based on topology and causal constraints [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/layer.py:14-56]().

```mermaid
    Mode --> Ulysses
    Mode --> KVGather
```
