## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the SGLang Diffusion serving interface, component-loading paths for image and video generation, quantization workflows, LoRA adapters, Cache-DiT acceleration, encoding/denoising stages, and the ComfyUI integration application (`ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion`). It covers request and server configuration options via `ServerArgs`, specialized component loaders, FSDP distribution, and runtime execution mapping [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:14-40](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:8-29](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-178](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:1-191](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:74-111]().

Sources: [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:14-40](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:8-29](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-178](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:1-191](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:74-111]()

---

## 1. OpenAI-Compatible Image/Video API and Server Arguments (`ServerArgs`)

SGLang Diffusion provides serving endpoints compatible with OpenAI-style image and video generation tasks, launched via `sglang serve`, alongside one-off execution via `sglang generate` [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/cli.mdx:6-7](). 

### Generation Interface and Entrypoints

Server options configure deployment topologies and model setups via `ServerArgs`, while request payloads control runtime sampling parameters without reloading weights [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:14-27](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:122-140](). For multi-partition models (such as MiniMax-H3), checkpoints are loaded based on semantic variants specified via `--model-variant` (e.g., `fl2va` for text-to-video-and-audio and frame conditioning, or `ref2va` for reference-conditioned requests) [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:35-37](), [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:48-65]().

Command-line parsing uses `FlexibleArgumentParser` and `ServerArgs.add_cli_args` to process parameters like `--model-path`, `--model-variant`, `--performance-mode`, and component path overrides [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:79-82](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_server_args.py:165-182](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/cli.mdx:73-92]().

### Server Arguments and Configuration

The component-oriented configuration contract defines how individual parts of diffusion pipelines are loaded and overridden:

| Input or operation | Configuration | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base model | `--model-path` | Selects the base model repository. |
| Component repository or directory | `--component-paths.<component>` | Replaces that component’s configuration and weights. |
| Component weights only | `--component-weights-paths.<component>` | Keeps the base component configuration and substitutes its weights. |
| Online component quantization | `--component-quantizations.<component>` | Requests an online quantization implementation for that component. |
| Online quantization exclusions | `--component-quantization-ignored-layers.<component>` | Excludes matching layers from component quantization. |
| Primary-transformer aliases | `--transformer-path`, `--transformer-weights-path`, `--quantization` | Convenience spellings for pipelines with one primary DiT. |
| Causal KV-cache quantization | `--kv-cache-quant` | Quantizes completed runtime cache chunks; it does not quantize checkpoint weights. |

[docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:18-29]()

Sources: [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:18-29]()

### API and Runtime Dataflow

At the model-configuration boundary, request or server arguments populate `ServerArgs`, which drives the `ComponentLoader` registry (`component_name_to_loader_cls`) to dispatch specialized loaders.

**Diagram: Serving Configuration to Component Loader Entities**
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        SERVE["sglang serve"]
        MODEL["Base model selection"]
        COMPONENT["Component or weights override"]
        QUANT["Component quantization request"]
    end

    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        ARGS["ServerArgs"]
        REGISTRY["component_name_to_loader_cls"]
        BASE["ComponentLoader"]
        TRANSFORMER["TransformerLoader"]
        ENCODER["TextEncoderLoader"]
        VAE["VAE loader"]
    end

    SERVE --> ARGS
    MODEL --> ARGS
    COMPONENT --> ARGS
    QUANT --> ARGS
    ARGS --> REGISTRY
    REGISTRY --> BASE
    BASE --> TRANSFORMER
    BASE --> ENCODER
    BASE --> VAE
```
Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-178](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:159-168](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/text_encoder_loader.py:76-87](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:18-38](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:122-140](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:18-29]()

Sources: [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:14-37](), [docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx:48-65](), [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:18-29](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-178](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py:1-191]()

## 2. LoRA Adapter Support and State Normalization

Diffusion LoRA support includes linear-layer wrappers that keep base-layer weights and adapter weights distinct. 

### LoRA Linear-Layer Behavior

`BaseLayerWithLoRA` wraps a base module and maintains adapter-related state, including `lora_weights_list`, `lora_path`, `strength`, and a disabled-by-default flag [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/lora/linear.py:145-183]().

`_compute_lora_delta` computes the ordinary projection as `x @ lora_A.T @ lora_B.T`. For stacked projections, it uses grouped `einsum` operations and flattens group and output dimensions [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/lora/linear.py:59-77]().

The optional `_add_lora_delta_in_gemm` path accumulates the scaled delta into the output through the second GEMM rather than materializing the full delta. `_can_add_lora_delta_in_gemm` restricts this optimization to matching 2D or 3D adapter tensors, compatible stacked group counts, and a request quality permitting lossless behavior [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/lora/linear.py:80-142]().

### LoRA Application Path

**Diagram: LoRA Linear Update and Code Entities**
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        BASEWEIGHT["Base linear projection"]
        ADAPTER["LoRA A and B adapter matrices"]
        QUALITY["Request permits lossless behavior"]
    end

    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        WRAPPER["BaseLayerWithLoRA"]
        DELTA["_compute_lora_delta"]
        GATE["_can_add_lora_delta_in_gemm"]
        FUSED["_add_lora_delta_in_gemm"]
        CONTEXT["get_forward_context_or_none"]
        QUALITYFN["quality_allows"]
    end

    BASEWEIGHT --> WRAPPER
    ADAPTER --> DELTA
    WRAPPER --> DELTA
    ADAPTER --> GATE
    QUALITY --> CONTEXT
    CONTEXT --> QUALITYFN
    QUALITYFN --> GATE
    GATE --> FUSED
```

## 3. FSDP Model Loading and Component Architecture

Component loading separates the model’s component configuration from its weight source. 

### FSDP Loading Mechanics

`fsdp_load.py` imports PyTorch FSDP primitives including `fully_shard`, `DeviceMesh`, `MixedPrecisionPolicy`, and `CPUOffloadPolicy`. Shard-condition resolution evaluates explicit conditions first, followed by model-declared repeated/no-split block classes, and finally common numbered block names [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:14-25](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:144-180]().

### Model Component Loaders

| Loader or component family | Responsibilities evidenced by the implementation |
| --- | --- |
| `TransformerLoader` | Shared loader for DiT transformer components (`transformer`, `unconditional_transformer`, `audio_dit`, `video_dit`). Resolves component-specific server-argument overrides and provides component attention-backend context [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:101-183](). |
| Text encoder loader | Resolves encoder quantization configuration, supports an SRT FP8 checkpoint adapter for eligible tensor-parallel encoders, and delegates serialized quantization to Transformers when appropriate [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/text_encoder_loader.py:127-183](). |
| VAE loader | Checks quantized-checkpoint metadata before selecting loader path; supports precision and memory-layout logic, including optional `channels_last_3d` conversion [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:62-100](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:116-166](). |
| `ComponentLoader` | Base class for component-specific loaders; subclasses register component names in `component_name_to_loader_cls` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-164](). |

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/component_loader.py:147-164](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/text_encoder_loader.py:127-183](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:101-183](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:62-100](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:116-166]()

### Component Model Loading Flow

`TransformerLoader` resolves transformer checkpoint files and a `TransformerQuantLoadSpec` through helpers in `transformer_load_utils.py` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:30-36](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:151-168]().

## 4. Quantization Systems and Optimization

Diffusion quantization is component-scoped. Selecting a component source and materializing its quantized checkpoint are distinct operations [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:8-12]().

### Quantization Configuration Resolution

`TransformerQuantLoadSpec` represents the resolved transformer loading plan, containing safetensors files or GGUF files, quantization configuration, parameter dtype, device-weight postprocess flags, and post-load hooks [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:151-168]().

For ModelOpt NVFP4, safetensors-derived layout information supersedes stale `config.json` exclusion lists while preserving explicit settings like packed-module mapping and scale layout [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:82-148]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:82-168]()

### Quantization Families and Loader Constraints

| Family or path | Relevant behavior |
| --- | --- |
| ModelOpt FP4 / NVFP4 | Runtime helpers normalize serialized NVFP4 weight bytes and transform scale layouts [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py:67-96](). |
| FP8 | FSDP loader includes `_maybe_dequantize_fp8` for cases where checkpoints store FP8 weights but parameters expect higher precision [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:183-195](). |
| BitsAndBytes 4-bit | FSDP loading includes helpers to build, split, and attach 4-bit quantization state [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:35-38](). |
| Nunchaku | Transformer quant-load plan carries `NunchakuConfig`; validation is delegated to helpers [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:151-168](). |
| Online quantization | Component-level CLI flags request supported implementations (`fp8`, `convrot_int8`, `mxfp4`) [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:18-24](). |

Sources: [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx:8-12](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/transformer_load_utils.py:82-168](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:35-38](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py:183-195]()

## 5. Caching Integration (Cache-DiT)

Cache-DiT settings are controlled via specific environment variables defined in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py`:

- `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED`: Master boolean toggle for cache-DiT acceleration (`False` by default) [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:74-74]().
- `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP`: Frame number, block number, and warmup step configurations for caching [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:75-77]().
- `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER` and `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_DMD`: Advanced prediction and distribution matching distillation acceleration flags [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:80-82]().

Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py:74-90]()

## 6. Encoding and Denoising Pipeline Stages

Diffusion pipelines are composed from model components and stage implementations. 

### Conditioning and Encoding

The component-loading system supports text encoder, image encoder, transformer, and VAE component families. Text-encoder loading imports configuration, model registry, tensor-parallel helpers, and checkpoint iterators [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/text_encoder_loader.py:11-24]().

### Denoising and Output Decoding

`TransformerLoader` serves video and audio DiT transformers, working alongside VAE components that handle target precision and memory layouts [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:159-168](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py:18-38]().

## 7. ComfyUI Integration App (`ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion`)

SGLang Diffusion provides a ComfyUI custom node package under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion` to bridge high-performance SGLang inference engines with ComfyUI node graphs.

### Architecture and Core Components

- **Nodes (`nodes.py`)**: Exposes ComfyUI-compatible node definitions for model loading, SGLang generation requests, LoRA loading, and component weight specification.
- **Generator Core (`core/generator.py`)**: Manages process execution, parameter serialization, and asynchronous handoff between ComfyUI execution graphs and the underlying SGLang Diffusion pipeline runtime.
- **Model Patches (`worker_patches/`)**: Implements model-specific graph patches (e.g., for MiniMax-H3) to align ComfyUI tensor formats with SGLang worker memory layouts.

**Diagram: ComfyUI Node Execution to SGLang Diffusion Generator Core**

```mermaid
    end

    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        NODES["nodes.py Node Class"]
        GENERATOR["core/generator.py SGLDiffusionGenerator"]
        WORKER["SGLang Diffusion Worker Pipeline"]
        PATCHES["worker_patches/h3.py"]
    end

    COMFYNODE --> NODES
    NODEPARAM --> NODES
    LORACOMFY --> NODES
    NODES --> GENERATOR
    GENERATOR --> PATCHES
    PATCHES --> WORKER
```
Sources: [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/nodes.py:1-50](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/core/generator.py:1-60]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes how the `multimodal_gen` test suite configures diffusion-generation test cases, validates performance and output consistency, manages platform-aware baselines, computes test partitions, applies diffusion fused kernels with strict numerical contracts, and runs CI ground-truth generation workflows [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_common.py:1-6](), [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-12]().

Sources: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_common.py:1-6`; `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-12`

## 1. Test Suite Architecture and Kernel Verification (`multimodal_gen`)

The multimodal generation test suite uses pytest parameterization and `DiffusionTestCase` definitions to exercise models through a running diffusion server instance [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py:78-139](). The core integration point is the `diffusion_server` pytest fixture defined in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_common.py`, which constructs command-line server arguments (`DiffusionServerArgs`), allocates dynamic network ports, and manages the lifecycle of the server process [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_common.py:141-199]().

Diffusion fused kernels under `sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion` enforce strict numerical contracts via `BitExactFusionGate` and verification mechanisms [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:1-26](), [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py:120-120](). Kernel test wiring is validated in `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py` [test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py:1-20]().

### Diagram: Test Execution and Code Entity Bridge

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

## 2. Testcase Configurations and Parameterization

Test cases are declared in platform-specific collections such as `ONE_GPU_CASES`, `ONE_GPU_MODELOPT_FP8_CASES`, and `TWO_GPU_CASES` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:4-16](). Each entry combines a test identifier, server arguments, sampling parameters (`DiffusionSamplingParams`), and validation control flags [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py:80-116]().

| Class Name | Module Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `DiffusionTestCase` | `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py` | Encapsulates a single test case ID, `DiffusionServerArgs`, `DiffusionSamplingParams`, and check flags (`run_perf_check`, `run_consistency_check`, etc.). |
| `ToleranceConfig` | `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py` | Holds relative tolerance ratios (`e2e`, `denoise_stage`, `load_peak_vram`, etc.) loaded via `ToleranceConfig.load_profile`. |
| `ScenarioConfig` | `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py` | Stores expected stage durations, step timings (`denoise_step_ms`), VRAM caps, and memory allocation peaks. |

`ToleranceConfig.load_profile` supports both legacy flat dictionaries and profile-based layouts (such as `pr_test` and `long_term`), while respecting environment overrides (`SGLANG_E2E_TOLERANCE`, `SGLANG_RUNTIME_PEAK_VRAM_TOLERANCE`) [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:60-113](). `ScenarioConfig.from_dict` parses expected scenario metrics from baseline JSON files [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:145-165]().

Sources: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:46-165`; `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py:78-116`

## 3. Performance and Consistency Baselines

### Performance Baselines

Performance regression thresholds and expected metrics are stored as JSON files under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/perf_baselines/` (e.g., `h100.json`, `b200.json`, `5090.json`) [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:12-16](); [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/perf_baselines/h100.json:1-51](). Each baseline file specifies metadata, calibration run identifiers, profile tolerances (`pr_test`), and scenario dictionaries [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/perf_baselines/h100.json:1-51]().

Developers can update or generate local performance baselines by executing test runs with the environment variable `SGLANG_GEN_BASELINE=1` and saving the resulting metrics into the appropriate platform scenario block [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:12-16]().

### Consistency References and Thresholds

Consistency ground-truth outputs (golden images, video frames, and audio waveforms) are fetched remotely from the `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion` repository at a pinned Git revision (`SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION`) [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/test_utils.py:35-40]().

When executing tests on Ascend NPU hardware (`current_platform.is_npu()`), the framework switches to an NPU-specific revision and directory path (`SGL_TEST_FILES_CONSISTENCY_GT_BASE_ASCEND`) to account for backend-specific numerical differences [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/test_utils.py:42-75](). Comparison helpers evaluate generated outputs against references using CLIP similarity, SSIM, PSNR, mean absolute difference, and audio spectral metrics [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/test_utils.py:77-112]().

### Diagram: Consistency Validation Dataflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CI_Data["sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion (SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION)"] -->|Downloads GT| GTStore["Consistency Ground Truth"]
    ServerOutput["Generated Media Output"] --> compare_with_gt["compare_with_gt / compare_audio_with_gt"]
    GTStore --> compare_with_gt
    Thresholds["Threshold Configs (h100.json / default ratios)"] --> compare_with_gt
    compare_with_gt --> AssertPass["Test Success / Failure Artifact"]

    classDef code font-family:monospace;
    class compare_with_gt,GTStore code;
```

Sources: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/perf_baselines/h100.json:1-51`; `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/test_utils.py:35-112`; `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py:12-16`

## 4. Diffusion Fused Kernels and Numerical Quality Contracts

Diffusion generation workloads rely on specialized fused kernels located under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:1-26](). Kernels are categorized by numerical contract and quality tier in `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx` [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx:11-36]():

- **Bit-exact**: Replicates every eager rounding boundary (`torch.equal`), verified at runtime via `BitExactFusionGate` [python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:52-61]().
- **Lossless (request-gated)**: Preserves reference math and operand precision while optimizing layout or launch overhead [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx:16-17]().
- **High (approximate)**: Permits lower-precision accumulation or quantization (e.g. NVFP4 / FP8 quant fusions) [docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx:18-20]().

### Diagram: Kernel Resolution and Code Entity Bridge

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Facade["sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion (__init__.py)"] -->|Lazy PEP 562 Resolution| Registry["_SPECS Registry"]
    Registry -->|Selects Backend| Triton["Triton / CUTLASS / JIT Backend"]
    Triton -->|Mounted at Module Site| Layer["layernorm.py / qwen_image.py"]
    Layer -->|Guarded by| Gate["BitExactFusionGate / VaeFastPathGate"]
    Gate -->|Tested in| Test["test_model_fast_paths.py"]

    classDef code font-family:monospace;
    class Facade,Registry,Triton,Layer,Gate,Test code;
```

Sources: `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py:1-47`; `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md:1-61`; `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx:11-36`; `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py:1-20`

## 5. Suite Entry Point and Partitioning

Test execution is coordinated via the suite entry point `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py`, which delegates execution to `diffusion_suite_runner.main()` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py:1-6]().

To distribute workloads across CI runners, `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/compute_diffusion_partitions.py` uses an AST-based parser (`DiffusionTestCaseVisitor`) defined in `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/diffusion_case_parser.py` [python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py](); `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/diffusion_case_parser.py:85-187`(). The parser inspects list assignments, `+=` augmentations, and `append()` expressions across conditional blocks without importing execution dependencies [scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/diffusion_case_parser.py:85-187]().

Sources: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py:1-6`; `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/diffusion_case_parser.py:85-187`

## 6. Diffusion CI Ground-Truth Generation Workflow

The GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml` automates the generation and publishing of reference ground truth [.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml:1-55](). It is triggered via `workflow_dispatch` with parameters for Git reference (`ref`), specific case IDs (`case_ids`), publication target directory (`publish_target_dir`), and whether to run official comparable cases (`run_official_cases`) [.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml:3-55]().

When `run_official_cases` is enabled, the `compute-official-gt-matrix` job dynamically builds a parallel execution matrix categorized by source groups (`diffusers`, `wan21`, `ltx`) [.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml:72-167](). Generated golden files are published back to `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion` under `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/official_generated` or `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/sglang_generated` using a personal access token with push permissions [.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml:69-89]().

### Diagram: Ground Truth Generation Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dispatch as "GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch"

    participant RemoteRepo as "sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion"

    Dispatch->>MatrixJob: "Trigger with inputs (ref, case_ids, run_official_cases)"
    MatrixJob->>MatrixJob: "Parse cases and assign runner groups"
    MatrixJob->>Runner: "Dispatch parametrized build matrix"
    Runner->>Runner: "Execute diffusion model & dump reference output"
    Runner->>RemoteRepo: "Publish artifacts to target dir (official_generated / sglang_generated)"

    classDef code font-family:monospace;

```

### Purpose and Scope

This page introduces SGLang’s domain-specific language (DSL) for composing LLM programs and outlines the contents of the `examples/` directory [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](). The frontend language provides a Pythonic abstraction for writing complex LLM workflows (such as multi-turn conversations, parallel generation, and branching logic) and executing them against SGLang runtime backends or OpenAI-compatible APIs [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](), [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:159-196]().

As a parent page, this section provides a high-level overview. For deep technical details, refer to the child pages:
- [Language IR and Interpreter](#23.1) — Covers the SGLang IR primitives (`gen`, `select`, `fork`), interpreter execution model, program composition, and `examples/frontend_language`.
- [Backend Integrations for Frontend Language](#23.2) — Covers runtime endpoint and OpenAI backends, how frontend programs map to server calls, and `examples/runtime` monitoring examples.

Sources: [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](), [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:159-196]()

### Frontend Language Workflow and Core Abstractions

The SGLang frontend language allows developers to define prompts and control flow programmatically using decorators and expression primitives [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](). Programs are encapsulated as functions (`SglFunction`), which build up a graph of expressions (`SglExpr`) executed by the interpreter (`StreamExecutor`) while maintaining prompt variables and state (`ProgramState`) [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](), [python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:71-80]().

**Diagram: Program Composition Space Mapping**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UserPrompt["User Prompt & Workflow (Natural Language Space)"] -->|Composed via Decorator| SglFunction["sglang.lang.ir.SglFunction"]
    SglFunction -->|Builds Expression Tree| SglExpr["sglang.lang.ir.SglExpr"]
    SglExpr -->|Interpreted by| StreamExecutor["sglang.lang.interpreter.StreamExecutor"]
    StreamExecutor -->|Mutates State| ProgramState["sglang.lang.interpreter.ProgramState"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](), [python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:71-80]()

### Language and Backend Integration Architecture

Once a frontend program is interpreted, its execution requests are dispatched through a backend interface [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:26-55](). SGLang supports native runtime endpoints (`RuntimeEndpoint`) communicating directly with local SGLang Runtime (SRT) instances, as well as third-party or OpenAI backends (`OpenAIBackend`) [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:159-196]().

**Diagram: Backend Execution Space Mapping**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    StreamExecutor["sglang.lang.interpreter.StreamExecutor"] -->|Dispatches Calls| RuntimeEndpoint["sglang.lang.backend.runtime_endpoint.RuntimeEndpoint"]
    StreamExecutor -->|Alternative Target| OpenAIBackend["sglang.lang.backend.openai.OpenAIBackend"]
    RuntimeEndpoint -->|Sends Requests To| SRTServer["SGLang Runtime SRT Server"]
    OpenAIBackend -->|Sends Requests To| OpenAIAPI["OpenAI-Compatible API Endpoint"]
```

Sources: [python/sglang/lang/ir.py:141-152](), [python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:71-80](), [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:26-55](), [python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:159-196]()

## Purpose and scope

This page explains the SGLang frontend language’s intermediate representation (IR), interpreter execution model, and composition primitives. It focuses on how a program is represented and executed, and points to `examples/frontend_language` for usage examples. 

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:515-642]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:57-108]()`

---

## Intermediate Representation (IR) primitives

The frontend IR represents operations in an LLM program, including generation, selection, variable access, multimodal inputs, and chat-role boundaries. The primitive implementations are located in `python/sglang/lang/ir.py`.

| IR entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `SglVariable` | Represents a variable that refers to a value generated or assigned during program execution. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:515-519]()` |
| `SglGen` | Represents a generation operation, with a prompt context and generation parameters. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:534-558]()` |
| `SglSelect` | Represents selection among candidate strings. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:612-623]()` |
| `SglImage` | Represents an image input in the program stream. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:642-642]()` |
| `SglVideo` | Represents a video input in the program stream. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:642-642]()` |
| `SglRoleBegin` / `SglRoleEnd` | Represent boundaries for chat roles such as system, user, and assistant. `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:642-642]()` |

`SglGen` carries generation settings such as sampling options and output constraints; `SglSelect` expresses a choice operation over candidate strings. These IR nodes let a program describe language-model interactions as composable operations rather than as one undifferentiated prompt.

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:515-642]()`

---

## Interpreter execution model

`StreamExecutor`, defined in `python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py`, evaluates the frontend program. It maintains execution context—including accumulated text, multimodal inputs, and values associated with variables—and processes IR operations as it runs the program.

The program-running entry points include `run_program` and `run_program_batch`. The former runs a program to completion and supports streaming; the latter runs multiple programs as a batch.

### Execution data flow

At a high level, execution proceeds from the program into the interpreter, then through the relevant IR operation. For a generation operation, the interpreter delegates the request to a backend such as `RuntimeEndpoint`; the backend communicates with the SGLang serving runtime and returns generated output to the interpreter. The interpreter updates its state and exposes the result to the caller.

Title: "Execution Data Flow Sequence"
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as "User"
    participant Program as "SglFunction"
    participant Executor as "StreamExecutor"
    participant Operation as "SglGen"
    participant Backend as "RuntimeEndpoint"
    participant Server as "SRT server"

    Caller->>Program: "run_program"
    Program->>Executor: "evaluate program"
    Executor->>Operation: "execute IR operation"
    Operation->>Backend: "generate request"
    Backend->>Server: "submit request"
    Server-->>Backend: "generation result"
    Backend-->>Executor: "return output"
    Executor-->>Caller: "program result or stream"
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:57-108]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:186-192]()`

### Batch execution

`run_program_batch` supports running multiple programs together. The interpreter also includes mechanisms for concurrent execution and prefix tracing, as described by the batch execution implementation.

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:93-108]()`

---

## Program composition and `fork`

SGLang programs compose IR operations with higher-level Python control flow. The `fork` operation creates branches from the current execution context so multiple child paths can proceed independently. Branches inherit the prompt context available at the fork point while keeping subsequent execution state separate.

This makes `fork` useful when a program needs to explore multiple continuations from shared context. `SglVariable` provides access to values associated with the current execution state, while generation and selection operations form the actions within each path.

Title: "Program Composition and Fork Mapping"
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Branching["Explore alternative continuations"]
        SharedContext["Continue from shared prompt context"]
        Values["Capture and reuse generated values"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Fork["StreamExecutor.fork"]
        Program["SglFunction"]
        Variable["SglVariable"]
        Generation["SglGen"]
        Selection["SglSelect"]
    end

    Branching --> Fork
    SharedContext --> Program
    Values --> Variable
    Fork --> Generation
    Fork --> Selection
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:1095]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:515-623]()`

---

## Multimodal inputs, roles, and constraints

### Multimodal inputs and chat-role boundaries

The IR includes nodes for image and video inputs, and nodes for beginning and ending a chat role. During interpretation, multimodal payloads are collected into execution state for backend requests.

The role-boundary nodes represent conversational structure in the program. The language layer’s chat-template support is represented by `ChatTemplate`; backend request construction connects frontend context and input payloads to the runtime.

### Structured generation

Generation parameters can carry output constraints, including regular-expression and JSON-schema constraints. These settings are associated with the generation operation and are passed through the frontend execution path to the backend.

Title: "Multimodal and Structured Generation Mapping"
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Chat["Represent chat turns"]
        Visual["Include visual context"]
        Constrained["Constrain generated output"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Role["SglRoleBegin / SglRoleEnd"]
        Media["SglImage / SglVideo"]
        Template["ChatTemplate"]
        Constraint["SglSamplingParams.regex / json_schema"]
        Gen["SglGen"]
    end

    Chat --> Role
    Chat --> Template
    Visual --> Media
    Constrained --> Constraint
    Constraint --> Gen
```

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:18-41]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/ir.py:642-642]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/chat_template.py:57-62]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:107-118]()`

---

## Execution backends

The frontend interpreter delegates model interaction through a backend abstraction. `RuntimeEndpoint` is the runtime-connected backend: it connects the frontend program to a running SGLang serving engine and submits generation requests to the runtime.

The separation between interpreter and backend keeps program evaluation distinct from the details of communicating with a serving runtime. The interpreter evaluates operations; the backend carries out the corresponding request and returns output.

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:27-55]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py:159-232]()`, `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:57-108]()`

---

## Examples and further reading

For concrete frontend-language usage and composition patterns, see `examples/frontend_language`. The interpreter’s program execution and streaming entry points are in `python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py`.

Sources: `[python/sglang/lang/interpreter.py:57-108]()`, `[examples/frontend_language]()`

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the backend interfaces relevant to SGLang frontend-language programs and external API clients: internal runtime generation requests (`GenerateReqInput`), OpenAI-compatible serving handlers (`OpenAIServingChat`, `OpenAIServingResponses`, `OpenAIServingCompletion`), chat encoding dispatchers, and how frontend programs or HTTP requests map to server calls, template resolution, and runtime execution parameters.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-60](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:1-100](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:49-146]()

---

## Backend Architecture and Frontend-to-Server Mapping

The SGLang backend exposes multiple API surfaces that translate external requests into internal `GenerateReqInput` structures or dispatch them through specialized protocol adapters and chat encoders.

### Integration Boundaries

| Boundary | Code Entity | Role in Integration |
|---|---|---|
| Chat Serving | `OpenAIServingChat` | Handles OpenAI chat completion endpoints, validation, and tool-call formatting. [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:1-100]() |
| Completion Serving | `OpenAIServingCompletion` | Processes legacy text completion endpoints (`/v1/completions`) and converts parameters. [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:49-60]() |
| Responses Serving | `OpenAIServingResponses` | Extends `OpenAIServingChat` to handle `/v1/responses` structured workflows. [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]() |
| Chat Encoding | `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` | Resolves model-specific chat/tool encoding strategies (e.g. DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, Inkling). [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-60]() |
| Internal Request | `GenerateReqInput` | Encapsulates tokenized prompt data, sampling parameters, and metadata for the runtime scheduler. [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:116-146]() |

---

## Runtime Endpoint Backend

The runtime endpoint receives structured inputs via `GenerateReqInput`. Handlers like `OpenAIServingChat`, `OpenAIServingCompletion`, and `OpenAIServingResponses` parse inbound conversations using Jinja templates, chat encoders, and tool-call parsers before passing generation jobs to the underlying runtime engines.

### Chat Encoding and Template Resolution

`resolve_chat_encoding_spec` determines the specific model-dependent chat encoder [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-59](). Tool payloads and assistant tool calls are normalized using functions like `normalize_tool_content` and `parse_tool_call_arguments` prior to rendering prompt strings [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:179-201]().

For text completions, `OpenAIServingCompletion._convert_to_internal_request` maps `CompletionRequest` parameters into internal `GenerateReqInput` instances, configuring sampling parameters, logprob tracking, routing keys, and LoRA paths [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:71-146]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py:20-59](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:179-201](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:71-146]()

---

## OpenAI Protocol Backends

SGLang provides full protocol compatibility layers for OpenAI endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`).

### Protocol Models and Serving Classes

`ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest` validate inbound API payloads using Pydantic models with strict field bounds (e.g. validating `n` against `OPENAI_MAX_N` and bounding `logprobs` to vocabulary sizes) [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:86-120](). `OpenAIServingResponses` inherits from `OpenAIServingChat` and initializes prompt token usage counters and tool servers [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:180-196]().

**Diagram: Protocol translation and serving dispatch**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural_Language_Space"
        OpenAI_Chat_Client["OpenAI Chat Client"]
        OpenAI_Completion_Client["OpenAI Completion Client"]
    end

    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        OpenAI_Chat_Client --> ChatCompletionRequest["ChatCompletionRequest"]
        OpenAI_Completion_Client --> CompletionRequest["CompletionRequest"]
        ChatCompletionRequest --> OpenAIServingChat["OpenAIServingChat"]
        CompletionRequest --> OpenAIServingCompletion["OpenAIServingCompletion"]
        OpenAIServingChat --> GenerateReqInput["GenerateReqInput"]
        OpenAIServingCompletion --> GenerateReqInput
    end
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:86-120](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:1-100](), [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:49-146]()

---

## Request Dataflow: API Request to Generation Input

The lifecycle of an inbound request moves from protocol validation through template rendering and sampling configuration into an internal generation struct.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as "API Client"
    participant Serving as "OpenAIServingCompletion / OpenAIServingChat"
    participant Protocol as "CompletionRequest"
    participant RuntimeInput as "GenerateReqInput"
    participant Engine as "TokenizerManager / Scheduler"

    Client->>Serving: "HTTP Request (/v1/completions)"
    Serving->>Protocol: "Validate payload and parse fields"
    Protocol-->>Serving: "Validated model instance"
    Serving->>RuntimeInput: "Build GenerateReqInput with sampling parameters"
    RuntimeInput->>Engine: "Dispatch generation request"
```

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_completions.py:63-146]()

---

## Monitoring and Observability Examples

SGLang tracks scheduler performance, token budgets, and resource utilizations through dedicated metrics structures. `SchedulerStats` records aggregate quantities such as running request counts, cache hit rates, token usage ratios across full-attention pools, and speculative decoding metrics.

Metrics collectors and reporters aggregate stage latencies and forward pass timings to expose Prometheus-compatible endpoints and runtime telemetry.

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:210-230]()

This page serves as a high-level index to SGLang-specific terminology, codebase jargon, abbreviations, and domain concepts. It maps high-level runtime and distributed abstractions to their corresponding implementation files and modules, pointing to specialized child pages for exhaustive definitions [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().

## 1. Runtime, Scheduling, and Memory Terms

The core serving runtime (SRT) manages incoming prompts, schedules requests into execution batches, allocates token-to-KV memory pools, and interfaces with hardware execution backends via components such as `ScheduleBatch` and `ForwardBatch` [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48](). Server arguments and process-wide configurations are managed via server parameter groups and inspected through runtime context modules [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:41-60]().

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping: Runtime and Scheduling

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        Req["Request"]
        Batch["Scheduler Batch"]
        Forward["Forward Batching"]
        Runner["Model Execution Runner"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntity["Code Entity Space"]
        ReqClass["Req [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]()"]
        BatchClass["ScheduleBatch [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]()"]
        ForwardClass["ForwardBatch [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]()"]
        RunnerClass["ModelRunner [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:72-76]()"]
    end
    Req --> ReqClass
    Batch --> BatchClass
    Forward --> ForwardClass
    Runner --> RunnerClass
```
Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48](), [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:41-76]()

For details on core SRT runtime terms, request lifecycle states, KV cache allocation, RadixCache, HiCache, HiSparse, and CUDA graphs, see [Glossary: Runtime, Scheduling, and Memory Terms](#24.1) [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:36-48]().

---

## 2. Distributed, Quantization, Multimodal, and Router Terms

Distributed execution strategies span Tensor Parallelism (TP), Pipeline Parallelism (PP), Data Parallelism (DP), Expert Parallelism (EP), and Context Parallelism (CP), coordinated via parallel state utilities [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:120-124](). Quantization configurations and transfer mechanisms (such as Mooncake and NIXL) coordinate state transfers and weight management across disaggregated instances [python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py:67-70](), [python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py:40-40]().

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping: Distributed and Configuration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NL["Natural Language Space"]
        TPPP["Tensor & Pipeline Parallelism"]
        Quant["Quantization & Disaggregation"]
        Context["Runtime Context & Server Args"]
        Transfer["Transfer Backends"]
    end
    subgraph CE["Code Entity Space"]
        ParallelState["parallel_state [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:120-124]()"]
        MooncakeEngine["mooncake_transfer_engine [python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py:67-70]()"]
        NixlConn["NixlKVManager [python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py:40-40]()"]
        RuntimeCtx["runtime_context [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:41-60]()"]
    end
    TPPP --> ParallelState
    Quant --> MooncakeEngine
    Context --> RuntimeCtx
    Transfer --> NixlConn
```

## Purpose and Scope

This page defines core SGLang Runtime (SRT) terms used in request scheduling, model execution, configuration, and KV-cache management. It focuses on the relationship between principal runtime entities and points to their primary implementation files. [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-20]() [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-23]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-20]() [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-23]()

---

## 1. Request and Batch Data Structures

A request passes through two related batch representations: `ScheduleBatch` holds high-level scheduling information, while `ForwardBatch` holds the lower-level data needed for a model forward pass. The code documents this relationship as `ScheduleBatch → ForwardBatch`; most scheduling data is CPU-side, and most forward-batch data consists of GPU tensors. [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-20]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-20]()

### `Req` (Request)

`Req` is the per-request entity used by scheduling and batch formation, encapsulating input token IDs, prompt details, generation states, and KV metadata. [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-100]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-100]()

### `ScheduleBatch`

`ScheduleBatch` is the scheduler-managed, high-level batch representation. It groups request scheduling information and is the source object from which `ForwardBatch` is constructed. The code describes most of its data as CPU-resident and identifies `scheduler.py::Scheduler` as its manager. [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:14-50]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:14-50]()

### `ForwardBatch`

`ForwardBatch` is the model-runner-facing representation of a batch. It contains lower-level forward data, mostly GPU tensors, and is constructed directly from a `ScheduleBatch` through `ForwardBatch.init_new`. [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-30]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-30]()

### Request-to-Forward Dataflow (Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
    NLReq["Request Input"]
    NLBatch["Scheduler Batch"]
    NLRunner["Model Runner Execution"]
  end

  subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
    Req["Req"]
    ScheduleBatch["ScheduleBatch"]
    Scheduler["python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py::Scheduler"]
    InitNew["ForwardBatch.init_new"]
    ForwardBatch["ForwardBatch"]
    ModelRunner["python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py::ModelRunner"]
  end

  NLReq --> Req
  NLBatch --> ScheduleBatch
  NLRunner --> ModelRunner

  Req --> ScheduleBatch
  Scheduler --> ScheduleBatch
  ScheduleBatch --> InitNew
  InitNew --> ForwardBatch
  ForwardBatch --> ModelRunner
```
*Diagram: Bridging natural language request concepts to code entities*

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:14-50]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-30]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:1-50]()

## 2. Server Configuration

### `ServerArgs`

`ServerArgs` is the public server-configuration record used to collect command-line and runtime inputs. `server_args.py` describes its responsibilities as argument construction, resolution, CLI registration, and network-port handling. [python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:1-50]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:1-50]()

### `RuntimeContext`

`RuntimeContext` is the process-wide home for configuration, parallel state, flags, resources, and forward state. Its module documentation distinguishes resolved configuration from mutable runtime state and process-owned handles. [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-30]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-30]()

### Configuration Resolution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  RawInput["ServerArgs raw inputs"]
  Resolve["python/sglang/srt/server_args.py::prepare_server_args"]
  Published["python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py::RuntimeContext"]
  Accessors["python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py::get_exec / get_schedule / get_memory"]

  RawInput --> Resolve
  Resolve --> Published
  Published --> Accessors
```
*Diagram: Configuration parameters resolution and publishing pipeline*

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:1-50]() [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-30]()

---

## 3. Memory Management and KV Cache

### KV Cache and Token Pools

The KV cache stores key/value state used by model attention. `ReqToTokenPool`, `TokenToKVPoolAllocator`, and `KVCache` manage the mapping and physical allocation of token blocks. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1-25]() [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:210-220]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1-25]() [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:210-220]()

### `RadixCache` and `UnifiedRadixCache`

`UnifiedRadixCache` is a `BasePrefixCache` implementation managing prefix sharing across requests using tree nodes and reference counting. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:210-225]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:210-225]()

### HiCache and `HiRadixCache`

HiCache provides multi-tier storage backing for radix caches, supporting device, host, and storage tiers via `HybridCacheController` and `BufferModePipeline`. [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:45-75]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:45-75]()

### `HiSparse`

`HiSparse` handles sparse memory pooling and coordination for models like DeepSeek-V4 via `HiSparseCoordinator` and `HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:1-30]() [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py:1-40]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:1-30]() [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py:1-40]()

### Cache and Storage Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ReqTokenPool["ReqToTokenPool"]
  KVAllocator["python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator::BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator"]
  UnifiedCache["python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py::UnifiedRadixCache"]
  Components["FullComponent / MambaComponent / SWAComponent"]
  TreeCore["UnifiedTreeCore / UnifiedTreeNode"]
  StoragePipeline["BufferModePipeline"]
  SparseCoordinator["HiSparseCoordinator"]
  SparseAllocator["HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator"]

  ReqTokenPool --> KVAllocator
  KVAllocator --> UnifiedCache
  UnifiedCache --> Components
  UnifiedCache --> TreeCore
  UnifiedCache --> StoragePipeline
  SparseCoordinator --> SparseAllocator
```
*Diagram: Hierarchical cache and memory allocation mapping*

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:45-120]() [python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:1-30]() [python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py:1-40]()

## 4. Execution, Scheduling, and CUDA Graphs

### Scheduler and Model Execution

The scheduler manages execution rounds and worker dispatch, while `ModelRunner` executes the forward pass using `ForwardBatch`. [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:14-50]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:1-50]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:14-50]() [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:1-50]()

### CUDA Graphs

CUDA graphs capture static execution paths for prefill and decode phases to reduce launch overhead. [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_config.py:1-30]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_config.py:1-30]()

### Breakable and Piecewise Graphs

A **breakable CUDA graph** allows partitioning execution when dynamic shapes or control flow break standard static graphs. A **piecewise CUDA graph** segments graph capture across pipeline parallel or tensor parallel stages. [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:50-70]()

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:50-70]()

---

## 5. Summary of Core Runtime Terms

| Term | Definition | Primary implementation pointer |
|---|---|---|
| `Req` | Per-request entity used in scheduling. | [`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`](python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-100)() |
| `ScheduleBatch` | Scheduler-managed high-level batch representation. | [`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`](python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:42-54)() |
| `ForwardBatch` | Model-runner batch containing GPU tensors. | [`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py`](python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:1-30)() |
| `ServerArgs` | Server configuration record. | [`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`](python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:1-50)() |
| `RuntimeContext` | Process-wide runtime context. | [`python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py`](python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:14-30)() |
| KV Cache Pools | Token and KV pool allocators for memory management. | [`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py`](python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1-25)() |

## Purpose and Scope

This leaf page defines distributed-execution, quantization, multimodal, routing, gateway, and simulator vocabulary used across the SGLang runtime (`sglang.srt`). It maps high-level architectural concepts and natural-language domain terms to exact code entities, classes, modules, and dispatch hooks present in the repository. The definitions incorporate mechanisms such as tensor and pipeline parallelism [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:10-24](), disaggregated prefill-decode coordination [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:10-25](), block-scaled quantization schemes [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:51-84](), and multimodal zero-copy feature transport [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:50-54]().

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:10-24](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:10-25](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:51-84](), [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:50-54]()

## Distributed Execution and Parallelism

### Parallelism Dimensions and Runtime Topology

SGLang structures multi-GPU and multi-node execution into orthogonal or composite parallel dimensions managed via process groups and rank coordinators (`GroupCoordinator`) in `parallel_state.py` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:10-24]().

| Term | Meaning | Code Connection / Implementation Entity |
|---|---|---|
| **TP — Tensor Parallelism** | Partitions individual tensor operations (matrix multiplications, attention projections) across multiple ranks within a Tensor Parallel group. | `GroupCoordinator`, `ColumnParallelLinear`, `RowParallelLinear`, `inplace_all_reduce` [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:186-194]() |
| **PP — Pipeline Parallelism** | Splits sequential model layers across distinct GPU ranks or nodes. Activations and hidden states are passed stage-by-stage using point-to-point communication. | `PPProxyTensors`, pipeline scheduling hooks, stage coordination flags [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:47-53]() |
| **DP — Data Parallelism** | Replicates the full model (or model shards) across independent data-parallel workers, load-balancing incoming prompt batches across replicas. | `DataParallelController`, global/local rank assignments, `derive_parallel_widths` [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:137-157]() |
| **EP — Expert Parallelism** | Distributes Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) network layers such that different GPU ranks host disjoint sets of expert feed-forward networks (FFNs). Tokens are dispatched to resident experts via all-to-all communication. | `MoeRunner`, `MoeRunnerConfig`, `get_moe_runner_backend` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:32-35]() |
| **CP — Context Parallelism** | Shards the sequence dimension of attention across ranks. During prefill or decode, queries, keys, and values are partitioned to fit massive context lengths into distributed memory pools. | `attn_cp_size`, `derive_attn_tp_size`, `derive_attention_ranks` [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:73-93]() |
| **DCP — Distributed Context Parallelism** | An advanced context-parallel layout optimized for decode phases or specific attention kernels, requiring specialized KV-cache sharding and index relayout. | `dcp_size`, `dcp_enabled`, parallel width derivation [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:137-157]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py:10-24](), [python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:47-53](), [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:73-93](), [python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py:137-157](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:32-35]()

### Disaggregation, Bootstrap, and KV Transfer

**Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (PD)** physically separates compute-heavy prompt ingestion (prefill) from memory-bound token generation (decode). The prefill instance processes the prompt, computes attention KV caches, and transmits them across the network. The decode instance receives the KV caches directly into its allocated KV cache pool, bypassing re-computation.

**Bootstrap** is the initial rendezvous and handshake protocol executed between prefill and decode instances. It coordinates rank topology, tensor shapes, and connection parameters before any KV block transmission occurs.

**KV Transfer** involves direct memory access (DMA) or high-speed transport layers to move KV cache pages and auxiliary runtime state tensors between worker memory spaces.

| Term | Definition and Runtime Role | Code Pointers |
|---|---|---|
| **Mooncake** | A high-performance KV cache transfer backend supporting peer-to-peer memory transfers, session registration, and metadata serialization. | `maybe_init_shared_mooncake_transfer_engine`, Mooncake transfer engine [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:10-12]() |
| **NIXL** | Network-Infiniband / X-Layer transfer backend that prepares state-transfer layouts, manages buffer selectors, and checks for layout mismatches across heterogeneous nodes. | State layouts, selector verification, NIXL connection modules [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:67-72]() |
| **MORI** | MoE Routing and Communication Interface providing specialized token dispatch hooks and row-alignment primitives for distributed expert layers. | `get_moe_a2a_backend`, MoE dispatch routing [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:38-45]() |
| **Staging** | Intermediate buffering and message handling architecture used during asynchronous block transfers. | `DpPaddingMode`, batch synchronization modes [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:153-164]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:10-12](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:67-72](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:38-45](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py:153-164]()

## Quantization System

### Quantization Terminology and Formats

SGLang integrates diverse quantization schemes to compress model weights and activation tensors, reducing memory bandwidth pressure and accelerating compute throughput.

| Term | Definition | Code Implementation / Reference |
|---|---|---|
| **FP8** | 8-bit floating point representations (such as `E4M3` and `E5M2`) used for weight matrices and dynamic activations. | `Fp8LinearMethod`, `scaled_fp8_quant`, `fp8_dtype` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:16-21]() |
| **E4M3** | An FP8 format with 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits, and 3 mantissa bits, offering higher precision for activations and weights. | `normalize_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz`, `fp8_dtype` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:21-28]() |
| **W8A8** | Weight-8-bit and Activation-8-bit execution mode, dispatching block-scaled or per-tensor quantization kernels. | `dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-15]() |
| **Block Quantization** | Quantization scheme where scaling factors are computed independently over localized sub-blocks (e.g., `128x128` blocks) rather than entire tensors. | `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, `block_fp8_scale_to_e8m0_128` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:46-63]() |
| **MXFP8** | Microscaled FP8 format adhering to OCP Microscaling Formats specifications, utilizing shared block exponents (e.g., `e8m0`). | `MXFP8QuantizeUtil`, `mxfp8_group_quantize` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:37-76]() |
| **MXFP4** | 4-bit microscaled format designed for next-generation hardware architectures. | `_MXFP4QuantizedData`, `MXFP4QuantizeUtil` [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:37-114]() |
| **NVFP4** | NVIDIA-specific 4-bit floating point quantization format supported on Blackwell GPUs. | `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE`, custom FP4 kernels [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:47-51]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:16-63](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-114](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:47-51]()

### Backend Kernel Dispatchers

Quantization formats map to specialized execution backends depending on the hardware architecture (NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300/MI350, CPU AMX).

| Backend | Runtime Role and Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Triton** | Implements custom JIT-compiled kernels for block-scaled GEMMs and activation quantization (`w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-15]() |
| **DeepGEMM** | High-performance assembly-level GEMM library optimized for Hopper FP8 and block-scaled matrix multiplication (`w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_deepgemm`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-15]() |
| **AITER** | AMD Radeon/ROCm kernel integration providing fused GEMMs, shuffles, and block-scale conversions (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`). [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:190-193]() |
| **FlashInfer** | Supplies optimized attention and quantization operator primitives (e.g., FP4 GEMM routines). [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:34-36]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:10-193](), [python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py:34-36]()

## Multimodal and Vision-Language Terms

### Processor and Tokenization Vocabulary

Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process multimodal prompts containing text interleaved with images, videos, or audio streams.

| Term | Definition and Runtime Behavior | Code Connection |
|---|---|---|
| **VLM — Vision-Language Model** | Architectures that combine a vision encoder (vision tower) with a multimodal projector and a language model backbone. | Model registry, VLM multimodal processor classes [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-95]() |
| **Processor Output** | Structured data container (`BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput`) holding tokenized input IDs, pixel/audio tensors, and image grid dimensions. | `BaseMultiModalProcessorOutput` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:63-95]() |
| **Multimodal Special Token** | Placeholder tokens (e.g., `<|image_pad|>`) recognized by `MultimodalSpecialTokens` to delimit and expand visual feature embeddings in the token stream. | `MultimodalSpecialTokens` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:99-118]() |
| **Feature Transport** | Zero-copy tensor sharing mechanism utilizing CUDA Inter-Process Communication proxies (`MultimodalFeatureTransport`) and memory pools. | `MultimodalFeatureTransport`, `move_feature_to_cpu` [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:50-53]() |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py:50-118]()

## Gateway, Routing, and Simulator Vocabulary

SGLang provides external orchestration and simulation tools that operate alongside or on top of the core serving engine (`srt`).

| Term | Definition and System Role |
|---|---|
| **`sgl-router`** | A slim, Rust-based KV-aware routing layer that inspects prompt tokens, tracks prefix cache locality across worker nodes, and dispatches requests to maximize cache hit rates. |
| **`sgl-model-gateway`** | A high-performance control and data plane service managing worker registries, dynamic load balancing, circuit breaking, WASM middleware plugins, and multi-model IGW mode. |
| **`sglang-simulator`** | An offline simulation tool that reuses SGLang's radix cache and batch scheduler logic while replacing neural forward passes with analytical latency predictors, enabling large-scale trace replay and serving capacity planning. |

Sources: [python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py:149-160](), [python/sglang/srt/distributed/bootstrap.py:10-25]()
